en.question: A company has a mobile application that makes HTTP API calls to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB routes requests to an AWS Lambda function. Many different versions of the application are in use at any given time, including versions that are in testing by a subset of users. The version of the application is defined in the user-agent header that is sent with all requests to the API. After a series of recent changes to the API, the company has observed issues with the application. The company needs to gather a metric for each API operation by response code for each version of the application that is in use. A DevOps engineer has modified the Lambda function to extract the API operation name, version information from the user-agent header and response code. Which additional set of actions should the DevOps engineer take to gather the required metrics?

options.A: Modify the Lambda function to write the API operation name, response code, and version number as a log line to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that increments a metric for each API operation name. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
options.B: Modify the Lambda function to write the API operation name, response code, and version number as a log line to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure a CloudWatch Logs Insights query to populate CloudWatch metrics from the log lines. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
options.C: Configure the ALB access logs to write to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Modify the Lambda function to respond to the ALB with the API operation name, response code, and version number as response metadata. Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that increments a metric for each API operation name. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
options.D: Configure AWS X-Ray integration on the Lambda function. Modify the Lambda function to create an X-Ray subsegment with the API operation name, response code, and version number. Configure X-Ray insights to extract an aggregated metric for each API operation name and to publish the metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The Lambda function already extracts the three attributes needed for monitoring:

- API operation name
- HTTP response code
- Mobile application version from the `User-Agent` header

The remaining requirement is to continuously convert those per-request attributes into CloudWatch metrics, separated by operation, response code, and application version.

## Correct answer: A

The Lambda function should emit a structured log event—preferably JSON or a consistently space-delimited format—containing the operation name, response code, and application version. A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can then publish a value of `1` for every matching request and use the extracted fields as metric dimensions.

CloudWatch Logs metric filters are specifically designed to convert matching log events into numerical CloudWatch metrics. AWS documents that the metric value can be `1` for each occurrence and that dimensions further identify each unique metric series. AWS also supports extracting dimensions from fields in JSON or space-delimited log events, with up to three dimensions. Therefore, the operation can identify the metric while response code and application version provide the requested breakdown. See [CloudWatch Logs metric filter concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html) and [publishing dimensions with metric filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/FilterAndPatternSyntaxForMetricFilters.html).

For example, the Lambda function could log:

```json
{"operation":"CreateOrder","responseCode":"500","appVersion":"4.2.1"}
```

The filter would publish a count of `1` and extract `responseCode` and `appVersion` as dimensions. The company should monitor dimension cardinality and cost because each unique dimension combination creates a distinct custom metric.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. CloudWatch Logs Insights query

CloudWatch Logs Insights is primarily a query and analysis capability; a normal Logs Insights query does not directly and continuously populate a CloudWatch custom metric as described. Even scheduled Logs Insights queries deliver results to destinations such as Amazon S3 or Amazon EventBridge rather than inherently creating the required dimensional CloudWatch metrics. Metric filters are the direct feature for converting incoming log events into metrics. See [automating log analysis with scheduled queries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/ScheduledQueries.html).

### C. ALB access logs to CloudWatch Logs with Lambda response metadata

This option contains unsupported assumptions. Application Load Balancer access logs are delivered as compressed files to an Amazon S3 bucket, not directly to a CloudWatch Logs log group. Although ALB access logs contain fields such as the request, user agent, and response status, the proposed mechanism of adding arbitrary Lambda response metadata for inclusion in the ALB access log is not the appropriate supported solution. See [Application Load Balancer access logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html).

### D. X-Ray subsegments and X-Ray Insights

X-Ray is intended for distributed tracing and request analysis. Subsegments provide timing and downstream-call details, while annotations can be indexed to filter and group traces; they do not cause X-Ray Insights to extract arbitrary fields and publish the requested custom CloudWatch metric dimensions. X-Ray group metrics count traces that match a group’s filter criteria, which is different from publishing a custom per-operation metric dimensioned by response code and application version. X-Ray tracing can also be sampled, making it unsuitable as the primary source for an exact request-count metric. See [X-Ray subsegments, annotations, and metadata](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-concepts.html) and [X-Ray group metrics in CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-console-groups.html).

**Answer: A**

zh.question: 某公司有一个移动应用程序，该应用程序向 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 发出 HTTP API 调用。ALB 将请求路由到一个 AWS Lambda 函数。在任意给定时间，都有许多不同版本的应用程序正在使用，其中包括由一部分用户测试的版本。应用程序版本由发送到 API 的所有请求中的 user-agent 标头定义。在对 API 进行一系列近期更改后，公司发现应用程序存在问题。公司需要按响应代码收集每个 API 操作的指标，并且要针对正在使用的每个应用程序版本分别收集。DevOps 工程师已修改 Lambda 函数，以提取 API 操作名称、user-agent 标头中的版本信息以及响应代码。DevOps 工程师还应采取哪组额外操作来收集所需指标？

options.A: 修改 Lambda 函数，将 API 操作名称、响应代码和版本号作为日志行写入 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 日志组。配置 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器，以便为每个 API 操作名称递增一个指标。将响应代码和应用程序版本指定为该指标的维度。
options.B: 修改 Lambda 函数，将 API 操作名称、响应代码和版本号作为日志行写入 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 日志组。配置 CloudWatch Logs Insights 查询，以根据日志行填充 CloudWatch 指标。将响应代码和应用程序版本指定为该指标的维度。
options.C: 配置 ALB 访问日志以写入 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 日志组。修改 Lambda 函数，使其向 ALB 返回包含 API 操作名称、响应代码和版本号的响应元数据。配置 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器，以便为每个 API 操作名称递增一个指标。将响应代码和应用程序版本指定为该指标的维度。
options.D: 在 Lambda 函数上配置 AWS X-Ray 集成。修改 Lambda 函数以创建包含 API 操作名称、响应代码和版本号的 X-Ray 子分段。配置 X-Ray Insights，以提取每个 API 操作名称的聚合指标并将该指标发布到 Amazon CloudWatch。将响应代码和应用程序版本指定为该指标的维度。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

Lambda 函数已经提取了监控所需的三个属性：

- API 操作名称
- HTTP 响应代码
- 来自 `User-Agent` 标头的移动应用程序版本

剩余要求是将这些每请求属性持续转换为 CloudWatch 指标，并按操作、响应代码和应用程序版本进行区分。

## 正确答案：A

Lambda 函数应发出一个结构化日志事件——最好采用 JSON 或一致的空格分隔格式——其中包含操作名称、响应代码和应用程序版本。随后，CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器可以为每个匹配请求发布值 `1`，并将提取的字段用作指标维度。

CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器专门用于将匹配的日志事件转换为数值型 CloudWatch 指标。AWS 文档指出，每次出现的指标值可以为 `1`，维度可进一步标识每个唯一的指标时间序列。AWS 还支持从 JSON 或空格分隔日志事件的字段中提取维度，最多支持三个维度。因此，操作可标识指标，而响应代码和应用程序版本可提供所需的细分。请参阅 [CloudWatch Logs metric filter concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html) 和 [publishing dimensions with metric filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/FilterAndPatternSyntaxForMetricFilters.html)。

例如，Lambda 函数可以记录：

```json
{"operation":"CreateOrder","responseCode":"500","appVersion":"4.2.1"}
```

筛选器将发布计数值 `1`，并将 `responseCode` 和 `appVersion` 提取为维度。公司应监控维度基数和成本，因为每个唯一的维度组合都会创建不同的自定义指标。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

### B. CloudWatch Logs Insights 查询

CloudWatch Logs Insights 主要是一项查询和分析功能；普通的 Logs Insights 查询不会如描述所述直接且持续地填充 CloudWatch 自定义指标。即使是计划的 Logs Insights 查询，也会将结果传送到 Amazon S3 或 Amazon EventBridge 等目标，而不是天然创建所需的具有维度的 CloudWatch 指标。指标筛选器才是将传入日志事件转换为指标的直接功能。请参阅 [automating log analysis with scheduled queries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/ScheduledQueries.html)。

### C. 将 ALB 访问日志写入 CloudWatch Logs 并使用 Lambda 响应元数据

该选项包含不受支持的假设。Application Load Balancer 访问日志会作为压缩文件传送到 Amazon S3 存储桶，而不是直接传送到 CloudWatch Logs 日志组。尽管 ALB 访问日志包含请求、user agent 和响应状态等字段，但提议通过添加任意 Lambda 响应元数据以将其包含在 ALB 访问日志中的机制，并不是适当的受支持解决方案。请参阅 [Application Load Balancer access logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html)。

### D. X-Ray 子分段和 X-Ray Insights

X-Ray 旨在用于分布式追踪和请求分析。子分段可提供时序和下游调用详细信息，而注释可被编入索引以筛选和分组追踪；它们不会使 X-Ray Insights 提取任意字段并发布所需的自定义 CloudWatch 指标维度。X-Ray 组指标会统计与某个组筛选条件匹配的追踪数量，这不同于发布按响应代码和应用程序版本设置维度的自定义每操作指标。X-Ray 追踪也可能会被采样，因此不适合作为精确请求计数指标的主要来源。请参阅 [X-Ray subsegments, annotations, and metadata](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-concepts.html) 和 [X-Ray group metrics in CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-console-groups.html)。

**答案：A**

en.question: A company provides an application to customers. The application has an Amazon API Gateway REST API that invokes an AWS Lambda function. On initialization, the Lambda function loads a large amount of data from an Amazon DynamoDB table. The data load process results in long cold-start times of 8-10 seconds. The DynamoDB table has DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) configured. Customers report that the application intermittently takes a long time to respond to requests. The application receives thousands of requests throughout the day. In the middle of the day, the application experiences 10 times more requests than at any other time of the day. Near the end of the day, the application's request volume decreases to 10% of its normal total. A DevOps engineer needs to reduce the latency of the Lambda function at all times of the day. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function with a concurrency value of 1. Delete the DAX cluster for the DynamoDB table.
options.B: Configure reserved concurrency on the Lambda function with a concurrency value of 0.
options.C: Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the Lambda function with provisioned concurrency values set to a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100.
options.D: Configure reserved concurrency on the Lambda function. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the API Gateway API with a reserved concurrency maximum value of 100.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The function performs expensive initialization by loading a large data set, causing 8–10 second cold starts. Traffic varies substantially during the day, including a predictable 10× peak and a large late-day decrease. The solution therefore needs to:

1. Keep at least some Lambda execution environments initialized to avoid cold starts during low-volume periods.
2. Increase and decrease that pre-initialized capacity as demand changes.

## Correct answer: C

**Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function, and use AWS Application Auto Scaling with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100.**

Lambda **provisioned concurrency** creates pre-initialized execution environments that are ready to respond immediately, specifically addressing initialization-related cold-start latency. By contrast, reserved concurrency does not pre-initialize environments. AWS documents these differences in [Understanding reserved concurrency and provisioned concurrency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html).

Application Auto Scaling can manage Lambda provisioned concurrency either according to a schedule or through a utilization-based target tracking policy. AWS provides an example that registers Lambda provisioned concurrency as a scalable target with `--min-capacity 1 --max-capacity 100`, exactly matching this option. The minimum of 1 maintains a baseline initialized environment during low traffic, while scaling toward 100 accommodates increased demand and scaling back in avoids maintaining peak capacity all day. See [Using Application Auto Scaling to automate provisioned concurrency management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html) and [Registering Lambda functions as scalable targets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-lambda.html).

Because the question describes a recurring midday peak, scheduled scaling could be used to provision capacity before the peak; target tracking can also adjust capacity according to sustained utilization.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Provisioned concurrency of 1 and delete DAX

A fixed provisioned concurrency value of 1 protects only one concurrent invocation from initialization latency. During the 10× traffic period, requests above that provisioned capacity can use ordinary on-demand concurrency and experience cold starts.

Deleting DAX is also counterproductive. DAX provides fast, in-memory reads with microsecond latency and can offload repeated read activity from DynamoDB. Removing it does not solve Lambda execution-environment initialization and could increase data-access latency. See [DAX use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html).

### B. Reserved concurrency of 0

Reserved concurrency does not keep environments initialized. More importantly, setting reserved concurrency to `0` intentionally throttles the function and prevents it from processing events, as documented in [Configuring reserved concurrency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html).

### D. Reserved concurrency on Lambda and Application Auto Scaling on API Gateway

Reserved concurrency allocates and caps concurrency for a Lambda function, but its environments are still created on demand, so cold starts remain possible. The scalable Lambda dimension supported by Application Auto Scaling is `lambda:function:ProvisionedConcurrency`, applied to a Lambda version or alias—not an API Gateway “reserved concurrency” setting. Therefore this option neither targets the cold-start mechanism nor describes a valid Application Auto Scaling configuration for the API.

**Answer: C**

zh.question: 一家公司向客户提供一款应用程序。该应用程序具有一个 Amazon API Gateway REST API，用于调用 AWS Lambda 函数。初始化期间，该 Lambda 函数会从 Amazon DynamoDB 表加载大量数据。数据加载过程导致较长的冷启动时间，为 8-10 秒。该 DynamoDB 表已配置 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)。客户报告该应用程序偶尔需要很长时间才能响应请求。该应用程序全天会收到数千个请求。在一天的中间时段，该应用程序的请求量是当天其他任何时段的 10 倍。接近一天结束时，该应用程序的请求量降至正常总量的 10%。一名 DevOps 工程师需要在一天中的任何时段都降低 Lambda 函数的延迟。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Lambda 函数上配置预置并发，且并发值设为 1。删除 DynamoDB 表的 DAX 集群。
options.B: 在 Lambda 函数上配置预留并发，且并发值设为 0。
options.C: 在 Lambda 函数上配置预置并发。在 Lambda 函数上配置 AWS Application Auto Scaling，并将预置并发值设为最小值 1、最大值 100。
options.D: 在 Lambda 函数上配置预留并发。在 API Gateway API 上配置 AWS Application Auto Scaling，并将预留并发最大值设为 100。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该函数通过加载大型数据集执行开销较高的初始化，导致冷启动耗时 8–10 秒。流量在一天中变化很大，包括可预测的 10 倍峰值和当天晚些时候的大幅下降。因此，该解决方案需要：

1. 保持至少一部分 Lambda 执行环境处于已初始化状态，以避免低流量期间的冷启动。
2. 随着需求变化增加和减少这部分预初始化容量。

## 正确答案：C

**在 Lambda 函数上配置预置并发，并使用 AWS Application Auto Scaling，将最小值设为 1、最大值设为 100。**

Lambda **预置并发**会创建已预初始化、可立即响应的执行环境，专门解决与初始化相关的冷启动延迟。相比之下，预留并发不会预初始化环境。AWS 在 [了解预留并发和预置并发](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html) 中说明了这些区别。

Application Auto Scaling 可以按计划或通过基于利用率的目标跟踪策略管理 Lambda 预置并发。AWS 提供了一个示例，将 Lambda 预置并发注册为可扩缩目标，并使用 `--min-capacity 1 --max-capacity 100`，这与该选项完全一致。最小值为 1 可在低流量期间维持一个已初始化环境作为基准；向 100 扩展可满足增长的需求，而缩减则避免全天维持峰值容量。请参阅 [使用 Application Auto Scaling 自动管理预置并发](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html) 和 [将 Lambda 函数注册为可扩缩目标](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-lambda.html)。

由于题目描述了每日重复出现的中午高峰，可以使用计划扩缩在高峰前预置容量；目标跟踪也可以根据持续的利用率调整容量。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. 预置并发为 1 并删除 DAX

固定为 1 的预置并发只能保护一个并发调用免受初始化延迟的影响。在流量达到 10 倍的时段，超过该预置容量的请求可能会使用普通的按需并发，并经历冷启动。

删除 DAX 同样适得其反。DAX 提供具有微秒级延迟的快速内存中读取，并且可以将重复读取活动从 DynamoDB 卸载。删除它无法解决 Lambda 执行环境初始化问题，反而可能增加数据访问延迟。请参阅 [DAX 使用案例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)。

### B. 预留并发为 0

预留并发不会保持环境处于已初始化状态。更重要的是，将预留并发设为 `0` 会故意限制该函数，并阻止其处理事件，如 [配置预留并发](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html) 中所述。

### D. 在 Lambda 上使用预留并发，并在 API Gateway 上使用 Application Auto Scaling

预留并发会为 Lambda 函数分配并限制并发量，但其环境仍按需创建，因此仍可能发生冷启动。Application Auto Scaling 支持的可扩缩 Lambda 维度是 `lambda:function:ProvisionedConcurrency`，应用于 Lambda 版本或别名，而不是 API Gateway 的“预留并发”设置。因此，该选项既未针对冷启动机制，也未描述 API 的有效 Application Auto Scaling 配置。

**答案：C**

en.question: A company is adopting AWS CodeDeploy to automate its application deployments for a Java-Apache Tomcat application with an Apache Webserver. The development team started with a proof of concept, created a deployment group for a developer environment, and performed functional tests within the application. After completion, the team will create additional deployment groups for staging and production. The current log level is configured within the Apache settings, but the team wants to change this configuration dynamically when the deployment occurs, so that they can set different log level configurations depending on the deployment group without having a different application revision for each group. How can these requirements be met with the LEAST management overhead and without requiring different script versions for each deployment group?

options.A: Tag the Amazon EC2 instances depending on the deployment group. Then place a script into the application revision that calls the metadata service and the EC2 API to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference the script as part of the AfterInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.
options.B: Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ NAME to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the BeforeInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.
options.C: Create a CodeDeploy custom environment variable for each environment. Then place a script into the application revision that checks this environment variable to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the ValidateService lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.
options.D: Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID to identify which deployment group the instance is part of to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the Install lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The requirement is to use **one application revision and one script** across development, staging, and production, while dynamically changing the Apache log level according to the CodeDeploy deployment group. The lowest-overhead solution should therefore use context that CodeDeploy already exposes to lifecycle hook scripts, without adding EC2 tags, API calls, IAM permissions, or separately maintained configuration.

## Correct answer: B

CodeDeploy automatically makes `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME` available to lifecycle hook scripts. A single script can branch on that value—for example, `Development`, `Staging`, or `Production`—and modify the Apache configuration accordingly.

AWS documentation provides essentially this exact use case: a script checks whether `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME` is `Staging` and changes Apache's `LogLevel` from `warn` to `debug`. AWS states that this script should be invoked during the `BeforeInstall` lifecycle event. This enables the same revision and script to be reused for every deployment group, with no additional infrastructure or per-group script versions. See the [CodeDeploy AppSpec hooks documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A:** This could potentially be engineered, but it adds unnecessary management overhead. The company would need to maintain EC2 tags, grant permission to call the EC2 API, query instance metadata to identify the instance, call the API, and implement tag-to-environment logic. CodeDeploy already supplies the deployment group directly to the hook through `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME`, so this is not the least-overhead approach. Although `AfterInstall` can be used for application configuration, the AWS-documented Apache log-level pattern specifically uses `BeforeInstall`.

- **C:** CodeDeploy exposes built-in variables to hook scripts, including `APPLICATION_NAME`, `DEPLOYMENT_ID`, `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME`, `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID`, and `LIFECYCLE_EVENT`; the documented mechanism is not to create arbitrary per-environment “CodeDeploy custom environment variables.” In addition, `ValidateService` is the final lifecycle event and is intended to verify that the deployment completed successfully, not to perform preinstallation configuration changes.

- **D:** `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID` is a real built-in variable and could identify a deployment group, but the proposed lifecycle hook is invalid. The `Install` event is reserved for the CodeDeploy agent to copy revision files to their destination and **cannot be used to run scripts**. Therefore, a script cannot be referenced under `Install` in the AppSpec file. A group name is also simpler and more readable for environment-based branching than maintaining mappings for opaque group IDs.

The lifecycle event purposes, the restriction on scripting the `Install` event, the available hook environment variables, and the Apache `LogLevel` example are all documented on the [AppSpec hooks reference page](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html).

Therefore, **B** meets the requirements with the least management overhead.

zh.question: 一家公司正在采用 AWS CodeDeploy 来自动化部署其使用 Apache Webserver 的 Java-Apache Tomcat 应用程序。开发团队从概念验证开始，为开发环境创建了一个部署组，并在应用程序内执行了功能测试。完成后，团队将为预发布和生产环境创建其他部署组。当前日志级别在 Apache 设置中配置，但团队希望在部署发生时动态更改此配置，以便能够根据部署组设置不同的日志级别配置，而无需为每个组使用不同的应用程序修订版本。如何以**最低**管理开销满足这些要求，并且不需要为每个部署组使用不同的脚本版本？

options.A: 根据部署组为 Amazon EC2 实例添加标签。然后，将一个脚本放入应用程序修订版本中，该脚本调用元数据服务和 EC2 API，以确定实例属于哪个部署组。使用此信息配置日志级别设置。在 appspec.yml 文件中，将该脚本作为 AfterInstall 生命周期挂钩的一部分进行引用。
options.B: 创建一个脚本，该脚本使用 CodeDeploy 环境变量 DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ NAME 来识别实例属于哪个部署组。使用此信息配置日志级别设置。在 appspec.yml 文件中，将此脚本作为 BeforeInstall 生命周期挂钩的一部分进行引用。
options.C: 为每个环境创建一个 CodeDeploy 自定义环境变量。然后，将一个脚本放入应用程序修订版本中，该脚本检查此环境变量，以确定实例属于哪个部署组。使用此信息配置日志级别设置。在 appspec.yml 文件中，将此脚本作为 ValidateService 生命周期挂钩的一部分进行引用。
options.D: 创建一个脚本，该脚本使用 CodeDeploy 环境变量 DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID 来识别实例属于哪个部署组，以配置日志级别设置。在 appspec.yml 文件中，将此脚本作为 Install 生命周期挂钩的一部分进行引用。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

要求是在开发、预发布和生产环境中使用**同一个应用程序修订版本和同一个脚本**，同时根据 CodeDeploy 部署组动态更改 Apache 日志级别。因此，管理开销最低的解决方案应使用 CodeDeploy 已向生命周期挂钩脚本公开的上下文，而无需添加 EC2 标签、API 调用、IAM 权限或单独维护的配置。

## 正确答案：B

CodeDeploy 会自动向生命周期挂钩脚本提供 `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME`。一个脚本可以根据该值进行分支处理，例如 `Development`、`Staging` 或 `Production`，并相应地修改 Apache 配置。

AWS 文档提供了几乎完全相同的用例：脚本检查 `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME` 是否为 `Staging`，并将 Apache 的 `LogLevel` 从 `warn` 更改为 `debug`。AWS 指出，应在 `BeforeInstall` 生命周期事件期间调用此脚本。这样可以针对每个部署组重用相同的修订版本和脚本，而无需额外的基础设施或每组单独的脚本版本。请参阅 [CodeDeploy AppSpec hooks 文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html)。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

- **A：** 虽然这在技术上可以实现，但会增加不必要的管理开销。公司需要维护 EC2 标签、授予调用 EC2 API 的权限、查询实例元数据以识别实例、调用 API，并实现标签到环境的逻辑。CodeDeploy 已经通过 `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME` 直接向挂钩提供部署组信息，因此这不是管理开销最低的方法。虽然 `AfterInstall` 可用于应用程序配置，但 AWS 文档中针对 Apache 日志级别的模式明确使用 `BeforeInstall`。

- **C：** CodeDeploy 向挂钩脚本公开内置变量，包括 `APPLICATION_NAME`、`DEPLOYMENT_ID`、`DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME`、`DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID` 和 `LIFECYCLE_EVENT`；文档中描述的机制并不是创建任意的、按环境区分的“CodeDeploy 自定义环境变量”。此外，`ValidateService` 是最后一个生命周期事件，用于验证部署是否成功完成，而不是执行安装前的配置更改。

- **D：** `DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID` 是真实的内置变量，可以用于标识部署组，但所建议的生命周期挂钩无效。`Install` 事件保留给 CodeDeploy agent 将修订文件复制到其目标位置，且**不能用于运行脚本**。因此，不能在 AppSpec 文件的 `Install` 下引用脚本。与为不透明的组 ID 维护映射相比，组名称对于按环境进行分支处理也更简单、更易读。

生命周期事件的用途、不能对 `Install` 事件编写脚本的限制、可用的挂钩环境变量以及 Apache `LogLevel` 示例，均记录在 [AppSpec hooks 参考页面](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure-hooks.html) 中。

因此，**B** 以最低管理开销满足这些要求。

en.question: A company requires its developers to tag all Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes in an account to indicate a desired backup frequency. This requirement Includes EBS volumes that do not require backups. The company uses custom tags named Backup_Frequency that have values of none, dally, or weekly that correspond to the desired backup frequency. An audit finds that developers are occasionally not tagging the EBS volumes. A DevOps engineer needs to ensure that all EBS volumes always have the Backup_Frequency tag so that the company can perform backups at least weekly unless a different value is specified. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up AWS Config in the account. Create a custom rule that returns a compliance failure for all Amazon EC2 resources that do not have a Backup Frequency tag applied. Configure a remediation action that uses a custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to apply the Backup_Frequency tag with a value of weekly.
options.B: Set up AWS Config in the account. Use a managed rule that returns a compliance failure for EC2::Volume resources that do not have a Backup Frequency tag applied. Configure a remediation action that uses a custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to apply the Backup_Frequency tag with a value of weekly.
options.C: Turn on AWS CloudTrail in the account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to EBS CreateVolume events. Configure a custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to apply the Backup_Frequency tag with a value of weekly. Specify the runbook as the target of the rule.
options.D: Turn on AWS CloudTrail in the account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to EBS CreateVolume events or EBS ModifyVolume events. Configure a custom AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to apply the Backup_Frequency tag with a value of weekly. Specify the runbook as the target of the rule.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs a continuous compliance-and-remediation mechanism for **all EBS volumes**, including existing volumes. If an EBS volume is missing the `Backup_Frequency` tag, the solution must add the conservative default value `weekly`. A developer-specified tag such as `none`, `daily`, or `weekly` must not be overwritten merely because the volume is otherwise modified.

## Correct answer: B

AWS Config provides the managed rule **`required-tags`** (`REQUIRED_TAGS`). This rule checks for specified tag keys and can optionally validate permitted values. Crucially, its supported resource types include **`AWS::EC2::Volume`**, and it is triggered by configuration changes. The rule can therefore be scoped to EBS volumes and configured to require `Backup_Frequency` (optionally with the accepted values `none,daily,weekly`). See the [`required-tags` managed rule documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/required-tags.html).

When an EBS volume is evaluated as noncompliant because the tag is absent, AWS Config can invoke a Systems Manager Automation runbook as a remediation action. AWS documents that Config remediation uses Systems Manager Automation documents and supports custom documents. In addition, the `required-tags` documentation specifically states that the managed `AWS-SetRequiredTags` document does **not** work as remediation for this rule, so a **custom Automation runbook** is appropriate. See [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html).

The custom runbook should add `Backup_Frequency=weekly` only to volumes that the rule identified as missing the required tag. Existing valid developer-selected values are therefore preserved.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A — Incorrect

A custom Config rule is unnecessary because the AWS-managed `required-tags` rule already supports `AWS::EC2::Volume`. Moreover, the option says to evaluate **all Amazon EC2 resources**, which is broader than the requirement and could mark unrelated EC2 resource types as noncompliant. The managed rule can be scoped directly to EBS volumes, making B more precise and operationally simpler.

### C — Incorrect

A rule that reacts only to `CreateVolume` is event-driven rather than a continuous inventory-based compliance check. It does not reliably address pre-existing untagged volumes, and it will not remediate a volume if someone later deletes the required tag. Tag deletion is performed through the separate [`DeleteTags` API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteTags.html), which this option does not monitor.

### D — Incorrect

Adding `ModifyVolume` still does not provide complete tag enforcement. `ModifyVolume` changes EBS properties such as size, volume type, IOPS, and throughput; it is not the API for changing tags. Tags are added or overwritten through [`CreateTags`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateTags.html) and removed through [`DeleteTags`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteTags.html). Therefore, monitoring `CreateVolume` and `ModifyVolume` would miss tag deletion and would not continuously evaluate all existing volumes. It could also apply `weekly` after an unrelated volume modification even when the developer already specified another valid backup frequency.

Thus, **B** is the solution that directly combines resource-specific continuous compliance detection with automatic remediation.

zh.question: 一家公司要求其开发人员为账户中的所有 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷添加标签，以指示所需的备份频率。该要求包括不需要备份的 EBS 卷。公司使用名为 Backup_Frequency 的自定义标签，其值为 none、dally 或 weekly，分别对应所需的备份频率。一项审计发现，开发人员偶尔不会为 EBS 卷添加标签。一名 DevOps 工程师需要确保所有 EBS 卷始终具有 Backup_Frequency 标签，以便公司能够至少每周执行备份，除非指定了其他值。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在账户中设置 AWS Config。创建一条自定义规则，对未应用 Backup Frequency 标签的所有 Amazon EC2 资源返回合规性失败。配置一项修复操作，使用自定义 AWS Systems Manager Automation 运行手册应用值为 weekly 的 Backup_Frequency 标签。
options.B: 在账户中设置 AWS Config。使用一条托管规则，对未应用 Backup Frequency 标签的 EC2::Volume 资源返回合规性失败。配置一项修复操作，使用自定义 AWS Systems Manager Automation 运行手册应用值为 weekly 的 Backup_Frequency 标签。
options.C: 在账户中启用 AWS CloudTrail。创建一条对 EBS CreateVolume 事件作出响应的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。配置一个自定义 AWS Systems Manager Automation 运行手册来应用值为 weekly 的 Backup_Frequency 标签。将该运行手册指定为该规则的目标。
options.D: 在账户中启用 AWS CloudTrail。创建一条对 EBS CreateVolume 事件或 EBS ModifyVolume 事件作出响应的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。配置一个自定义 AWS Systems Manager Automation 运行手册来应用值为 weekly 的 Backup_Frequency 标签。将该运行手册指定为该规则的目标。

zh.explanation:
## 问题要求

公司需要一种针对**所有 EBS 卷**（包括现有卷）的持续合规与修复机制。如果 EBS 卷缺少 `Backup_Frequency` 标签，解决方案必须添加保守的默认值 `weekly`。开发人员指定的标签值，例如 `none`、`daily` 或 `weekly`，不得仅因卷被以其他方式修改而遭到覆盖。

## 正确答案：B

AWS Config 提供托管规则 **`required-tags`** (`REQUIRED_TAGS`)。该规则检查指定的标签键，并且可以选择验证允许的值。关键在于，其支持的资源类型包括 **`AWS::EC2::Volume`**，并且由配置更改触发。因此，该规则可以限定为 EBS 卷，并配置为要求 `Backup_Frequency`（可选择设置允许的值为 `none,daily,weekly`）。请参阅 [`required-tags` 托管规则文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/required-tags.html)。

当 EBS 卷因缺少标签而被评估为不合规时，AWS Config 可以调用 Systems Manager Automation 运行手册作为修复操作。AWS 文档说明，Config 修复使用 Systems Manager Automation 文档，并支持自定义文档。此外，`required-tags` 文档特别指出，托管的 `AWS-SetRequiredTags` 文档**不能**用作此规则的修复措施，因此使用**自定义 Automation 运行手册**是合适的。请参阅 [使用 AWS Config 修复不合规资源](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html)。

自定义运行手册应仅向被规则识别为缺少必需标签的卷添加 `Backup_Frequency=weekly`。因此，现有的、由开发人员选择的有效值将得到保留。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A — 错误

不需要自定义 Config 规则，因为 AWS 托管的 `required-tags` 规则已经支持 `AWS::EC2::Volume`。此外，该选项表示评估**所有 Amazon EC2 资源**，这比要求的范围更广，并且可能将无关的 EC2 资源类型标记为不合规。托管规则可以直接限定为 EBS 卷，因此 B 更精确且在运维上更简单。

### C — 错误

仅对 `CreateVolume` 作出响应的规则是事件驱动的，而不是基于资源清单的持续合规检查。它无法可靠地处理预先存在且未添加标签的卷，并且如果有人随后删除了必需标签，也不会修复该卷。标签删除通过单独的 [`DeleteTags` API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteTags.html) 执行，而该选项并未监控此 API。

### D — 错误

添加 `ModifyVolume` 仍无法提供完整的标签强制执行。`ModifyVolume` 用于更改 EBS 属性，例如大小、卷类型、IOPS 和吞吐量；它不是用于更改标签的 API。标签通过 [`CreateTags`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateTags.html) 添加或覆盖，并通过 [`DeleteTags`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteTags.html) 删除。因此，监控 `CreateVolume` 和 `ModifyVolume` 会遗漏标签删除，也无法持续评估所有现有卷。此外，即使开发人员已经指定了其他有效的备份频率，它也可能在无关的卷修改后应用 `weekly`。

因此，**B** 是将特定资源的持续合规检测与自动修复直接结合的解决方案。

en.question: A company is using an Amazon Aurora cluster as the data store for its application. The Aurora cluster is configured with a single DB instance. The application performs read and write operations on the database by using the cluster's instance endpoint. The company has scheduled an update to be applied to the cluster during an upcoming maintenance window. The cluster must remain available with the least possible interruption during the maintenance window. What should a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Add a reader instance to the Aurora cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster endpoint for write operations. Update the Aurora cluster's reader endpoint for reads.
options.B: Add a reader instance to the Aurora cluster. Create a custom ANY endpoint for the cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster's custom ANY endpoint for read and write operations.
options.C: Turn on the Multi-AZ option on the Aurora cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster endpoint for write operations. Update the Aurora cluster’s reader endpoint for reads.
options.D: Turn on the Multi-AZ option on the Aurora cluster. Create a custom ANY endpoint for the cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster's custom ANY endpoint for read and write operations

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The Aurora cluster currently has only one DB instance, and the application connects through that instance's endpoint. This creates two availability problems:

1. There is no Aurora Replica that Aurora can promote if maintenance makes the writer unavailable.
2. An instance endpoint remains tied to one specific DB instance and does not automatically follow a failover.

The question asks for the configuration that provides the **least possible interruption** for both reads and writes during maintenance.

## Correct answer: A

**Add a reader instance to the Aurora cluster. Use the cluster endpoint for writes and the reader endpoint for reads.**

An Aurora Replica provides a promotion target if the current writer becomes unavailable. AWS states that when a problem affects the primary instance, a reader can take over as the primary through failover. AWS also specifically documents that an existing single-instance Aurora cluster can be converted to a Multi-AZ cluster by **adding a reader DB instance in a different Availability Zone**. See [High availability for Aurora DB instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html).

The endpoint changes are also important:

- The **cluster endpoint** always represents the current writer. If Aurora promotes the reader, the endpoint is updated to connect to the new writer.
- The **reader endpoint** routes read-only connections among available Aurora Replicas.
- Unlike an instance endpoint, the cluster and reader endpoints automatically adjust when an instance becomes unavailable.

AWS explicitly recommends the cluster endpoint for read/write or general-purpose connections and the reader endpoint for read-only connections when high availability is important. See [Amazon Aurora endpoint connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Endpoints.html).

This architecture therefore supplies a failover target and removes the application's dependency on the original instance endpoint.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Add a reader and use a custom `ANY` endpoint for all operations

Aurora does support custom endpoints of type `ANY`, contrary to comments claiming that such endpoints do not exist. However, an `ANY` custom endpoint can include both writer and reader instances, and Aurora distributes connections among associated instances with equal probability. Consequently, a connection that needs to perform writes could be directed to a read-only Aurora Replica. A custom `ANY` endpoint is therefore not an appropriate replacement for the cluster endpoint for mixed read/write traffic. See [Specifying properties for custom endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Custom.Considerations.html).

### C. Turn on the Multi-AZ option and use the standard endpoints

For an **existing** single-instance Aurora cluster, the documented method to make the DB-instance layer Multi-AZ is to add a reader instance in another AZ. There is not a separate modification in this scenario that merely turns the existing lone DB instance into a standby-backed Aurora deployment. Option A states the concrete required action; option C omits it. Aurora's distributed storage is already replicated across AZs, but DB-instance failover still requires a reader instance that can be promoted. See [High availability for Aurora DB instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html).

### D. Turn on Multi-AZ and use a custom `ANY` endpoint for all operations

This has both problems described above: it does not clearly specify adding the required reader instance to the existing cluster, and an `ANY` endpoint can send a write-capable connection to a read-only instance. The cluster endpoint—not an `ANY` custom endpoint—is the correct endpoint for write traffic.

zh.question: 一家公司将 Amazon Aurora 集群用作其应用程序的数据存储。该 Aurora 集群配置了单个 DB 实例。应用程序通过该集群的实例终端节点对数据库执行读取和写入操作。该公司计划在即将到来的维护时段内对集群应用更新。集群必须在维护时段内保持可用，并将中断降至最低。DevOps 工程师应如何做才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 向 Aurora 集群添加一个读取器实例。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群终端节点进行写入操作。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群的读取器终端节点进行读取操作。
options.B: 向 Aurora 集群添加一个读取器实例。为集群创建一个自定义 `ANY` 终端节点。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群的自定义 `ANY` 终端节点进行读取和写入操作。
options.C: 在 Aurora 集群上启用 Multi-AZ 选项。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群终端节点进行写入操作。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群的读取器终端节点进行读取操作。
options.D: 在 Aurora 集群上启用 Multi-AZ 选项。为集群创建一个自定义 `ANY` 终端节点。更新应用程序以使用 Aurora 集群的自定义 `ANY` 终端节点进行读取和写入操作。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

Aurora cluster 当前只有一个 DB instance，并且应用程序通过该实例的 endpoint 进行连接。这会造成两个可用性问题：

1. 如果维护导致 writer 不可用，则没有可供 Aurora 提升的 Aurora Replica。
2. instance endpoint 始终绑定到某个特定 DB instance，且不会自动跟随故障转移。

题目要求提供一种配置，以便在维护期间为读取和写入操作实现**尽可能少的中断**。

## 正确答案：A

**向 Aurora cluster 添加一个 reader instance。使用 cluster endpoint 进行写入，使用 reader endpoint 进行读取。**

如果当前 writer 变得不可用，Aurora Replica 可作为提升目标。AWS 指出，当问题影响 primary instance 时，reader 可以通过故障转移接管并成为 primary。AWS 还特别说明，现有的单实例 Aurora cluster 可以通过**在不同 Availability Zone 中添加一个 reader DB instance**转换为 Multi-AZ cluster。请参阅 [Aurora DB instances 的高可用性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html)。

endpoint 的变更同样很重要：

- **cluster endpoint** 始终表示当前 writer。如果 Aurora 提升 reader，该 endpoint 会更新以连接到新的 writer。
- **reader endpoint** 会在可用的 Aurora Replicas 之间路由只读连接。
- 与 instance endpoint 不同，cluster 和 reader endpoints 会在某个 instance 不可用时自动调整。

AWS 明确建议：当高可用性十分重要时，应将 cluster endpoint 用于读/写或通用连接，并将 reader endpoint 用于只读连接。请参阅 [Amazon Aurora endpoint connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Endpoints.html)。

因此，该架构提供了一个故障转移目标，并消除了应用程序对原始 instance endpoint 的依赖。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B. 添加 reader，并将自定义 `ANY` endpoint 用于所有操作

与声称此类 endpoint 不存在的评论相反，Aurora 确实支持 `ANY` 类型的自定义 endpoints。但是，`ANY` 自定义 endpoint 可以同时包含 writer 和 reader instances，Aurora 会以相等的概率在关联 instances 之间分配连接。因此，需要执行写入的连接可能被定向到只读 Aurora Replica。自定义 `ANY` endpoint 因此不适合替代 cluster endpoint 来处理混合读/写流量。请参阅 [Specifying properties for custom endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Custom.Considerations.html)。

### C. 启用 Multi-AZ 选项并使用标准 endpoints

对于**现有的**单实例 Aurora cluster，使 DB-instance 层实现 Multi-AZ 的文档化方法是在另一个 AZ 中添加 reader instance。在此场景中，并不存在一项单独的修改操作，可以仅将现有的单个 DB instance 变为具有 standby 支持的 Aurora deployment。选项 A 陈述了所需的具体操作；选项 C 则遗漏了该操作。Aurora 的分布式存储已在多个 AZ 之间复制，但 DB-instance 故障转移仍需要一个可以被提升的 reader instance。请参阅 [Aurora DB instances 的高可用性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html)。

### D. 启用 Multi-AZ，并将自定义 `ANY` endpoint 用于所有操作

该选项同时存在上述两个问题：它没有明确指定要向现有 cluster 添加所需的 reader instance，并且 `ANY` endpoint 可能会将具备写入能力的连接发送到只读 instance。cluster endpoint，而非 `ANY` 自定义 endpoint，才是写入流量的正确 endpoint。

en.question: A company must encrypt all AMIs that the company shares across accounts. A DevOps engineer has access to a source account where an unencrypted custom AMI has been built. The DevOps engineer also has access to a target account where an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group will launch EC2 instances from the AMI. The DevOps engineer must share the AMI with the target account. The company has created an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in the source account. Which additional steps should the DevOps engineer perform to meet the requirements? (Choose three.)

options.A: In the source account, copy the unencrypted AMI to an encrypted AMI. Specify the KMS key in the copy action.
options.B: In the source account, copy the unencrypted AMI to an encrypted AMI. Specify the default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption key in the copy action.
options.C: In the source account, create a KMS grant that delegates permissions to the Auto Scaling group service-linked role in the target account.
options.D: In the source account, modify the key policy to give the target account permissions to create a grant. In the target account, create a KMS grant that delegates permissions to the Auto Scaling group service-linked role.
options.E: In the source account, share the unencrypted AMI with the target account.
options.F: In the source account, share the encrypted AMI with the target account.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The source AMI is unencrypted, but the company requires every cross-account shared AMI to be encrypted. The target account will also use the AMI through an EC2 Auto Scaling group, so the target account needs both launch permission for the encrypted AMI and the required cross-account KMS authorization for the Auto Scaling service-linked role.

## Correct answers: A, D, F

### A. Copy the unencrypted AMI to an encrypted AMI using the company KMS key

When `CopyImage` is called with both encryption enabled and a `KmsKeyId`, EC2 copies an unencrypted AMI's snapshots to snapshots encrypted by the specified customer managed KMS key. This creates the encrypted AMI required for sharing. See [Use encryption with EBS-backed AMIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AMIEncryption.html).

### D. Update the source key policy and create the grant from the target account

This matches AWS's documented cross-account configuration for EC2 Auto Scaling:

1. In the account that owns the customer managed key, update the key policy to allow the external/target account to use the key and call `kms:CreateGrant`.
2. From the account containing the Auto Scaling group, create a KMS grant whose grantee principal is that account's `AWSServiceRoleForAutoScaling` service-linked role.

AWS explicitly states that when the KMS key and Auto Scaling group are in different accounts, a grant must be used together with the key policy, and documents these two steps in this order. See [Key policy requirements for cross-account EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/key-policy-requirements-EBS-encryption.html).

### F. Share the encrypted AMI with the target account

The encrypted copy—not the original unencrypted AMI—must receive launch permissions for the target account. EC2 allows an AMI backed by encrypted snapshots to be shared when the snapshots use a shareable customer managed KMS key and the recipient is authorized to use that key. See [Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Use the default EBS encryption key — Incorrect

The default Amazon EBS key is normally the AWS managed key `aws/ebs`. EC2 documentation states that an AMI backed by snapshots encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared. A customer managed KMS key must be used for this cross-account scenario. See [AMI sharing considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html).

### C. Create only a grant in the source account — Incorrect

This does not implement the documented EC2 Auto Scaling cross-account process. AWS requires the source key policy to authorize the external account, after which an authorized identity in the target account creates the grant for the target account's Auto Scaling service-linked role. Option C omits the required source-key policy update and places the grant-creation step in the wrong account. See [cross-account access to a customer managed key for EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/key-policy-requirements-EBS-encryption.html).

### E. Share the unencrypted AMI — Incorrect

Sharing the original AMI would directly violate the requirement that all shared AMIs be encrypted. The engineer must first produce the encrypted copy and share that AMI instead.

Therefore, the required sequence is **A → D → F**.

zh.question: 一家公司必须对其跨账户共享的所有 AMI 进行加密。一名 DevOps 工程师可以访问源账户，其中已构建了一个未加密的自定义 AMI。该 DevOps 工程师还可以访问目标账户，其中的 Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 组将从该 AMI 启动 EC2 实例。该 DevOps 工程师必须将该 AMI 共享给目标账户。公司已在源账户中创建了一个 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥。DevOps 工程师还应执行哪些步骤来满足要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 在源账户中，将未加密的 AMI 复制为加密的 AMI。在复制操作中指定该 KMS 密钥。
options.B: 在源账户中，将未加密的 AMI 复制为加密的 AMI。在复制操作中指定默认的 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 加密密钥。
options.C: 在源账户中，创建一个 KMS 授权，以便将权限委托给目标账户中的 Auto Scaling 组服务关联角色。
options.D: 在源账户中，修改密钥策略以授予目标账户创建授权的权限。在目标账户中，创建一个 KMS 授权，以便将权限委托给 Auto Scaling 组服务关联角色。
options.E: 在源账户中，将未加密的 AMI 共享给目标账户。
options.F: 在源账户中，将加密的 AMI 共享给目标账户。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

源 AMI 未加密，但公司要求每个跨账户共享的 AMI 都必须加密。目标账户还将通过 EC2 Auto Scaling 组使用该 AMI，因此目标账户既需要获得加密 AMI 的启动权限，也需要获得 Auto Scaling 服务关联角色所需的跨账户 KMS 授权。

## 正确答案：A、D、F

### A. 使用公司的 KMS 密钥将未加密的 AMI 复制为加密的 AMI

当调用 `CopyImage` 并同时启用加密及指定 `KmsKeyId` 时，EC2 会将未加密 AMI 的快照复制为由指定客户自主管理 KMS 密钥加密的快照。这会创建共享所需的加密 AMI。请参阅 [对 EBS 支持的 AMI 使用加密](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AMIEncryption.html)。

### D. 更新源密钥策略，并从目标账户创建授权

这符合 AWS 针对 EC2 Auto Scaling 的跨账户配置文档：

1. 在拥有客户自主管理密钥的账户中，更新密钥策略，以允许外部/目标账户使用该密钥并调用 `kms:CreateGrant`。
2. 从包含 Auto Scaling 组的账户中，创建一个 KMS 授权，其被授权主体为该账户的 `AWSServiceRoleForAutoScaling` 服务关联角色。

AWS 明确指出，当 KMS 密钥和 Auto Scaling 组位于不同账户时，必须将授权与密钥策略结合使用，并按此顺序记录了这两个步骤。请参阅 [跨账户 EBS 加密的密钥策略要求](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/key-policy-requirements-EBS-encryption.html)。

### F. 将加密的 AMI 共享给目标账户

必须向目标账户授予加密副本（而非原始未加密 AMI）的启动权限。当快照使用可共享的客户自主管理 KMS 密钥，且接收方被授权使用该密钥时，EC2 允许共享由加密快照支持的 AMI。请参阅 [与特定 AWS 账户共享 AMI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 使用默认 EBS 加密密钥 — 错误

默认 Amazon EBS 密钥通常是 AWS 托管密钥 `aws/ebs`。EC2 文档指出，不能共享由默认 AWS 托管密钥加密的快照支持的 AMI。此跨账户场景必须使用客户自主管理 KMS 密钥。请参阅 [AMI 共享注意事项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html)。

### C. 仅在源账户中创建授权 — 错误

这并未实现文档规定的 EC2 Auto Scaling 跨账户流程。AWS 要求源密钥策略授权外部账户，之后由目标账户中已获授权的身份为该目标账户的 Auto Scaling 服务关联角色创建授权。选项 C 遗漏了所需的源密钥策略更新，并且在错误的账户中执行了授权创建步骤。请参阅 [EC2 Auto Scaling 对客户自主管理密钥的跨账户访问](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/key-policy-requirements-EBS-encryption.html)。

### E. 共享未加密的 AMI — 错误

共享原始 AMI 将直接违反所有共享 AMI 都必须加密的要求。工程师必须先创建加密副本，然后共享该 AMI。

因此，所需的顺序为 **A → D → F**。

en.question: A company uses AWS CodePipeline pipelines to automate releases of its application A typical pipeline consists of three stages build, test, and deployment. The company has been using a separate AWS CodeBuild project to run scripts for each stage. However, the company now wants to use AWS CodeDeploy to handle the deployment stage of the pipelines. The company has packaged the application as an RPM package and must deploy the application to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an EC2 Auto Scaling group and are launched from a common AMI. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer perform to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create a new version of the common AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed. Update the IAM role of the EC2 instances to allow access to CodeDeploy.
options.B: Create a new version of the common AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed. Create an AppSpec file that contains application deployment scripts and grants access to CodeDeploy.
options.C: Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the Auto Scaling group as the deployment target. Add a step to the CodePipeline pipeline to use EC2 Image Builder to create a new AMI. Configure CodeDeploy to deploy the newly created AMI.
options.D: Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the Auto Scaling group as the deployment target. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to use the CodeDeploy action to deploy the application.
options.E: Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the EC2 instances that are launched from the common AMI as the deployment target. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to use the CodeDeploy action to deploy the application.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company wants to replace the custom CodeBuild-based deployment step with a native CodeDeploy deployment to a dynamically managed fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The solution therefore must:

1. Prepare every instance launched from the shared AMI to participate in CodeDeploy deployments.
2. Configure CodeDeploy and CodePipeline to deploy to the Auto Scaling group.

## Correct answers: A and D

### A. Install the CodeDeploy agent in a new common AMI and update the EC2 instance IAM role

For an EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy deployment, each target instance must have the **CodeDeploy agent installed and running** and must have an **IAM instance profile** attached. AWS specifically supports using a custom AMI that already contains the CodeDeploy agent, which is appropriate for instances launched automatically by an Auto Scaling group. The instance profile supplies the permissions needed by the agent, including access to the relevant S3 artifact and CodeDeploy resource-kit buckets when S3 is used.

AWS documents that target instances must have the agent installed and an IAM instance profile attached, and it explicitly lists a custom AMI with the agent preinstalled as an Auto Scaling integration option: [Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises compute platform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-server.html), [CodeDeploy and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-auto-scaling.html), and [Configure an EC2 instance for CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/instances-ec2-configure.html).

Thus, although “allow access to CodeDeploy” is general wording, A represents the required instance preparation: install the agent and attach/update the required instance role.

### D. Create an in-place CodeDeploy deployment group targeting the Auto Scaling group and use the CodeDeploy pipeline action

An **in-place deployment** updates the application on the existing EC2 instances, which matches deploying a new RPM package rather than replacing the instances or producing a new AMI for every release.

For Auto Scaling integration, AWS directs users to create a CodeDeploy deployment group that specifies the **Auto Scaling group name**. The CodePipeline deployment stage should then use the native CodeDeploy action, configured with the CodeDeploy application and deployment group. See [CodeDeploy and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-auto-scaling.html) and the [AWS CodeDeploy deploy action reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeDeploy.html).

The deployment input artifact must also contain an AppSpec file and the scripts needed to install/start/validate the RPM. The CodeDeploy pipeline action consumes that artifact and invokes the configured deployment group.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Incorrect

An AppSpec file can define file mappings, filesystem permissions, and lifecycle-event scripts, but it **does not grant AWS IAM access to CodeDeploy**. AWS access is granted through IAM roles and policies. The AppSpec `permissions` section only applies owner, mode, and other operating-system permissions to copied files and directories. See [AppSpec file structure for EC2/On-Premises deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure.html).

An AppSpec file is required in the deployment artifact, but B incorrectly treats it as the mechanism for granting CodeDeploy access and omits the required EC2 instance profile configuration.

### C. Incorrect

EC2 Image Builder is unnecessary for this requested deployment model. The application is already packaged as an RPM, and an in-place CodeDeploy deployment installs the new application revision on the existing fleet. CodeDeploy does not perform an in-place application deployment by “deploying a newly created AMI.” Building a new AMI for every release would instead be an immutable-image workflow and would require updating the Auto Scaling launch template and replacing instances.

### E. Incorrect

A CodeDeploy deployment group can identify instances by EC2 tags, Auto Scaling group names, or both. Because the fleet is explicitly managed by an Auto Scaling group, the deployment group should target the **Auto Scaling group**, as in D. This automatically accounts for scaling events and replacement instances. A common source AMI by itself is not a CodeDeploy deployment-target selector, and configuring individual current instances would not correctly represent the dynamic fleet. See [Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises compute platform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-server.html).

**Final answer: A and D.**

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS CodePipeline 管道来自动发布其应用程序。一个典型的管道包含三个阶段：构建、测试和部署。该公司一直为每个阶段使用单独的 AWS CodeBuild 项目来运行脚本。但是，公司现在希望使用 AWS CodeDeploy 来处理管道的部署阶段。公司已将应用程序打包为 RPM 包，并且必须将应用程序部署到一组 Amazon EC2 实例。EC2 实例位于一个 EC2 Auto Scaling 组中，并且从一个通用 AMI 启动。DevOps 工程师应执行哪种步骤组合来满足这些要求？（选择两个。）

options.A: 创建一个安装了 CodeDeploy agent 的新版通用 AMI。更新 EC2 实例的 IAM 角色，以允许访问 CodeDeploy。
options.B: 创建一个安装了 CodeDeploy agent 的新版通用 AMI。创建一个包含应用程序部署脚本并授予 CodeDeploy 访问权限的 AppSpec 文件。
options.C: 在 CodeDeploy 中创建一个应用程序。配置就地部署类型。将 Auto Scaling 组指定为部署目标。在 CodePipeline 管道中添加一个步骤以使用 EC2 Image Builder 创建新的 AMI。配置 CodeDeploy 以部署新创建的 AMI。
options.D: 在 CodeDeploy 中创建一个应用程序。配置就地部署类型。将 Auto Scaling 组指定为部署目标。更新 CodePipeline 管道以使用 CodeDeploy 操作部署应用程序。
options.E: 在 CodeDeploy 中创建一个应用程序。配置就地部署类型。将从通用 AMI 启动的 EC2 实例指定为部署目标。更新 CodePipeline 管道以使用 CodeDeploy 操作部署应用程序。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

公司希望将基于自定义 CodeBuild 的部署步骤替换为原生 CodeDeploy 部署，以部署到由 Auto Scaling 组动态管理的一组 EC2 实例。因此，该解决方案必须：

1. 准备好从共享 AMI 启动的每个实例，以便其参与 CodeDeploy 部署。
2. 配置 CodeDeploy 和 CodePipeline，以部署到 Auto Scaling 组。

## 正确答案：A 和 D

### A. 在新的通用 AMI 中安装 CodeDeploy agent，并更新 EC2 实例 IAM 角色

对于 EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy 部署，每个目标实例都必须安装并运行 **CodeDeploy agent**，并且必须附加 **IAM instance profile**。AWS 明确支持使用已经包含 CodeDeploy agent 的自定义 AMI，这适用于由 Auto Scaling 组自动启动的实例。实例配置文件提供 agent 所需的权限，包括在使用 S3 时访问相关 S3 构件和 CodeDeploy resource-kit 存储桶的权限。

AWS 文档说明目标实例必须安装 agent 并附加 IAM instance profile，同时明确将预安装 agent 的自定义 AMI 列为 Auto Scaling 集成选项：[EC2/On-Premises 计算平台上的部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-server.html)、[CodeDeploy 和 Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-auto-scaling.html)以及[为 CodeDeploy 配置 EC2 实例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/instances-ec2-configure.html)。

因此，尽管“允许访问 CodeDeploy”是较笼统的表述，A 代表了必需的实例准备工作：安装 agent 并附加或更新所需的实例角色。

### D. 创建以 Auto Scaling 组为目标的就地 CodeDeploy 部署组，并使用 CodeDeploy 管道操作

**就地部署**会在现有 EC2 实例上更新应用程序，这符合部署新 RPM 包的要求，而不是替换实例或为每次发布生成新的 AMI。

对于 Auto Scaling 集成，AWS 指示用户创建一个指定 **Auto Scaling 组名称** 的 CodeDeploy 部署组。随后，CodePipeline 部署阶段应使用原生 CodeDeploy 操作，并配置 CodeDeploy 应用程序和部署组。请参阅 [CodeDeploy 和 Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-auto-scaling.html) 和 [AWS CodeDeploy 部署操作参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeDeploy.html)。

部署输入构件还必须包含 AppSpec 文件以及安装、启动和验证 RPM 所需的脚本。CodeDeploy 管道操作会使用该构件并调用已配置的部署组。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B. 不正确

AppSpec 文件可以定义文件映射、文件系统权限和生命周期事件脚本，但它**不会授予对 CodeDeploy 的 AWS IAM 访问权限**。AWS 访问权限通过 IAM 角色和策略授予。AppSpec 的 `permissions` 部分只会将所有者、模式和其他操作系统权限应用于已复制的文件和目录。请参阅 [EC2/On-Premises 部署的 AppSpec 文件结构](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-structure.html)。

部署构件中需要 AppSpec 文件，但 B 错误地将其视为授予 CodeDeploy 访问权限的机制，并且遗漏了必需的 EC2 instance profile 配置。

### C. 不正确

对于所需的部署模型，不需要 EC2 Image Builder。应用程序已经打包为 RPM，并且就地 CodeDeploy 部署会在现有实例组上安装新的应用程序修订版。CodeDeploy 不会通过“部署新创建的 AMI”来执行就地应用程序部署。每次发布都构建新的 AMI 属于不可变镜像工作流，必须更新 Auto Scaling 启动模板并替换实例。

### E. 不正确

CodeDeploy 部署组可以通过 EC2 标签、Auto Scaling 组名称或两者来识别实例。由于该实例组明确由 Auto Scaling 组管理，部署组应像 D 一样以 **Auto Scaling 组** 为目标。这样可自动处理扩缩容事件和替换实例。通用源 AMI 本身不是 CodeDeploy 部署目标选择器，而配置当前的单个实例无法正确表示动态实例组。请参阅 [EC2/On-Premises 计算平台上的部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-server.html)。

**最终答案：A 和 D。**

en.question: A company’s security team requires that all external Application Load Balancers (ALBs) and Amazon API Gateway APIs are associated with AWS WAF web ACLs. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts, all of which are included in a single organization in AWS Organizations. The company has configured AWS Config for the organization. During an audit, the company finds some externally facing ALBs that are not associated with AWS WAF web ACLs. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to prevent future violations? (Choose two.)

options.A: Delegate AWS Firewall Manager to a security account.
options.B: Delegate Amazon GuardDuty to a security account.
options.C: Create an AWS Firewall Manager policy to attach AWS WAF web ACLs to any newly created ALBs and API Gateway APIs.
options.D: Create an Amazon GuardDuty policy to attach AWS WAF web ACLs to any newly created ALBs and API Gateway APIs.
options.E: Configure an AWS Config managed rule to attach AWS WAF web ACLs to any newly created ALBs and API Gateway APIs.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs an organization-wide mechanism that **automatically enforces AWS WAF web ACL associations**, including for newly created in-scope Application Load Balancers and API Gateway APIs. AWS Config is already enabled, which satisfies one of the prerequisites for using AWS Firewall Manager.

## Correct answers: A and C

### A. Delegate AWS Firewall Manager to a security account

AWS Firewall Manager is the AWS service designed to centrally administer security policies across accounts in AWS Organizations. The organization management account designates a Firewall Manager administrator account; AWS then registers that account as an Organizations delegated administrator. The administrator can apply policies across accounts and organizational units.

AWS also lists an administrator account and AWS Config as Firewall Manager prerequisites. Therefore, delegating Firewall Manager administration to the security account is the appropriate centralized security operating model. See [AWS Firewall Manager prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-prereq.html) and [Creating an AWS Firewall Manager default administrator account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/enable-integration.html).

### C. Create an AWS Firewall Manager policy to attach AWS WAF web ACLs to newly created ALBs and API Gateway APIs

A Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy centrally creates and manages web ACLs for resources within its scope. It can be configured to create web ACLs for resources that do not already have one and to **automatically remediate noncompliant resources** by associating the policy-managed web ACL.

The policy can be scoped by AWS Organizations accounts/OUs and resource types. Firewall Manager continuously evaluates resources within that scope, so newly created eligible resources are brought under policy management. AWS specifically documents that Firewall Manager policies can automatically remediate noncompliant resources and automatically apply to in-scope resources in newly added organization accounts. See [Using AWS WAF policies with Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html), [Creating an AWS Firewall Manager policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/create-policy.html), and [Using AWS Firewall Manager policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/working-with-policies.html).

Together, **A establishes centralized administration**, and **C establishes preventive, automatic enforcement**.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Delegate Amazon GuardDuty to a security account

GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that generates and manages security findings. Delegating GuardDuty can centralize threat detection, but it does not create or enforce AWS WAF web ACL associations. GuardDuty findings can be processed through EventBridge for custom response automation, but there is no native “GuardDuty policy” for attaching web ACLs. See [Managing Amazon GuardDuty findings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/findings_management.html).

### D. Create an Amazon GuardDuty policy to attach AWS WAF web ACLs

This policy type does not exist. GuardDuty detects potentially malicious activity and produces findings; AWS Firewall Manager is the service that provides organization-wide AWS WAF policy enforcement.

### E. Configure an AWS Config managed rule to attach AWS WAF web ACLs

The relevant AWS Config managed rules are evaluative controls:

- `ALB_WAF_ENABLED` **checks** whether WAF is enabled on an ALB and reports it as noncompliant otherwise.
- `API_GW_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF` **checks** whether an API Gateway stage uses an approved web ACL and reports noncompliance otherwise.

The managed rules themselves do not attach web ACLs to newly created resources. AWS Config remediation would require a separately configured remediation action, such as a Systems Manager Automation document or custom automation, which option E does not specify. Firewall Manager supplies the required native cross-account policy enforcement and automatic remediation. See [alb-waf-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/alb-waf-enabled.html) and [api-gw-associated-with-waf](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/api-gw-associated-with-waf.html).

zh.question: 某公司的安全团队要求所有面向外部的 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 和 Amazon API Gateway API 都必须关联 AWS WAF web ACL。该公司拥有数百个 AWS 账户，且所有账户都包含在 AWS Organizations 的一个组织中。该公司已为该组织配置 AWS Config。在一次审计中，该公司发现一些面向外部的 ALB 未关联 AWS WAF web ACL。DevOps 工程师应采取哪种步骤组合来防止未来出现违规情况？（选择两个。）

options.A: 将 AWS Firewall Manager 委派给一个安全账户。
options.B: 将 Amazon GuardDuty 委派给一个安全账户。
options.C: 创建 AWS Firewall Manager 策略，为任何新创建的 ALB 和 API Gateway API 附加 AWS WAF web ACL。
options.D: 创建 Amazon GuardDuty 策略，为任何新创建的 ALB 和 API Gateway API 附加 AWS WAF web ACL。
options.E: 配置 AWS Config 托管规则，为任何新创建的 ALB 和 API Gateway API 附加 AWS WAF web ACL。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

公司需要一种覆盖整个组织的机制，能够**自动强制执行 AWS WAF web ACL 关联**，包括对新创建的、范围内的 Application Load Balancer 和 API Gateway API。AWS Config 已为组织启用，满足使用 AWS Firewall Manager 的一项前提条件。

## 正确答案：A 和 C

### A. 将 AWS Firewall Manager 委派给一个安全账户

AWS Firewall Manager 是专为在 AWS Organizations 的多个账户中集中管理安全策略而设计的 AWS 服务。组织管理账户指定一个 Firewall Manager 管理员账户；随后 AWS 会将该账户注册为 Organizations 委派管理员。该管理员可以跨账户和组织单元应用策略。

AWS 还将管理员账户和 AWS Config 列为 Firewall Manager 的前提条件。因此，将 Firewall Manager 管理权限委派给安全账户是适当的集中式安全运营模式。参阅 [AWS Firewall Manager prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-prereq.html) 和 [Creating an AWS Firewall Manager default administrator account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/enable-integration.html)。

### C. 创建 AWS Firewall Manager 策略，为新创建的 ALB 和 API Gateway API 附加 AWS WAF web ACL

Firewall Manager AWS WAF 策略会集中创建和管理其范围内资源的 web ACL。可以将其配置为：为尚未拥有 web ACL 的资源创建 web ACL，并通过关联由策略管理的 web ACL 来**自动修复不合规资源**。

该策略可以按 AWS Organizations 账户/OU 和资源类型定义范围。Firewall Manager 会持续评估该范围内的资源，因此新创建的符合条件的资源会被纳入策略管理。AWS 专门说明，Firewall Manager 策略可以自动修复不合规资源，并自动应用于新加入组织账户中的范围内资源。参阅 [Using AWS WAF policies with Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html)、[Creating an AWS Firewall Manager policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/create-policy.html) 和 [Using AWS Firewall Manager policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/working-with-policies.html)。

两者结合，**A 建立集中管理**，而 **C 建立预防性的自动强制执行**。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 将 Amazon GuardDuty 委派给一个安全账户

GuardDuty 是一种威胁检测服务，用于生成和管理安全发现结果。委派 GuardDuty 可以集中进行威胁检测，但不能创建或强制执行 AWS WAF web ACL 关联。虽然可以通过 EventBridge 处理 GuardDuty 发现结果以实现自定义响应自动化，但不存在用于附加 web ACL 的原生“GuardDuty 策略”。参阅 [Managing Amazon GuardDuty findings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/findings_management.html)。

### D. 创建 Amazon GuardDuty 策略以附加 AWS WAF web ACL

此类策略并不存在。GuardDuty 检测潜在恶意活动并生成发现结果；AWS Firewall Manager 才是提供组织范围 AWS WAF 策略强制执行的服务。

### E. 配置 AWS Config 托管规则以附加 AWS WAF web ACL

相关 AWS Config 托管规则属于评估性控制：

- `ALB_WAF_ENABLED` 会**检查**是否已在 ALB 上启用 WAF；否则将其报告为不合规。
- `API_GW_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF` 会**检查** API Gateway 阶段是否使用经批准的 web ACL；否则将其报告为不合规。

托管规则本身不会将 web ACL 附加到新创建的资源。AWS Config 修复需要另外配置修复操作，例如 Systems Manager Automation 文档或自定义自动化，而选项 E 并未说明这一点。Firewall Manager 提供所需的原生跨账户策略强制执行和自动修复。参阅 [alb-waf-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/alb-waf-enabled.html) 和 [api-gw-associated-with-waf](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/api-gw-associated-with-waf.html)。

en.question: A company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys and manual key rotation to meet regulatory compliance requirements. The security team wants to be notified when any keys have not been rotated after 90 days. Which solution will accomplish this?

options.A: Configure AWS KMS to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when keys are more than 90 days old.
options.B: Configure an Amazon EventBridge event to launch an AWS Lambda function to call the AWS Trusted Advisor API and publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
options.C: Develop an AWS Config custom rule that publishes to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when keys are more than 90 days old.
options.D: Configure AWS Security Hub to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when keys are more than 90 days old.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company performs **manual rotation of AWS KMS keys** and needs a compliance check that identifies keys that have gone more than 90 days without rotation, followed by an Amazon SNS notification.

## Correct answer: C

**Develop an AWS Config custom rule that publishes to an Amazon SNS topic when keys are more than 90 days old.**

AWS Config supports custom rules backed by Lambda functions. A custom rule can run **periodically**, inspect the relevant KMS key and manual-rotation metadata, compare the last rotation/replacement date with the 90-day requirement, and report overdue keys as `NON_COMPLIANT`. AWS Config supports periodic evaluations at a configured frequency, such as every 24 hours ([AWS Config rule components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_components.html)). AWS documents that custom Lambda rules can contain organization-specific compliance logic and can be invoked periodically ([Creating AWS Config custom Lambda rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules_lambda-functions.html)).

AWS Config can then send compliance-state notifications for custom or managed rules to an SNS topic ([AWS Config SNS notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/notifications-for-AWS-Config.html)).

A custom rule is required because the AWS Config managed rule `cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled` only checks whether **automatic key rotation is enabled**; it does not enforce that manually rotated keys were replaced within 90 days ([cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled.html)).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A. Configure AWS KMS to publish to SNS when keys are more than 90 days old — Incorrect.**  
  AWS KMS does not provide a native age-threshold notification that directly publishes to SNS. KMS can emit an EventBridge event when key material is actually rotated, but that is not an alert for the absence of rotation over a 90-day period. Also, AWS defines manual rotation as creating a new KMS key and replacing references to the old key, commonly by updating an alias ([Rotate keys manually](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys-manually.html)). Custom compliance logic is therefore needed to evaluate the company's manual-rotation process.

- **B. Use EventBridge and Lambda to call the Trusted Advisor API — Incorrect.**  
  Trusted Advisor is not the service that evaluates a custom 90-day manual KMS rotation policy. Its API exposes supported Trusted Advisor checks, but it does not provide the required organization-specific KMS manual-rotation-age check ([Trusted Advisor check reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor-check-reference.html)). AWS Config custom rules are designed for this kind of custom compliance evaluation.

- **D. Configure Security Hub to publish to SNS — Incorrect.**  
  Security Hub's KMS rotation control, **KMS.4**, uses the AWS Config managed rule `cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled` and checks whether automatic rotation is enabled. It does not check whether the company's manual rotation occurred within the last 90 days ([Security Hub KMS controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/kms-controls.html)). Security Hub can aggregate findings, but it does not natively implement this specific manual-rotation-age policy.

Therefore, **C** is the only option that provides the necessary customizable, periodic compliance check and SNS notification path.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥和手动密钥轮换来满足监管合规要求。安全团队希望在任何密钥超过 90 天未轮换时收到通知。哪种解决方案可以实现此目标？

options.A: 配置 AWS KMS，在密钥超过 90 天时发布到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。
options.B: 配置一个 Amazon EventBridge 事件来启动 AWS Lambda 函数，以调用 AWS Trusted Advisor API 并发布到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。
options.C: 开发一条 AWS Config 自定义规则，在密钥超过 90 天时发布到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。
options.D: 配置 AWS Security Hub，在密钥超过 90 天时发布到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

该公司执行 **AWS KMS 密钥的手动轮换**，并且需要一项合规性检查来识别超过 90 天未轮换的密钥，然后发送 Amazon SNS 通知。

## 正确答案：C

**开发一条 AWS Config 自定义规则，在密钥超过 90 天时发布到 Amazon SNS 主题。**

AWS Config 支持由 Lambda 函数支持的自定义规则。自定义规则可以**定期**运行，检查相关的 KMS 密钥和手动轮换元数据，将上次轮换/替换日期与 90 天要求进行比较，并将逾期密钥报告为 `NON_COMPLIANT`。AWS Config 支持按照配置的频率（例如每 24 小时）进行定期评估（[AWS Config rule components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_components.html)）。AWS 文档说明，自定义 Lambda 规则可以包含组织特定的合规逻辑，并且可以定期调用（[Creating AWS Config custom Lambda rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules_lambda-functions.html)）。

随后，AWS Config 可以将自定义或托管规则的合规状态通知发送到 SNS 主题（[AWS Config SNS notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/notifications-for-AWS-Config.html)）。

必须使用自定义规则，因为 AWS Config 托管规则 `cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled` 仅检查是否**启用了自动密钥轮换**；它不会强制要求手动轮换的密钥必须在 90 天内被替换（[cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled.html)）。

## 其他选项为何不正确

- **A. 配置 AWS KMS，在密钥超过 90 天时发布到 SNS — 不正确。**  
  AWS KMS 不提供直接发布到 SNS 的原生期限阈值通知功能。KMS 可以在密钥材料实际轮换时发出 EventBridge 事件，但这不是针对 90 天内未发生轮换的告警。此外，AWS 将手动轮换定义为创建新的 KMS 密钥并将对旧密钥的引用替换为新密钥的过程，通常通过更新别名完成（[Rotate keys manually](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys-manually.html)）。因此，需要自定义合规逻辑来评估该公司的手动轮换流程。

- **B. 使用 EventBridge 和 Lambda 调用 Trusted Advisor API — 不正确。**  
  Trusted Advisor 并非用于评估自定义的 90 天 KMS 手动轮换策略的服务。其 API 可提供受支持的 Trusted Advisor 检查，但不提供所需的、组织特定的 KMS 手动轮换期限检查（[Trusted Advisor check reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor-check-reference.html)）。AWS Config 自定义规则正是为此类自定义合规评估而设计的。

- **D. 配置 Security Hub 发布到 SNS — 不正确。**  
  Security Hub 的 KMS 轮换控制项 **KMS.4** 使用 AWS Config 托管规则 `cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled`，并检查是否已启用自动轮换。它不检查公司的手动轮换是否在过去 90 天内发生（[Security Hub KMS controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/kms-controls.html)）。Security Hub 可以聚合发现结果，但不会原生实施此特定的手动轮换期限策略。

因此，只有 **C** 能够提供所需的可自定义、定期合规检查和 SNS 通知路径。

en.question: A security review has identified that an AWS CodeBuild project is downloading a database population script from an Amazon S3 bucket using an unauthenticated request. The security team does not allow unauthenticated requests to S3 buckets for this project. How can this issue be corrected in the MOST secure manner?

options.A: Add the bucket name to the AllowedBuckets section of the CodeBuild project settings. Update the build spec to use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
options.B: Modify the S3 bucket settings to enable HTTPS basic authentication and specify a token. Update the build spec to use cURL to pass the token and download the database population script.
options.C: Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Modify the service role for the CodeBuild project to include Amazon S3 access. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script.
options.D: Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket with a bucket policy. Use the AWS CLI to download the database population script using an IAM access key and a secret access key.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The CodeBuild build currently retrieves an S3 object anonymously. The secure correction must both:

1. Remove public/unauthenticated access to the object.
2. Give the build an authenticated AWS identity with only the permissions it needs.

## Correct answer: C

**Remove unauthenticated access from the S3 bucket, grant the CodeBuild service role the required S3 permission, and use the AWS CLI to download the object.**

CodeBuild uses its **service role** for operations that it performs on the customer's behalf. AWS specifically documents adding permissions such as `s3:GetObject` to this role and recommends restricting the policy resources to the specific resources required. Therefore, the role should ideally receive only `s3:GetObject` on the database script's object ARN, plus any required KMS permission if the object uses a customer-managed KMS key. See [Allow CodeBuild to interact with other AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/setting-up-service-role.html).

The bucket's anonymous/public grant should be removed, and S3 Block Public Access should also be enabled as appropriate. S3 Block Public Access can reject public bucket policies and ignore or block public ACLs. See [Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html).

This approach lets the AWS CLI make an authenticated request under the CodeBuild service role instead of placing credentials in the build configuration. IAM roles provide temporary credentials, and AWS strongly recommends temporary role credentials instead of long-term IAM access keys. See [AWS security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A — Incorrect.** CodeBuild does not authorize S3 access through an `AllowedBuckets` project setting. Access to other AWS services is controlled through the CodeBuild service role and IAM/resource policies. Merely changing the build command to the AWS CLI does not grant permission to a private object.

- **B — Incorrect.** Amazon S3 does not provide a bucket setting for HTTPS Basic Authentication with a custom token. Authenticated S3 API requests use AWS authentication mechanisms such as AWS Signature Version 4; the AWS CLI performs this signing by using AWS credentials. See [Authenticating Requests (AWS Signature Version 4)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/developerguide/sig-v4-authenticating-requests.html).

- **D — Incorrect.** Although this could authenticate the request, supplying an IAM access key and secret access key to the build introduces long-term credentials that must be stored, protected, and rotated. A CodeBuild service role provides temporary credentials automatically and is more secure. AWS also warns that `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` should never be stored as clear-text CodeBuild environment variables because this can cause unauthorized access and data exposure. See [CodeBuild.2: CodeBuild project environment variables should not contain clear text credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/codebuild-controls.html).

Therefore, **C** is the most secure answer.

zh.question: 一次安全审查发现，一个 AWS CodeBuild 项目正在使用未经身份验证的请求从 Amazon S3 存储桶下载数据库填充脚本。安全团队不允许此项目对 S3 存储桶发出未经身份验证的请求。应如何以最安全的方式解决此问题？

options.A: 将存储桶名称添加到 CodeBuild 项目设置的 AllowedBuckets 部分。更新构建规范以使用 AWS CLI 下载数据库填充脚本。
options.B: 修改 S3 存储桶设置以启用 HTTPS 基本身份验证并指定一个令牌。更新构建规范以使用 cURL 传递该令牌并下载数据库填充脚本。
options.C: 使用存储桶策略移除对 S3 存储桶的未经身份验证访问。修改 CodeBuild 项目的服务角色以包含 Amazon S3 访问权限。使用 AWS CLI 下载数据库填充脚本。
options.D: 使用存储桶策略移除对 S3 存储桶的未经身份验证访问。使用 IAM 访问密钥和私有访问密钥，通过 AWS CLI 下载数据库填充脚本。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求
