Increasing shards is specifically appropriate when the application is consistently hitting shard-level read limits; each shard has defined read throughput, and AWS recommends adding shards when consistent read throttling is observed. The question does not indicate read throttling. See [Read throttling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-record-processor-additional-considerations.html).

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师管理一个运行在 Amazon EC2 上的大型商业网站。该网站使用 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 收集和处理 Web 日志。DevOps 工程师管理 Kinesis 消费者应用程序，该应用程序也运行在 Amazon EC2 上。数据量突然增加会导致 Kinesis 消费者应用程序处理滞后，并且 Kinesis 数据流会在记录得到处理之前丢弃记录。DevOps 工程师必须实施一个解决方案来改善流处理。哪种解决方案能够以最高的运营效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 修改 Kinesis 消费者应用程序，将日志持久存储在 Amazon S3 中。使用 Amazon EMR 直接处理 Amazon S3 中的数据以获取客户洞察。将结果存储在 Amazon S3 中。
options.B: 根据 Amazon CloudWatch `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` 指标，通过添加更多 EC2 实例对 Kinesis 消费者应用程序进行水平扩展。增加 Kinesis 数据流的保留期限。
options.C: 将 Kinesis 消费者应用程序转换为作为 AWS Lambda 函数运行。将 Kinesis 数据流配置为 Lambda 函数的事件源，以处理数据流。
options.D: 增加 Kinesis 数据流中的分片数量以提高总体吞吐量，从而使消费者应用程序能够更快地处理数据。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

流正在接收 Web 日志数据，但 **基于 EC2 的消费者无法在流量高峰期间足够快地处理记录**。当消费者滞后接近流的保留期限时，较早的记录会在处理前过期。因此，该解决方案需要同时解决以下两点：

1. 突然负载增加期间的消费者处理能力。
2. 在消费者追赶处理进度时防止记录过期。

## 正确答案：B

**根据 `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` 对 Kinesis 消费者应用程序进行水平扩展，并增加流保留期限。**

当消费者处理滞后时，AWS 明确建议先查看 `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` 指标。该指标跟踪消费者的读取位置相对于流中记录的位置。AWS 还指出，当迭代器年龄接近保留期限时，记录会面临过期风险；在解决底层消费者问题期间，增加保留期限是防止数据丢失的快速方法。迭代器年龄逐渐增加通常表明处理资源不足，或者处理逻辑未能随流吞吐量扩展。请参阅 [消费者记录处理正在滞后](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/troubleshooting-consumers.html)。

添加 EC2 消费者实例可提供更多处理资源和并行度。对于基于 KCL 的消费者，额外实例上的工作线程会对分片处理进行负载均衡。AWS 文档说明，可以通过将实例数量增加到不超过开放分片数量来扩展处理能力，并且 EC2 Auto Scaling 可以根据适当的指标自动扩展实例。请参阅 [示例：重新分片、扩展和并行处理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-record-processor-scaling.html)。

因此，B 以最小的架构变更直接解决这两种症状：

- 当消费者滞后增加时进行横向扩展。
- 延长记录保留时间，确保瞬时流量高峰不会导致记录在处理前过期。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. 将日志存储在 S3 中并使用 Amazon EMR

这是一项重大重新设计，无法直接解决当前瓶颈。现有消费者已经处理滞后，它仍需先从 Kinesis 读取记录并将其写入 S3，因此仅添加 S3 持久化逻辑并不能确保记录在过期前从 Kinesis 中被检索。运行 EMR 处理管道也比扩展现有消费者引入更多架构和运营工作。

### C. 将消费者转换为 AWS Lambda

Lambda 原生集成 Kinesis 事件源，并可减少服务器管理，但 **仅进行转换并不能保证足够的处理吞吐量或防止记录过期**。默认情况下，Lambda 从每个分片一次处理一个批次。额外的每分片并发需要配置 `ParallelizationFactor` 等设置，并且函数还必须具备足够的并发能力。AWS 指出，如果函数无法处理并发批次，可能需要预留并发或提高配额。请参阅 [轮询和批处理流](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html)。

该选项没有指定任何此类吞吐量或保留期限保障措施。它还需要迁移应用程序，而 B 则直接使用有文档说明的滞后指标和保留机制来改进现有架构。因此，尽管在适当设计的实施中 Lambda 可以具备运营效率，C 仍不是最佳的完整答案。

### D. 增加分片数量

增加分片可提高流吞吐量，并可能增加消费者并行度，但该场景指出限制因素是 **消费者应用程序的处理能力**。仅增加分片不会为 EC2 消费者集群增加 CPU 或内存，还可能增加与相同底层资源竞争的记录处理器数量。当消费者处理滞后时，AWS 建议检查处理节点是否具备足够的物理资源。此外，D 没有增加保留期限，因此已经滞后的消费者仍可能因记录过期而丢失记录。

当应用程序持续达到分片级读取限制时，增加分片是特别合适的做法；每个分片都有定义的读取吞吐量，AWS 建议在观察到持续读取限流时增加分片。题目未指出存在读取限流。请参阅 [读取限流](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-record-processor-additional-considerations.html)。

en.question: A company recently created a new AWS Control Tower landing zone in a new organization in AWS Organizations. The landing zone must be able to demonstrate compliance with the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks for AWS Foundations. The company’s security team wants to use AWS Security Hub to view compliance across all accounts. Only the security team can be allowed to view aggregated Security Hub findings. In addition, specific users must be able to view findings from their own accounts within the organization. All accounts must be enrolled in Security Hub after the accounts are created. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements in the MOST automated way? (Choose three.)

options.A: Turn on trusted access for Security Hub in the organization’s management account. Create a new security account by using AWS Control Tower. Configure the new security account as the delegated administrator account for Security Hub. In the new security account, provide Security Hub with the CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations standards.
options.B: Turn on trusted access for Security Hub in the organization’s management account. From the management account, provide Security Hub with the CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations standards.
options.C: Create an AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) permission set that includes the required permissions. Use the CreateAccountAssignment API operation to associate the security team users with the permission set and with the delegated security account.
options.D: Create an SCP that explicitly denies any user who is not on the security team from accessing Security Hub.
options.E: In Security Hub, turn on automatic enablement.
options.F: In the organization’s management account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to the CreateManagedAccount event. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Security Hub CreateMembers API operation to add new accounts to Security Hub. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs an organization-wide Security Hub design that:

1. Uses the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark.
2. Centralizes organization-wide findings in a dedicated security account.
3. Restricts access to the aggregated findings to the security team while still allowing authorized users in member accounts to see only their own account's findings.
4. Automatically enrolls newly created organization accounts.

## Correct answers: A, C, and E

### A. Configure a dedicated Security Hub delegated administrator and enable the CIS standard

This establishes the correct multi-account security architecture. When the Organizations management account designates a member account as the Security Hub delegated administrator, Security Hub becomes a trusted service and the delegated administrator can manage member accounts and view their data. AWS also recommends using an account other than the Organizations management account because billing/organization administrators and security administrators are typically different people.

The security account can therefore be the central account for organization-wide Security Hub findings and CIS compliance. See [Integrating Security Hub CSPM with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/designate-orgs-admin-account.html).

Security Hub's default standards under local configuration include the **CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0**, so it can evaluate the landing zone accounts against the required CIS benchmark. See [Turning off automatically enabled security standards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-auto-enabled-standards.html).

### C. Assign the security team access to the delegated security account through IAM Identity Center

A permission set defines the IAM permissions users receive in a target AWS account. Assigning the security team's users and the Security Hub permission set to the delegated security account gives only those users the required access to the centralized Security Hub view. IAM Identity Center provisions the corresponding IAM role and policies in that account. See [Manage AWS accounts with permission sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/permissionsetsconcept.html).

The Security Hub account model then provides the required visibility boundary: the delegated administrator can view findings for any member account, whereas a member account can view findings only for its current account. Thus, users who have appropriate Security Hub permissions in their own member accounts can view their own findings without being able to view organization-wide findings. See [Allowed actions by administrator and member accounts in Security Hub CSPM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-accounts-allowed-actions.html).

### E. Turn on Security Hub automatic enablement

With Organizations integration and local configuration, automatic enablement adds each newly created organization account as a Security Hub member and enables Security Hub in that account. It can also automatically enable the default standards, including CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0. This directly satisfies the requirement to enroll accounts after creation with the least custom automation. See [Automatically enabling new organization accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/accounts-orgs-auto-enable.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Use the Organizations management account without configuring a delegated administrator

This does not establish the intended dedicated security administration boundary. AWS recommends a separate delegated administrator instead of using the Organizations management account, particularly because security users and organization/billing administrators usually have different responsibilities. It also fails to describe how the security team alone receives access to aggregated findings.

### D. Deny all non-security-team users access to Security Hub through an SCP

This conflicts with the requirement that specific users must be able to view findings from their own accounts. An explicit SCP deny would impose a broad organization-level access restriction and could block those authorized member-account users. Security Hub already supplies the proper account boundary: the delegated administrator can view findings for all members, while member accounts are limited to their own findings. Access within each account should be granted using IAM/Identity Center permissions, not a blanket organization-wide deny.

### F. Build an EventBridge and Lambda account-enrollment workflow

This is unnecessary custom automation. Security Hub has native Organizations automatic enablement for new accounts, making option E simpler and more operationally reliable. In addition, `CreateMembers` primarily creates an administrator-member relationship; the proposed workflow does not describe enabling Security Hub and its standards in each new account as comprehensively as the native organization integration does.

Therefore, **A, C, and E** provide the most automated and appropriately separated solution.

zh.question: 一家公司最近在 AWS Organizations 的新组织中创建了一个新的 AWS Control Tower landing zone。该 landing zone 必须能够证明符合 Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks for AWS Foundations。公司的安全团队希望使用 AWS Security Hub 查看所有账户的合规性。只允许安全团队查看聚合的 Security Hub 发现。此外，特定用户必须能够查看组织内其自身账户中的发现。所有账户都必须在创建后加入 Security Hub。哪种步骤组合能够以**最自动化**的方式满足这些要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 在组织的管理账户中为 Security Hub 开启受信任访问。使用 AWS Control Tower 创建一个新的安全账户。将该新安全账户配置为 Security Hub 的委派管理员账户。在新安全账户中，为 Security Hub 提供 CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations 标准。
options.B: 在组织的管理账户中为 Security Hub 开启受信任访问。从管理账户中，为 Security Hub 提供 CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations 标准。
options.C: 创建一个包含所需权限的 AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) 权限集。使用 CreateAccountAssignment API 操作，将安全团队用户与该权限集以及委派安全账户关联。
options.D: 创建一个 SCP，显式拒绝不属于安全团队的任何用户访问 Security Hub。
options.E: 在 Security Hub 中开启自动启用。
options.F: 在组织的管理账户中，创建一个对 CreateManagedAccount 事件作出响应的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个使用 Security Hub CreateMembers API 操作将新账户添加到 Security Hub 的 AWS Lambda 函数。配置 EventBridge 规则来调用该 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

公司需要一个全组织范围的 Security Hub 设计，该设计应：

1. 使用 CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark。
2. 在专用安全账户中集中管理全组织范围的发现。
3. 将聚合发现的访问权限限制为安全团队，同时仍允许成员账户中的授权用户仅查看其自身账户的发现。
4. 自动将新创建的组织账户加入其中。

## 正确答案：A、C 和 E

### A. 配置专用的 Security Hub 委派管理员并启用 CIS 标准

这建立了正确的多账户安全架构。当 Organizations 管理账户将某个成员账户指定为 Security Hub 委派管理员时，Security Hub 将成为受信任服务，并且该委派管理员可以管理成员账户和查看其数据。AWS 还建议使用 Organizations 管理账户以外的账户，因为计费/组织管理员和安全管理员通常不是同一批人员。

因此，安全账户可以作为全组织范围 Security Hub 发现和 CIS 合规性的中央账户。参阅 [将 Security Hub CSPM 与 AWS Organizations 集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/designate-orgs-admin-account.html)。

Security Hub 在本地配置下默认启用的标准包括 **CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0**，因此可以依据所需的 CIS 基准评估 landing zone 中的账户。参阅 [关闭自动启用的安全标准](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-auto-enabled-standards.html)。

### C. 通过 IAM Identity Center 为安全团队分配对委派安全账户的访问权限

权限集定义用户在目标 AWS 账户中获得的 IAM 权限。将安全团队用户和 Security Hub 权限集分配给委派安全账户，可使只有这些用户获得访问集中式 Security Hub 视图所需的权限。IAM Identity Center 会在该账户中预置相应的 IAM 角色和策略。参阅 [使用权限集管理 AWS 账户](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/permissionsetsconcept.html)。

随后，Security Hub 的账户模型将提供所需的可见性边界：委派管理员可以查看任意成员账户的发现，而成员账户只能查看其当前账户的发现。因此，在其自身成员账户中具有适当 Security Hub 权限的用户可以查看自己的发现，但不能查看全组织范围的发现。参阅 [Security Hub CSPM 中管理员和成员账户允许执行的操作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-accounts-allowed-actions.html)。

### E. 开启 Security Hub 自动启用

通过 Organizations 集成和本地配置，自动启用会将每个新创建的组织账户添加为 Security Hub 成员，并在该账户中启用 Security Hub。它还可以自动启用默认标准，包括 CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0。这以最少的自定义自动化直接满足了在账户创建后将其加入的要求。参阅 [自动启用新的组织账户](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/accounts-orgs-auto-enable.html)。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B. 使用 Organizations 管理账户，而不配置委派管理员

这无法建立预期的专用安全管理边界。AWS 建议使用单独的委派管理员，而非 Organizations 管理账户，尤其是因为安全用户与组织/计费管理员通常承担不同职责。该选项也没有说明如何确保只有安全团队获得对聚合发现的访问权限。

### D. 通过 SCP 拒绝所有非安全团队用户访问 Security Hub

这与“特定用户必须能够查看其自身账户中的发现”这一要求相冲突。显式 SCP 拒绝会施加广泛的组织级访问限制，并可能阻止那些已获授权的成员账户用户。Security Hub 已提供适当的账户边界：委派管理员可以查看所有成员的发现，而成员账户仅限查看自身发现。每个账户内的访问权限应通过 IAM/Identity Center 权限授予，而不是采用一刀切的全组织范围拒绝策略。

### F. 构建 EventBridge 和 Lambda 账户注册工作流程

这是不必要的自定义自动化。Security Hub 对新账户提供原生的 Organizations 自动启用功能，因此选项 E 更简单且在运营上更可靠。此外，`CreateMembers` 主要用于创建管理员与成员的关系；与原生组织集成相比，所提议的工作流程并未全面说明如何在每个新账户中启用 Security Hub 及其标准。

因此，**A、C 和 E** 提供了自动化程度最高且职责分离合理的解决方案。

en.question: A company runs applications in AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The applications use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon S3. The company wants to detect potentially compromised EC2 instances, suspicious network activity, and unusual API activity in its existing AWS accounts and in any AWS accounts that the company creates in the future. When the company detects one of these events, the company wants to use an existing Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send a notification to its operational support team for investigation and remediation. Which solution will meet these requirements in accordance with AWS best practices?

options.A: In the organization’s management account, configure an AWS account as the Amazon GuardDuty administrator account. In the GuardDuty administrator account, add the company’s existing AWS accounts to GuardDuty as members. In the GuardDuty administrator account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match GuardDuty events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.
options.B: In the organization’s management account, configure Amazon GuardDuty to add newly created AWS accounts by invitation and to send invitations to the existing AWS accounts. Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that accepts the GuardDuty invitation and creates an Amazon EventBridge rule. Configure the rule with an event pattern to match GuardDuty events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic. Configure the CloudFormation stack set to deploy into all AWS accounts in the organization.
options.C: In the organization’s management account, create an AWS CloudTrail organization trail. Activate the organization trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Create an SCP that enables VPC Flow Logs in each account in the organization. Configure AWS Security Hub for the organization. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match Security Hub events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.
options.D: In the organization’s management account, configure an AWS account as the AWS CloudTrail administrator account. In the CloudTrail administrator account, create a CloudTrail organization trail. Add the company’s existing AWS accounts to the organization trail. Create an SCP that enables VPC Flow Logs in each account in the organization. Configure AWS Security Hub for the organization. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match Security Hub events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: A

The company needs centralized threat detection across an AWS Organizations environment for compromised EC2 instances, suspicious network activity, and unusual API activity. It also needs to cover existing and future accounts and route detections to an existing SNS topic.

### Why A is correct

Amazon GuardDuty is designed for this threat-detection use case. Its foundational data sources include AWS CloudTrail management events for API activity, VPC Flow Logs for network activity, and Route 53 Resolver DNS query logs. GuardDuty analyzes independent streams of these data sources, so the company does not need to create a CloudTrail organization trail or explicitly enable VPC Flow Logs merely to supply GuardDuty. See [GuardDuty foundational data sources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_data-sources.html).

For multi-account deployments, AWS recommends integrating GuardDuty with AWS Organizations. The organization’s management account designates a member account as the delegated GuardDuty administrator, which can centrally enable and manage GuardDuty for organization member accounts and view their findings. This is the best-practice model represented by option A. See [Managing multiple GuardDuty accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_accounts.html) and [Managing GuardDuty accounts with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_organizations.html).

GuardDuty automatically publishes findings to Amazon EventBridge. In a multi-account environment, a rule in the delegated administrator account can process applicable findings from the administrator and member accounts, with the existing SNS topic configured as the rule target. This provides centralized notification without deploying a separate rule in every account. See [Processing GuardDuty findings with EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_eventbridge.html).

For complete future-account coverage, the organization should configure GuardDuty auto-enable as `NEW` or `ALL`: `NEW` covers accounts that subsequently join the organization, while `ALL` covers existing and future accounts. This is a native part of the Organizations-integrated GuardDuty architecture in A. See [Setting GuardDuty organization auto-enable preferences](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/set-guardduty-auto-enable-preferences.html).

### Why B is incorrect

B uses the legacy invitation-based account-association method instead of the recommended AWS Organizations integration. Organization member accounts can be managed directly by the delegated GuardDuty administrator and automatically covered through organization auto-enable settings; they do not need per-account invitation acceptance and EventBridge deployment. See [GuardDuty account-management methods](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_accounts.html) and [GuardDuty invitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_invitations.html).

B also does not reliably cover future accounts. Its StackSet can accept a GuardDuty invitation only after an invitation exists; it does not itself ensure that the required invitation is created and sent for every future account. Furthermore, deploying an EventBridge rule to every account is unnecessary because the delegated administrator can centrally receive and route member-account findings.

### Why C is incorrect

A CloudTrail organization trail records API activity, but it does not perform GuardDuty’s threat analytics for compromised EC2 instances, suspicious network behavior, DNS activity, and anomalous API calls. Security Hub aggregates and normalizes security findings; this option does not enable GuardDuty or another detector that would generate all the required findings.

An SCP also cannot enable VPC Flow Logs. SCPs define the maximum permissions available to accounts and organizational units; they are permission guardrails, not resource-provisioning or service-configuration mechanisms. See [Service control policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

### Why D is incorrect

D has the same core problems as C. A CloudTrail organization trail provides centralized API logging, not GuardDuty’s managed threat detection across API, network-flow, and DNS activity. Security Hub does not replace GuardDuty as the underlying detector, and an SCP cannot create or enable VPC Flow Logs. Manually associating existing accounts with CloudTrail therefore does not provide the required detection architecture or the best-practice method for protecting future accounts.

zh.question: 一家公司在属于 AWS Organizations 中某个组织的 AWS 账户中运行应用程序。这些应用程序使用 Amazon EC2 实例和 Amazon S3。该公司希望在其现有 AWS 账户以及未来创建的任何 AWS 账户中，检测可能已遭入侵的 EC2 实例、可疑网络活动和异常 API 活动。当公司检测到其中任一事件时，希望使用现有的 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题向其运营支持团队发送通知，以便进行调查和修复。哪种解决方案能够按照 AWS 最佳实践满足这些要求？

options.A: 在组织的管理账户中，将一个 AWS 账户配置为 Amazon GuardDuty 管理员账户。在 GuardDuty 管理员账户中，将公司的现有 AWS 账户作为成员添加到 GuardDuty。在 GuardDuty 管理员账户中，创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，并配置事件模式以匹配 GuardDuty 事件，然后将匹配的事件转发到 SNS 主题。
options.B: 在组织的管理账户中，将 Amazon GuardDuty 配置为通过邀请添加新创建的 AWS 账户，并向现有 AWS 账户发送邀请。创建一个 AWS CloudFormation StackSet，用于接受 GuardDuty 邀请并创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则。为该规则配置事件模式以匹配 GuardDuty 事件，然后将匹配的事件转发到 SNS 主题。将 CloudFormation StackSet 配置为部署到组织中的所有 AWS 账户。
options.C: 在组织的管理账户中，创建一个 AWS CloudTrail 组织跟踪。在组织中的所有 AWS 账户中激活该组织跟踪。创建一个 SCP，在组织中的每个账户中启用 VPC Flow Logs。为组织配置 AWS Security Hub。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，并配置事件模式以匹配 Security Hub 事件，然后将匹配的事件转发到 SNS 主题。
options.D: 在组织的管理账户中，将一个 AWS 账户配置为 AWS CloudTrail 管理员账户。在 CloudTrail 管理员账户中，创建一个 CloudTrail 组织跟踪。将公司的现有 AWS 账户添加到该组织跟踪。创建一个 SCP，在组织中的每个账户中启用 VPC Flow Logs。为组织配置 AWS Security Hub。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，并配置事件模式以匹配 Security Hub 事件，然后将匹配的事件转发到 SNS 主题。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：A

该公司需要在 AWS Organizations 环境中集中进行威胁检测，以发现已遭入侵的 EC2 实例、可疑网络活动和异常 API 活动。此外，还需要覆盖现有和未来账户，并将检测结果路由到现有 SNS 主题。

### A 为何正确

Amazon GuardDuty 专为此类威胁检测使用场景设计。其基础数据源包括用于 API 活动的 AWS CloudTrail 管理事件、用于网络活动的 VPC Flow Logs，以及 Route 53 Resolver DNS 查询日志。GuardDuty 会分析这些数据源的独立数据流，因此公司无需仅仅为了向 GuardDuty 提供数据而创建 CloudTrail 组织跟踪或显式启用 VPC Flow Logs。请参阅 [GuardDuty 基础数据源](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_data-sources.html)。

对于多账户部署，AWS 建议将 GuardDuty 与 AWS Organizations 集成。组织的管理账户会指定一个成员账户作为委派 GuardDuty 管理员，该账户可集中为组织成员账户启用和管理 GuardDuty，并查看其发现结果。这正是选项 A 所代表的最佳实践模型。请参阅 [管理多个 GuardDuty 账户](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_accounts.html) 和 [使用 AWS Organizations 管理 GuardDuty 账户](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_organizations.html)。

GuardDuty 会自动将发现结果发布到 Amazon EventBridge。在多账户环境中，委派管理员账户中的规则可以处理来自管理员账户和成员账户的适用发现结果，并将现有 SNS 主题配置为规则目标。这样无需在每个账户中部署单独的规则，即可提供集中通知。请参阅 [使用 EventBridge 处理 GuardDuty 发现结果](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_eventbridge.html)。

为完整覆盖未来账户，组织应将 GuardDuty 自动启用配置为 `NEW` 或 `ALL`：`NEW` 覆盖随后加入组织的账户，而 `ALL` 覆盖现有和未来账户。这是 A 中与 Organizations 集成的 GuardDuty 架构的原生组成部分。请参阅 [设置 GuardDuty 组织自动启用首选项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/set-guardduty-auto-enable-preferences.html)。

### B 为何不正确

B 使用传统的基于邀请的账户关联方法，而不是推荐的 AWS Organizations 集成。组织成员账户可以由委派 GuardDuty 管理员直接管理，并通过组织自动启用设置自动受到保护；它们不需要逐账户接受邀请和部署 EventBridge。请参阅 [GuardDuty 账户管理方法](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_accounts.html) 和 [GuardDuty 邀请](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_invitations.html)。

B 也无法可靠地覆盖未来账户。其 StackSet 只能在邀请已存在后接受 GuardDuty 邀请；它本身无法确保为每个未来账户创建和发送所需的邀请。此外，无需在每个账户中部署 EventBridge 规则，因为委派管理员可以集中接收和路由成员账户的发现结果。

### C 为何不正确

CloudTrail 组织跟踪会记录 API 活动，但不会执行 GuardDuty 针对已遭入侵的 EC2 实例、可疑网络行为、DNS 活动和异常 API 调用所提供的威胁分析。Security Hub 会聚合和规范化安全发现结果；该选项未启用 GuardDuty 或其他能够生成所有所需发现结果的检测器。

SCP 也无法启用 VPC Flow Logs。SCP 定义账户和组织单位可获得的最大权限；它们是权限防护机制，而不是资源预置或服务配置机制。请参阅 [服务控制策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

### D 为何不正确

D 与 C 存在相同的核心问题。CloudTrail 组织跟踪提供集中式 API 日志记录，而不是 GuardDuty 对 API、网络流量和 DNS 活动进行的托管威胁检测。Security Hub 无法取代作为底层检测器的 GuardDuty，并且 SCP 无法创建或启用 VPC Flow Logs。因此，手动将现有账户关联到 CloudTrail 并不能提供所需的检测架构，也不是保护未来账户的最佳实践方法。

en.question: A company’s DevOps engineer is working in a multi-account environment. The company uses AWS Transit Gateway to route all outbound traffic through a network operations account. In the network operations account, all account traffic passes through a firewall appliance for inspection before the traffic goes to an internet gateway. The firewall appliance sends logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and includes event severities of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and INFO. The security team wants to receive an alert if any CRITICAL events occur. What should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary to monitor the firewall state. If the firewall reaches a CRITICAL state or logs a CRITICAL event, use a CloudWatch alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.
options.B: Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric filter by using a search for CRITICAL events. Publish a custom metric for the finding. Use a CloudWatch alarm based on the custom metric to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.
options.C: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in the network operations account. Configure GuardDuty to monitor flow logs. Create an Amazon EventBridge event rule that is invoked by GuardDuty events that are CRITICAL. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.
options.D: Use AWS Firewall Manager to apply consistent policies across all accounts. Create an Amazon EventBridge event rule that is invoked by Firewall Manager events that are CRITICAL. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The firewall appliance already writes its inspection events to **Amazon CloudWatch Logs**. The requirement is to detect any log event whose severity is `CRITICAL` and notify the security team. Therefore, the solution should transform matching log entries into an alarmable signal and send the alarm notification through Amazon SNS.

## Correct answer: B

Create a **CloudWatch Logs metric filter** on the firewall appliance's log group with a filter pattern that matches `CRITICAL` events. Configure the filter to publish a custom metric value, such as `1`, for every matching event. Then create a CloudWatch alarm that enters the `ALARM` state when the metric is greater than zero and configure the alarm to publish to an SNS topic subscribed by the security team.

AWS documents that a metric filter can count occurrences of matching keywords by publishing a metric value of `1` for each matching log event. CloudWatch also supports the **metric filter approach** for alarming on logs: create a metric filter on a log group and then create a standard metric alarm on the resulting metric. See [Create a metric filter for a log group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html) and [Alarming on logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Alarm-On-Logs.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A — Incorrect.** CloudWatch Synthetics canaries are scheduled scripts intended to monitor endpoints, APIs, URLs, website content, availability, and latency. They are not the appropriate mechanism for matching severity values in firewall appliance logs that are already in CloudWatch Logs. A metric filter directly addresses the stated log-monitoring requirement. See [Synthetic monitoring (canaries)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries.html).

- **C — Incorrect.** GuardDuty analyzes supported security telemetry, including its own independent stream of VPC flow log data, to generate GuardDuty threat findings. It does not use the firewall appliance's existing CloudWatch log events and their vendor-defined `CRITICAL` field as the direct alarm source. Enabling GuardDuty could provide additional threat detection, but it does not satisfy the specific requirement to alert whenever the appliance writes a `CRITICAL` event. See [GuardDuty data sources — VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_data-sources.html).

- **D — Incorrect.** AWS Firewall Manager centrally deploys and manages supported firewall policies, such as AWS Network Firewall protections, across accounts and VPCs in an AWS Organization. The scenario describes a firewall appliance already sending logs to CloudWatch Logs; it does not state that the appliance or its severity events are managed by Firewall Manager. Firewall Manager events therefore are not the direct source for detecting these `CRITICAL` log entries. See [Using AWS Network Firewall policies in Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/network-firewall-policies.html).

Therefore, **B** is the most direct and appropriate solution.

zh.question: 某公司的 DevOps 工程师在多账户环境中工作。该公司使用 AWS Transit Gateway 将所有出站流量通过网络运营账户进行路由。在网络运营账户中，所有账户流量在前往互联网网关之前都会通过防火墙设备进行检查。该防火墙设备将日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch Logs，并且日志包含 CRITICAL、HIGH、MEDIUM、LOW 和 INFO 事件严重性。安全团队希望在发生任何 CRITICAL 事件时收到警报。DevOps 工程师应如何做才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary 来监控防火墙状态。如果防火墙达到 CRITICAL 状态或记录了 CRITICAL 事件，则使用 CloudWatch 警报向 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题发布通知。将安全团队的电子邮件地址订阅到该主题。
options.B: 使用对 CRITICAL 事件的搜索创建 Amazon CloudWatch 指标筛选器。为该发现发布一个自定义指标。使用基于该自定义指标的 CloudWatch 警报向 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题发布通知。将安全团队的电子邮件地址订阅到该主题。
options.C: 在网络运营账户中启用 Amazon GuardDuty。配置 GuardDuty 以监控流日志。创建一条由 CRITICAL GuardDuty 事件触发的 Amazon EventBridge 事件规则。将 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题定义为目标。将安全团队的电子邮件地址订阅到该主题。
options.D: 使用 AWS Firewall Manager 在所有账户中应用一致的策略。创建一条由 CRITICAL Firewall Manager 事件触发的 Amazon EventBridge 事件规则。将 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题定义为目标。将安全团队的电子邮件地址订阅到该主题。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

防火墙设备已经将其检查事件写入 **Amazon CloudWatch Logs**。要求是检测严重性为 `CRITICAL` 的任何日志事件，并通知安全团队。因此，解决方案应将匹配的日志条目转换为可用于警报的信号，并通过 Amazon SNS 发送警报通知。

## 正确答案：B

在防火墙设备的日志组上创建一个 **CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器**，并使用匹配 `CRITICAL` 事件的筛选模式。配置该筛选器，使其针对每个匹配事件发布一个自定义指标值，例如 `1`。然后创建一个 CloudWatch 警报，当该指标大于零时使警报进入 `ALARM` 状态，并将警报配置为发布到安全团队已订阅的 SNS 主题。

AWS 文档说明，指标筛选器可以通过为每个匹配的日志事件发布指标值 `1` 来统计匹配关键字的出现次数。CloudWatch 也支持使用 **指标筛选器方法** 对日志设置警报：在日志组上创建指标筛选器，然后针对生成的指标创建标准指标警报。请参阅 [Create a metric filter for a log group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html) 和 [Alarming on logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Alarm-On-Logs.html)。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

- **A — 不正确。** CloudWatch Synthetics canary 是计划运行的脚本，旨在监控终端节点、API、URL、网站内容、可用性和延迟。对于已位于 CloudWatch Logs 中的防火墙设备日志中严重性值的匹配，它并不是合适的机制。指标筛选器可直接满足所述的日志监控要求。请参阅 [Synthetic monitoring (canaries)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries.html)。

- **C — 不正确。** GuardDuty 会分析受支持的安全遥测数据，包括其自身独立的 VPC 流日志数据流，以生成 GuardDuty 威胁发现。它不会将防火墙设备现有的 CloudWatch 日志事件及其由供应商定义的 `CRITICAL` 字段用作直接警报源。启用 GuardDuty 可以提供额外的威胁检测，但无法满足在设备每次写入 `CRITICAL` 事件时发出警报这一特定要求。请参阅 [GuardDuty data sources — VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_data-sources.html)。

- **D — 不正确。** AWS Firewall Manager 可在 AWS Organization 中跨账户和 VPC 集中部署和管理受支持的防火墙策略，例如 AWS Network Firewall 防护。该场景描述的是一个已经将日志发送到 CloudWatch Logs 的防火墙设备；并未说明该设备或其严重性事件由 Firewall Manager 管理。因此，Firewall Manager 事件不是检测这些 `CRITICAL` 日志条目的直接来源。请参阅 [Using AWS Network Firewall policies in Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/network-firewall-policies.html)。

因此，**B** 是最直接且最合适的解决方案。

en.question: A company is divided into teams. Each team has an AWS account, and all the accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team must retain full administrative rights to its AWS account. Each team also must be allowed to access only AWS services that the company approves for use. AWS services must gain approval through a request and approval process. How should a DevOps engineer configure the accounts to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to provision IAM policies in each account to deny access to restricted AWS services. In each account, configure AWS Config rules that ensure that the policies are attached to IAM principals in the account.
options.B: Use AWS Control Tower to provision the accounts into OUs within the organization. Configure AWS Control Tower to enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure IAM Identity Center to provide administrative access. Include deny policies on user roles for restricted AWS services.
options.C: Place all the accounts under a new top-level OU within the organization. Create an SCP that denies access to restricted AWS services. Attach the SCP to the OU.
options.D: Create an SCP that allows access to only approved AWS services. Attach the SCP to the root OU of the organization. Remove the FullAWSAccess SCP from the root OU of the organization.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: D

The company needs a centralized, preventive control with an **approval-first** model: each team can remain the administrator of its own account, but an AWS service must be unavailable until the company explicitly approves it.

Create an SCP that allows only approved AWS services, attach it to the organization root, and remove the default `FullAWSAccess` SCP from the root. This implements the AWS Organizations **allow-list strategy**. AWS specifically documents replacing `FullAWSAccess` with a policy that permits only selected services so that new AWS services are not automatically available and must be explicitly added to the allow list. See [SCP evaluation in AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html) and the [AWS Organizations policy tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_tutorials_basic.html).

Removing `FullAWSAccess` from the root is necessary because leaving that broad allow policy attached at the same level would defeat the restrictive allow list. Under SCP allow-list evaluation, an action must be explicitly allowed at **every applicable level** of the Organizations hierarchy. Therefore, the approved-service allow list at the root constrains all descendant OUs and accounts; a broader policy such as `FullAWSAccess` attached to a lower-level OU or account cannot override a service that the root policy does not allow.

This configuration is compatible with the requirement that teams retain administrative rights. SCPs do not grant permissions; they define the **maximum permissions available** to identities in member accounts. Teams can retain account-level administrator roles, including IAM permissions such as `AdministratorAccess`, but those permissions are effective only for actions permitted by the applicable SCPs. Member-account administrators cannot modify or bypass an SCP imposed through AWS Organizations. See [Service control policies in AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

Thus, each team has full administrative control **within the boundary of company-approved AWS services**, while all unapproved services—including newly released services—are denied by default.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. CloudFormation StackSets, IAM policies, and AWS Config

This places the restrictions inside each member account. Because each team has full administrative access, its administrators could modify or detach the IAM policies, create other principals, or otherwise bypass account-local controls. AWS Config can evaluate resource and configuration compliance, but it is not an organization-level permissions boundary that prevents API access. An SCP is the appropriate preventive guardrail because member-account administrators cannot override it.

### B. AWS Control Tower, IAM Identity Center, and role deny policies

Deny policies attached to IAM Identity Center roles restrict only those roles. A local account administrator could potentially use or create another IAM principal or access path that does not have the same deny policy. This does not provide the required account-wide maximum-permissions boundary. It also follows a deny-list approach for known restricted services rather than requiring every service to be explicitly approved.

### C. An SCP that denies restricted services

Although an SCP would be enforceable against member-account administrators, this option implements a **deny list**. Services that are not named in the deny policy remain potentially usable. Consequently, a newly released or otherwise unreviewed AWS service could be used before the company adds it to the restricted-services list.

That violates the request-and-approval requirement. AWS’s allow-list approach provides the required default-deny behavior: a new service remains unavailable until an administrator explicitly adds it to the approved list. Moving all accounts into a new top-level OU is also unnecessary when the policy is intended to apply across the organization.

zh.question: 一家公司划分为多个团队。每个团队都有一个 AWS 账户，并且所有账户都属于 AWS Organizations 中的一个组织。每个团队都必须保留其 AWS 账户的完整管理权限。同时，每个团队只能访问公司批准使用的 AWS 服务。AWS 服务必须通过请求和审批流程才能获得批准。DevOps 工程师应如何配置这些账户以满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS CloudFormation StackSets 在每个账户中预置 IAM 策略，以拒绝访问受限的 AWS 服务。在每个账户中，配置 AWS Config 规则以确保这些策略已附加到该账户中的 IAM 主体。
options.B: 使用 AWS Control Tower 将账户预置到组织内的 OU 中。配置 AWS Control Tower 以启用 AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)。配置 IAM Identity Center 以提供管理访问权限。对用户角色包含针对受限 AWS 服务的拒绝策略。
options.C: 将所有账户置于组织内一个新的顶级 OU 下。创建一个拒绝访问受限 AWS 服务的 SCP。将该 SCP 附加到该 OU。
options.D: 创建一个仅允许访问已批准 AWS 服务的 SCP。将该 SCP 附加到组织的根 OU。移除组织根 OU 上的 FullAWSAccess SCP。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：D

公司需要一种集中式预防性控制，并采用**先审批**模型：每个团队可以继续担任自己账户的管理员，但在公司明确批准之前，AWS 服务必须不可用。

创建一个仅允许已批准 AWS 服务的 SCP，将其附加到组织根，并从根中移除默认的 `FullAWSAccess` SCP。这实现了 AWS Organizations 的**允许列表策略**。AWS 专门说明了将 `FullAWSAccess` 替换为仅允许选定服务的策略，从而确保新的 AWS 服务不会自动可用，而是必须明确添加到允许列表中。请参阅 [AWS Organizations 中的 SCP 评估](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html) 和 [AWS Organizations 策略教程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_tutorials_basic.html)。

必须从根中移除 `FullAWSAccess`，因为如果在同一层级保留该宽泛的允许策略，就会削弱限制性的允许列表。在 SCP 允许列表评估下，一个操作必须在 Organizations 层级结构的**每个适用层级**上被显式允许。因此，根级别的已批准服务允许列表会约束所有下级 OU 和账户；附加到较低级别 OU 或账户的更宽泛策略（如 `FullAWSAccess`）无法覆盖根策略未允许的服务。

此配置与团队必须保留管理权限的要求兼容。SCP 不授予权限；它们定义成员账户中身份可获得的**最大权限**。团队可以保留账户级管理员角色，包括 `AdministratorAccess` 等 IAM 权限，但这些权限仅对适用 SCP 所允许的操作生效。成员账户管理员无法修改或绕过通过 AWS Organizations 强制实施的 SCP。请参阅 [AWS Organizations 中的服务控制策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

因此，每个团队都可以在公司批准的 AWS 服务这一边界内拥有完整管理控制权，而所有未经批准的服务（包括新发布的服务）默认都会被拒绝。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. CloudFormation StackSets、IAM 策略和 AWS Config

此方案将限制置于每个成员账户内部。由于每个团队拥有完整管理访问权限，其管理员可以修改或解除附加 IAM 策略、创建其他主体，或者以其他方式绕过账户本地控制。AWS Config 可以评估资源和配置合规性，但它不是能阻止 API 访问的组织级权限边界。SCP 才是合适的预防性护栏，因为成员账户管理员无法覆盖它。

### B. AWS Control Tower、IAM Identity Center 和角色拒绝策略

附加到 IAM Identity Center 角色的拒绝策略只会限制这些角色。本地账户管理员可能使用或创建不具有相同拒绝策略的其他 IAM 主体或访问路径。这无法提供所需的账户范围最大权限边界。它还采用了针对已知受限服务的拒绝列表方法，而不是要求每项服务都必须获得明确批准。

### C. 拒绝受限服务的 SCP

尽管 SCP 可对成员账户管理员强制执行，但该选项实施的是**拒绝列表**。未在拒绝策略中列出的服务仍有可能被使用。因此，新发布或尚未审查的 AWS 服务可能在公司将其添加到受限服务列表之前就被使用。

这违反了请求和审批要求。AWS 的允许列表方法提供了所需的默认拒绝行为：新服务会保持不可用，直到管理员将其明确添加到已批准列表中。如果该策略旨在应用于整个组织，也没有必要将所有账户移到一个新的顶级 OU 中。

en.question: A DevOps engineer used an AWS CloudFormation custom resource to set up AD Connector. The AWS Lambda function ran and created AD Connector, but CloudFormation is not transitioning from CREATE_IN_PROGRESS to CREATE_COMPLETE. Which action should the engineer take to resolve this issue?

options.A: Ensure the Lambda function code has exited successfully.
options.B: Ensure the Lambda function code returns a response to the pre-signed URL.
options.C: Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has cloudformation:UpdateStack permissions for the stack ARN.
options.D: Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has ds:ConnectDirectory permissions for the AWS account.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

This is a Lambda-backed CloudFormation custom resource. The Lambda function successfully performed the underlying operation—creating the AD Connector—but CloudFormation is still waiting for the custom resource provider to report the result.

AWS documents that a custom-resource request contains a `ResponseURL`, which is a pre-signed Amazon S3 URL. The provider must send a JSON response with a status of `SUCCESS` or `FAILED` to that URL. CloudFormation waits for this response and proceeds with the stack operation only after receiving `SUCCESS`; merely completing the Lambda invocation does not complete the CloudFormation resource operation. See [How custom resources work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/template-custom-resources.html).

## Correct answer

**B. Ensure the Lambda function code returns a response to the pre-signed URL.**

The function must send a `SUCCESS` response to the request's pre-signed `ResponseURL`, including the required identifiers and a stable `PhysicalResourceId`. For supported inline Lambda implementations, the CloudFormation `cfn-response`/`cfnresponse` module can perform this callback; its `send` method accepts a response status such as `SUCCESS` or `FAILED`. See the [`cfn-response` module documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-lambda-function-code-cfnresponsemodule.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A. Ensure the Lambda function code has exited successfully.** Incorrect. A successful Lambda exit is not itself the custom-resource response. CloudFormation remains waiting until the provider sends a properly formatted response to the pre-signed URL. If no response is sent, the stack operation eventually fails or times out.
- **C. Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has `cloudformation:UpdateStack` permissions for the stack ARN.** Incorrect. The Lambda function does not update the stack directly. It reports the custom-resource result through the pre-signed `ResponseURL`, after which CloudFormation advances the stack state. `cloudformation:UpdateStack` is unnecessary for this callback.
- **D. Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has `ds:ConnectDirectory` permissions for the AWS account.** Incorrect in this scenario. The question states that the function already created the AD Connector, demonstrating that the directory creation call succeeded. The unresolved problem is notification of completion to CloudFormation, not authorization to create the directory.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师使用 AWS CloudFormation 自定义资源来设置 AD Connector。AWS Lambda 函数已运行并创建了 AD Connector，但 CloudFormation 未从 CREATE_IN_PROGRESS 转换为 CREATE_COMPLETE。工程师应采取哪项操作来解决此问题？

options.A: 确保 Lambda 函数代码已成功退出。
options.B: 确保 Lambda 函数代码向预签名 URL 返回响应。
options.C: 确保 Lambda 函数 IAM 角色具有针对该堆栈 ARN 的 cloudformation:UpdateStack 权限。
options.D: 确保 Lambda 函数 IAM 角色具有针对该 AWS 账户的 ds:ConnectDirectory 权限。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

这是一个由 Lambda 支持的 CloudFormation 自定义资源。Lambda 函数已成功执行底层操作——创建 AD Connector——但 CloudFormation 仍在等待自定义资源提供程序报告结果。

AWS 文档指出，自定义资源请求包含一个 `ResponseURL`，它是一个预签名的 Amazon S3 URL。提供程序必须向该 URL 发送包含 `SUCCESS` 或 `FAILED` 状态的 JSON 响应。CloudFormation 会等待此响应，并且仅在收到 `SUCCESS` 后才会继续执行堆栈操作；仅完成 Lambda 调用并不会完成 CloudFormation 资源操作。请参阅 [自定义资源的工作原理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/template-custom-resources.html)。

## 正确答案

**B. 确保 Lambda 函数代码向预签名 URL 返回响应。**

该函数必须向请求中的预签名 `ResponseURL` 发送 `SUCCESS` 响应，其中包括必需的标识符和稳定的 `PhysicalResourceId`。对于受支持的内联 Lambda 实现，CloudFormation 的 `cfn-response`/`cfnresponse` 模块可以执行此回调；其 `send` 方法接受 `SUCCESS` 或 `FAILED` 等响应状态。请参阅 [`cfn-response` 模块文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-lambda-function-code-cfnresponsemodule.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

- **A. 确保 Lambda 函数代码已成功退出。** 不正确。Lambda 成功退出本身并不是自定义资源响应。CloudFormation 会一直等待，直到提供程序向预签名 URL 发送格式正确的响应。如果未发送响应，堆栈操作最终会失败或超时。
- **C. 确保 Lambda 函数 IAM 角色具有针对该堆栈 ARN 的 `cloudformation:UpdateStack` 权限。** 不正确。Lambda 函数不会直接更新堆栈。它通过预签名 `ResponseURL` 报告自定义资源结果，随后 CloudFormation 才会推进堆栈状态。此回调不需要 `cloudformation:UpdateStack`。
- **D. 确保 Lambda 函数 IAM 角色具有针对该 AWS 账户的 `ds:ConnectDirectory` 权限。** 在此情景中不正确。题目指出该函数已创建 AD Connector，这表明目录创建调用已成功。未解决的问题是向 CloudFormation 通知完成状态，而不是创建目录的授权问题。

en.question: A company uses AWS CodeCommit for source code control. Developers apply their changes to various feature branches and create pull requests to move those changes to the main branch when the changes are ready for production. The developers should not be able to push changes directly to the main branch. The company applied the AWSCodeCommitPowerUser managed policy to the developers’ IAM role, and now these developers can push changes to the main branch directly on every repository in the AWS account. What should the company do to restrict the developers’ ability to push changes to the main branch directly?

options.A: Create an additional policy to include a Deny rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions. Include a restriction for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.
options.B: Remove the IAM policy, and add an AWSCodeCommitReadOnly managed policy. Add an Allow rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.
options.C: Modify the IAM policy. Include a Deny rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.
options.D: Create an additional policy to include an Allow rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions. Include a restriction for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the feature branches.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The developers already have broad CodeCommit write permissions through the AWS-managed `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` policy. The company must preserve their ability to work on feature branches while preventing **direct changes to `main`** in selected repositories.

## Correct answer: A

Create and attach an additional IAM policy containing an explicit **`Deny`** for:

- `codecommit:GitPush` — prevents direct Git pushes
- `codecommit:PutFile` — prevents creating or updating a file through the CodeCommit API/console

Scope the statement to the required repository ARNs and use the `codecommit:References` condition key for `refs/heads/main`.

AWS explicitly documents this branch-protection pattern: create a conditional policy whose `Deny` applies to specified CodeCommit actions, repository resources, and branch references. AWS's example uses `codecommit:References` with `refs/heads/main`. For a deny statement containing `GitPush`, AWS also specifies including the `Null` condition because of how Git and `git-receive-pack` process pushes. See [Configure an IAM policy to limit pushes and merges to a branch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-conditional-branch.html).

This additional explicit deny overrides the broad allow granted by `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser`. IAM policy evaluation states that an applicable explicit deny overrides an allow. See [IAM policy evaluation logic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html).

A representative statement would follow this pattern:

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": [
    "codecommit:GitPush",
    "codecommit:PutFile"
  ],
  "Resource": [
    "arn:aws:codecommit:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:REPOSITORY_NAME"
  ],
  "Condition": {
    "StringEqualsIfExists": {
      "codecommit:References": "refs/heads/main"
    },
    "Null": {
      "codecommit:References": "false"
    }
  }
}
```

This blocks direct updates to `main` without denying the pull-request merge APIs, so the intended controlled promotion workflow can continue.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Replace PowerUser with ReadOnly and allow writes conditioned on `main`

This is incorrect because:

1. An `Allow` conditioned on the `main` branch would permit the very direct changes that must be prevented.
2. `AWSCodeCommitReadOnly` is intended for users who can read repository contents but cannot change them, so replacing PowerUser would also remove many capabilities developers may need. See [AWS managed policies for CodeCommit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html).

A least-privilege custom allow model could theoretically be designed for feature branches, but that is not what this option describes.

### C. Modify the existing AWSCodeCommitPowerUser policy

`AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` is an **AWS-managed policy**. AWS-managed policies cannot be edited by customers; only customer-managed and inline policies can be edited. Therefore, the company must attach a separate customer-managed or inline deny policy rather than modify the AWS-managed policy. See [Edit IAM policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_manage-edit.html).

### D. Add an allow for feature branches

The existing `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` policy already allows `GitPush` and broad `Put*` actions on `Resource: "*"`. Adding another allow for feature branches does not remove that existing permission to push to `main`. IAM combines applicable allows, whereas an explicit deny overrides them. Therefore, a branch-specific **deny** is required, not another allow. See [AWSCodeCommitPowerUser](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html) and [IAM policy evaluation logic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS CodeCommit 进行源代码控制。开发人员将更改应用到不同的功能分支，并在更改准备好用于生产时创建拉取请求，以将这些更改移至主分支。开发人员不应能够直接将更改推送到主分支。该公司已将 AWSCodeCommitPowerUser 托管策略应用于开发人员的 IAM 角色，现在这些开发人员可以直接将更改推送到 AWS 账户中每个存储库的主分支。公司应如何限制开发人员直接将更改推送到主分支的能力？

options.A: 创建额外的策略，为 GitPush 和 PutFile 操作添加 Deny 规则。在策略语句中针对特定存储库添加限制，并使用引用主分支的条件。
options.B: 移除 IAM 策略，并添加 AWSCodeCommitReadOnly 托管策略。为 GitPush 和 PutFile 操作添加 Allow 规则，在策略语句中针对特定存储库添加限制，并使用引用主分支的条件。
options.C: 修改 IAM 策略。为 GitPush 和 PutFile 操作添加 Deny 规则，在策略语句中针对特定存储库添加限制，并使用引用主分支的条件。
options.D: 创建额外的策略，为 GitPush 和 PutFile 操作添加 Allow 规则。在策略语句中针对特定存储库添加限制，并使用引用功能分支的条件。

zh.explanation:
## 题目在问什么

开发人员已经通过 AWS 托管的 `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` 策略拥有广泛的 CodeCommit 写入权限。公司必须保留他们在功能分支上工作的能力，同时防止他们在选定的存储库中**直接更改 `main`**。

## 正确答案：A

创建并附加额外的 IAM 策略，其中包含针对以下操作的显式 **`Deny`**：

- `codecommit:GitPush` — 防止直接 Git 推送
- `codecommit:PutFile` — 防止通过 CodeCommit API/控制台创建或更新文件

将该语句的范围限定为所需的存储库 ARN，并对 `refs/heads/main` 使用 `codecommit:References` 条件键。

AWS 明确记录了此分支保护模式：创建条件策略，使其 `Deny` 适用于指定的 CodeCommit 操作、存储库资源和分支引用。AWS 的示例针对 `refs/heads/main` 使用 `codecommit:References`。对于包含 `GitPush` 的拒绝语句，AWS 还规定应包含 `Null` 条件，这是由于 Git 和 `git-receive-pack` 处理推送的方式所致。请参阅 [配置 IAM 策略以限制向分支推送和合并](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-conditional-branch.html)。

这个额外的显式拒绝会覆盖 `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` 授予的广泛允许权限。IAM 策略评估规定，适用的显式拒绝会覆盖允许。请参阅 [IAM 策略评估逻辑](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)。

一个代表性语句如下所示：

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": [
    "codecommit:GitPush",
    "codecommit:PutFile"
  ],
  "Resource": [
    "arn:aws:codecommit:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:REPOSITORY_NAME"
  ],
  "Condition": {
    "StringEqualsIfExists": {
      "codecommit:References": "refs/heads/main"
    },
    "Null": {
      "codecommit:References": "false"
    }
  }
}
```

这会阻止直接更新 `main`，但不会拒绝拉取请求合并 API，因此预期的受控提升工作流程可以继续进行。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

### B. 将 PowerUser 替换为 ReadOnly，并允许以 `main` 为条件的写入

此选项不正确，原因如下：

1. 以 `main` 分支为条件的 `Allow` 会允许恰恰需要阻止的直接更改。
2. `AWSCodeCommitReadOnly` 面向可以读取存储库内容但不能更改内容的用户，因此替换 PowerUser 还会移除开发人员可能需要的许多功能。请参阅 [CodeCommit 的 AWS 托管策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html)。

理论上可以为功能分支设计最小权限的自定义允许模型，但这不是该选项所描述的内容。

### C. 修改现有的 AWSCodeCommitPowerUser 策略

`AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` 是一项 **AWS 托管策略**。客户无法编辑 AWS 托管策略；只有客户托管策略和内联策略可以编辑。因此，公司必须附加单独的客户托管或内联拒绝策略，而不是修改 AWS 托管策略。请参阅 [编辑 IAM 策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_manage-edit.html)。

### D. 为功能分支添加允许

现有的 `AWSCodeCommitPowerUser` 策略已经允许针对 `Resource: "*"` 的 `GitPush` 和广泛的 `Put*` 操作。为功能分支添加另一项允许不会移除现有的推送到 `main` 的权限。IAM 会合并适用的允许，而显式拒绝会覆盖这些允许。因此，需要按分支指定的 **拒绝**，而不是另一个允许。请参阅 [AWSCodeCommitPowerUser](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html) 和 [IAM 策略评估逻辑](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)。

en.question: A company manages a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store the data. The company has configured Amazon Route 53 with an alias record that points to the ALB. A new company guideline requires a geographically isolated disaster recovery (DR) site with an RTO of 4 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes. Which DR strategy will meet these requirements with the LEAST change to the application stack?

options.A: Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different Availability Zone. Create an RDS read replica in the new Availability Zone, and configure the new stack to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a failover routing policy.
options.B: Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. Create an RDS read replica in the new Region, and configure the new stack to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a latency routing policy.
options.C: Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. In the event of an outage, copy and restore the latest RDS snapshot from the primary Region to the DR Region. Adjust the Route 53 record set to point to the ALB in the DR Region.
options.D: Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. Create an RDS read replica in the new Region, and configure the new environment to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a failover routing policy. In the event of an outage, promote the read replica to primary.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The requirement is for a **geographically isolated** DR site, an **RTO of 4 hours**, an **RPO of 15 minutes**, and the **least change** to the existing EC2/ALB/RDS/Route 53 architecture.

A separate Availability Zone is not enough for regional geographic isolation. The standby therefore needs to be in a **different AWS Region**. To minimize recovery time and data loss, the database should already exist there and receive ongoing replication rather than being created only after the disaster.

## Correct answer: D

**D** implements an active-passive, cross-Region DR design:

- The EC2 Auto Scaling group and ALB are pre-created in the DR Region, avoiding the need to build the application tier during recovery.
- Amazon RDS supports creating a read replica in a different Region specifically to improve disaster recovery capabilities. After its initial creation, RDS continually replicates subsequent database changes to it. AWS notes that cross-Region replicas can experience additional replication lag, so `ReplicaLag` should be monitored against the 15-minute RPO target. See [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html).
- During a disaster, the replica is promoted to a writable standalone DB instance. AWS explicitly identifies read-replica promotion as a failure-recovery mechanism and states that promotion generally takes several minutes or longer, which is compatible with the stated 4-hour RTO. See [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html).
- Route 53 failover routing provides the intended active-passive behavior: traffic goes to the primary resource while healthy and to the secondary resource when the primary is unhealthy. See [Failover routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html).

This keeps the application architecture substantially unchanged while providing a warm standby application tier and continuously replicated database in a geographically separate Region.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

A different Availability Zone is still within the **same AWS Region**, so it does not satisfy the requirement for a geographically isolated DR site. In addition, the option never promotes the read replica; an RDS for MySQL read replica is read-only until promoted, so the failed-over application could not perform normal writes.

### B

The different Region and cross-Region read replica are appropriate, but the routing and database-failover mechanisms are not:

- **Latency routing** is intended to select a resource based on network latency, not to maintain a strict primary/secondary DR relationship.
- It could send production traffic to the secondary application during normal operation.
- The option does not promote the read replica, so the DR database remains read-only.

For an active-passive DR design, Route 53 **failover routing**, as used in D, is the appropriate policy.

### C

This is a backup-and-restore strategy rather than a continuously replicated standby database. RDS supports copying snapshots across Regions, but copying the snapshot and then restoring a new DB instance introduces additional recovery steps and variable recovery time. See [Copying a DB snapshot for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html).

More importantly, restoring the “latest snapshot” does not establish that the recovery point is within 15 minutes. RDS automated snapshots are created during the configured backup window; although RDS point-in-time recovery can provide finer recovery points when automated backups and transaction logs are used, this option specifies copying and restoring the latest snapshot, not cross-Region point-in-time backup replication. AWS distinguishes snapshot-based restore from asynchronous read-replica replication in [Resilience in Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html). Therefore, C cannot reliably satisfy the stated 15-minute RPO and is operationally slower than promoting a pre-existing read replica.

zh.question: 一家公司管理着一个 Web 应用程序，该程序运行在 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例上。EC2 实例在多个 Availability Zones 中的一个 Auto Scaling 组内运行。该应用程序使用一个 Amazon RDS for MySQL DB 实例来存储数据。该公司已将 Amazon Route 53 配置为使用指向 ALB 的别名记录。一项新的公司准则要求建立一个地理隔离的灾难恢复 (DR) 站点，RTO 为 4 小时，RPO 为 15 分钟。哪种 DR 策略能够以对应用程序堆栈进行最少更改的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 在不同的 Availability Zone 中启动除 Amazon RDS 之外所有组件的副本环境。在新的 Availability Zone 中创建一个 RDS 只读副本，并将新堆栈配置为指向本地 RDS DB 实例。使用运行状况检查配置故障转移路由策略，将新堆栈添加到 Route 53 记录集中。
options.B: 在不同的 AWS Region 中启动除 Amazon RDS 之外所有组件的副本环境。在新的 Region 中创建一个 RDS 只读副本，并将新堆栈配置为指向本地 RDS DB 实例。使用运行状况检查配置延迟路由策略，将新堆栈添加到 Route 53 记录集中。
options.C: 在不同的 AWS Region 中启动除 Amazon RDS 之外所有组件的副本环境。发生中断时，将最新的 RDS 快照从主 Region 复制并恢复到 DR Region。调整 Route 53 记录集，使其指向 DR Region 中的 ALB。
options.D: 在不同的 AWS Region 中启动除 Amazon RDS 之外所有组件的副本环境。在新的 Region 中创建一个 RDS 只读副本，并将新环境配置为指向本地 RDS DB 实例。使用运行状况检查配置故障转移路由策略，将新堆栈添加到 Route 53 记录集中。发生中断时，将只读副本提升为主实例。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

要求是建立一个**地理隔离的** DR 站点，具备 **4 小时的 RTO**、**15 分钟的 RPO**，并且对现有的 EC2/ALB/RDS/Route 53 架构进行**最少更改**。

单独的 Availability Zone 不足以实现 Region 级别的地理隔离。因此，备用站点需要位于**不同的 AWS Region**。为了最大限度缩短恢复时间和减少数据丢失，数据库应当已经存在于该 Region 中并持续接收复制，而不是仅在灾难发生后才创建。

## 正确答案：D

**D** 实现了主动-被动的跨 Region DR 设计：

- EC2 Auto Scaling 组和 ALB 已在 DR Region 中预先创建，从而避免在恢复期间构建应用程序层。
- Amazon RDS 支持在不同 Region 中创建只读副本，专门用于提高灾难恢复能力。初始创建后，RDS 会持续将后续数据库更改复制到该副本。AWS 指出，跨 Region 副本可能会出现额外的复制延迟，因此应根据 15 分钟 RPO 目标监控 `ReplicaLag`。请参阅 [在不同 AWS Region 中创建只读副本](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html)。
- 灾难期间，该副本会被提升为可写的独立 DB 实例。AWS 明确将只读副本提升识别为一种故障恢复机制，并指出提升通常需要数分钟或更长时间，这与所述的 4 小时 RTO 兼容。请参阅 [将只读副本提升为独立 DB 实例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)。
- Route 53 故障转移路由提供预期的主动-被动行为：主资源运行正常时，流量会转至主资源；主资源不健康时，流量会转至辅助资源。请参阅 [故障转移路由](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html)。

该方案在保持应用程序架构基本不变的同时，在地理上独立的 Region 中提供了温备用应用程序层和持续复制的数据库。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

不同的 Availability Zone 仍位于**同一 AWS Region**内，因此不满足地理隔离 DR 站点的要求。此外，该选项从未提升只读副本；RDS for MySQL 只读副本在提升前为只读状态，因此故障转移后的应用程序无法执行正常写入。

### B

不同 Region 和跨 Region 只读副本是合适的，但路由和数据库故障转移机制并不合适：

- **延迟路由**旨在根据网络延迟选择资源，而不是维护严格的主/备用 DR 关系。
- 它可能会在正常运行期间将生产流量发送到辅助应用程序。
- 该选项未提升只读副本，因此 DR 数据库仍为只读。

对于主动-被动 DR 设计，D 所使用的 Route 53 **故障转移路由**才是合适的策略。

### C

这是备份与恢复策略，而不是持续复制的备用数据库。RDS 支持跨 Region 复制快照，但复制快照然后恢复新的 DB 实例会引入额外的恢复步骤和不确定的恢复时间。请参阅 [复制 Amazon RDS 的 DB 快照](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html)。

更重要的是，恢复“最新快照”无法保证恢复点在 15 分钟以内。RDS 自动快照会在配置的备份窗口期间创建；虽然在使用自动备份和事务日志时，RDS 时间点恢复可以提供更精细的恢复点，但此选项指定的是复制和恢复最新快照，而不是跨 Region 的时间点备份复制。AWS 在 [Amazon RDS 中的弹性](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html)中区分了基于快照的恢复和异步只读副本复制。因此，C 无法可靠地满足所述的 15 分钟 RPO，且在操作上比提升预先存在的只读副本更慢。

en.question: A large enterprise is deploying a web application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for Oracle DB instance and Amazon DynamoDB. There are separate environments for development, testing, and production. What is the MOST secure and flexible way to obtain password credentials during deployment?

options.A: Retrieve an access key from an AWS Systems Manager SecureString parameter to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from a Systems Manager SecureString parameter.
options.B: Launch the EC2 instances with an EC2 IAM role to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.
options.C: Retrieve an access key from an AWS Systems Manager plaintext parameter to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from a Systems Manager SecureString parameter.
options.D: Launch the EC2 instances with an EC2 IAM role to access AWS services. Store the database passwords in an encrypted config file with the application artifacts.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The application needs two distinct kinds of credentials:

1. Credentials that allow the EC2-hosted application to call AWS services such as DynamoDB and Secrets Manager.
2. Password credentials for the RDS for Oracle database.

The most secure design should avoid long-term AWS access keys, keep database passwords outside deployment artifacts, support centralized lifecycle management and rotation, and allow separate permissions/secrets for development, testing, and production.

## Correct answer: B

**Launch the EC2 instances with an EC2 IAM role to access AWS services, and retrieve the database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.**

An IAM role attached through an EC2 instance profile supplies the application with **temporary security credentials**. AWS automatically refreshes these credentials before they expire, so the application does not need to store or manage a long-term access key. The role can be scoped with least-privilege permissions, including access to only the appropriate DynamoDB resources and environment-specific database secret. AWS documents this behavior in [How roles for Amazon EC2 instances work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html).

Secrets Manager is purpose-built for credentials such as database passwords. It lets the application replace hard-coded credentials with an API call to retrieve the secret. Amazon RDS can generate and store the master password in Secrets Manager, encrypt it with KMS, and rotate an RDS-managed secret automatically. This includes support for RDS for Oracle, as described in [Managing master user passwords with AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html).

Separate IAM roles, secret names, KMS keys, and resource policies can be used for development, testing, and production, making this both secure and flexible.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Access key in Parameter Store SecureString; database credentials in Parameter Store SecureString

Although `SecureString` encrypts the stored values, placing an AWS access key in Parameter Store still means managing a long-term credential. AWS recommends using IAM roles and temporary credentials whenever possible because temporary credentials have limited lifetimes and are generated dynamically. See [Alternatives to long-term access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds-programmatic-access.html).

Parameter Store can securely hold database passwords, but it does not provide native automatic secret rotation. AWS explicitly states that Parameter Store does not provide automatic rotation and recommends Secrets Manager when rotation is required: [Use AWS Secrets Manager secrets in Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/integrating_parameterstore.html). Therefore, A is less secure and less flexible than B.

### C. Access key in a plaintext parameter; database credentials in Parameter Store SecureString

This has both weaknesses of A and additionally stores the AWS access key in plaintext. It exposes a reusable long-term credential and is clearly inferior to an EC2 IAM role with automatically refreshed temporary credentials. Parameter Store also lacks native automatic rotation for the database password.

### D. EC2 IAM role; database passwords in an encrypted application config file

The IAM role portion is correct, but packaging database passwords with application artifacts is poor secret-management practice. Even if encrypted, the credential becomes coupled to artifact distribution, decryption-key access, environment promotion, and redeployment. It also lacks Secrets Manager's centralized retrieval and managed rotation capabilities. Secrets Manager keeps the password out of the artifact and allows runtime retrieval under least-privilege IAM authorization.

Therefore, **B** is the most secure and flexible solution.

zh.question: 一家大型企业正在 AWS 上部署一个 Web 应用程序。该应用程序运行在 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例上。这些实例在跨多个可用区的 Auto Scaling 组中运行。应用程序将数据存储在 Amazon RDS for Oracle 数据库实例和 Amazon DynamoDB 中。开发、测试和生产环境相互独立。在部署期间获取密码凭证的最安全且最灵活的方法是什么？

options.A: 从 AWS Systems Manager SecureString 参数中检索访问密钥以访问 AWS 服务。从 Systems Manager SecureString 参数中检索数据库凭证。
options.B: 使用 EC2 IAM 角色启动 EC2 实例以访问 AWS 服务。从 AWS Secrets Manager 检索数据库凭证。
options.C: 从 AWS Systems Manager 明文参数中检索访问密钥以访问 AWS 服务。从 Systems Manager SecureString 参数中检索数据库凭证。
options.D: 使用 EC2 IAM 角色启动 EC2 实例以访问 AWS 服务。将数据库密码存储在随应用程序工件提供的加密配置文件中。

zh.explanation:
## 题目在问什么

该应用程序需要两类不同的凭证：

1. 允许托管在 EC2 上的应用程序调用 DynamoDB 和 Secrets Manager 等 AWS 服务的凭证。
2. RDS for Oracle 数据库的密码凭证。

最安全的设计应避免使用长期 AWS 访问密钥，将数据库密码置于部署工件之外，支持集中式生命周期管理和轮换，并允许为开发、测试和生产环境配置独立的权限和机密。

## 正确答案：B

**使用 EC2 IAM 角色启动 EC2 实例以访问 AWS 服务，并从 AWS Secrets Manager 检索数据库凭证。**

通过 EC2 实例配置文件附加的 IAM 角色会向应用程序提供**临时安全凭证**。AWS 会在这些凭证过期前自动刷新它们，因此应用程序无需存储或管理长期访问密钥。该角色可通过最小权限原则限定权限，包括仅访问相应的 DynamoDB 资源和特定环境的数据库机密。AWS 在 [How roles for Amazon EC2 instances work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html) 中说明了此行为。

Secrets Manager 专为数据库密码等凭证而设计。它允许应用程序通过 API 调用检索机密，从而替代硬编码凭证。Amazon RDS 可以在 Secrets Manager 中生成并存储主密码，使用 KMS 对其加密，并自动轮换由 RDS 管理的机密。这包括对 RDS for Oracle 的支持，如 [Managing master user passwords with AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) 所述。

可以为开发、测试和生产环境使用独立的 IAM 角色、机密名称、KMS 密钥和资源策略，因此该方案既安全又灵活。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. Parameter Store SecureString 中的访问密钥；Parameter Store SecureString 中的数据库凭证

尽管 `SecureString` 会加密存储的值，但在 Parameter Store 中放置 AWS 访问密钥仍意味着需要管理长期凭证。AWS 建议尽可能使用 IAM 角色和临时凭证，因为临时凭证的有效期有限且会动态生成。请参阅 [Alternatives to long-term access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds-programmatic-access.html)。

Parameter Store 可以安全地保存数据库密码，但它不提供原生的自动机密轮换。AWS 明确指出 Parameter Store 不提供自动轮换，并建议在需要轮换时使用 Secrets Manager：[Use AWS Secrets Manager secrets in Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/integrating_parameterstore.html)。因此，A 不如 B 安全和灵活。

### C. 明文参数中的访问密钥；Parameter Store SecureString 中的数据库凭证

此选项同时具有 A 的两项弱点，此外还以明文形式存储 AWS 访问密钥。它暴露了可重复使用的长期凭证，显然不如使用可自动刷新的临时凭证的 EC2 IAM 角色。Parameter Store 同样缺乏数据库密码的原生自动轮换功能。

### D. EC2 IAM 角色；加密应用程序配置文件中的数据库密码

IAM 角色部分是正确的，但将数据库密码与应用程序工件一起打包是不良的机密管理做法。即使经过加密，该凭证也会与工件分发、解密密钥访问、环境提升和重新部署产生耦合。它也不具备 Secrets Manager 的集中检索和托管轮换功能。Secrets Manager 会将密码置于工件之外，并允许在最小权限 IAM 授权下于运行时检索。

因此，**B** 是最安全且最灵活的解决方案。

en.question: The security team depends on AWS CloudTrail to detect sensitive security issues in the company’s AWS account. The DevOps engineer needs a solution to auto-remediate CloudTrail being turned off in an AWS account. What solution ensures the LEAST amount of downtime for the CloudTrail log deliveries?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the CloudTrail StopLogging event. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.
options.B: Deploy the AWS-managed CloudTrail-enabled AWS Config rule, set with a periodic interval of 1 hour. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for AWS Config rules compliance change. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on the ARN of the resource in which StopLogging was called. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for a scheduled event every 5 minutes. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to call StartLogging on a CloudTrail trail in the AWS account. Add the Lambda function ARN as a target to the EventBridge rule.
options.D: Launch a t2.nano instance with a script running every 5 minutes that uses the AWS SDK to query CloudTrail in the current account. If the CloudTrail trail is disabled, have the script re-enable the trail.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The requirement is not merely to detect that a CloudTrail trail has stopped logging; it is to **automatically restart logging with the least possible interruption to log delivery**. Therefore, an event-driven response to the `StopLogging` API call is preferable to periodic polling or periodic compliance evaluation.

## Correct answer: A

**A. Create an EventBridge rule for the CloudTrail `StopLogging` event and invoke a Lambda function that calls `StartLogging` for the affected trail.**

`StopLogging` is a write management API operation. AWS documents that CloudTrail sends events representing public AWS API requests to the default EventBridge event bus as `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` events, and that EventBridge rules in the normal enabled state can match write management events. This allows the remediation Lambda function to be invoked shortly after the stop operation instead of waiting for a polling interval. See [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html) and the [EventBridge API-call rule tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-api-call.html).

The Lambda function can then call CloudTrail `StartLogging`, which starts recording API calls and log-file delivery. The `Name` parameter can be either the trail name or its CloudTrail ARN, so using the affected trail ARN is valid. See the [`StartLogging` API reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_StartLogging.html).

Because this design reacts directly to the API event, it minimizes the period between `StopLogging` and `StartLogging` and therefore provides the least downtime among the choices.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Periodic AWS Config evaluation every hour

The `cloudtrail-enabled` managed rule does detect whether a trail is enabled, but AWS documents that its trigger type is **Periodic**. With the proposed one-hour interval, the trail could remain noncompliant and logging could remain stopped until the next evaluation and subsequent compliance-change event. See [`cloudtrail-enabled`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudtrail-enabled.html).

This can provide remediation, but it does not provide the least downtime compared with directly reacting to `StopLogging`.

### C. Scheduled EventBridge invocation every 5 minutes

A five-minute schedule is polling-based rather than event-driven. Depending on when logging is stopped, remediation can be delayed by almost five minutes. It is therefore slower than matching the actual `StopLogging` event. The option also says only to call `StartLogging` on a trail, without clearly identifying the affected trail or first checking its status.

### D. EC2 instance running a script every 5 minutes

This has the same possible five-minute detection delay as option C, so it cannot provide the least downtime. It also introduces an unnecessary continuously running EC2 instance, operating-system maintenance, script supervision, and a potential single point of failure when EventBridge and Lambda provide a managed event-driven solution.

## Conclusion

**Answer A** is the best solution because it detects the mutating `StopLogging` API call through EventBridge and immediately invokes Lambda to call `StartLogging` on the affected trail.

zh.question: 安全团队依赖 AWS CloudTrail 来检测公司 AWS 账户中的敏感安全问题。DevOps 工程师需要一种解决方案，以自动修复 AWS 账户中 CloudTrail 被关闭的情况。哪种解决方案可确保 CloudTrail 日志交付的停机时间最短？

options.A: 为 CloudTrail StopLogging 事件创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，该函数使用 AWS SDK 对调用 StopLogging 的资源 ARN 调用 StartLogging。将 Lambda 函数 ARN 作为目标添加到 EventBridge 规则中。
options.B: 部署 AWS 托管的 CloudTrail-enabled AWS Config 规则，并将其设置为 1 小时的定期执行间隔。为 AWS Config 规则合规性变更创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，该函数使用 AWS SDK 对调用 StopLogging 的资源 ARN 调用 StartLogging。将 Lambda 函数 ARN 作为目标添加到 EventBridge 规则中。
options.C: 为每 5 分钟执行一次的计划事件创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，该函数使用 AWS SDK 对 AWS 账户中的 CloudTrail trail 调用 StartLogging。将 Lambda 函数 ARN 作为目标添加到 EventBridge 规则中。
options.D: 启动一个 t2.nano 实例，并运行一个每 5 分钟使用 AWS SDK 查询当前账户中 CloudTrail 的脚本。如果 CloudTrail trail 已被禁用，则让脚本重新启用该 trail。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查内容

要求不仅仅是检测某个 CloudTrail trail 是否已停止日志记录；而是要**以对日志交付造成尽可能少的中断，自动重新启动日志记录**。因此，对 `StopLogging` API 调用作出事件驱动响应，比定期轮询或定期合规性评估更合适。

## 正确答案：A

**A. 为 CloudTrail `StopLogging` 事件创建 EventBridge 规则，并调用一个 Lambda 函数，该函数会对受影响的 trail 调用 `StartLogging`。**

`StopLogging` 是一个写入管理 API 操作。AWS 文档说明，CloudTrail 会将表示公开 AWS API 请求的事件作为 `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` 事件发送到默认 EventBridge 事件总线，并且处于正常启用状态的 EventBridge 规则可以匹配写入管理事件。这样可以在停止操作后不久调用修复 Lambda 函数，而无需等待轮询间隔。请参阅 [通过 AWS CloudTrail 传送的 AWS 服务事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html) 和 [EventBridge API 调用规则教程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-api-call.html)。

随后，Lambda 函数可以调用 CloudTrail `StartLogging`，这会开始记录 API 调用和日志文件交付。`Name` 参数可以是 trail 名称或其 CloudTrail ARN，因此使用受影响 trail 的 ARN 是有效的。请参阅 [`StartLogging` API 参考](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_StartLogging.html)。

由于此设计直接响应 API 事件，它可将 `StopLogging` 和 `StartLogging` 之间的时间降至最低，因此在所有选项中提供最短的停机时间。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B. 每小时进行一次定期 AWS Config 评估

托管的 `cloudtrail-enabled` 规则确实可以检测 trail 是否已启用，但 AWS 文档说明其触发器类型为**定期**。按照建议的每小时执行间隔，trail 可能会一直处于不合规状态且日志记录保持停止，直到下一次评估及后续的合规性变更事件发生。请参阅 [`cloudtrail-enabled`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudtrail-enabled.html)。

这可以提供修复，但与直接响应 `StopLogging` 相比，它无法提供最短停机时间。

### C. 每 5 分钟计划调用一次 EventBridge

每 5 分钟执行一次的计划是基于轮询的，而不是事件驱动的。根据日志记录被停止的时间，修复最多可能延迟近 5 分钟。因此，它比匹配实际的 `StopLogging` 事件更慢。该选项还仅说明对一个 trail 调用 `StartLogging`，没有明确识别受影响的 trail，也没有先检查其状态。

### D. 运行每 5 分钟执行一次脚本的 EC2 实例

此选项与 C 具有同样最长达 5 分钟的检测延迟，因此无法提供最短停机时间。它还引入了一个不必要的持续运行 EC2 实例、操作系统维护、脚本监控，以及潜在的单点故障；而 EventBridge 和 Lambda 可提供托管的事件驱动解决方案。

## 结论

**答案 A** 是最佳解决方案，因为它通过 EventBridge 检测会更改状态的 `StopLogging` API 调用，并立即调用 Lambda，对受影响的 trail 调用 `StartLogging`。

options.A: Create an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. Update the route tables for the subnets that are running the CodeBuild job.
options.B: Update the repository policy’s Principal statement to include the ARN of the role that the CodeBuild project uses.
options.C: Share the CodeArtifact repository with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
options.D: Update the role that the CodeBuild project uses so that the role has sufficient permissions to use the CodeArtifact repository.
options.E: Specify the account that hosts the repository as the delegated administrator for CodeArtifact in the organization.

en.explanation:
## Correct answers: A and D

### Scenario

A company centrally stores Python packages in an AWS CodeArtifact repository whose resource policy allows read actions for any principal (`"Principal": "*"`) that satisfies the `aws:PrincipalOrgID` condition for the organization. A development team in a member account of that same organization builds an application with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild. The CodeBuild project runs inside a VPC that, for compliance reasons, has **no internet connectivity**. The team has already created the CodeArtifact VPC endpoints and updated `buildspec.yaml`, yet the package download still fails.

Two things are therefore still missing: (1) complete private network reachability for the package download path, and (2) identity-based IAM permissions on the CodeBuild service role that let it authenticate to CodeArtifact and read from the repository.

---

## Why A is correct

**A. Create an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint and update the route tables for the subnets running the CodeBuild job.**

CodeArtifact uses Amazon S3 to store package assets. The CodeArtifact interface endpoints (`com.amazonaws.region.codeartifact.api` and `com.amazonaws.region.codeartifact.repositories`) let the build reach the CodeArtifact control plane and repository endpoint to obtain an auth token and package **metadata**, but downloading the package **assets** requires reachability to Amazon S3. In a VPC with no internet gateway and no NAT, that traffic can only flow through an Amazon S3 **gateway** endpoint.
