The company needs a fully managed pipeline that continuously exports **CloudWatch performance and custom metrics**, automatically includes future metrics, transforms each batch, and stores the transformed data in Amazon S3.

**Option B** provides the required pipeline:

**CloudWatch metric stream (All metrics) → Amazon Data Firehose → AWS Lambda transformation → Amazon S3**

CloudWatch metric streams are designed to continuously export CloudWatch metric updates. When a stream is configured for **All metrics**, all metrics in the account are included, so newly published application and custom metrics are captured without maintaining namespace or metric-selection filters. AWS also states that new metrics matching a metric stream's configuration are automatically added to the stream. See [Use metric streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Metric-Streams.html).

The metric stream sends its records to Amazon Data Firehose, which can deliver them to an S3 bucket. Firehose can invoke a Lambda function synchronously for each buffered batch and then send the transformed records to the configured destination. This satisfies the requirement to transform the metric data before storage while using managed services and requiring minimal ongoing administration. See [Set up a metric stream using Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-metric-streams-setup-datalake.html) and [Transform source data in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

This option uses the correct service chain, but it describes selectively including application metrics and a CloudWatch namespace rather than selecting **All metrics**. When individual metrics are selected within a namespace, only those selected metrics are included. Future metrics are automatically included only when they match the stream's existing filters. Consequently, adding metrics outside the selected metric or namespace scope can require filter changes. Selecting **All metrics** avoids that maintenance and more reliably fulfills the requirement to collect any new metrics with the least operational overhead. See [CloudWatch metric-stream configuration and filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-metric-streams-setup-datalake.html).

### C

CloudWatch Logs metric filters inspect **log events** and create metrics from values found in matching events. They do not export the applications' existing CloudWatch performance and custom metrics, and new log-derived measurements would require suitable filter patterns to be configured. This option also does not provide the required Lambda transformation step and incorrectly describes direct delivery from a custom metric stream to S3 instead of the supported Firehose delivery path. See [Create metrics from log events using metric filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html).

### D

CloudWatch Logs subscription filters forward matching **log events** to destinations such as Firehose; they do not stream CloudWatch metric data. Although Firehose and Lambda could transform and store those logs, the resulting pipeline would process application logs rather than the required performance and custom metrics. See [CloudWatch Logs subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html).

Therefore, **B** is the best solution because it automatically exports all current and future CloudWatch metrics through a managed Firehose transformation and S3 delivery pipeline without requiring ongoing filter maintenance.

zh.question: 一家公司在同一个 AWS 账户中运行多个应用程序。这些应用程序将日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch。一个数据分析团队需要从这些应用程序中收集性能指标和自定义指标。分析团队需要先转换指标数据，然后再将数据存储到 Amazon S3 存储桶中。分析团队必须自动收集添加到 CloudWatch 命名空间中的任何新指标。哪种解决方案能以最低的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置一个 CloudWatch 指标流，以包含来自应用程序和 CloudWatch 命名空间的指标。配置该指标流以将指标传送到 Amazon Data Firehose 传输流。配置 Firehose 传输流以调用 AWS Lambda 函数来转换数据。配置该传输流以将转换后的数据发送到 S3 存储桶。
options.B: 配置一个 CloudWatch 指标流，以包含所有指标并将指标传送到 Amazon Data Firehose 传输流。配置 Firehose 传输流以调用 AWS Lambda 函数来转换数据。配置该传输流以将转换后的数据发送到 S3 存储桶。
options.C: 为 CloudWatch 日志配置指标筛选器以创建自定义指标。配置一个 CloudWatch 指标流，将应用程序指标传送到 S3 存储桶。
options.D: 在应用程序日志组上配置订阅筛选器，以 Amazon Data Firehose 传输流为目标。配置 Firehose 传输流以调用 AWS Lambda 函数来转换数据。配置该传输流以将转换后的数据发送到 S3 存储桶。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：B

该公司需要一个完全托管的管道，该管道可持续导出 **CloudWatch 性能指标和自定义指标**、自动包含未来的指标、转换每个批次，并将转换后的数据存储在 Amazon S3 中。

**选项 B** 提供了所需的管道：

**CloudWatch 指标流（所有指标）→ Amazon Data Firehose → AWS Lambda 转换 → Amazon S3**

CloudWatch 指标流专为持续导出 CloudWatch 指标更新而设计。当流配置为 **所有指标** 时，账户中的所有指标都会被包含，因此无需维护命名空间或指标选择筛选器，即可捕获新发布的应用程序指标和自定义指标。AWS 还说明，符合指标流配置的新指标会自动添加到该流中。请参阅 [使用指标流](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Metric-Streams.html)。

指标流将其记录发送到 Amazon Data Firehose，后者可以将这些记录传送到 S3 存储桶。Firehose 可以针对每个缓冲批次同步调用 Lambda 函数，然后将转换后的记录发送到已配置的目标位置。这在使用托管服务且只需极少持续管理的同时，满足了在存储前转换指标数据的要求。请参阅 [使用 Amazon Data Firehose 设置指标流](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-metric-streams-setup-datalake.html) 和 [在 Amazon Data Firehose 中转换源数据](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html)。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A

此选项使用了正确的服务链，但它描述的是选择性地包含应用程序指标和某个 CloudWatch 命名空间，而不是选择 **所有指标**。当在某个命名空间内选择单独的指标时，只有这些选定的指标会被包含。只有未来指标符合该流现有筛选器时，才会自动包含这些指标。因此，在所选指标或命名空间范围之外添加指标时，可能需要更改筛选器。选择 **所有指标** 可以避免这种维护，并且更可靠地满足以最低运营开销收集任何新指标的要求。请参阅 [CloudWatch 指标流配置和筛选](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-metric-streams-setup-datalake.html)。

### C

CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器会检查 **日志事件**，并根据匹配事件中发现的值创建指标。它们不会导出应用程序现有的 CloudWatch 性能指标和自定义指标，并且新的源自日志的测量值需要配置适当的筛选器模式。此选项也未提供所需的 Lambda 转换步骤，并且错误地描述了从自定义指标流直接传送到 S3，而非使用受支持的 Firehose 传送路径。请参阅 [使用指标筛选器从日志事件创建指标](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html)。

### D

CloudWatch Logs 订阅筛选器会将匹配的 **日志事件** 转发到 Firehose 等目标位置；它们不会流式传输 CloudWatch 指标数据。尽管 Firehose 和 Lambda 可以转换并存储这些日志，但生成的管道处理的是应用程序日志，而不是所需的性能指标和自定义指标。请参阅 [CloudWatch Logs 订阅筛选器](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html)。

因此，**B** 是最佳解决方案，因为它通过托管的 Firehose 转换和 S3 传送管道，自动导出所有当前及未来的 CloudWatch 指标，无需持续维护筛选器。

en.question: A company uses an HPC platform to run analysis jobs for data. The company uses AWS CodeBuild to create container images and store the images on Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The images are then deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). To maintain compliance, the company needs to ensure that the images are signed before the images are deployed on Amazon EKS. The signing keys must be rotated periodically and must be managed automatically. The company needs to track who generates the signatures. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Use CodeBuild to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use AWS Signer to sign the image. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.
options.B: Use AWS Lambda to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use a Lambda function to sign the image. Use Amazon CloudWatch to track who generates the signatures.
options.C: Use AWS Lambda to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use AWS Signer to sign the image. Use Amazon CloudWatch to track who generates the signatures.
options.D: Use CodeBuild to build the image. Sign the image by using AWS Signer before pushing the image to Amazon ECR. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: D

**D — Use CodeBuild to build the image. Sign the image by using AWS Signer before pushing the image to Amazon ECR. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.**

### Scenario

An HPC company already builds container images with AWS CodeBuild, stores them in Amazon ECR, and deploys them to Amazon EKS. For compliance, every image must be signed before it is deployed on EKS, the signing keys must be rotated periodically and managed automatically (i.e., not managed by the company), and the company must be able to determine which identity produced each signature. The solution must add the least operational effort to the existing pipeline.

Three requirements drive the choice:

1. **Managed signing with automatic key lifecycle** → AWS Signer.
2. **Attribution of who signed** → AWS CloudTrail.
3. **Least operational effort** → keep the work inside the CodeBuild stage that already exists; do not introduce new compute or custom code.

### Why D is correct

**Signing in the CodeBuild stage is the documented, lowest-effort pattern.** Amazon ECR describes the manual (Notation CLI + AWS Signer plugin) workflow exactly this way: "Manual signing uses the Notation CLI and AWS Signer plugin to sign images before pushing them to Amazon ECR." This is precisely the sequence in option D — CodeBuild builds the image, the AWS Signer plugin signs it as part of the same build, and the signed image (with its signature artifact) lands in the ECR private repository. Because the signing step is inserted into the build job that already runs, no additional service, no extra pipeline stage, and no re-fetch of the image is required. See [Signing images manually in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-signing-manual.html) and the overview of ECR signing methods in [Signing container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-signing.html). The mechanics of the `notation sign` operation, including how the signature is produced and stored alongside the image in the repository, are covered in [Sign a container image](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/image-signing-steps.html).

**AWS Signer satisfies the "keys must be managed automatically and rotated" requirement.** AWS Signer is a fully managed code-signing service: a signing profile encapsulates the code-signing certificate and its public and private keys, and AWS manages that signing material and its lifecycle on the customer's behalf. The company never provisions, stores, or rotates signing keys itself. See [Signing profiles in AWS Signer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/signing-profiles.html) and [What is AWS Signer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/Welcome.html).

**AWS CloudTrail satisfies the "track who generates the signatures" requirement.** CloudTrail records AWS API activity, including the identity of the principal (IAM user or assumed role) that made each request, the time of the call, and the source IP. Signing calls made from the CodeBuild service role are therefore attributable to a specific identity. See [Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/cloudtrail-integration.html).

**The compliance goal is met.** The requirement is that images are signed before they are deployed on Amazon EKS. Signing as part of the build, so that only signed images ever reach the registry, satisfies that requirement and is the stricter, best-practice posture: an unsigned artifact never becomes deployable from ECR. Prerequisites and configuration for the container image signing workflow are documented in [Prerequisites for signing container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/image-signing-prerequisites.html).

### Why the other options are incorrect

- **A — CodeBuild retrieves the previously pushed image, AWS Signer signs it, CloudTrail tracks signers.** This option uses the right services (Signer for managed keys, CloudTrail for attribution), but it adds an unnecessary step: an extra round trip in which CodeBuild goes back to Amazon ECR to retrieve an image that the same pipeline just built and pushed. That is strictly more pipeline work than signing inline during the existing build stage, so it does not meet the "LEAST operational effort" bar. It also creates a window in which unsigned images exist in the registry, requiring extra controls to prevent an unsigned image from being deployed.

- **B — Lambda retrieves the image, a Lambda function signs it, CloudWatch tracks signers.** This is the worst option on both requirements. Hand-rolling signing logic in a Lambda function means the company must implement the signing code and own the entire signing-key lifecycle, including generation, storage, and rotation — the opposite of "managed automatically." It also introduces a new compute service when CodeBuild is already present. Finally, Amazon CloudWatch provides metrics, logs, and alarms for operational monitoring; it is not the service that records which AWS principal invoked an API operation. That is CloudTrail's role, as described in [Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/cloudtrail-integration.html).

- **C — Lambda retrieves the image, AWS Signer signs it, CloudWatch tracks signers.** Using AWS Signer is correct, but this option fails on two counts. First, adding AWS Lambda as a separate retrieval/orchestration path is unnecessary operational overhead when the CodeBuild build already exists and can invoke the Signer plugin directly. Second, and decisively, CloudWatch does not provide the authoritative identity audit trail for API calls; CloudTrail is the required service for determining who generated each signature.

### Summary

Option D keeps everything inside managed AWS services and inside the pipeline stage that already exists: CodeBuild builds the image, the AWS Signer plugin signs it before the push to Amazon ECR (AWS owns the certificate and key lifecycle), and CloudTrail supplies the identity-level audit trail of signing activity. That combination meets the compliance, key-management, and attribution requirements with the least operational effort.

zh.question: 某公司使用 HPC 平台运行数据分析作业。该公司使用 AWS CodeBuild 创建容器镜像，并将镜像存储在 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 中。随后这些镜像被部署到 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上。为保持合规性，公司需要确保镜像在部署到 Amazon EKS 之前已完成签名。签名密钥必须定期轮换，并且必须自动管理。公司需要跟踪是谁生成了签名。哪种解决方案能以最少的运维工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 CodeBuild 检索先前推送到 Amazon ECR 的镜像。使用 AWS Signer 对镜像签名。使用 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪是谁生成了签名。
options.B: 使用 AWS Lambda 检索先前推送到 Amazon ECR 的镜像。使用 Lambda 函数对镜像签名。使用 Amazon CloudWatch 跟踪是谁生成了签名。
options.C: 使用 AWS Lambda 检索先前推送到 Amazon ECR 的镜像。使用 AWS Signer 对镜像签名。使用 Amazon CloudWatch 跟踪是谁生成了签名。
options.D: 使用 CodeBuild 构建镜像。在将镜像推送到 Amazon ECR 之前，使用 AWS Signer 对镜像签名。使用 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪是谁生成了签名。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：D

**D — 使用 CodeBuild 构建镜像。在将镜像推送到 Amazon ECR 之前，使用 AWS Signer 对镜像签名。使用 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪是谁生成了签名。**

### 场景

一家 HPC 公司已经使用 AWS CodeBuild 构建容器镜像，将其存储在 Amazon ECR 中，并部署到 Amazon EKS。出于合规要求，每个镜像在部署到 EKS 之前都必须完成签名，签名密钥必须定期轮换并自动管理（即不由公司自行管理），并且公司必须能够确定是哪个身份生成了每个签名。该解决方案必须为现有管道增加最少的运维工作量。

有三项要求决定了选择：

1. **具备自动密钥生命周期管理的托管签名** → AWS Signer。
2. **签名者归属识别** → AWS CloudTrail。
3. **最少的运维工作量** → 将工作保留在已有的 CodeBuild 阶段内；不引入新的计算资源或自定义代码。

### 为什么 D 正确

**在 CodeBuild 阶段签名是有文档记载的、开销最低的模式。** Amazon ECR 对手动签名（Notation CLI + AWS Signer 插件）工作流的描述正是如此："手动签名使用 Notation CLI 和 AWS Signer 插件在将镜像推送到 Amazon ECR 之前对其签名。" 这恰好就是选项 D 中的顺序——CodeBuild 构建镜像，AWS Signer 插件在同一次构建中对其签名，已签名的镜像（连同其签名工件）进入 ECR 私有存储库。由于签名步骤被插入到已经运行的构建作业中，因此不需要额外的服务、额外的管道阶段，也不需要重新拉取镜像。参见 [Signing images manually in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-signing-manual.html) 以及 [Signing container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-signing.html) 中对 ECR 签名方法的概述。关于 `notation sign` 操作的机制，包括签名如何生成并与镜像一起存储在存储库中，可参见 [Sign a container image](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/image-signing-steps.html)。

**AWS Signer 满足"密钥必须自动管理并轮换"的要求。** AWS Signer 是一项完全托管的代码签名服务：签名配置文件封装了代码签名证书及其公钥和私钥，AWS 代表客户管理这些签名材料及其生命周期。公司无需自行预置、存储或轮换签名密钥。参见 [Signing profiles in AWS Signer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/signing-profiles.html) 和 [What is AWS Signer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/Welcome.html)。

**AWS CloudTrail 满足"跟踪是谁生成了签名"的要求。** CloudTrail 记录 AWS API 活动，包括发出每个请求的主体身份（IAM 用户或已担任的角色）、调用时间和源 IP。因此，从 CodeBuild 服务角色发出的签名调用可以归属到具体的身份。参见 [Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/cloudtrail-integration.html)。

**合规目标得以满足。** 要求是镜像在部署到 Amazon EKS 之前已完成签名。作为构建的一部分进行签名，使得只有已签名的镜像才会进入注册表，这既满足该要求，也是更严格的最佳实践姿态：未签名的工件永远不会从 ECR 变得可部署。容器镜像签名工作流的先决条件和配置记录在 [Prerequisites for signing container images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signer/latest/developerguide/image-signing-prerequisites.html) 中。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

- **A — CodeBuild 检索先前推送的镜像，AWS Signer 对其签名，CloudTrail 跟踪签名者。** 该选项使用了正确的服务（Signer 提供托管密钥，CloudTrail 提供归属识别），但它增加了不必要的步骤：额外的一次往返，让 CodeBuild 回到 Amazon ECR 去检索同一管道刚刚构建并推送的镜像。这严格来说比在现有构建阶段内联签名需要更多的管道工作，因此不符合"最少运维工作量"的标准。它还会造成一个时间窗口，期间注册表中存在未签名的镜像，需要额外的控制措施来防止未签名镜像被部署。

- **B — Lambda 检索镜像，Lambda 函数对其签名，CloudWatch 跟踪签名者。** 这在两项要求上都是最差的选项。在 Lambda 函数中自行编写签名逻辑意味着公司必须实现签名代码并承担整个签名密钥生命周期，包括生成、存储和轮换——这与"自动管理"背道而驰。它还在 CodeBuild 已经存在的情况下引入了新的计算服务。最后，Amazon CloudWatch 提供用于运维监控的指标、日志和告警；它并不是记录哪个 AWS 主体调用了 API 操作的服务。那是 CloudTrail 的职责，如 [Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/cloudtrail-integration.html) 中所述。

- **C — Lambda 检索镜像，AWS Signer 对其签名，CloudWatch 跟踪签名者。** 使用 AWS Signer 是正确的，但该选项在两点上不成立。首先，在 CodeBuild 构建已经存在且可以直接调用 Signer 插件的情况下，添加 AWS Lambda 作为独立的检索/编排路径是不必要的运维开销。其次，也是决定性的一点，CloudWatch 并不提供 API 调用的权威身份审计跟踪；确定谁生成了每个签名所需的服务是 CloudTrail。

### 小结

选项 D 将所有工作都保留在托管的 AWS 服务和已经存在的管道阶段内：CodeBuild 构建镜像，AWS Signer 插件在推送到 Amazon ECR 之前对其签名（AWS 负责证书和密钥生命周期），CloudTrail 提供签名活动的身份级审计跟踪。这一组合以最少的运维工作量满足了合规、密钥管理和归属识别的要求。

en.question: A company uses an AWS CodeArtifact repository to store Python packages that the company developed internally. A DevOps engineer needs to use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to an Amazon EC2 instance. The application uses a Python package that is stored in the CodeArtifact repository. A BeforeInstall lifecycle event hook will install the package. The DevOps engineer needs to grant the EC2 instance access to the CodeArtifact repository. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Create a service-linked role for CodeArtifact. Associate the role with the EC2 instance. Use the aws codeartifact get-authorization-token CLI command on the instance.
options.B: Configure a resource-based policy for the CodeArtifact repository that allows the ReadFromRepository action for the EC2 instance principal.
options.C: Configure ACLs on the CodeArtifact repository to allow the EC2 instance to access the Python package.
options.D: Create an instance profile that contains an IAM role that has access to CodeArtifact. Associate the instance profile with the EC2 instance. Use the aws codeartifact login CLI command on the instance.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The `BeforeInstall` hook runs **on the EC2 instance** and must use `pip` to retrieve a private Python package from CodeArtifact. Therefore, the process running on the instance needs an AWS identity with the required CodeArtifact permissions, and `pip` must be configured with a CodeArtifact endpoint and authorization token.

## Correct answer: D

Create an **EC2 instance profile containing an IAM role**, grant that role access to CodeArtifact, associate the instance profile with the EC2 instance, and run `aws codeartifact login --tool pip ...` in the hook.

An EC2 application obtains the temporary credentials of its attached IAM role through instance metadata. When using the CLI/API to configure the role, AWS specifies that the role is placed in an instance profile and the instance profile is associated with the EC2 instance. These credentials are automatically rotated ([IAM roles for applications on EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)).

The `aws codeartifact login` command obtains an authorization token and configures the selected package manager with both that token and the correct repository endpoint. `pip` is a supported `--tool` value ([CodeArtifact authorization tokens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/tokens-authentication.html)). The role should include the permissions needed to download packages, including:

- `codeartifact:GetAuthorizationToken`
- `codeartifact:GetRepositoryEndpoint`
- `codeartifact:ReadFromRepository`
- `sts:GetServiceBearerToken`

AWS documents this permission pattern and the use of `aws codeartifact login --tool pip` for Python package retrieval ([Using Python packages with IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/using-python-packages-in-codebuild.html)). Although that example uses CodeBuild, the same CodeArtifact authentication and package-manager requirements apply to the EC2 role used here.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Service-linked role for CodeArtifact

CodeArtifact **does not support service-linked roles**, so such a role cannot be created and associated with the instance. Additionally, merely calling `get-authorization-token` does not configure `pip` with the repository endpoint and token as `login` does ([How CodeArtifact works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)).

### B. Repository resource policy for the EC2 instance principal

CodeArtifact does support repository resource policies, but an **EC2 instance is not an IAM principal** that can be named in the policy. Supported principals include AWS accounts, IAM users, IAM roles, federated users, and AWS services. The relevant principal for workload access would be the EC2 instance's IAM role, not the instance itself ([How CodeArtifact works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)).

Also, granting only `codeartifact:ReadFromRepository` is not sufficient for the package manager workflow. The workload still needs authorization-token and repository-endpoint permissions, and `sts:GetServiceBearerToken`; AWS notes that `sts:GetServiceBearerToken` must be granted by the IAM user or role and has no effect in a CodeArtifact domain resource policy ([CodeArtifact authorization tokens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/tokens-authentication.html)). Repository policies are valid generally, including for granting read access to IAM principals, but this option specifies the wrong principal and incomplete permissions ([CodeArtifact repository policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/repo-policies.html)).

### C. Repository ACLs

CodeArtifact **does not support ACLs**. Access is managed through IAM identity-based policies and supported CodeArtifact resource-based policies ([How CodeArtifact works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS CodeArtifact 存储公司内部开发的 Python 包。一名 DevOps 工程师需要使用 AWS CodeDeploy 将应用程序部署到 Amazon EC2 实例。该应用程序使用存储在 CodeArtifact 存储库中的 Python 包。一个 BeforeInstall 生命周期事件挂钩将安装该包。DevOps 工程师需要授予 EC2 实例访问 CodeArtifact 存储库的权限。哪种解决方案能够满足此要求？

options.A: 为 CodeArtifact 创建服务相关角色。将该角色关联到 EC2 实例。在该实例上使用 aws codeartifact get-authorization-token CLI 命令。
options.B: 为 CodeArtifact 存储库配置基于资源的策略，允许 EC2 实例主体执行 ReadFromRepository 操作。
options.C: 在 CodeArtifact 存储库上配置 ACL，以允许 EC2 实例访问 Python 包。
options.D: 创建一个包含具有 CodeArtifact 访问权限的 IAM 角色的实例配置文件。将该实例配置文件关联到 EC2 实例。在该实例上使用 aws codeartifact login CLI 命令。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

`BeforeInstall` 挂钩在 **EC2 实例上**运行，并且必须使用 `pip` 从 CodeArtifact 获取私有 Python 包。因此，在实例上运行的进程需要一个具有所需 CodeArtifact 权限的 AWS 身份，并且必须使用 CodeArtifact 端点和授权令牌配置 `pip`。

## 正确答案：D

创建一个**包含 IAM 角色的 EC2 实例配置文件**，授予该角色访问 CodeArtifact 的权限，将实例配置文件关联到 EC2 实例，并在挂钩中运行 `aws codeartifact login --tool pip ...`。

EC2 应用程序通过实例元数据获取其所附加 IAM 角色的临时凭证。使用 CLI/API 配置该角色时，AWS 规定应将该角色放入实例配置文件中，并将实例配置文件关联到 EC2 实例。这些凭证会自动轮换（[EC2 上应用程序的 IAM 角色](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html)）。

`aws codeartifact login` 命令会获取授权令牌，并使用该令牌及正确的存储库端点配置选定的包管理器。`pip` 是受支持的 `--tool` 值（[CodeArtifact 授权令牌](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/tokens-authentication.html)）。该角色应包含下载包所需的权限，包括：

- `codeartifact:GetAuthorizationToken`
- `codeartifact:GetRepositoryEndpoint`
- `codeartifact:ReadFromRepository`
- `sts:GetServiceBearerToken`

AWS 记录了此权限模式以及使用 `aws codeartifact login --tool pip` 获取 Python 包的方法（[将 Python 包与 IAM 角色结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/using-python-packages-in-codebuild.html)）。尽管该示例使用 CodeBuild，但相同的 CodeArtifact 身份验证和包管理器要求同样适用于此处使用的 EC2 角色。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. CodeArtifact 的服务相关角色

CodeArtifact **不支持服务相关角色**，因此无法创建此类角色并将其关联到实例。此外，仅调用 `get-authorization-token` 不会像 `login` 那样使用存储库端点和令牌配置 `pip`（[CodeArtifact 如何与 IAM 协同工作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)）。

### B. 针对 EC2 实例主体的存储库资源策略

CodeArtifact 支持存储库基于资源的策略，但 **EC2 实例不是**可以在策略中指定的 IAM 主体。支持的主体包括 AWS 账户、IAM 用户、IAM 角色、联合用户和 AWS 服务。工作负载访问的相关主体应是 EC2 实例的 IAM 角色，而不是实例本身（[CodeArtifact 如何与 IAM 协同工作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)）。

此外，仅授予 `codeartifact:ReadFromRepository` 不足以支持包管理器工作流程。该工作负载仍需要授权令牌和存储库端点权限，以及 `sts:GetServiceBearerToken`；AWS 指出，必须由 IAM 用户或角色授予 `sts:GetServiceBearerToken`，并且该权限在 CodeArtifact 域资源策略中无效（[CodeArtifact 授权令牌](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/tokens-authentication.html)）。存储库策略通常是有效的，包括用于向 IAM 主体授予读取访问权限，但此选项指定了错误的主体且权限不完整（[CodeArtifact 存储库策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/repo-policies.html)）。

### C. 存储库 ACL

CodeArtifact **不支持 ACL**。访问通过 IAM 基于身份的策略和受支持的 CodeArtifact 基于资源的策略进行管理（[CodeArtifact 如何与 IAM 协同工作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)）。

en.question: A company has a file-reading application that saves files to a database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Regulations require the company to delete files from EC2 instances every day at a specific time. The company must delete database records that are older than 60 days. The database record deletion must occur after the file deletions. The company has created scripts to delete files and database records. The company needs to receive an email notification for any failure of the deletion scripts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to automatically invoke a Systems Manager Automation document at the specified time each day. Configure the Automation document to use a run command to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send failure notifications to the company.
options.B: Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to automatically invoke a Systems Manager Automation document at the specified time each day. Configure the Automation document to use a run command to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Create a conditional statement inside the Automation document as the last step to check for errors. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send failure notifications as email messages to the company.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function at the specified time. Add the necessary permissions for the invocation to the Lambda function's resource-based policy. Configure the Lambda function to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Configure the Lambda function to use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send failure notifications to the company.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function at the specified time. Add the necessary permissions for the invocation to the Lambda function's resource-based policy. Configure the Lambda function to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Configure the Lambda function to use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send failure notifications as email messages to the company.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company already has deletion scripts. The solution must:

1. Run every day at a specific time.
2. Execute the file-deletion script before the database-record-deletion script.
3. Run against EC2 instances.
4. Send an email if either script fails.
5. Require the least development effort.

## Correct answer: A

**Use a Systems Manager State Manager association to schedule an Automation runbook, execute the scripts sequentially with Run Command, and route Automation failure events through EventBridge to an SNS email subscription.**

This is the most managed and lowest-code solution:

- State Manager associations can run an Automation runbook on a recurring cron or rate schedule. AWS documents selecting an Automation runbook and configuring **On Schedule** with a cron or rate expression. [Scheduling Automation with a State Manager association](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/scheduling-automations-state-manager-associations.html)
- An Automation runbook can contain ordered steps, and the `aws:runCommand` action runs commands on targeted managed EC2 instances. Multiple Run Command actions can be included in one runbook, so the file-deletion action can be placed before the database-record-deletion action. [Automation `aws:runCommand` action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-action-runcommand.html)
- Systems Manager emits EventBridge events when an Automation execution or individual Automation step changes status. EventBridge rules can specifically match `Failed` and `TimedOut` statuses and route them to an SNS topic. [Systems Manager EventBridge event types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/reference-eventbridge-events.html)
- EventBridge can use an SNS topic as its target, and the SNS topic can have an email subscription. [Sending EventBridge events as email through SNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-s3-object-created-tutorial.html)

Therefore, option A uses the existing scripts, provides deterministic ordering, and uses native managed-service failure events rather than requiring custom monitoring or notification code.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B

This uses the appropriate Systems Manager scheduling and execution mechanism, but it adds unnecessary custom error-handling logic inside the runbook and uses SES directly.

A final conditional step would need to collect and interpret the preceding step results and be carefully configured to execute even after a failed step. EventBridge can already match native Automation `Failed` or `TimedOut` status-change events. In addition, SES requires a verified sending identity and code or API actions to compose and send the email. [Creating and verifying SES email identities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/creating-identities.html)

This is more development and configuration effort than EventBridge routing an Automation failure event to an SNS email subscription.

### C

This requires writing, deploying, securing, monitoring, and maintaining a custom Lambda function. The scripts are intended to operate on the EC2 instances, whereas Lambda does not directly execute local EC2 scripts. The function would need additional remote-execution logic, such as calling Systems Manager APIs, which largely recreates the managed orchestration already provided by Automation.

Lambda also has a maximum execution timeout of 900 seconds, or 15 minutes, which can be problematic for deletion jobs whose duration might grow with the volume of files or database records. [Lambda timeout configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html)

Although SNS is an appropriate notification service, the Lambda orchestration creates more development effort than option A.

### D

This has the same unnecessary custom Lambda orchestration and 15-minute execution limit as option C. It also adds SES identity verification and email-sending implementation instead of using a simple SNS email subscription. Consequently, it requires the most custom development and setup among the choices.

## Conclusion

**A** best satisfies the scheduling, ordering, EC2 execution, and failure-email requirements by combining native Systems Manager Automation, State Manager scheduling, EventBridge failure detection, and SNS email delivery with minimal custom code.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个文件读取应用程序，该应用程序将文件保存到运行在 Amazon EC2 实例上的数据库中。法规要求该公司每天在特定时间从 EC2 实例中删除文件。公司必须删除超过 60 天的数据库记录。数据库记录删除必须在文件删除之后进行。公司已创建用于删除文件和数据库记录的脚本。公司需要在删除脚本发生任何失败时收到电子邮件通知。哪种解决方案能以最少的开发工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS Systems Manager State Manager 在每天指定时间自动调用 Systems Manager Automation 文档。将 Automation 文档配置为使用 run command 按顺序运行删除脚本。创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向公司发送失败通知。
options.B: 使用 AWS Systems Manager State Manager 在每天指定时间自动调用 Systems Manager Automation 文档。将 Automation 文档配置为使用 run command 按顺序运行删除脚本。在 Automation 文档的最后一步中创建条件语句以检查错误。使用 Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) 以电子邮件消息的形式向公司发送失败通知。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，在指定时间调用 AWS Lambda 函数。为调用向 Lambda 函数的基于资源的策略添加必要权限。将 Lambda 函数配置为按顺序运行删除脚本。将 Lambda 函数配置为使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向公司发送失败通知。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，在指定时间调用 AWS Lambda 函数。为调用向 Lambda 函数的基于资源的策略添加必要权限。将 Lambda 函数配置为按顺序运行删除脚本。将 Lambda 函数配置为使用 Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) 以电子邮件消息的形式向公司发送失败通知。

zh.explanation:
## 问题的要求

公司已经有删除脚本。该解决方案必须：

1. 每天在特定时间运行。
2. 在数据库记录删除脚本之前执行文件删除脚本。
3. 针对 EC2 实例运行。
4. 任一脚本失败时发送电子邮件。
5. 所需开发工作量最少。

## 正确答案：A

**使用 Systems Manager State Manager 关联来调度 Automation runbook，通过 Run Command 按顺序执行脚本，并通过 EventBridge 将 Automation 失败事件路由到 SNS 电子邮件订阅。**

这是托管程度最高且代码量最少的解决方案：

- State Manager 关联可以按照重复的 cron 或 rate 计划运行 Automation runbook。AWS 文档说明了如何选择 Automation runbook 并使用 cron 或 rate 表达式配置 **On Schedule**。 [Scheduling Automation with a State Manager association](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/scheduling-automations-state-manager-associations.html)
- Automation runbook 可以包含有序步骤，而 `aws:runCommand` 操作会在目标受管 EC2 实例上运行命令。一个 runbook 中可包含多个 Run Command 操作，因此可将文件删除操作置于数据库记录删除操作之前。 [Automation `aws:runCommand` action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-action-runcommand.html)
- 当 Automation 执行或单个 Automation 步骤变更状态时，Systems Manager 会发出 EventBridge 事件。EventBridge 规则可以专门匹配 `Failed` 和 `TimedOut` 状态，并将其路由到 SNS 主题。 [Systems Manager EventBridge event types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/reference-eventbridge-events.html)
- EventBridge 可以将 SNS 主题作为目标，而 SNS 主题可以具有电子邮件订阅。 [Sending EventBridge events as email through SNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-s3-object-created-tutorial.html)

因此，选项 A 使用现有脚本，提供确定性的执行顺序，并使用原生托管服务失败事件，而无需自定义监控或通知代码。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B

该选项使用了合适的 Systems Manager 调度和执行机制，但它在 runbook 内增加了不必要的自定义错误处理逻辑，并且直接使用 SES。

最后的条件步骤需要收集并解释先前步骤的结果，同时还必须仔细配置，以确保在步骤失败后仍能执行。EventBridge 已可匹配原生 Automation `Failed` 或 `TimedOut` 状态变更事件。此外，SES 需要经过验证的发件人身份，以及用于编写和发送电子邮件的代码或 API 操作。 [Creating and verifying SES email identities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/creating-identities.html)

与 EventBridge 将 Automation 失败事件路由到 SNS 电子邮件订阅相比，这需要更多开发和配置工作。

### C

该选项需要编写、部署、保护、监控和维护自定义 Lambda 函数。这些脚本旨在 EC2 实例上运行，而 Lambda 无法直接执行 EC2 上的本地脚本。该函数将需要额外的远程执行逻辑，例如调用 Systems Manager API，这在很大程度上重新实现了 Automation 已提供的托管编排能力。

Lambda 的最大执行超时时间也是 900 秒，即 15 分钟；对于持续时间可能随文件或数据库记录数量增加而增长的删除作业，这可能会造成问题。 [Lambda timeout configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html)

尽管 SNS 是合适的通知服务，但 Lambda 编排比选项 A 带来更多开发工作量。

### D

该选项与 C 一样，具有不必要的自定义 Lambda 编排和 15 分钟执行限制。它还增加了 SES 身份验证和电子邮件发送实现，而不是使用简单的 SNS 电子邮件订阅。因此，在所有选项中，它需要最多的自定义开发和设置工作。

## 结论

**A** 通过结合原生 Systems Manager Automation、State Manager 调度、EventBridge 失败检测和 SNS 电子邮件传递，以最少的自定义代码最佳地满足了调度、顺序、EC2 执行和失败电子邮件通知要求。

en.question: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations that has all features enabled to manage its AWS accounts. Amazon EQ instances run in the AWS accounts. The company requires that all current EC2 instances must use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2). The company needs to block AWS API calls that originate from EC2 instances that do not use IMDSv2. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a new SCP statement that denies the ec2:RunInstances action when the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key is not equal to the value of required. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
options.B: Create a new SCP statement that denies the ec2:RunInstances action when the ec2:MetadataHttpPutResponseHopLimit condition key value is greater than two. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
options.C: Create a new SCP statement that denies "*" when the ec2:RoleDelivery condition key value is less than two. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
options.D: Create a new SCP statement that denies when the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key value is not equal to required. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: C

The company must do more than require IMDSv2 for future EC2 launches. It needs an organization-wide guardrail that blocks AWS API calls made with EC2 instance-role credentials that existing instances obtained through IMDSv1.

Create an SCP that denies all actions when `ec2:RoleDelivery` is less than `2.0`, and attach the SCP to the organization root:

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "*",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "NumericLessThan": {
      "ec2:RoleDelivery": "2.0"
    }
  }
}
```

The `ec2:RoleDelivery` condition key identifies the IMDS version through which EC2 role credentials were delivered:

- `1.0` indicates credentials delivered through IMDSv1.
- `2.0` indicates credentials delivered through IMDSv2.

Therefore, the explicit deny prevents credentials obtained through IMDSv1 from being used to call AWS APIs. This applies to credentials from currently running instances, which directly satisfies the requirement. AWS specifically documents using `ec2:RoleDelivery` in an IAM policy or AWS Organizations SCP to reject API calls made with EC2 role credentials obtained through IMDSv1. See [Transition to using Instance Metadata Service Version 2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html).

Attaching the SCP to the organization root establishes the guardrail for all applicable member accounts in the organization.

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A — Incorrect.** Denying `ec2:RunInstances` when `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` is not `required` is a valid launch-time control that prevents new instances from being launched without requiring IMDSv2. However, it neither changes existing instances nor blocks AWS API calls made with credentials that current instances obtained through IMDSv1. AWS shows this condition as a way to control instance launches in [EC2 Auto Scaling launch-template permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-launch-template-permissions.html).

- **B — Incorrect.** `ec2:MetadataHttpPutResponseHopLimit` controls the response hop limit for IMDSv2 token requests. It does not indicate whether instance-role credentials were delivered through IMDSv1 or IMDSv2. In addition, restricting `ec2:RunInstances` affects future launches rather than API calls originating from currently running instances. AWS describes the hop-limit setting separately from the requirement for metadata tokens in [Configure instance metadata options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-options.html).

- **D — Incorrect.** `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` is used when controlling EC2 metadata-option configuration, such as requests involving `RunInstances` or `ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions`. It is not the condition key that records how the credentials used for an arbitrary AWS API call were obtained. Consequently, a broad deny based on `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` does not reliably evaluate API calls made by current instances. The appropriate credential-delivery context key is `ec2:RoleDelivery`, as documented in the [IMDSv2 transition guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html).

Thus, **C** is the only option that directly denies AWS API calls made with EC2 role credentials delivered through IMDSv1.

zh.question: 一家公司使用启用了所有功能的 AWS Organizations 组织来管理其 AWS 账户。Amazon EQ 实例运行在这些 AWS 账户中。该公司要求所有当前 EC2 实例都必须使用 Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2)。该公司需要阻止源自未使用 IMDSv2 的 EC2 实例的 AWS API 调用。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一条新的 SCP 语句：当 `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` 条件键不等于 `required` 时，拒绝 `ec2:RunInstances` 操作。将该 SCP 附加到组织根节点。
options.B: 创建一条新的 SCP 语句：当 `ec2:MetadataHttpPutResponseHopLimit` 条件键值大于 2 时，拒绝 `ec2:RunInstances` 操作。将该 SCP 附加到组织根节点。
options.C: 创建一条新的 SCP 语句：当 `ec2:RoleDelivery` 条件键值小于 2 时，拒绝 `"*"`。将该 SCP 附加到组织根节点。
options.D: 创建一条新的 SCP 语句：当 `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` 条件键值不等于 `required` 时，拒绝操作。将该 SCP 附加到组织根节点。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：C

公司不能仅要求未来启动的 EC2 实例使用 IMDSv2。它需要一个组织范围的护栏，用于阻止 EC2 实例角色凭证所发起的 AWS API 调用，而这些凭证是现有实例通过 IMDSv1 获取的。

创建一个 SCP：当 `ec2:RoleDelivery` 小于 `2.0` 时拒绝所有操作，并将该 SCP 附加到组织根节点：

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "*",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "NumericLessThan": {
      "ec2:RoleDelivery": "2.0"
    }
  }
}
```

`ec2:RoleDelivery` 条件键用于标识 EC2 角色凭证通过哪个 IMDS 版本交付：

- `1.0` 表示凭证通过 IMDSv1 交付。
- `2.0` 表示凭证通过 IMDSv2 交付。

因此，显式拒绝会阻止通过 IMDSv1 获取的凭证用于调用 AWS API。这适用于当前正在运行的实例所使用的凭证，因此直接满足了要求。AWS 专门说明，可以在 IAM policy 或 AWS Organizations SCP 中使用 `ec2:RoleDelivery` 来拒绝使用通过 IMDSv1 获取的 EC2 角色凭证发起的 API 调用。请参阅 [迁移到使用 Instance Metadata Service Version 2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html)。

将 SCP 附加到组织根节点，可为组织中的所有适用成员账户建立该护栏。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

- **A — 不正确。** 当 `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` 不为 `required` 时拒绝 `ec2:RunInstances`，是一项有效的启动时控制措施，可防止在未要求使用 IMDSv2 的情况下启动新实例。但是，它既不会更改现有实例，也不会阻止当前实例使用通过 IMDSv1 获取的凭证发起 AWS API 调用。AWS 在 [EC2 Auto Scaling launch-template permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-launch-template-permissions.html) 中将此条件展示为一种控制实例启动的方式。

- **B — 不正确。** `ec2:MetadataHttpPutResponseHopLimit` 控制 IMDSv2 令牌请求的响应跳数限制。它并不表明实例角色凭证是通过 IMDSv1 还是 IMDSv2 交付的。此外，限制 `ec2:RunInstances` 影响的是未来的启动，而不是源自当前运行中实例的 API 调用。AWS 在 [Configure instance metadata options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-options.html) 中将跳数限制设置与元数据令牌要求分别进行了说明。

- **D — 不正确。** `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` 用于控制 EC2 元数据选项配置，例如涉及 `RunInstances` 或 `ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions` 的请求。它不是用于记录任意 AWS API 调用所使用凭证获取方式的条件键。因此，基于 `ec2:MetadataHttpTokens` 的广泛拒绝无法可靠地评估由当前实例发起的 API 调用。合适的凭证交付上下文键是 `ec2:RoleDelivery`，如 [IMDSv2 transition guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html) 中所述。

因此，只有 **C** 会直接拒绝使用通过 IMDSv1 交付的 EC2 角色凭证发起的 AWS API 调用。

en.question: A DevOps team supports an application that runs on a large number of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The DevOps team uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy the EC2 instances. The application recently experienced an issue. A single instance returned errors to a large percentage of requests. The EC2 instance responded as healthy to both Amazon EC2 and Elastic Load Balancing health checks. The DevOps team collects application logs in Amazon CloudWatch by using the embedded metric format. The DevOps team needs to receive an alert if any EC2 instance is responsible for more than half of all errors. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule that groups logs from the CloudWatch application logs based on instance ID and errors.
options.B: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups. Use the CloudFormation stack to group the resources for the application. Add the application to CloudWatch Application Insights. Use the resource group to identify the application.
options.C: Create a metric filter for the application logs to count the occurrence of the term "Error.'' Create a CloudWatch alarm that uses the METRIC_COUNT function to determine whether errors have occurred. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to send a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify the DevOps team.
options.D: Create a CloudWatch alarm that uses the INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC function to determine whether a specific instance is responsible for more than half of all errors reported by EC2 instances. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to send a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify the DevOps team.
options.E: Create a CloudWatch subscription filter for the application logs that filters for errors and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send the instance ID and error and in a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify the DevOps team.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The EC2 and load balancer health checks cannot detect this failure because the problematic instance remains infrastructure-level healthy. The alert therefore must be derived from the application error logs and must dynamically identify whether **any one instance contributes more than 50% of all errors**, even as Auto Scaling adds or removes instances.

## Correct answers: A and D

### A. Create a Contributor Insights rule grouped by instance ID and errors

CloudWatch Contributor Insights is designed to analyze high-cardinality log data and identify top contributors, including bad hosts and sources generating the most errors. A custom rule can use a log field such as the instance ID as its contributor key, filter for error events, and aggregate by `Count`. This avoids creating and maintaining a separate alarm or metric for every dynamically changing EC2 instance.

AWS documents that Contributor Insights rules can use log fields as contributor keys, apply filters, and rank contributors by occurrence count. See [Create a Contributor Insights rule in CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights-CreateRule.html) and [Use Contributor Insights to analyze high-cardinality data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights.html).

### D. Alarm on an `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC` expression and notify through SNS

For a count-based error rule, the alarm can compare:

- `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC("ErrorRule", "MaxContributorValue")` — the error count from the instance that is currently the top contributor.
- `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC("ErrorRule", "Sum")` — the error count across all contributing instances.

Conceptually, the alarm expression is:

```text
100 * MaxContributorValue / Sum > 50
```

This detects when whichever instance is currently the largest contributor is responsible for more than half of all errors. The alarm can then publish to SNS.

AWS documents that `MaxContributorValue` represents the value of the top contributor, `Sum` represents the total from all contributors, and `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC` can be used in CloudWatch alarms and percentage calculations. See [Graphing metrics generated by Contributor Insights rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights-GraphReportData.html).

Together, **A and D** provide a managed, dynamically scaling solution with the least operational overhead.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. CloudWatch Application Insights

Application Insights can scan application resources, configure recommended monitoring, detect anomalies and log errors, and correlate observations into problems. However, this option does not define the required deterministic calculation that compares each instance's errors with the total error count. It also introduces resource-group and Application Insights configuration when Contributor Insights directly supports top-contributor analysis. See [CloudWatch Application Insights features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/appinsights-what-is.html).

### C. Metric filter with `METRIC_COUNT`

A metric filter for the word `Error` could produce an aggregate error metric, but it would not by itself determine which instance generated the errors or calculate that instance's share of the total.

Additionally, `METRIC_COUNT` does **not** count error occurrences. It returns the number of metric time series in an array. Therefore, it is the wrong function for this requirement. See [CloudWatch metric math syntax and functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/using-metric-math.html).

### E. Subscription filter and Lambda

A subscription filter can forward matching log events to Lambda, but the described function merely sends each instance ID and error to SNS. It does not maintain totals per instance, calculate each instance's percentage of all errors, or evaluate a 50% threshold. Implementing those capabilities would require custom aggregation/state management, retries, deployment, and ongoing Lambda maintenance, resulting in more operational overhead than Contributor Insights and a native CloudWatch alarm. See [Real-time processing of log data with CloudWatch Logs subscriptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Subscriptions.html).

zh.question: 某 DevOps 团队支持一个运行在 Auto Scaling 组中大量 Amazon EC2 实例上的应用程序。该 DevOps 团队使用 AWS CloudFormation 部署 EC2 实例。该应用程序最近发生了一个问题：单个实例对大量请求返回错误。该 EC2 实例对 Amazon EC2 和 Elastic Load Balancing 健康检查均响应为正常。DevOps 团队通过使用嵌入式指标格式在 Amazon CloudWatch 中收集应用程序日志。如果任何 EC2 实例导致的错误超过所有错误的一半，DevOps 团队需要收到警报。哪种步骤组合能够以最低的运营开销满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 创建一个 CloudWatch Contributor Insights 规则，该规则根据实例 ID 和错误对 CloudWatch 应用程序日志进行分组。
options.B: 在 AWS Resource Groups 中创建一个资源组。使用 CloudFormation 堆栈对应用程序的资源进行分组。将应用程序添加到 CloudWatch Application Insights。使用资源组来识别该应用程序。
options.C: 为应用程序日志创建一个指标筛选器，以统计术语 "Error.'' 的出现次数。创建一个使用 METRIC_COUNT 函数来确定是否发生错误的 CloudWatch 警报。将 CloudWatch 警报配置为向 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题发送通知，以通知 DevOps 团队。
options.D: 创建一个使用 INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC 函数的 CloudWatch 警报，以确定某个特定实例是否导致超过 EC2 实例报告的所有错误的一半。将 CloudWatch 警报配置为向 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题发送通知，以通知 DevOps 团队。
options.E: 为应用程序日志创建一个 CloudWatch 订阅筛选器，该筛选器筛选错误并调用 AWS Lambda 函数。配置 Lambda 函数，以在发送给 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题、用于通知 DevOps 团队的通知中发送实例 ID 和错误。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

EC2 和负载均衡器健康检查无法检测到此故障，因为有问题的实例在基础设施层面仍保持健康。因此，警报必须从应用程序错误日志中得出，并且必须动态识别 **任意单个实例是否导致超过所有错误的 50%**，即使 Auto Scaling 添加或移除实例也是如此。

## 正确答案：A 和 D

### A. 创建按实例 ID 和错误分组的 Contributor Insights 规则

CloudWatch Contributor Insights 专为分析高基数日志数据并识别主要贡献者而设计，包括故障主机和产生最多错误的来源。自定义规则可以使用实例 ID 等日志字段作为其贡献者键，筛选错误事件，并按 `Count` 聚合。这避免了为每个动态变化的 EC2 实例创建和维护单独的警报或指标。

AWS 文档说明，Contributor Insights 规则可以使用日志字段作为贡献者键、应用筛选器，并按出现次数对贡献者进行排名。请参阅 [在 CloudWatch 中创建 Contributor Insights 规则](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights-CreateRule.html) 和 [使用 Contributor Insights 分析高基数数据](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights.html)。

### D. 对 `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC` 表达式设置警报并通过 SNS 通知

对于基于计数的错误规则，警报可以比较：

- `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC("ErrorRule", "MaxContributorValue")` — 当前排名最高的贡献者实例产生的错误计数。
- `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC("ErrorRule", "Sum")` — 所有贡献实例的错误总计数。

从概念上讲，警报表达式为：

```text
100 * MaxContributorValue / Sum > 50
```

这会检测当前作为最大贡献者的任意实例是否导致超过一半的所有错误。随后，该警报可以发布到 SNS。

AWS 文档说明，`MaxContributorValue` 表示排名最高的贡献者的值，`Sum` 表示所有贡献者的总值，并且 `INSIGHT_RULE_METRIC` 可用于 CloudWatch 警报和百分比计算。请参阅 [绘制由 Contributor Insights 规则生成的指标图表](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContributorInsights-GraphReportData.html)。

A 和 D 共同提供了一个托管式、可动态扩展且运营开销最低的解决方案。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. CloudWatch Application Insights

Application Insights 可以扫描应用程序资源、配置推荐的监控、检测异常和日志错误，并将观察结果关联为问题。但是，此选项并未定义所需的确定性计算，以将每个实例的错误与错误总数进行比较。与直接支持主要贡献者分析的 Contributor Insights 相比，它还引入了资源组和 Application Insights 配置。请参阅 [CloudWatch Application Insights 功能](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/appinsights-what-is.html)。

### C. 使用 `METRIC_COUNT` 的指标筛选器

针对单词 `Error` 的指标筛选器可以生成汇总错误指标，但它本身无法确定哪个实例产生了错误，也无法计算该实例占错误总数的比例。

此外，`METRIC_COUNT` **不会**统计错误出现次数。它返回数组中指标时间序列的数量。因此，它不适用于此要求。请参阅 [CloudWatch 指标数学语法和函数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/using-metric-math.html)。

### E. 订阅筛选器和 Lambda

订阅筛选器可以将匹配的日志事件转发至 Lambda，但所描述的函数仅将每个实例 ID 和错误发送到 SNS。它不会维护每个实例的总计数、计算每个实例占所有错误的百分比，或评估 50% 阈值。实现这些功能将需要自定义聚合和状态管理、重试、部署以及持续的 Lambda 维护，其运营开销高于 Contributor Insights 和原生 CloudWatch 警报。请参阅 [使用 CloudWatch Logs 订阅实时处理日志数据](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Subscriptions.html)。

en.question: A company is using AWS CloudFormation to perform deployments of its application environment. A deployment failed during a recent update to the existing CloudFormation stack. A DevOps engineer discovered that some resources in the stack were manually modified. The DevOps engineer needs a solution that detects manual modification of resources and sends an alert to the DevOps lead. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the DevOps lead to the topic by using an email address. Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPLIANT resources status. Set the SNS topic as the rule target.
options.B: Tag all CloudFormation resources with a specific tag. Create an AWS Config custom rule by using the AWS Config Rules Development Kit Library (RDKlib) that checks all resource changes that have the specific tag. Configure the custom rule to mark all the tagged resource changes as NON_COMPLIANT when the change is not performed by CloudFormation. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPUANT resources status. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends an email message to the DevOps lead. Set the Lambda function as the rule target.
options.C: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the DevOps lead to the topic by using an email address. Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the COMPLIANT resources status. Set the SNS topic as the rule target.
options.D: Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPLIANT resources status. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends an email message to the DevOps lead. Set the Lambda function as the rule target.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs to detect **configuration drift caused by out-of-band/manual changes** to resources managed by an existing CloudFormation stack and notify the DevOps lead, while minimizing custom code and operational maintenance.

## Correct answer: A

AWS Config provides the managed rule **`CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK`** specifically for this purpose. It invokes CloudFormation stack drift detection and evaluates a stack as:

- `COMPLIANT` when the stack is `IN_SYNC`
- `NON_COMPLIANT` when the stack is `DRIFTED`

Therefore, an EventBridge rule can match the AWS Config compliance-change event when the result becomes `NON_COMPLIANT`. AWS documentation explicitly supports using **Config Rules Compliance Change** events to notify when a compliance check fails. EventBridge can then target an SNS topic directly, and the DevOps lead can receive the alert through an email subscription. This uses managed services without notification code, resulting in the least operational effort.

See:

- [AWS Config managed rule: cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check.html)
- [Monitoring AWS Config with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/monitor-config-with-cloudwatchevents.html)
- [EventBridge tutorial showing an SNS topic as a direct rule target with an email subscription](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-input-transformer-tutorial.html)

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B

This unnecessarily creates and maintains a **custom AWS Config rule**, tagging scheme, RDKlib evaluation logic, and Lambda notification function. The AWS-managed drift rule already detects the required condition. In addition, AWS Config configuration changes do not inherently provide the simple “not performed by CloudFormation” classification assumed by this custom-rule design. Even if custom logic could be developed with additional data sources, it would require substantially more operational effort than option A.

### C

A drifted stack is evaluated as `NON_COMPLIANT`, not `COMPLIANT`. Matching `COMPLIANT` events would notify when the stack is in sync or returns to compliance rather than when manual modifications cause drift. The managed-rule documentation explicitly maps `DRIFTED` to `NON_COMPLIANT`.

### D

This can detect the same noncompliant drift condition, but using a Lambda function solely to implement email delivery introduces code, permissions, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. EventBridge supports SNS as a direct target, and SNS supports email subscriptions, so the Lambda function is unnecessary. Thus, D does not provide the **least operational effort** compared with A.

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 AWS CloudFormation 对其应用程序环境执行部署。在最近对现有 CloudFormation 堆栈进行更新期间，某次部署失败。DevOps 工程师发现，堆栈中的一些资源被手动修改。DevOps 工程师需要一种能够检测资源手动修改并向 DevOps 负责人发送警报的解决方案。哪种解决方案能够以最低的运维工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。使用电子邮件地址为 DevOps 负责人订阅该主题。创建一个标识符为 CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK 的 AWS Config 托管规则。创建一个在资源状态为 NON_COMPLIANT 时调用的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。将 SNS 主题设置为该规则的目标。
options.B: 使用特定标签标记所有 CloudFormation 资源。使用 AWS Config Rules Development Kit Library (RDKlib) 创建一个 AWS Config 自定义规则，该规则检查具有该特定标签的所有资源更改。当更改不是由 CloudFormation 执行时，将自定义规则配置为把所有带标签的资源更改标记为 NON_COMPLIANT。创建一个在资源状态为 NON_COMPUANT 时调用的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个向 DevOps 负责人发送电子邮件的 AWS Lambda 函数。将 Lambda 函数设置为该规则的目标。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。使用电子邮件地址为 DevOps 负责人订阅该主题。创建一个标识符为 CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK 的 AWS Config 托管规则。创建一个在资源状态为 COMPLIANT 时调用的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。将 SNS 主题设置为该规则的目标。
options.D: 创建一个标识符为 CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK 的 AWS Config 托管规则。创建一个在资源状态为 NON_COMPLIANT 时调用的 Amazon EventBridge 规则。创建一个向 DevOps 负责人发送电子邮件的 AWS Lambda 函数。将 Lambda 函数设置为该规则的目标。

zh.explanation:
## 题目在问什么

公司需要检测由对现有 CloudFormation 堆栈所管理资源进行带外/手动更改而导致的**配置漂移**，并通知 DevOps 负责人，同时最大限度地减少自定义代码和运维维护。

## 正确答案：A

AWS Config 提供了专门用于此目的的托管规则 **`CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK`**。该规则会调用 CloudFormation 堆栈漂移检测，并将堆栈评估为：

- 当堆栈为 `IN_SYNC` 时，状态为 `COMPLIANT`
- 当堆栈为 `DRIFTED` 时，状态为 `NON_COMPLIANT`

因此，EventBridge 规则可以在结果变为 `NON_COMPLIANT` 时匹配 AWS Config 合规性变更事件。AWS 文档明确支持使用 **Config Rules Compliance Change** 事件，在合规性检查失败时发送通知。随后，EventBridge 可以直接将 SNS 主题作为目标，DevOps 负责人则可以通过电子邮件订阅接收警报。该方案使用托管服务而无需编写通知代码，因此运维工作量最低。

参阅：

- [AWS Config 托管规则：cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check.html)
- [使用 Amazon EventBridge 监控 AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/monitor-config-with-cloudwatchevents.html)
- [展示将 SNS 主题作为直接规则目标并使用电子邮件订阅的 EventBridge 教程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-input-transformer-tutorial.html)

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### B

该方案不必要地创建并维护了一个**自定义 AWS Config 规则**、标签方案、RDKlib 评估逻辑以及 Lambda 通知函数。AWS 托管的漂移规则已经能够检测所需的条件。此外，AWS Config 配置更改并不会天然提供此自定义规则设计所假设的简单“不是由 CloudFormation 执行”的分类。即使通过额外数据源可以开发自定义逻辑，其运维工作量也会明显高于选项 A。

### C

发生漂移的堆栈会被评估为 `NON_COMPLIANT`，而不是 `COMPLIANT`。匹配 `COMPLIANT` 事件会在堆栈处于同步状态或恢复合规时发送通知，而不是在手动修改导致漂移时发送通知。托管规则文档明确将 `DRIFTED` 映射为 `NON_COMPLIANT`。

### D

该方案可以检测相同的不合规漂移状况，但仅为了实现电子邮件投递而使用 Lambda 函数会引入代码、权限、部署、监控和维护工作。EventBridge 支持将 SNS 作为直接目标，而 SNS 支持电子邮件订阅，因此不需要 Lambda 函数。与 A 相比，D 无法实现**最低的运维工作量**。

en.question: A DevOps engineer deployed multiple AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower to support different business, technical, and administrative units in a company. A security team needs the DevOps engineer to automate AWS Control Tower guardrails for the company. The guardrails must be applied to all accounts in an OU of the company's organization in AWS Organizations. The security team needs a solution that has version control and can be reviewed and rolled back if necessary. The security team will maintain the management of the solution in its OU. The security team wants to limit the type of guardrails that are allowed and allow only new guardrails that are approved by the security team. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create individual AWS CloudFormation templates that align to a guardrail. Store the templates in an AWS CodeCommit repository. Create an AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl logical resource in the template for each OU in the organization. Configure an AWS Code Build project that an Amazon EventBridge rule will invoke for the security team's AWS CodeCommit changes.
options.B: Create individual AWS CloudFormation templates that align to a guardrail. Store the templates in an AWS CodeCommit repository. Create an AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl logical resource in the template for each account in the organization. Configure an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in the security team's account. Advise the security team to invoke the pipeline and provide these parameters when starting the pipeline.
options.C: Create individual AWS CloudFormation templates that align to a guardrail. Store the templates in an AWS CodeCommit repository. Create an AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl logical resource in the template for each OU in the organization. Configure an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in the security team's account that an Amazon EventBridge rule will invoke for the security team's CodeCommit changes.
options.D: Configure an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in the security team's account that an Amazon EventBridge rule will invoke for PutObject events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create individual AWS CloudFormation templates that align to a guardrail. Store the templates in the S3 bucket. Create an AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl logical resource in the template for each OU in the organization.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs an infrastructure-as-code workflow that:

- Enables approved AWS Control Tower controls (formerly called guardrails) for **every account in a target OU**.
- Keeps the permitted controls under **version control** so changes can be reviewed and reverted.
- Is managed by the security team from its account/OU.
- Automatically deploys approved repository changes with minimal operational effort.

## Correct answer: C

**C** provides the best combination of the correct deployment scope, governance, version control, and automated delivery:

1. An `AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl` resource represents each approved control as CloudFormation/IaC. AWS documents that Control Tower controls can be managed programmatically with CloudFormation and that controls apply to an **entire OU and every account within that OU**, including newly created accounts. The `EnableControl` operation creates the applicable resources on the specified OU and the accounts it contains. See [API for controls and a new CloudFormation resource](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/2022-all.html).
2. The target should be the **OU**, not each individual account. AWS's `EnableControl` example uses an Organizations OU ARN as `TargetIdentifier`. See [Use EnableControl with an AWS SDK or CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/code-library/latest/ug/controltower_example_controltower_EnableControl_section.html).
3. Storing the approved templates in CodeCommit provides Git history and supports pull-request review and approval. AWS documents that reviewers can inspect changes, comment on them, and approve pull requests. See [Review a pull request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-review-pull-request.html).
4. CodePipeline is the appropriate orchestration service for deploying the CloudFormation templates. AWS documents pipelines with a CodeCommit source and CloudFormation deployment actions, including CloudFormation change sets followed by a manual approval action before execution. This allows the security team to control which proposed guardrail changes are deployed. See [CloudFormation deployment actions in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-cloudformation-action.html).
5. EventBridge provides efficient event-driven automation. AWS states that a CodeCommit source action can use an EventBridge rule to start the pipeline when the source changes. See [CodeCommit source actions and EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/triggering.html).

Therefore, **C** allows the security team to maintain an approved catalog of guardrail templates, review changes through repository/pipeline controls, revert repository changes when necessary, and automatically apply approved controls at OU scope.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

Although this option correctly uses CodeCommit and targets OUs, it invokes a **CodeBuild project directly**. CodeBuild is primarily a build/execution service and does not by itself provide CodePipeline's structured source, change-set, approval, and deployment stages. A custom CodeBuild script would have to implement deployment sequencing, status handling, and approval controls, increasing operational overhead. CodePipeline has native CloudFormation deployment and approval actions, making C more operationally efficient.

### B

This option has two major problems:

- It creates an `AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl` resource for **each account**, while Control Tower controls are enabled against an **OU target** and then apply to the accounts in that OU. This would also create unnecessary maintenance as accounts are added or moved.
- The security team must manually invoke the pipeline and supply parameters. This is less automated and operationally efficient than triggering the pipeline from approved CodeCommit changes through EventBridge.

### D

This option stores templates in Amazon S3 and starts the pipeline from `PutObject` events. S3 can retain object versions if versioning is separately enabled, but the option does not specify that configuration and does not provide the Git commit, branching, pull-request review, and approval workflow offered by CodeCommit. A direct `PutObject` event can also start deployment merely because a file was uploaded, rather than because a reviewed repository change was approved. Thus, it does not satisfy the version-control and review requirements as effectively as C.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师使用 AWS Control Tower 部署了多个 AWS 账户，以支持公司中不同的业务、技术和管理单位。安全团队需要该 DevOps 工程师为公司自动化 AWS Control Tower guardrails。这些 guardrails 必须应用于公司在 AWS Organizations 中某个 OU 内的所有账户。安全团队需要一种具备版本控制、可进行审查并且在必要时可回滚的解决方案。安全团队将在其 OU 中维护该解决方案的管理工作。安全团队希望限制允许使用的 guardrails 类型，并且仅允许安全团队批准的新 guardrails。哪种解决方案能够以最高的运营效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建与某个 guardrail 对应的单独 AWS CloudFormation 模板。将模板存储在 AWS CodeCommit 存储库中。在模板中为组织中的每个 OU 创建一个 AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl 逻辑资源。配置一个 AWS CodeBuild 项目，由 Amazon EventBridge 规则针对安全团队的 AWS CodeCommit 更改调用该项目。
options.B: 创建与某个 guardrail 对应的单独 AWS CloudFormation 模板。将模板存储在 AWS CodeCommit 存储库中。在模板中为组织中的每个账户创建一个 AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl 逻辑资源。在安全团队的账户中配置一个 AWS CodePipeline 管道。建议安全团队调用该管道，并在启动管道时提供这些参数。
options.C: 创建与某个 guardrail 对应的单独 AWS CloudFormation 模板。将模板存储在 AWS CodeCommit 存储库中。在模板中为组织中的每个 OU 创建一个 AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl 逻辑资源。在安全团队的账户中配置一个 AWS CodePipeline 管道，由 Amazon EventBridge 规则针对安全团队的 CodeCommit 更改调用该管道。
options.D: 在安全团队的账户中配置一个 AWS CodePipeline 管道，由 Amazon EventBridge 规则针对 Amazon S3 存储桶的 PutObject 事件调用该管道。创建与某个 guardrail 对应的单独 AWS CloudFormation 模板。将模板存储在 S3 存储桶中。在模板中为组织中的每个 OU 创建一个 AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl 逻辑资源。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

公司需要一个基础设施即代码工作流程，该工作流程应：

- 为**目标 OU 中的每个账户**启用已批准的 AWS Control Tower controls（以前称为 guardrails）。
- 将允许使用的 controls 保留在**版本控制**中，以便可以审查和还原更改。
- 由安全团队从其账户/OU 中管理。
- 以最少的运营工作量自动部署已批准的存储库更改。

## 正确答案：C

**C** 在正确的部署范围、治理、版本控制和自动化交付之间提供了最佳组合：

1. `AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl` 资源将每个已批准的 control 表示为 CloudFormation/IaC。AWS 文档说明，可以使用 CloudFormation 以编程方式管理 Control Tower controls，并且 controls 会应用于**整个 OU 及该 OU 中的每个账户**，包括新创建的账户。`EnableControl` 操作会在指定 OU 及其包含的账户上创建适用资源。请参阅 [API for controls and a new CloudFormation resource](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/2022-all.html)。
2. 目标应当是 **OU**，而不是每个单独的账户。AWS 的 `EnableControl` 示例将 Organizations OU ARN 用作 `TargetIdentifier`。请参阅 [Use EnableControl with an AWS SDK or CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/code-library/latest/ug/controltower_example_controltower_EnableControl_section.html)。
3. 将已批准的模板存储在 CodeCommit 中可提供 Git 历史记录，并支持拉取请求审查和批准。AWS 文档说明，审查者可以检查更改、添加评论以及批准拉取请求。请参阅 [Review a pull request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-review-pull-request.html)。
4. CodePipeline 是部署 CloudFormation 模板的适当编排服务。AWS 文档介绍了包含 CodeCommit 源和 CloudFormation 部署操作的管道，其中包括 CloudFormation 更改集，随后是在执行前进行的手动审批操作。这使安全团队能够控制部署哪些提议的 guardrail 更改。请参阅 [CloudFormation deployment actions in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-cloudformation-action.html)。
5. EventBridge 提供高效的事件驱动自动化。AWS 表示，当源发生更改时，CodeCommit 源操作可以使用 EventBridge 规则启动管道。请参阅 [CodeCommit source actions and EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/triggering.html)。

因此，**C** 允许安全团队维护经过批准的 guardrail 模板目录，通过存储库/管道控制审查更改，在必要时还原存储库更改，并在 OU 范围内自动应用已批准的 controls。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

尽管此选项正确地使用 CodeCommit 并以 OU 为目标，但它会直接调用 **CodeBuild 项目**。CodeBuild 主要是一项构建/执行服务，本身并不提供 CodePipeline 的结构化源、变更集、审批和部署阶段。自定义 CodeBuild 脚本必须实现部署排序、状态处理和审批控制，这会增加运营开销。CodePipeline 具有原生的 CloudFormation 部署和审批操作，因此 C 的运营效率更高。

### B

此选项有两个主要问题：

- 它为**每个账户**创建 `AWS::ControlTower::EnableControl` 资源，而 Control Tower controls 是针对 **OU 目标**启用的，随后会应用于该 OU 中的账户。这还会在添加或移动账户时造成不必要的维护工作。
- 安全团队必须手动调用管道并提供参数。这比通过 EventBridge 根据已批准的 CodeCommit 更改触发管道的方式自动化程度更低、运营效率更低。

### D

此选项将模板存储在 Amazon S3 中，并通过 `PutObject` 事件启动管道。如果单独启用了版本控制，S3 可以保留对象版本，但该选项未说明此配置，也未提供 CodeCommit 所具备的 Git 提交、分支、拉取请求审查和审批工作流程。直接的 `PutObject` 事件还可能仅因文件上传就启动部署，而不是因为已审查的存储库更改获得批准才启动部署。因此，它无法像 C 一样有效满足版本控制和审查要求。

en.question: A company runs a web application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company uses Amazon CloudFront to distribute the application. The company recently enabled AWS WAF. The company set up Amazon CloudWatch Logs to send logs to an aws-waf-logs log group. The company wants a DevOps engineer to receive alerts if there are sudden changes in blocked traffic. The company does not want to receive alerts for other changes in AWS WAF log behavior. The company will tune AWS WAF rules over time. The DevOps engineer is currently subscribed to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in the environment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a CloudWatch Logs metrics filter for blocked requests on the AWS WAF log group to create a custom metric. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using CloudWatch anomaly detection and the published custom metric. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.
options.B: Create a CloudWatch anomaly detector for the log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using metrics that the CloudWatch anomaly detector publishes. Use the high setting for the LogAnomalyPriority metric. Configure the alarm to go into alarm state if a static threshold of one anomaly is detected. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.
options.C: Create a CloudWatch metrics filter for counted requests on the AWS WAF log group to create a custom metric. Create a CloudWatch alarm that activates when the sum of blocked requests in the custom metric during a period of 1 hour is greater than a static estimate for the acceptable number of blocked requests in 1 hour. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.
options.D: Create a CloudWatch anomaly detector for the log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using metrics that the CloudWatch anomaly detector publishes. Use the medium setting for the LogAnomalyPriority metric. Configure the alarm to go into alarm state if a sum of anomalies over 1 hour is greater than an expected value. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs an alert that is:

1. Scoped specifically to **AWS WAF blocked requests**, not to arbitrary changes in WAF log patterns.
2. Able to detect **sudden deviations** without maintaining a fixed threshold.
3. Able to adapt as traffic patterns and WAF rules change over time.
4. Delivered through the existing Amazon SNS topic.

## Correct answer: A

Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that matches WAF records whose terminating `action` is `BLOCK`, publish each match as a custom CloudWatch metric, and apply a CloudWatch anomaly detection alarm to that metric.

AWS WAF log records include an `action` field that identifies the terminating action applied to a request, including `block`. Therefore, the metric filter can isolate only blocked requests and avoid reacting to unrelated WAF log changes. See [AWS WAF web ACL log fields](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-fields.html).

CloudWatch Logs metric filters can count matching log events by publishing a metric value of `1` for every match. This produces a blocked-request count metric from the WAF log group. See [Create a metric filter for a log group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html).

CloudWatch anomaly detection supports **custom metrics**, continuously learns expected metric behavior, accounts for trends and seasonality, and permits alarms when the actual metric moves outside the expected band. This avoids maintaining a static threshold while WAF rules and normal traffic evolve. See [Using CloudWatch anomaly detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Anomaly_Detection.html). The alarm can use the existing SNS topic as its notification action.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B — Incorrect

A CloudWatch **log anomaly detector** analyzes the overall patterns and contents of the entire log group. It can flag new patterns, changes in known patterns, new dynamic-token values, or changes in token occurrence counts. Consequently, it could alert on changes unrelated to blocked traffic, violating the requirement not to receive alerts for other WAF log behavior.

Additionally, log anomaly detectors publish an `AnomalyCount` metric, with `LogAnomalyPriority` as a dimension; they do not publish a dedicated blocked-request metric. See [Log anomaly detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogsAnomalyDetection.html) and [Metrics published by log anomaly detectors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogsAnomalyDetection-Metrics.html).

### C — Incorrect

This option filters **counted requests**, rather than the terminating WAF `BLOCK` action requested by the scenario. It is also internally inconsistent because it proposes creating a metric for counted requests and then describes summing blocked requests from that metric.

More importantly, a fixed hourly threshold is a static estimate. It would require ongoing manual adjustment as traffic and WAF rules change, and it may miss a short-lived sudden change that is diluted across the one-hour aggregation period. CloudWatch metric anomaly detection is the better fit because its expected range adapts to historical and evolving behavior.

### D — Incorrect

Like B, this uses log-group-wide anomaly detection rather than a metric scoped specifically to blocked requests. A medium-priority anomaly could represent any unusual WAF log pattern, not necessarily a change in blocked traffic. The static expected anomaly-count threshold also measures the number of detected log anomalies rather than the volume of blocked requests.

Therefore, **A** provides both the required filtering precision and the adaptive alerting behavior.

zh.question: 一家公司的 Web 应用程序运行在 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上。该公司使用 Amazon CloudFront 分发该应用程序。该公司最近启用了 AWS WAF。该公司设置 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 将日志发送到 aws-waf-logs 日志组。如果被阻止的流量发生突然变化，该公司希望 DevOps 工程师能够收到警报。该公司不希望针对 AWS WAF 日志行为中的其他变化收到警报。该公司将随着时间推移调整 AWS WAF 规则。DevOps 工程师当前订阅了该环境中的 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 为 AWS WAF 日志组中的被阻止请求创建 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器，以创建自定义指标。使用 CloudWatch 异常检测和已发布的自定义指标创建 CloudWatch 警报。配置该警报以通知 SNS 主题，从而向 DevOps 工程师发出警报。
options.B: 为该日志组创建 CloudWatch 异常检测器。使用 CloudWatch 异常检测器发布的指标创建 CloudWatch 警报。对 LogAnomalyPriority 指标使用高优先级设置。将警报配置为在检测到一个异常的静态阈值时进入警报状态。配置该警报以通知 SNS 主题，从而向 DevOps 工程师发出警报。
options.C: 为 AWS WAF 日志组中的已计数请求创建 CloudWatch 指标筛选器，以创建自定义指标。创建一个 CloudWatch 警报，当 1 小时时间段内自定义指标中被阻止请求的总和大于 1 小时内可接受被阻止请求数量的静态估算值时激活该警报。配置该警报以通知 SNS 主题，从而向 DevOps 工程师发出警报。
options.D: 为该日志组创建 CloudWatch 异常检测器。使用 CloudWatch 异常检测器发布的指标创建 CloudWatch 警报。对 LogAnomalyPriority 指标使用中优先级设置。将警报配置为在 1 小时内异常总数大于预期值时进入警报状态。配置该警报以通知 SNS 主题，从而向 DevOps 工程师发出警报。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

公司需要的警报应当：

1. 专门限定于 **AWS WAF 被阻止的请求**，而不是 WAF 日志模式中的任意变化。
2. 能够检测 **突然的偏差**，而无需维护固定阈值。
3. 能够随着流量模式和 WAF 规则随时间变化而适应。
4. 通过现有的 Amazon SNS 主题发送。

## 正确答案：A

创建一个 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器，用于匹配终止 `action` 为 `BLOCK` 的 WAF 记录，将每次匹配发布为自定义 CloudWatch 指标，并对该指标应用 CloudWatch 异常检测警报。

AWS WAF 日志记录包含 `action` 字段，用于标识应用于请求的终止操作，其中包括 `block`。因此，指标筛选器可以仅分离被阻止的请求，并避免对无关的 WAF 日志变化作出响应。请参阅 [AWS WAF web ACL log fields](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-fields.html)。

CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器可以通过为每个匹配项发布指标值 `1` 来统计匹配的日志事件。这会从 WAF 日志组生成被阻止请求计数指标。请参阅 [Create a metric filter for a log group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html)。

CloudWatch 异常检测支持 **自定义指标**，会持续学习预期的指标行为，考虑趋势和季节性，并允许在实际指标超出预期范围时触发警报。这样便无需在 WAF 规则和正常流量不断演变时维护静态阈值。请参阅 [Using CloudWatch anomaly detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Anomaly_Detection.html)。该警报可以使用现有 SNS 主题作为其通知操作。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B — 不正确

CloudWatch **日志异常检测器**会分析整个日志组的总体模式和内容。它可以标记新模式、已知模式的变化、新的动态令牌值，或令牌出现次数的变化。因此，它可能会针对与被阻止流量无关的变化发出警报，违反了不希望针对其他 WAF 日志行为收到警报的要求。

此外，日志异常检测器会发布 `AnomalyCount` 指标，并将 `LogAnomalyPriority` 作为维度；它们不会发布专门的被阻止请求指标。请参阅 [Log anomaly detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogsAnomalyDetection.html) 和 [Metrics published by log anomaly detectors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogsAnomalyDetection-Metrics.html)。

### C — 不正确

此选项筛选的是 **已计数请求**，而不是该场景所要求的终止 WAF `BLOCK` 操作。它在内部也不一致，因为其建议创建已计数请求的指标，随后却描述了从该指标中汇总被阻止请求。
