更重要的是，固定的每小时阈值是静态估算。随着流量和 WAF 规则变化，它需要持续手动调整，并且可能遗漏在一小时聚合周期内被稀释的短暂突然变化。CloudWatch 指标异常检测更适合，因为其预期范围会适应历史行为和不断演变的行为。

### D — 不正确

与 B 类似，此选项使用的是日志组范围的异常检测，而不是专门限定于被阻止请求的指标。中优先级异常可能表示任何异常的 WAF 日志模式，不一定是被阻止流量的变化。静态的预期异常计数阈值衡量的也是检测到的日志异常数量，而不是被阻止请求的数量。

因此，**A** 同时提供了所需的筛选精度和自适应警报行为。

en.question: A video platform company is migrating its video catalog to AWS. The company will host MP4 videos files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company will use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon EC2 instances to serve the video files. Users first connect to a frontend application that redirects to a video URL. The video URL contains an authorization token in CloudFront. The cache is activated on the CloudFront distribution. Authorization token check activity needs to be logged in Amazon CloudWatch. The company wants to prevent direct access to video files on CloudFront and Amazon S3 and wants to implement checks of the authorization token that the frontend application provides. The company also wants to perform regular rolling updates of the code that checks the authorization token signature. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Implement an authorization token check in Lambda@Edge as a trigger on the CloudFront distribution. Enable CloudWatch logging for the Lambda@Edge function. Attach the Lambda@Edge function to the CloudFront distribution. Implement CloudFront continuous deployment to perform updates.
options.B: Implement an authorization token check in CloudFront Functions. Enable CloudWatch logging for the CloudFront function. Attach the CloudFront function to the CloudFront distribution. Implement CloudFront continuous deployment to perform updates.
options.C: Implement an authorization token check in the application code that is installed on the EC2 instances. Install the CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances. Configure the application to log to the CloudWatch agent. Implement a second CloudFront distribution. Migrate the traffic from the first CloudFront distribution by using Amazon Route 53 weighted routing.
options.D: Implement an authorization token check in CloudFront Functions. Enable CloudWatch logging for the CloudFront function. Attach the CloudFront function to the CloudFront distribution. Implement a second CloudFront distribution. Migrate the traffic from the first CloudFront distribution by using Amazon Route 53 weighted routing.

en.explanation:
## What the question is testing

The authorization check must run on **every viewer request before CloudFront serves an object from its cache**. The company also needs CloudWatch logging and a low-operations way to canary/roll out updated authorization code.

## Correct answer: B

**Use a CloudFront Function on the viewer request, log with `console.log()` to CloudWatch Logs, and use CloudFront continuous deployment for controlled updates.**

AWS explicitly identifies **request authorization**, including validation of hashed tokens such as JWTs, as an appropriate CloudFront Functions use case. CloudFront Functions executes at the viewer-request stage, so an invalid request can receive a `401` response before CloudFront returns a cached video or contacts an origin. AWS also provides an official CloudFront Functions example that verifies a JWT signature with HMAC, checks `nbf` and `exp`, retrieves the secret from CloudFront KeyValueStore, and returns `401 Unauthorized` when validation fails ([CloudFront Functions versus Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/edge-functions-choosing.html), [JWT validation example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/example_cloudfront_functions_kvs_jwt_verify_section.html)).

CloudFront Functions supports logging: lines generated by `console.log()` are automatically sent to CloudWatch Logs for a function in the `LIVE` stage. The logs are placed in `us-east-1` under `/aws/cloudfront/function/<FunctionName>` ([edge-function logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/edge-functions-logs.html)). This directly refutes the comments claiming that CloudFront Functions cannot log to CloudWatch.

CloudFront continuous deployment creates a staging distribution, sends a controlled portion of traffic to it, allows monitoring, and then promotes the tested staging configuration to the primary distribution. This provides the requested rolling/canary update process without manually operating a second distribution and Route 53 migration ([continuous deployment workflow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/continuous-deployment-workflow.html)).

CloudFront Functions is preferable to Lambda@Edge here because the documented workload is a lightweight request-authorization check. It can be built and tested within CloudFront, supports very high scale, and avoids the additional Lambda version, replication, regional logging, and IAM operational considerations associated with Lambda@Edge.

> To prevent bypass through a direct S3 URL, the S3 origin should also be private and accessible through CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC). The answer choices omit this common origin-security prerequisite; among the listed choices, B is the best solution for the authorization, logging, and rolling-update requirements.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Lambda@Edge
Lambda@Edge can perform authorization and can send logs to CloudWatch, so it is technically possible. However, AWS recommends CloudFront Functions for lightweight token-based request authorization. Lambda@Edge is intended for workloads needing capabilities such as longer execution, adjustable resources, third-party libraries, network access, file-system access, or request-body access—none of which is required here. It therefore introduces more operational overhead than necessary.

### C. Authorization on EC2 with Route 53 weighted routing
This checks authorization too late. Because CloudFront caching is enabled, a cache hit can be served without sending the request to the EC2 origin, so EC2 application code cannot enforce authorization on every viewer request. This option also requires managing EC2 code, the CloudWatch agent, a second distribution, and Route 53 weighted migration, which is substantially more operational work.

### D. CloudFront Function plus a manually managed second distribution
The CloudFront Function portion is appropriate, but manually creating another distribution and shifting DNS with Route 53 weighted routing is unnecessary. CloudFront continuous deployment already supplies a staging distribution, traffic controls, monitoring, and promotion workflow specifically for safe configuration and function-association rollouts. Therefore, D requires more operational effort than B.

zh.question: 一家视频平台公司正在将其视频目录迁移到 AWS。该公司将在 Amazon S3 存储桶中托管 MP4 视频文件。该公司将使用 Amazon CloudFront 和 Amazon EC2 实例来提供视频文件。用户首先连接到一个前端应用程序，该应用程序会重定向到一个视频 URL。该视频 URL 包含 CloudFront 中的授权令牌。CloudFront 分配已启用缓存。需要将授权令牌检查活动记录到 Amazon CloudWatch 中。该公司希望防止通过 CloudFront 和 Amazon S3 直接访问视频文件，并希望对前端应用程序提供的授权令牌实施检查。该公司还希望定期对检查授权令牌签名的代码执行滚动更新。哪种解决方案能够以**最少的运营工作量**满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Lambda@Edge 中实现授权令牌检查，并将其作为 CloudFront 分配上的触发器。为 Lambda@Edge 函数启用 CloudWatch 日志记录。将 Lambda@Edge 函数附加到 CloudFront 分配。实施 CloudFront 持续部署以执行更新。
options.B: 在 CloudFront Functions 中实现授权令牌检查。为 CloudFront 函数启用 CloudWatch 日志记录。将 CloudFront 函数附加到 CloudFront 分配。实施 CloudFront 持续部署以执行更新。
options.C: 在安装于 EC2 实例上的应用程序代码中实现授权令牌检查。在 EC2 实例上安装 CloudWatch agent。将应用程序配置为向 CloudWatch agent 写入日志。实施第二个 CloudFront 分配。使用 Amazon Route 53 加权路由将流量从第一个 CloudFront 分配迁移出去。
options.D: 在 CloudFront Functions 中实现授权令牌检查。为 CloudFront 函数启用 CloudWatch 日志记录。将 CloudFront 函数附加到 CloudFront 分配。实施第二个 CloudFront 分配。使用 Amazon Route 53 加权路由将流量从第一个 CloudFront 分配迁移出去。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查的内容

授权检查必须在 **CloudFront 从其缓存提供对象之前的每个查看者请求上**运行。公司还需要 CloudWatch 日志记录，以及一种低运营成本的方法来对更新后的授权代码进行金丝雀发布或逐步推出。

## 正确答案：B

**在查看者请求上使用 CloudFront Function，通过 `console.log()` 记录到 CloudWatch Logs，并使用 CloudFront 持续部署进行受控更新。**

AWS 明确指出，**请求授权**（包括验证 JWT 等哈希令牌）是适合使用 CloudFront Functions 的场景。CloudFront Functions 在查看者请求阶段执行，因此，无效请求可以在 CloudFront 返回缓存的视频或联系源站之前收到 `401` 响应。AWS 还提供了一个官方 CloudFront Functions 示例，该示例使用 HMAC 验证 JWT 签名，检查 `nbf` 和 `exp`，从 CloudFront KeyValueStore 获取密钥，并在验证失败时返回 `401 Unauthorized`（[CloudFront Functions 与 Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/edge-functions-choosing.html)，[JWT 验证示例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/example_cloudfront_functions_kvs_jwt_verify_section.html)）。

CloudFront Functions 支持日志记录：由 `console.log()` 生成的日志行会自动发送到处于 `LIVE` 阶段的函数的 CloudWatch Logs。日志位于 `us-east-1` 中的 `/aws/cloudfront/function/<FunctionName>` 下（[边缘函数日志记录](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/edge-functions-logs.html)）。这直接反驳了声称 CloudFront Functions 无法记录到 CloudWatch 的评论。

CloudFront 持续部署会创建一个暂存分配，将受控比例的流量发送到该分配，允许进行监控，然后将经过测试的暂存配置提升为主分配。这提供了所需的滚动/金丝雀更新流程，而无需手动运营第二个分配并执行 Route 53 迁移（[持续部署工作流程](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/continuous-deployment-workflow.html)）。

在此场景中，CloudFront Functions 优于 Lambda@Edge，因为文档所述的工作负载是轻量级请求授权检查。它可以在 CloudFront 内构建和测试，支持极高规模，并避免了 Lambda@Edge 所带来的额外 Lambda 版本、复制、区域日志记录和 IAM 运营注意事项。

> 为防止通过直接 S3 URL 绕过访问，S3 源站还应设为私有，并只能通过 CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) 访问。答案选项省略了这一常见的源站安全前提条件；在所列选项中，B 是最符合授权、日志记录和滚动更新要求的解决方案。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. Lambda@Edge
Lambda@Edge 可以执行授权，也可以将日志发送到 CloudWatch，因此从技术上可行。但是，AWS 建议针对轻量级的基于令牌的请求授权使用 CloudFront Functions。Lambda@Edge 适用于需要更长执行时间、可调整资源、第三方库、网络访问、文件系统访问或请求正文访问等能力的工作负载，而此处并不需要这些能力。因此，它引入了不必要的额外运营开销。

### C. 在 EC2 上授权并使用 Route 53 加权路由
此方案执行授权检查的时间太晚。由于 CloudFront 缓存已启用，缓存命中可以在不将请求发送到 EC2 源站的情况下直接提供，因此 EC2 应用程序代码无法对每个查看者请求强制执行授权。该选项还需要管理 EC2 代码、CloudWatch agent、第二个分配以及 Route 53 加权迁移，运营工作量明显更大。

### D. CloudFront Function 加上手动管理的第二个分配
CloudFront Function 部分是合适的，但手动创建另一个分配并通过 Route 53 加权路由转移 DNS 是不必要的。CloudFront 持续部署已提供了一个暂存分配、流量控制、监控和提升工作流程，专门用于安全地推出配置和函数关联变更。因此，D 比 B 需要更多运营工作量。

en.question: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts in a hierarchical structure. An SCP that is associated with the organization root allows IAM users to be created. A DevOps team must be able to create IAM users with any level of permissions. Developers must also be able to create IAM users. However, developers must not be able to grant new IAM users excessive permissions. The developers have the CreateAndManageUsers role in each account. The DevOps team must be able to prevent other users from creating IAM users. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create an SCP in the organization to deny users the ability to create and modify IAM users. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization. Attach the CreateAndManageUsers role to developers.
options.B: Create an SCP in the organization to grant users that have the DeveloperBoundary policy attached the ability to create new IAM users and to modify IAM users. Configure the SCP to require users to attach the PermissionBoundaries policy to any new IAM user. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
options.C: Create an IAM permissions policy named PermissionBoundaries within each account. Configure the PermissionBoundaries policy to specify the maximum permissions that a developer can grant to a new IAM user.
options.D: Create an IAM permissions policy named PermissionBoundaries within each account. Configure PermissionsBoundaries to allow users who have the PermissionBoundaries policy to create new IAM users.
options.E: Create an IAM permissions policy named DeveloperBoundary within each account. Configure the DeveloperBoundary policy to allow developers to create IAM users and to assign policies to IAM users of only if the developer includes the PermissionBoundaries policy as the permissions boundary. Attach the DeveloperBoundary policy to the CreateAndManageUsers role within each account.

en.explanation:
## What the question is testing

The company needs delegated IAM administration with two different trust levels:

- The **DevOps team** must retain unrestricted ability to create IAM users and assign any required permissions.
- **Developers** must be able to create and manage users, but every user they create must be constrained by an approved permissions boundary.
- Merely allowing IAM actions in the root SCP is insufficient because an SCP establishes only the maximum available permissions; it does not grant permissions to principals.

## Correct answers: C and E

### C. Create the `PermissionBoundaries` policy in every account

This policy defines the **maximum permissions** that an IAM user created by a developer can receive. A permissions boundary does not grant permissions by itself; it limits the effective permissions granted by the user's identity-based policies.

AWS documents this exact delegation pattern: create a customer managed policy to serve as the boundary for newly created users, thereby restricting what those users can do even if the delegated administrator attaches broader identity policies. See [Delegating responsibility to others using permissions boundaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html).

### E. Grant the developers conditional IAM administration permissions

`DeveloperBoundary` is the permissions policy attached to the developers' `CreateAndManageUsers` role. It permits user creation and policy assignment only when the request specifies the approved `PermissionBoundaries` policy as the new user's permissions boundary, using the `iam:PermissionsBoundary` condition key.

AWS's documented example uses the same design: the delegated administrator is allowed to call actions such as `iam:CreateUser` and `iam:AttachUserPolicy` only when the required boundary is present. Attempts to create a user without that boundary fail. See [Delegating responsibility to others using permissions boundaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html).

Together, C and E separate the two necessary controls:

1. **C defines the maximum permissions** available to developer-created users.
2. **E grants the developers user-management permissions conditionally**, requiring that boundary.

The DevOps team can retain a separate, unrestricted IAM administration policy. It can also control which other principals receive `iam:CreateUser`; the root SCP's allowance does not itself give that permission to anyone. AWS explicitly states that SCPs never grant permissions and that users and roles still require IAM permission policies. See [SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Incorrect

An unconditional SCP deny for creating or modifying IAM users at the organization root would apply to principals in all affected member accounts. The developers' role—and even an `AdministratorAccess` policy—could not override the SCP deny. This would prevent both developers and DevOps principals in member accounts from performing the required operations, unless the SCP contained an explicit exception, which the option does not specify.

AWS states that if an action is blocked by an SCP at a parent level, a user or role cannot perform it even with an IAM policy granting `*/*`: [SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

### B. Incorrect

An SCP cannot **grant** users the ability to create or modify IAM users. SCPs only establish the maximum permissions available; an identity-based IAM policy must provide the actual allow. In addition, applying a restrictive SCP at the root risks restricting the DevOps team's requirement to create users with any level of permissions.

See [SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

### D. Incorrect

A permissions boundary cannot grant the ability to create IAM users. It only limits permissions that are granted through identity-based policies. The developer role still needs an identity-based permissions policy authorizing `iam:CreateUser` and the associated management actions. AWS's documented delegation procedure explicitly uses both a boundary and a separate permissions policy: [Delegating responsibility to others using permissions boundaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Organizations 中的组织以层次结构管理多个 AWS 账户。与组织根关联的 SCP 允许创建 IAM 用户。DevOps 团队必须能够创建具有任意权限级别的 IAM 用户。开发人员也必须能够创建 IAM 用户。但是，开发人员不得向新的 IAM 用户授予过多权限。开发人员在每个账户中拥有 CreateAndManageUsers 角色。DevOps 团队必须能够阻止其他用户创建 IAM 用户。哪种步骤组合可以满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 在组织中创建一个 SCP，以拒绝用户创建和修改 IAM 用户的能力。将该 SCP 附加到组织根。将 CreateAndManageUsers 角色附加给开发人员。
options.B: 在组织中创建一个 SCP，向附加了 DeveloperBoundary 策略的用户授予创建新 IAM 用户和修改 IAM 用户的能力。配置该 SCP，要求用户为任何新的 IAM 用户附加 PermissionBoundaries 策略。将该 SCP 附加到组织根。
options.C: 在每个账户中创建一个名为 PermissionBoundaries 的 IAM 权限策略。配置 PermissionBoundaries 策略，以指定开发人员可以授予新 IAM 用户的最大权限。
options.D: 在每个账户中创建一个名为 PermissionBoundaries 的 IAM 权限策略。配置 PermissionsBoundaries，以允许拥有 PermissionBoundaries 策略的用户创建新的 IAM 用户。
options.E: 在每个账户中创建一个名为 DeveloperBoundary 的 IAM 权限策略。配置 DeveloperBoundary 策略，以允许开发人员创建 IAM 用户，并且仅当开发人员将 PermissionBoundaries 策略作为权限边界包含在内时，才允许向 IAM 用户分配策略。将 DeveloperBoundary 策略附加到每个账户中的 CreateAndManageUsers 角色。

zh.explanation:
## 本题考查的内容

公司需要委派 IAM 管理职责，并且存在两个不同的信任级别：

- **DevOps 团队**必须保留不受限制地创建 IAM 用户并分配任何所需权限的能力。
- **开发人员**必须能够创建和管理用户，但他们创建的每个用户都必须受到经批准的权限边界约束。
- 仅在根 SCP 中允许 IAM 操作是不够的，因为 SCP 仅建立可用权限的最大范围；它不会向主体授予权限。

## 正确答案：C 和 E

### C. 在每个账户中创建 `PermissionBoundaries` 策略

此策略定义开发人员创建的 IAM 用户可获得的**最大权限**。权限边界本身不会授予权限；它会限制通过用户的基于身份的策略授予的有效权限。

AWS 记录了这种确切的委派模式：创建一个客户托管策略，作为新创建用户的边界，从而限制这些用户可以执行的操作，即使被委派的管理员附加了更广泛的基于身份的策略也是如此。请参阅[使用权限边界向他人委派责任](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html)。

### E. 向开发人员授予有条件的 IAM 管理权限

`DeveloperBoundary` 是附加到开发人员 `CreateAndManageUsers` 角色的权限策略。它仅在请求使用 `iam:PermissionsBoundary` 条件键指定经批准的 `PermissionBoundaries` 策略作为新用户的权限边界时，才允许创建用户和分配策略。

AWS 的文档示例采用相同的设计：仅当存在所需边界时，才允许被委派的管理员调用 `iam:CreateUser` 和 `iam:AttachUserPolicy` 等操作。尝试在没有该边界的情况下创建用户将会失败。请参阅[使用权限边界向他人委派责任](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html)。

C 和 E 共同分离了两项必要的控制：

1. **C 定义开发人员创建的用户可拥有的最大权限**。
2. **E 有条件地授予开发人员用户管理权限**，要求使用该边界。

DevOps 团队可以保留单独且不受限制的 IAM 管理策略。它还可以控制哪些其他主体会获得 `iam:CreateUser`；根 SCP 中的允许本身不会向任何人授予该权限。AWS 明确指出，SCP 永远不会授予权限，用户和角色仍然需要 IAM 权限策略。请参阅[SCP 对权限的影响](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. 错误

在组织根处无条件地通过 SCP 拒绝创建或修改 IAM 用户，将适用于所有受影响成员账户中的主体。开发人员角色——甚至具有 `AdministratorAccess` 策略的主体——都无法覆盖 SCP 拒绝。这会阻止成员账户中的开发人员和 DevOps 主体执行所需操作，除非 SCP 包含明确的例外情况，但该选项未作说明。

AWS 指出，如果某项操作被父级的 SCP 阻止，即使 IAM 策略授予 `*/*`，用户或角色也无法执行该操作：[SCP 对权限的影响](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

### B. 错误

SCP 无法**授予**用户创建或修改 IAM 用户的能力。SCP 只建立可用权限的最大范围；基于身份的 IAM 策略必须提供实际的允许。此外，在根级别应用限制性 SCP 可能会限制 DevOps 团队创建具有任意权限级别用户的要求。

请参阅[SCP 对权限的影响](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

### D. 错误

权限边界无法授予创建 IAM 用户的能力。它仅限制通过基于身份的策略授予的权限。开发人员角色仍然需要一个基于身份的权限策略来授权 `iam:CreateUser` 和相关管理操作。AWS 记录的委派流程明确同时使用边界和单独的权限策略：[使用权限边界向他人委派责任](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html)。

en.question: A company has deployed a landing zone that has a well-defined AWS Organizations structure and an SCP. The company's development team can create their AWS resources only by using AWS CloudFormation and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). A DevOps engineer notices that Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues that are deployed in different CloudFormation stacks have different configurations. The DevOps engineer also notices that the application cost allocation tag is not always set. The DevOps engineer needs a solution that will enforce tagging and promote the reuse of code. The DevOps engineer needs to avoid different configurations for the deployed SQS queues. What should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Organizations tag policy to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use CloudFormation to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CloudFormation StackSets.
options.B: Update the SCP to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use CloudFormation modules to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CloudFormation stacks.
options.C: Use AWS CDK tagging to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation StackSets. Instruct the development team to use the AWS CDK to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CDK stacks.
options.D: Use AWS CDK tagging to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use the AWS CDK to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CDK feature flags.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs two distinct controls:

1. **A preventive tagging guardrail** so an SQS queue cannot be created without the application cost-allocation tag.
2. **A reusable, standardized SQS definition** so independently deployed CloudFormation stacks do not define queues with inconsistent configurations.

## Correct answer: B

An **SCP** can deny the underlying `sqs:CreateQueue` request when the required request tag is missing or invalid. This applies even when CloudFormation makes the API request on behalf of the development team, because the guardrail is evaluated against the resource-creation request. AWS specifically recommends considering an SCP for resource-creation guardrails because tagging compliance reporting alone does not stop administrators from creating untagged resources. Amazon SQS also supports tag-aware authorization during `CreateQueue`; AWS's SQS example demonstrates a queue-creation request being allowed or denied based on the tag passed in the request. See [Consider creating an SCP to set guardrails around resource creation requests](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-best-practices.html) and [Testing tag-based access control for SQS queue creation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-abac-testing-access-control.html).

**CloudFormation modules** directly address reuse and consistency. AWS describes modules as packaged resource configurations that can be included across stack templates in a transparent, manageable, and repeatable way. A company-defined SQS module can encapsulate approved settings—such as encryption, dead-letter queue configuration, visibility timeout, retention, and standard tags—while exposing only approved parameters. Developers then deploy normal CloudFormation stacks that consume this reusable module. See [Use modules to reuse resource configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html).

Therefore, **B** combines the correct preventive organization-level control with the CloudFormation feature specifically designed for reusable resource configurations.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

A tag policy is useful for standardizing tag keys, capitalization, values, and supported-resource compliance. Current AWS functionality can also enforce required tag keys for IaC, but CloudFormation enforcement requires activation and configuration of the `AWS::TagPolicies::TaggingComplianceValidator` Hook in **fail mode** in each applicable account and Region. The option only says to create a tag policy and omits this required enforcement mechanism. See [Enforce required tag keys with IaC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/enforce-required-tag-keys-iac.html).

Additionally, **StackSets are primarily a deployment mechanism for deploying the same stack across multiple accounts and Regions**. They are not the best answer for packaging an approved SQS configuration for reuse inside different, independently authored application stacks. CloudFormation modules are designed for that purpose. See [CloudFormation StackSets for multi-account and multi-Region deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html).

### C

AWS CDK tagging adds tags to constructs and includes them in the synthesized CloudFormation template. However, simply instructing developers to use CDK tags is not an independent enforcement guardrail: developers can omit or remove the tagging code. See [Tags and the AWS CDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/tagging.html).

The option also does not specify a reusable CDK construct or another mechanism that mandates one approved SQS configuration. StackSets address multi-account and multi-Region distribution, not by themselves the reuse of an SQS configuration across independently developed application stacks.

### D

CDK tagging has the same enforcement problem as option C: it applies tags when included in the CDK application, but does not prevent developers from omitting the tagging operation.

CDK **feature flags** are configuration switches used to enable potentially breaking CDK behaviors across releases. They are not a deployment mechanism and do not enforce standard SQS configurations or required cost-allocation tags. See [AWS CDK feature flags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/featureflags.html).

zh.question: 某公司已部署了一个具有明确定义的 AWS Organizations 结构和 SCP 的 landing zone。该公司的开发团队只能使用 AWS CloudFormation 和 AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) 创建 AWS 资源。一名 DevOps 工程师发现，部署在不同 CloudFormation 堆栈中的 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列具有不同的配置。该 DevOps 工程师还发现，应用程序成本分配标签并非始终已设置。该 DevOps 工程师需要一个能够强制实施标签并促进代码复用的解决方案。该 DevOps 工程师需要避免已部署的 SQS 队列出现不同配置。该 DevOps 工程师应如何做才能满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Organizations 标签策略，以在 CloudFormation 堆栈中强制实施成本分配标签。指示开发团队使用 CloudFormation 定义 SQS 队列。指示开发团队使用 CloudFormation StackSets 部署 SQS 队列。
options.B: 更新 SCP，以在 CloudFormation 堆栈中强制实施成本分配标签。指示开发团队使用 CloudFormation modules 定义 SQS 队列。指示开发团队使用 CloudFormation 堆栈部署 SQS 队列。
options.C: 使用 AWS CDK tagging 在 CloudFormation StackSets 中强制实施成本分配标签。指示开发团队使用 AWS CDK 定义 SQS 队列。指示开发团队使用 CDK stacks 部署 SQS 队列。
options.D: 使用 AWS CDK tagging 在 CloudFormation 堆栈中强制实施成本分配标签。指示开发团队使用 AWS CDK 定义 SQS 队列。指示开发团队使用 CDK feature flags 部署 SQS 队列。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查的内容

该公司需要两项不同的控制措施：

1. **预防性标签防护机制**，以确保无法在没有应用程序成本分配标签的情况下创建 SQS 队列。
2. **可复用的标准化 SQS 定义**，以确保独立部署的 CloudFormation 堆栈不会定义配置不一致的队列。

## 正确答案：B

**SCP** 可以在必需的请求标签缺失或无效时拒绝底层的 `sqs:CreateQueue` 请求。即使 CloudFormation 代表开发团队发出 API 请求，该机制仍然适用，因为该防护机制会针对资源创建请求进行评估。AWS 专门建议考虑使用 SCP 作为资源创建防护机制，因为仅靠标签合规性报告并不能阻止管理员创建未加标签的资源。Amazon SQS 还支持在 `CreateQueue` 期间进行标签感知型授权；AWS 的 SQS 示例展示了如何根据请求中传递的标签来允许或拒绝队列创建请求。请参阅 [考虑创建 SCP 以围绕资源创建请求设置防护机制](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-best-practices.html) 和 [测试基于标签的 SQS 队列创建访问控制](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-abac-testing-access-control.html)。

**CloudFormation modules** 可直接解决复用和一致性问题。AWS 将 modules 描述为可打包的资源配置，能够以透明、可管理且可重复的方式包含在多个堆栈模板中。公司定义的 SQS module 可以封装已批准的设置，例如加密、死信队列配置、可见性超时、保留期和标准标签，同时仅公开已批准的参数。随后，开发人员部署使用这一可复用 module 的常规 CloudFormation 堆栈。请参阅 [使用 modules 复用资源配置](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html)。

因此，**B** 将正确的组织级预防性控制与专为可复用资源配置而设计的 CloudFormation 功能结合在一起。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A

标签策略适用于标准化标签键、大小写、值和受支持资源的合规性。当前 AWS 功能也可以对 IaC 强制实施必需的标签键，但 CloudFormation 强制实施要求在每个适用账户和 Region 中，以 **fail mode** 激活并配置 `AWS::TagPolicies::TaggingComplianceValidator` Hook。该选项仅说明创建标签策略，遗漏了这一必需的强制实施机制。请参阅 [使用 IaC 强制实施必需的标签键](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/enforce-required-tag-keys-iac.html)。

此外，**StackSets 主要是一种在多个账户和 Region 中部署相同堆栈的部署机制**。对于在不同、独立编写的应用程序堆栈中复用经批准的 SQS 配置，它们并不是最佳答案。CloudFormation modules 正是为此目的而设计的。请参阅 [用于多账户和多 Region 部署的 CloudFormation StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html)。

### C

AWS CDK tagging 会向 constructs 添加标签，并将其包含在合成的 CloudFormation 模板中。但是，仅仅指示开发人员使用 CDK 标签并不是独立的强制实施防护机制：开发人员可以省略或删除标签代码。请参阅 [Tags and the AWS CDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/tagging.html)。

该选项也没有指定可复用的 CDK construct，或其他强制采用一种经批准 SQS 配置的机制。StackSets 用于跨账户和跨 Region 分发，而不是单独用于在独立开发的应用程序堆栈之间复用 SQS 配置。

### D

CDK tagging 存在与选项 C 相同的强制实施问题：在 CDK 应用程序包含标签操作时会添加标签，但无法阻止开发人员省略该操作。

CDK **feature flags** 是用于在不同版本之间启用可能造成破坏性影响的 CDK 行为的配置开关。它们不是部署机制，也不会强制实施标准 SQS 配置或必需的成本分配标签。请参阅 [AWS CDK feature flags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/featureflags.html)。

en.question: A DevOps team manages a company's AWS account. The company wants to ensure that specific AWS resource configuration changes are automatically reverted. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Use AWS Config rules to detect changes in resource configurations. Configure remediation action that uses AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to revert the configuration changes.
options.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor resource metrics. When an alarm is activated, use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify an administrator to manually reverts the configuration changes.
options.C: Use AWS CloudFormation to create a stack that deploys the necessary configuration changes. Update the stack when configuration changes need to be reverted.
options.D: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for noncompliant configurations. Manually apply necessary changes based on Trusted Advisor recommendations.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs a control that can evaluate AWS resource configurations and **automatically revert specified configuration changes** when resources become noncompliant. This requires both configuration-compliance detection and automated remediation.

## Correct answer: A

**A. Use AWS Config rules to detect changes in resource configurations. Configure a remediation action that uses AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to revert the configuration changes.**

AWS Config rules evaluate resources for compliance. When a resource is found to be noncompliant, AWS Config can apply a remediation action through an AWS Systems Manager Automation document. AWS provides managed remediation documents, and custom Automation documents can also be associated with Config rules. AWS Config explicitly supports selecting **Automatic remediation** so that noncompliant resources are remediated without administrator intervention. Therefore, an Automation document can perform the API operations needed to restore the required configuration. See [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html) and [Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **B is incorrect.** CloudWatch alarms primarily evaluate metrics and can publish notifications to SNS when alarm states change. In this option, SNS only notifies an administrator, who must manually revert the change. It neither provides AWS Config-style configuration compliance evaluation nor satisfies the requirement for automatic reversion. See [CloudWatch alarm actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarm-actions.html).

- **C is incorrect.** CloudFormation can establish and update an infrastructure configuration, and drift detection can identify differences between actual resource properties and the expected template properties. However, the proposed solution requires someone or another process to update the stack when a change needs to be reverted; it does not describe automatic detection and remediation of the specified changes. The CloudFormation drift workflow reports drift for review rather than automatically restoring the resource. See [Detect drift on individual stack resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/detect-drift-resource.html).

- **D is incorrect.** Trusted Advisor presents check results and recommended actions that customers can review and follow. The option explicitly requires manually applying the changes, so it does not meet the automatic-reversion requirement. See [Get started with Trusted Advisor Recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/get-started-with-aws-trusted-advisor.html).

Thus, **A** is the only option that directly combines resource-configuration compliance detection with automatic remediation.

zh.question: 一个 DevOps 团队管理一家公司的 AWS 账户。该公司希望确保特定的 AWS 资源配置更改能够被自动还原。哪种解决方案可以满足此要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS Config 规则检测资源配置的更改。配置使用 AWS Systems Manager Automation 文档的修复操作，以还原配置更改。
options.B: 使用 Amazon CloudWatch 警报监控资源指标。警报触发时，使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题通知管理员手动还原配置更改。
options.C: 使用 AWS CloudFormation 创建一个堆栈，以部署所需的配置更改。当需要还原配置更改时，更新该堆栈。
options.D: 使用 AWS Trusted Advisor 检查不合规配置。根据 Trusted Advisor 建议手动应用必要的更改。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司需要一种控制机制，能够评估 AWS 资源配置，并在资源变得不合规时**自动还原指定的配置更改**。这既需要配置合规性检测，也需要自动修复。

## 正确答案：A

**A. 使用 AWS Config 规则检测资源配置的更改。配置使用 AWS Systems Manager Automation 文档的修复操作，以还原配置更改。**

AWS Config 规则会评估资源的合规性。当发现资源不合规时，AWS Config 可以通过 AWS Systems Manager Automation 文档执行修复操作。AWS 提供托管修复文档，也可以将自定义 Automation 文档与 Config 规则关联。AWS Config 明确支持选择**自动修复**，以便在无需管理员干预的情况下修复不合规资源。因此，Automation 文档可以执行恢复所需配置所需的 API 操作。请参阅 [使用 AWS Config 修复不合规资源](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html) 和 [为 AWS Config 设置自动修复](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html)。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

- **B 不正确。** CloudWatch 警报主要评估指标，并且可以在警报状态发生变化时向 SNS 发布通知。在此选项中，SNS 仅通知管理员，管理员必须手动还原更改。它既不提供 AWS Config 风格的配置合规性评估，也不满足自动还原的要求。请参阅 [CloudWatch 警报操作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarm-actions.html)。

- **C 不正确。** CloudFormation 可以建立和更新基础设施配置，漂移检测可以识别实际资源属性与预期模板属性之间的差异。但是，所提出的解决方案要求在需要还原更改时由某个人或其他流程更新堆栈；它没有描述对指定更改进行自动检测和修复。CloudFormation 漂移工作流程会报告漂移以供审查，而不是自动恢复资源。请参阅 [检测单个堆栈资源的漂移](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/detect-drift-resource.html)。

- **D 不正确。** Trusted Advisor 提供检查结果和建议的操作，客户可以审查并执行这些操作。该选项明确要求手动应用更改，因此不满足自动还原要求。请参阅 [开始使用 Trusted Advisor Recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/get-started-with-aws-trusted-advisor.html)。

因此，**A** 是唯一直接将资源配置合规性检测与自动修复结合起来的选项。

en.question: A company hosts an application in its AWS account. The application uses an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that contain sensitive information. The company needs to capture object-level S3 API calls, including calls that are rejected because the calls were made by using credentials that are not valid. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail in the account. Enable S3 data events logging. Configure the trail to log to Amazon CloudWatch.
options.B: Create a new S3 bucket. Configure access logging on the application's S3 bucket. Deliver the access logs to the new S3 bucket.
options.C: Configure Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection enabled for the account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches findings that are associated with the S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the target.
options.D: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail and a new S3 bucket in the account. Configure the trail to log to the S3 new bucket.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: B

The application stores sensitive objects in Amazon S3 and needs to record both:

- object-level operations such as `GetObject`, `PutObject`, and `DeleteObject`, and
- requests that fail authentication because the supplied credentials are invalid.

The invalid-credentials requirement is decisive. AWS distinguishes an **authentication failure**, where the credentials cannot establish a valid identity, from an **authorization failure** such as `AccessDenied`, where the caller is authenticated but lacks permission.

### Why B is correct

**B. Create a new S3 bucket, enable server access logging on the application bucket, and deliver the logs to the new bucket.**

Amazon S3 server access logging provides detailed records for requests made to a bucket. AWS's comparison of S3 logging options shows that server access logs cover both **object operations** and **authentication failures**, whereas CloudTrail does not deliver records for requests that fail authentication because the supplied credentials are invalid. See [Logging options for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html).

The server access log format includes fields such as the requested operation, object key, HTTP status, and S3 error code. For an unauthenticated request, the requester field can contain `-`, allowing failed requests for which S3 cannot identify an authenticated principal to be represented in the log. See [Amazon S3 server access log format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/LogFormat.html).

Delivering the logs to a separate S3 bucket also separates the audit records from the sensitive application data and avoids the complications of writing access logs back into the source bucket. S3 server access log delivery is best effort, but among the available choices, this is the only solution that supports the required invalid-credential authentication failures. See [Logging requests with server access logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ServerLogs.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. CloudTrail S3 data events delivered to CloudWatch Logs

CloudTrail S3 data events can record object-level API operations, including operations such as `GetObject`, `PutObject`, and `DeleteObject`. However, AWS explicitly states that CloudTrail does **not** deliver logs for requests that fail authentication because the supplied credentials are invalid. CloudTrail can record authorization failures such as `AccessDenied` and requests made anonymously, but those are different from the authentication failures required here. Sending CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs changes the destination and enables monitoring; it does not cause CloudTrail to capture events that it excludes. See [Logging options for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html) and [Amazon S3 CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-s3-info.html).

### C. GuardDuty S3 Protection with EventBridge and Amazon SQS

GuardDuty is a threat-detection service, not a comprehensive request-auditing service. S3 Protection analyzes CloudTrail S3 data events and generates findings only when activity indicates a potential threat. EventBridge and SQS can route those findings, but they do not create a complete record of every S3 object request. GuardDuty's S3 analysis also relies on activity involving valid IAM or AWS STS credentials, so it does not satisfy the requirement to capture all requests rejected because credentials are invalid. See [GuardDuty S3 Protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/s3-protection.html).

### D. CloudTrail delivered to a new S3 bucket

Creating a trail and configuring an S3 destination does not by itself enable S3 object-level data events. CloudTrail trails record S3 management events by default, while object-level operations must be explicitly selected as data events. More importantly, even if S3 data events were enabled, CloudTrail would still omit requests that fail authentication because the credentials are invalid. Therefore, changing the CloudTrail destination to an S3 bucket does not meet either part of the requirement as written. See [Amazon S3 CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-s3-info.html) and [Logging options for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html).

**Therefore, B is the correct solution.**

zh.question: 一家公司在其 AWS 账户中托管一个应用程序。该应用程序使用一个 Amazon S3 存储桶来存储包含敏感信息的对象。公司需要捕获对象级别的 S3 API 调用，包括因使用无效凭证而被拒绝的调用。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在该账户中创建一个 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪。启用 S3 数据事件日志记录。将该跟踪配置为记录到 Amazon CloudWatch。
options.B: 创建一个新的 S3 存储桶。在应用程序的 S3 存储桶上配置访问日志记录。将访问日志传送到新的 S3 存储桶。
options.C: 为该账户配置并启用 S3 保护的 Amazon GuardDuty。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，用于匹配与该 S3 存储桶关联的发现结果。将该规则配置为使用 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列作为目标。
options.D: 在该账户中创建一个 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪和一个新的 S3 存储桶。将该跟踪配置为记录到新的 S3 存储桶。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：B

该应用程序在 Amazon S3 中存储敏感对象，并且需要记录以下两类内容：

- `GetObject`、`PutObject` 和 `DeleteObject` 等对象级操作，以及
- 因所提供的凭证无效而导致身份验证失败的请求。

无效凭证这一要求具有决定性作用。AWS 区分了 **身份验证失败**（凭证无法建立有效身份）和 **授权失败**（例如 `AccessDenied`，即调用方已通过身份验证但没有权限）。

### 为什么 B 正确

**B. 创建一个新的 S3 存储桶，在应用程序存储桶上启用服务器访问日志记录，并将日志传送到新存储桶。**

Amazon S3 服务器访问日志记录会为对存储桶发出的请求提供详细记录。AWS 对 S3 日志记录选项的比较表明，服务器访问日志同时涵盖 **对象操作** 和 **身份验证失败**；而对于因所提供的凭证无效而导致身份验证失败的请求，CloudTrail 不会传送记录。请参阅 [Amazon S3 的日志记录选项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html)。

服务器访问日志格式包括请求的操作、对象键、HTTP 状态和 S3 错误代码等字段。对于未经身份验证的请求，请求者字段可以包含 `-`，从而使 S3 无法识别已验证主体的失败请求也能够在日志中体现。请参阅 [Amazon S3 服务器访问日志格式](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/LogFormat.html)。

将日志传送到单独的 S3 存储桶，还可以将审计记录与敏感应用程序数据分离，并避免将访问日志写回源存储桶所带来的复杂问题。S3 服务器访问日志的传送采用尽力而为机制，但在可用选项中，这是唯一支持所需的无效凭证身份验证失败记录的解决方案。请参阅 [使用服务器访问日志记录请求](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ServerLogs.html)。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 将 CloudTrail S3 数据事件传送到 CloudWatch Logs

CloudTrail S3 数据事件可以记录对象级 API 操作，包括 `GetObject`、`PutObject` 和 `DeleteObject` 等操作。但是，AWS 明确说明，CloudTrail **不会**传送因所提供凭证无效而导致身份验证失败的请求日志。CloudTrail 可以记录诸如 `AccessDenied` 的授权失败以及匿名发出的请求，但这些不同于本题所要求的身份验证失败。将 CloudTrail 事件发送到 CloudWatch Logs 只是改变了目标位置并启用了监控；不会使 CloudTrail 捕获原本排除的事件。请参阅 [Amazon S3 的日志记录选项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html) 和 [Amazon S3 CloudTrail 事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-s3-info.html)。

### C. 使用 EventBridge 和 Amazon SQS 的 GuardDuty S3 Protection

GuardDuty 是威胁检测服务，而不是全面的请求审计服务。S3 Protection 会分析 CloudTrail S3 数据事件，并且仅当活动表明存在潜在威胁时才生成发现结果。EventBridge 和 SQS 可以路由这些发现结果，但它们不会创建每个 S3 对象请求的完整记录。GuardDuty 的 S3 分析还依赖涉及有效 IAM 或 AWS STS 凭证的活动，因此无法满足捕获所有因凭证无效而被拒绝的请求这一要求。请参阅 [GuardDuty S3 Protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/s3-protection.html)。

### D. 将 CloudTrail 传送到新的 S3 存储桶

创建跟踪并配置 S3 目标位置，本身不会启用 S3 对象级数据事件。CloudTrail 跟踪默认记录 S3 管理事件，而对象级操作必须明确选择为数据事件。更重要的是，即使启用了 S3 数据事件，CloudTrail 仍会省略因凭证无效而导致身份验证失败的请求。因此，将 CloudTrail 的目标位置改为 S3 存储桶并不能满足题目所述的任一要求。请参阅 [Amazon S3 CloudTrail 事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-s3-info.html) 和 [Amazon S3 的日志记录选项](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/logging-with-S3.html)。

**因此，B 是正确的解决方案。**

en.question: A DevOps administrator is responsible for managing the security of a company's Amazon CloudWatch Logs log groups. The company's security policy states that employee IDs must not be visible in logs except by authorized personnel. Employee IDs follow the pattern of Emp-XXXXXX, where each X is a digit. An audit discovered that employee IDs are found in a single log file. The log file is available to engineers, but the engineers are not authorized to view employee IDs. Engineers currently have an AWS IAM Identity Center permission that allows logs:* on all resources in the account. The administrator must mask the employee ID so that new log entries that contain the employee ID are not visible to unauthorized personnel. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create a new data protection policy on the log group. Add an Emp-\d{6} custom data identifier configuration. Create an IAM policy that has a Deny action for the Action":"logs:Unmask" permission on the resource. Attach the policy to the engineering accounts.
options.B: Create a new data protection policy on the log group. Add managed data identifiers for the personal data category. Create an IAM policy that has a Deny action for the "NotAction":"logs:Unmask" permission on the resource. Attach the policy to the engineering accounts.
options.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to parse a log file entry, remove the employee ID, and write the results to a new log file. Create a Lambda subscription filter on the log group and select the Lambda function. Grant the lambda:InvokeFunction permission to the log group.
options.D: Create an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream that has an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination. Create a Firehose subscription filter on the log group that uses the Firehose delivery stream. Remove the "logs:*" permission on the engineering accounts. Create an Amazon Macie job on the S3 bucket that has an Emp-\d{6} custom identifier.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The engineers currently have broad `logs:*` permissions, which include the ability to request unmasked log data. The solution must:

1. Detect the company-specific employee ID format `Emp-XXXXXX`.
2. Mask matching values in **newly ingested** CloudWatch Logs events.
3. Prevent engineers from using their broad permissions to unmask those values.
4. Do this with the least custom processing and operational overhead.

## Correct answer: A

Create a **CloudWatch Logs data protection policy** on the affected log group and define a custom data identifier with the regular expression `Emp-\d{6}`. Include the de-identification/masking operation in that policy. CloudWatch Logs custom data identifiers are specifically intended for business-specific sensitive values such as company employee IDs that managed identifiers might not recognize. AWS even documents an employee-ID regular expression as the representative use case for custom identifiers ([Custom data identifiers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL-custom-data-identifiers.html)).

CloudWatch Logs data protection policies detect and mask matching sensitive data at ingestion. By default, matching data is masked at CloudWatch Logs egress points, and only principals with `logs:Unmask` can view the original value. Importantly, the policy affects data ingested after the policy is established, which matches the requirement to protect **new log entries** ([Help protect sensitive log data with masking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/mask-sensitive-log-data.html)).

Because the engineers already have `logs:*`, they otherwise also have `logs:Unmask`. An explicit identity-policy `Deny` for `logs:Unmask` overrides that existing broad `Allow`, ensuring the engineers see only masked values. AWS IAM policy evaluation specifies that an explicit deny overrides an allow ([IAM policy evaluation logic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)). Authorized personnel can retain `logs:Unmask` through separate permission sets that are not subject to this deny.

This is the most operationally efficient solution because masking is performed natively by CloudWatch Logs without Lambda code, duplicate log storage, delivery pipelines, or post-ingestion discovery jobs.

> If the regular expression is written directly in JSON, its backslash must be JSON-escaped, such as `Emp-\\d{6}`. The option's `Emp-\d{6}` expresses the intended regular expression.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B

Managed identifiers for the broad personal-data category are not the precise choice for a proprietary employee-ID format. A custom data identifier is designed for exactly this situation.

More critically, a deny statement using `"NotAction": "logs:Unmask"` has the opposite effect from what is required: with `Effect: Deny`, it denies applicable actions **other than** `logs:Unmask`. It does not deny `logs:Unmask`; therefore, the engineers' existing `logs:*` allow can continue to grant unmasking. AWS documents that `NotAction` with `Deny` explicitly denies actions not listed and exempts the listed action from that deny ([IAM `NotAction`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_notaction.html)).

### C

A Lambda subscription can transform and write a separate copy of the log data, but it does not mask or remove the employee ID from the original events already stored in the source CloudWatch Logs log group. Engineers with `logs:*` could continue to read the original log events. This solution also introduces Lambda code, invocation permissions, error handling, monitoring, and duplicate-log management, making it less operationally efficient than native data protection.

### D

A CloudWatch Logs subscription to Amazon Data Firehose and Amazon S3 creates another destination; it does not sanitize the original CloudWatch Logs events. Amazon Macie discovers and reports sensitive data in S3, but it does not provide inline masking of CloudWatch Logs events. Removing all CloudWatch Logs permissions from engineers also removes their legitimate ability to inspect the logs rather than allowing them to view masked logs. This design adds Firehose, S3, Macie, and additional access-management overhead without directly meeting the masking requirement.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 管理员负责管理某公司 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 日志组的安全性。公司的安全策略规定，除非是授权人员，否则员工 ID 不得在日志中可见。员工 ID 遵循 Emp-XXXXXX 模式，其中每个 X 都是一个数字。一次审计发现，员工 ID 存在于一个日志文件中。该日志文件可供工程师访问，但工程师无权查看员工 ID。工程师当前拥有一项 AWS IAM Identity Center 权限，该权限允许对账户中的所有资源执行 logs:* 操作。管理员必须对员工 ID 进行掩码处理，以便包含员工 ID 的新日志条目不会对未授权人员可见。哪种解决方案能够以最高的运营效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 在日志组上创建新的数据保护策略。添加 Emp-\d{6} 自定义数据标识符配置。创建一个 IAM 策略，在资源上针对 Action":"logs:Unmask" 权限设置 Deny 操作。将该策略附加到工程账户。
options.B: 在日志组上创建新的数据保护策略。为个人数据类别添加托管数据标识符。创建一个 IAM 策略，在资源上针对 "NotAction":"logs:Unmask" 权限设置 Deny 操作。将该策略附加到工程账户。
options.C: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来解析日志文件条目、删除员工 ID，并将结果写入新的日志文件。在日志组上创建 Lambda 订阅筛选器并选择该 Lambda 函数。向日志组授予 lambda:InvokeFunction 权限。
options.D: 创建一个以 Amazon S3 存储桶为目标的 Amazon Data Firehose 传输流。创建一个使用该 Firehose 传输流的日志组 Firehose 订阅筛选器。移除工程账户上的 "logs:*" 权限。在 S3 存储桶上创建一个具有 Emp-\d{6} 自定义标识符的 Amazon Macie 作业。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查的内容

工程师当前拥有广泛的 `logs:*` 权限，其中包括请求未掩码日志数据的能力。该解决方案必须：

1. 检测公司特有的员工 ID 格式 `Emp-XXXXXX`。
2. 对**新摄取**的 CloudWatch Logs 事件中匹配的值进行掩码处理。
3. 防止工程师利用其广泛权限取消这些值的掩码。
4. 以最少的自定义处理和运营开销实现这一点。

## 正确答案：A

在受影响的日志组上创建 **CloudWatch Logs 数据保护策略**，并使用正则表达式 `Emp-\d{6}` 定义自定义数据标识符。在该策略中包含去标识化/掩码操作。CloudWatch Logs 自定义数据标识符专门用于识别托管标识符可能无法识别的、业务特定的敏感值，例如公司员工 ID。AWS 甚至将员工 ID 正则表达式作为自定义标识符的典型使用案例进行了说明（[自定义数据标识符](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL-custom-data-identifiers.html)）。

CloudWatch Logs 数据保护策略会在摄取时检测并掩码匹配的敏感数据。默认情况下，匹配的数据会在 CloudWatch Logs 输出点被掩码，并且只有拥有 `logs:Unmask` 权限的主体才能查看原始值。重要的是，该策略会影响在策略建立后摄取的数据，这符合保护**新日志条目**的要求（[使用掩码帮助保护敏感日志数据](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/mask-sensitive-log-data.html)）。

由于工程师已经拥有 `logs:*`，他们原本也拥有 `logs:Unmask`。针对 `logs:Unmask` 的显式身份策略 `Deny` 会覆盖现有的广泛 `Allow`，从而确保工程师只能看到掩码值。AWS IAM 策略评估规定，显式拒绝会覆盖允许（[IAM 策略评估逻辑](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)）。授权人员可以通过不受该拒绝影响的单独权限集保留 `logs:Unmask` 权限。

这是运营效率最高的解决方案，因为掩码由 CloudWatch Logs 原生执行，无需 Lambda 代码、重复日志存储、传输管道或摄取后的发现作业。

> 如果直接在 JSON 中编写正则表达式，其反斜杠必须进行 JSON 转义，例如 `Emp-\\d{6}`。选项中的 `Emp-\d{6}` 表示预期的正则表达式。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B

用于广泛个人数据类别的托管标识符并不是专有员工 ID 格式的精准选择。自定义数据标识符正是为这种情况设计的。

更关键的是，使用 `"NotAction": "logs:Unmask"` 的拒绝语句与要求的效果相反：使用 `Effect: Deny` 时，它会拒绝适用的、**除** `logs:Unmask` 之外的操作。它不会拒绝 `logs:Unmask`；因此，工程师现有的 `logs:*` 允许仍可授予取消掩码的权限。AWS 文档说明，带有 `Deny` 的 `NotAction` 会显式拒绝未列出的操作，并使列出的操作免受该拒绝影响（[IAM `NotAction`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_notaction.html)）。

### C

Lambda 订阅可以转换日志数据并写入一个单独的副本，但它不会对仍存储在源 CloudWatch Logs 日志组中的原始事件进行掩码或删除员工 ID。拥有 `logs:*` 的工程师仍然可以读取原始日志事件。该解决方案还引入了 Lambda 代码、调用权限、错误处理、监控和重复日志管理，因此其运营效率低于原生数据保护。

### D

将 CloudWatch Logs 订阅到 Amazon Data Firehose 和 Amazon S3 只会创建另一个目标位置；它不会清理原始 CloudWatch Logs 事件。Amazon Macie 会发现并报告 S3 中的敏感数据，但不会对 CloudWatch Logs 事件提供内联掩码。移除工程师的所有 CloudWatch Logs 权限，也会移除他们检查日志的正当能力，而不是让他们查看已掩码的日志。该设计增加了 Firehose、S3、Macie 以及额外的访问管理开销，却无法直接满足掩码要求。

en.question: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage many AWS accounts. The company has enabled all features for the organization. The company uses AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy configurations to the accounts. The company uses AWS Config to monitor an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to ensure that all object uploads to the S3 bucket use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS Config conformance pack that includes the s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled rule. Deploy the conformance pack to the accounts. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
options.B: Create an SCP that includes a deny statement for the s3:createBucket action and a condition statement where s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
options.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set to enable an AWS CloudTrail trail to capture S3 data events for the organization. In the stack set, create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match S3 PutObject events that do not use AWS KMS encryption. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
options.D: Create an SCP that includes a deny statement for the s3:putObject action and a condition where s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs a **preventive organization-wide control** that rejects every S3 object upload unless the upload requests server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Merely detecting or reporting noncompliance after an upload does not satisfy “ensure.”

## Correct answer: D

Attach an SCP at the organization root that explicitly denies `s3:PutObject` when `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` is not `aws:kms`.

This is the correct control because:

- `s3:PutObject` is the action used to upload objects.
- `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` represents the requested server-side encryption method.
- Requiring the value `aws:kms` ensures that uploads use SSE-KMS rather than SSE-S3 (`AES256`) or no explicitly requested acceptable encryption method.
- An explicit deny in an SCP at the organization root affects member accounts beneath the root, regardless of permissions granted by IAM policies at lower levels. AWS documents that root- and OU-level deny statements apply restrictions to all accounts below them in the organization: [SCP evaluation and strategy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html).
- AWS provides a closely related SCP example that denies unencrypted S3 uploads by applying conditions to `s3:PutObject` and `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption`: [SCP-AMS-004: Restrict S3 uploads](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managedservices/latest/userguide/scp-library-compliance.html).

A representative policy structure is:

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"
    }
  }
}
```

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. AWS Config conformance pack with `s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled`

AWS Config is primarily a detective compliance service; this option reports bucket configuration rather than preventing a noncompliant upload. Additionally, the specified managed rule considers a bucket compliant if it has default encryption or a policy denying uploads that do not use either AES-256 or AWS KMS. It therefore does not specifically guarantee that every upload must use KMS. See [s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled.html).

### B. Deny `s3:CreateBucket`

This applies the deny to the wrong API action. `s3:CreateBucket` governs bucket creation, not object uploads. The encryption request header represented by `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` must be evaluated on object-writing operations such as `s3:PutObject`. Therefore, this option would not enforce KMS encryption for uploaded objects.

### C. CloudTrail data events, EventBridge, and SNS

This is a monitoring and notification solution. CloudTrail records S3 object-level API operations, and EventBridge reacts when a matching data event occurs. By then, the `PutObject` request has already been processed. It can alert the company about a noncompliant upload but does not reject the upload. AWS describes this flow as logging S3 object-level operations and invoking a target in response to the data event: [Log Amazon S3 object-level operations using EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-s3-data-events.html).

Therefore, **D** is the only option that provides the required preventive, organization-wide enforcement.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Organizations 中的一个组织来管理多个 AWS 账户。该公司已为该组织启用所有功能。该公司使用 AWS CloudFormation StackSets 将配置部署到这些账户。该公司使用 AWS Config 监控一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。该公司需要确保向该 S3 存储桶上传的所有对象都使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 加密。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 AWS Config 一致性包，其中包含 s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled 规则。将该一致性包部署到这些账户。将该规则配置为以 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题为目标。
options.B: 创建一个 SCP，其中包含针对 s3:createBucket 操作的拒绝语句，以及当 s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption 不为 aws:kms 时的条件语句。将该 SCP 附加到组织的根节点。
options.C: 创建一个 AWS CloudFormation stack set，以启用一个 AWS CloudTrail 跟踪来捕获组织的 S3 数据事件。在该 stack set 中，创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以匹配未使用 AWS KMS 加密的 S3 PutObject 事件。将该规则配置为以 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题为目标。
options.D: 创建一个 SCP，其中包含针对 s3:putObject 操作的拒绝语句，以及当 s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption 不为 aws:kms 时的条件。将该 SCP 附加到组织的根节点。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

公司需要一个**预防性的组织范围控制措施**，以拒绝每一次 S3 对象上传，除非上传请求使用 AWS KMS 密钥的服务端加密 (SSE-KMS)。仅在上传后检测或报告不合规并不能满足“确保”这一要求。

## 正确答案：D

在组织根节点附加一个 SCP，当 `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` 不为 `aws:kms` 时，显式拒绝 `s3:PutObject`。

这是正确的控制措施，原因如下：

- `s3:PutObject` 是用于上传对象的操作。
- `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` 表示所请求的服务端加密方法。
- 要求该值为 `aws:kms` 可确保上传使用 SSE-KMS，而不是 SSE-S3 (`AES256`) 或未显式请求可接受加密方法的情况。
- 组织根节点中的 SCP 显式拒绝会影响根节点下的成员账户，无论较低层级的 IAM 策略授予了何种权限。AWS 说明，根节点和 OU 级别的拒绝语句会对组织中其下方的所有账户施加限制：[SCP evaluation and strategy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html)。
- AWS 提供了一个密切相关的 SCP 示例，该示例通过对 `s3:PutObject` 和 `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` 应用条件来拒绝未加密的 S3 上传：[SCP-AMS-004: Restrict S3 uploads](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managedservices/latest/userguide/scp-library-compliance.html)。

一个具有代表性的策略结构如下：

```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"
    }
  }
}
```

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. 包含 `s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled` 的 AWS Config 一致性包

AWS Config 主要是一项检测型合规服务；此选项报告的是存储桶配置，而不是阻止不合规上传。此外，指定的托管规则会在存储桶启用了默认加密，或具有拒绝不使用 AES-256 或 AWS KMS 的上传的策略时，将该存储桶视为合规。因此，它并不能专门保证每次上传都必须使用 KMS。参见 [s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled.html)。

### B. 拒绝 `s3:CreateBucket`

此选项将拒绝应用于错误的 API 操作。`s3:CreateBucket` 管理的是存储桶创建，而不是对象上传。由 `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` 表示的加密请求标头必须在诸如 `s3:PutObject` 等对象写入操作中进行评估。因此，此选项无法为上传的对象强制实施 KMS 加密。

### C. CloudTrail 数据事件、EventBridge 和 SNS

这是一个监控和通知解决方案。CloudTrail 会记录 S3 对象级 API 操作，而 EventBridge 会在匹配的数据事件发生时作出响应。此时，`PutObject` 请求已经被处理。它可以就不合规上传向公司发出警报，但不能拒绝上传。AWS 将此流程描述为记录 S3 对象级操作，并响应数据事件调用目标：[Log Amazon S3 object-level operations using EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-s3-data-events.html)。

因此，**D** 是唯一能够提供所需预防性、组织范围强制执行的选项。

en.question: A company uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster and loads transactional data into the database every 5 hours. Data analysts use the Aurora PostgreSQL database to run short-running queries, create complex aggregated queries, and create simple reports that use the data. The data analysts also manually update the data, including deleting and inserting data. The data analysts have reported performance issues. The database team recently identified a long-running idle transaction connection that affected performance by blocking other queries and preventing VACUUM operations. The team wants to be proactively notified about these potential operational issues and about the recommended actions to fix the issues. The company's AWS account uses Amazon DevOps Guru to monitor all the applications in the account. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Turn on Performance Insights and DevOps Guru in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure DevOps Guru to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
options.B: Turn on Performance Insights in the existing Aurora PostrgreSQL DB cluster. Configure Amazon EventBridge to receive events from the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
options.C: Turn on Performance Insights and DevOps Guru in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
options.D: Turn on Performance Insights in the existing Aurora PostrgreSQL DB cluster. Configure Amazon EventBridge to receive events from the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure DevOps Guru to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The team needs **proactive detection of an Aurora PostgreSQL database condition**, specifically a long-running `idle in transaction` session, plus **recommended corrective actions** and **notifications to the database team**.

## Correct answer: A

**Turn on Performance Insights and DevOps Guru for the existing Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, and configure DevOps Guru notifications through Amazon SNS.**

This is the native DevOps Guru for RDS solution:

- DevOps Guru for RDS collects Aurora database performance data from **Performance Insights**, analyzes it, and publishes insights. AWS states that Performance Insights is required for the detailed analysis and recommendations provided by DevOps Guru for RDS. The setup workflow includes turning on Performance Insights and ensuring that the Aurora resource is covered by DevOps Guru. See [Analyzing Aurora performance anomalies with Amazon DevOps Guru for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/devops-guru-for-rds.html).
- A DevOps Guru **proactive insight** contains anomalies, related metrics, and recommendations intended to address database issues before they become larger problems.
- AWS has a specific Aurora PostgreSQL proactive insight for a connection that remains `idle in transaction` for more than 1,800 seconds. AWS explains that this condition can hold locks, block other queries, and prevent `VACUUM` or autovacuum from cleaning dead rows. The insight includes actions such as ending the transaction, terminating the connection, configuring `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`, checking autocommit, and correcting application transaction logic. See [Database has long running idle in transaction connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/PostgreSQL.Tuning_proactive_insights.html).
- DevOps Guru can publish notifications to an **Amazon SNS topic**, which can notify the database team. See [Adding Amazon SNS notification topics in the DevOps Guru console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/devops-guru/latest/userguide/update-notifications.html).

The account already using DevOps Guru does not remove the need for Performance Insights, and the Aurora resource must be within DevOps Guru's analyzed resource coverage. Option A describes the direct, service-native configuration without adding an unrelated event-routing component.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B

This option enables Performance Insights but does not use DevOps Guru for the actual analysis and recommendations. EventBridge can receive supported RDS/Aurora events, but it does not analyze Performance Insights database-load metrics or generate DevOps Guru proactive insights and corrective recommendations. It therefore does not satisfy the requirement for proactive operational diagnosis and recommended actions.

### C

The Performance Insights and DevOps Guru components are appropriate, but the notification mechanism is wrong. DevOps Guru notification settings use **Amazon SNS topics**. An Aurora DB cluster does not directly send DevOps Guru insight notifications through Amazon SES. SES is an email-sending service, not the native DevOps Guru notification integration.

### D

DevOps Guru for RDS consumes **Performance Insights metrics directly**; EventBridge is not required between Aurora and DevOps Guru. Configuring EventBridge to receive Aurora events does not contribute to detecting the `idle in transaction` proactive insight or generating the associated recommendations. Option D therefore adds an unrelated event path, whereas option A provides the direct supported configuration: Performance Insights, DevOps Guru coverage, and SNS notifications.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群，并且每 5 小时将事务数据加载到数据库中。数据分析师使用 Aurora PostgreSQL 数据库运行短时查询、创建复杂的聚合查询，以及创建使用这些数据的简单报告。数据分析师还会手动更新数据，包括删除和插入数据。数据分析师报告了性能问题。数据库团队最近发现一个长时间运行的空闲事务连接，该连接通过阻塞其他查询并阻止 VACUUM 操作而影响了性能。团队希望能够主动收到有关这些潜在运营问题以及修复这些问题的建议操作的通知。公司的 AWS 账户使用 Amazon DevOps Guru 监控账户中的所有应用程序。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在现有 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群中启用 Performance Insights 和 DevOps Guru。配置 DevOps Guru 以使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向数据库团队发送通知。
options.B: 在现有 Aurora PostrgreSQL DB 集群中启用 Performance Insights。配置 Amazon EventBridge 以接收来自现有 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群的事件。配置 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群以使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向数据库团队发送通知。
options.C: 在现有 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群中启用 Performance Insights 和 DevOps Guru。配置 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群以使用 Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) 向数据库团队发送通知。
options.D: 在现有 Aurora PostrgreSQL DB 集群中启用 Performance Insights。配置 Amazon EventBridge 以接收来自现有 Aurora PostgreSQL DB 集群的事件。配置 DevOps Guru 以使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 向数据库团队发送通知。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考察的内容

团队需要**主动检测 Aurora PostgreSQL 数据库状况**，具体而言是长时间运行的 `idle in transaction` 会话，还需要获得**建议的纠正操作**以及**发送给数据库团队的通知**。

## 正确答案：A

**为现有 Aurora PostgreSQL 集群启用 Performance Insights 和 DevOps Guru，并通过 Amazon SNS 配置 DevOps Guru 通知。**

这是适用于 RDS 的原生 DevOps Guru 解决方案：

- 适用于 RDS 的 DevOps Guru 从 **Performance Insights** 收集 Aurora 数据库性能数据，对其进行分析并发布洞察。AWS 表示，Performance Insights 是 DevOps Guru for RDS 提供详细分析和建议所必需的。设置流程包括启用 Performance Insights，并确保 Aurora 资源处于 DevOps Guru 的覆盖范围内。请参阅 [Analyzing Aurora performance anomalies with Amazon DevOps Guru for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/devops-guru-for-rds.html)。
- DevOps Guru 的**主动洞察**包含异常、相关指标以及建议，旨在于数据库问题演变为更大问题之前加以解决。
- AWS 针对保持 `idle in transaction` 状态超过 1,800 秒的连接提供了专门的 Aurora PostgreSQL 主动洞察。AWS 说明，这种状况可能会持有锁、阻塞其他查询，并阻止 `VACUUM` 或 autovacuum 清理死行。该洞察包含结束事务、终止连接、配置 `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`、检查自动提交以及修正应用程序事务逻辑等操作。请参阅 [Database has long running idle in transaction connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/PostgreSQL.Tuning_proactive_insights.html)。
- DevOps Guru 可以将通知发布到 **Amazon SNS 主题**，该主题可通知数据库团队。请参阅 [Adding Amazon SNS notification topics in the DevOps Guru console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/devops-guru/latest/userguide/update-notifications.html)。

该账户已使用 DevOps Guru 并不意味着无需 Performance Insights，而且 Aurora 资源必须在 DevOps Guru 所分析的资源覆盖范围内。选项 A 描述了直接的、服务原生的配置，无需添加无关的事件路由组件。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### B

该选项启用了 Performance Insights，但没有使用 DevOps Guru 进行实际分析和提供建议。EventBridge 可以接收受支持的 RDS/Aurora 事件，但它不会分析 Performance Insights 数据库负载指标，也不会生成 DevOps Guru 主动洞察和纠正建议。因此，它无法满足主动运营诊断和建议操作的要求。

### C

Performance Insights 和 DevOps Guru 组件是合适的，但通知机制错误。DevOps Guru 的通知设置使用 **Amazon SNS 主题**。Aurora DB 集群无法通过 Amazon SES 直接发送 DevOps Guru 洞察通知。SES 是电子邮件发送服务，而不是原生的 DevOps Guru 通知集成。

### D

适用于 RDS 的 DevOps Guru 会**直接**使用 Performance Insights 指标；在 Aurora 与 DevOps Guru 之间不需要 EventBridge。配置 EventBridge 接收 Aurora 事件无助于检测 `idle in transaction` 主动洞察，也无助于生成相关建议。因此，选项 D 添加了无关的事件路径，而选项 A 提供了直接且受支持的配置：Performance Insights、DevOps Guru 覆盖范围和 SNS 通知。

en.question: A DevOps engineer is implementing governance controls for a company that requires its infrastructure to be housed within the United States. The company has many AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that has all features enabled. The engineer must restrict which AWS Regions the company can use. The engineer must also ensure that an alert is sent as soon as possible if any activity outside the governance policy occurs. The controls must be automatically enabled on any new Region outside the United States. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create an Organizations SCP deny policy that has a condition that the aws:RequestedRegion property does not match a list of all US Regions. Include an exception in the policy for global services. Attach the policy to the root of the organization.
options.B: Configure AWS CloudTrail to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Enable CloudTrail for all Regions. Use a CloudWatch Logs metric filter to create a metric in non-US Regions. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to send an alert if the metric is greater than 0.
options.C: Use an AWS Lambda function that checks for AWS service activity. Deploy the Lambda function to all Regions. Write an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the Lambda function every hour. Configure the rule to send an alert if the Lambda function finds any activity in a non-US Region.
options.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to query Amazon Inspector to look for service activity in non-US Regions. Configure the Lambda function to send alerts if Amazon Inspector finds any activity.
options.E: Create an Organizations SCP allow policy that has a condition that the aws:RequestedRegion property matches a list of all US Regions. Include an exception in the policy for global services. Attach the policy to the root of the organization.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs two complementary controls across an AWS Organization:

1. A **preventive control** that blocks use of every non-US AWS Region, including non-US Regions introduced in the future.
2. A **detective control** that reports attempted or otherwise recorded activity outside the approved Regions as quickly as possible.

## Correct answers: A and B

### A. Attach a Region-deny SCP to the organization root

This is the appropriate preventive control. An SCP with an explicit `Deny`, a `StringNotEquals` condition on `aws:RequestedRegion`, and a list of approved US Regions denies requests to every Region that is not on that list. Because the condition works as a deny-all-except-US rule, a newly introduced non-US Region is automatically denied without requiring the policy to be updated.

The exception for global services is required because services such as IAM, Route 53, and CloudFront use global or designated Regional endpoints even though their resources or effects can be global. AWS provides essentially this same SCP pattern: `Deny` with `NotAction` for exempt global services and `aws:RequestedRegion` for the approved Regions. Attaching the policy at the root applies the explicit denial to all member accounts below the root. See [SCP syntax examples for Region restrictions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_syntax.html) and [how SCP explicit denies affect accounts beneath the attachment point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html).

### B. Send multi-Region CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs and alarm on non-US activity

This provides the detective control. CloudTrail can send trail events to CloudWatch Logs, where a metric filter can identify events whose `awsRegion` is outside the approved US Regions. A CloudWatch alarm can then notify the company when the resulting metric exceeds zero.

AWS documents the exact monitoring flow: send CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs, define metric filters, assign CloudWatch metrics, and create alarms that send notifications. See [Monitoring CloudTrail log files with CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/monitor-cloudtrail-log-files-with-cloudwatch-logs.html) and [creating metric filters and alarms for CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudwatch-alarms-for-cloudtrail.html).

A multi-Region trail logs events from all enabled Regions. When an opt-in Region is enabled, CloudTrail creates an identical copy of each multi-Region trail in that Region, supporting automatic coverage as Regions become enabled. See [CloudTrail multi-Region trails and opt-in Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### C. Periodically run Lambda functions in every Region

This is unnecessarily complex and does not satisfy the requirements as effectively:

- Running once per hour is not an alert **as soon as possible**.
- The Lambda function and EventBridge rule would need deployment and lifecycle management in every Region.
- The option does not provide automatic deployment into newly introduced Regions.
- CloudTrail with CloudWatch Logs metric filters and alarms is the native event-driven monitoring solution for AWS API activity.

### D. Query Amazon Inspector for service activity

Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability-management service that scans supported resources such as EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions. It is not a general audit log of AWS API or service activity by Region. CloudTrail is the correct service for recording that activity.

### E. Attach an SCP allow policy for US Regions

An SCP allow-list strategy can be implemented, but this option merely says to attach another `Allow` policy. AWS Organizations attaches the `FullAWSAccess` SCP by default, and effective allow-list designs must deliberately replace or otherwise structure the existing allow policies at the relevant levels. Simply attaching an additional conditional `Allow` is not the direct, reliable Region restriction described here.

By contrast, an explicit `Deny` at the root overrides allows below it and immediately enforces the boundary throughout the organization. AWS specifically recommends deny statements for broad restrictions and documents the `Deny` plus `aws:RequestedRegion` pattern. Therefore A is the unambiguous governance control, not E.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师正在为一家公司实施治理控制，该公司要求其基础设施必须部署在美国境内。该公司在一个已启用所有功能的 AWS Organizations 组织中拥有许多 AWS 账户。工程师必须限制公司可以使用的 AWS 区域。工程师还必须确保，如果发生任何违反治理策略的活动，能够尽快发送警报。对于美国以外的任何新区域，这些控制措施必须自动启用。哪种步骤组合能够满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 创建一个 Organizations SCP 拒绝策略，其中包含一个条件：`aws:RequestedRegion` 属性不匹配所有美国区域的列表。为全局服务在策略中添加例外。将该策略附加到组织的根节点。
options.B: 配置 AWS CloudTrail 将日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch Logs。为所有区域启用 CloudTrail。使用 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器在非美国区域中创建指标。配置 CloudWatch 警报，以便在该指标大于 0 时发送警报。
options.C: 使用一个 AWS Lambda 函数检查 AWS 服务活动。将该 Lambda 函数部署到所有区域。编写一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，每小时运行一次该 Lambda 函数。如果 Lambda 函数发现非美国区域中存在任何活动，则配置该规则发送警报。
options.D: 使用一个 AWS Lambda 函数查询 Amazon Inspector，以查找非美国区域中的服务活动。配置该 Lambda 函数，以便在 Amazon Inspector 发现任何活动时发送警报。
options.E: 创建一个 Organizations SCP 允许策略，其中包含一个条件：`aws:RequestedRegion` 属性匹配所有美国区域的列表。为全局服务在策略中添加例外。将该策略附加到组织的根节点。

zh.explanation:
## 题目在问什么

该公司需要在 AWS Organization 中实施两种互补的控制措施：

1. 一项**预防性控制**，阻止使用任何非美国 AWS 区域，包括未来新增的非美国区域。
2. 一项**检测性控制**，尽快报告在获批区域之外尝试进行或以其他方式被记录的活动。

## 正确答案：A 和 B

### A. 将区域拒绝 SCP 附加到组织根节点

这是适当的预防性控制。包含显式 `Deny`、针对 `aws:RequestedRegion` 的 `StringNotEquals` 条件以及获批美国区域列表的 SCP，会拒绝对不在该列表中的每个区域发出的请求。由于该条件以“除美国区域外全部拒绝”的方式运作，因此新推出的非美国区域会被自动拒绝，而无需更新策略。

全局服务需要例外，因为 IAM、Route 53 和 CloudFront 等服务使用全局或指定的区域终端节点，即使其资源或影响可能是全局性的。AWS 提供了基本相同的 SCP 模式：对豁免的全局服务使用 `NotAction` 的 `Deny`，并使用 `aws:RequestedRegion` 限制获批区域。将该策略附加到根节点，会使显式拒绝应用于根节点下的所有成员账户。请参阅 [SCP syntax examples for Region restrictions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_syntax.html) 和 [how SCP explicit denies affect accounts beneath the attachment point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html)。

### B. 将多区域 CloudTrail 事件发送到 CloudWatch Logs，并对非美国区域活动触发警报

这提供了检测性控制。CloudTrail 可以将跟踪事件发送到 CloudWatch Logs，其中指标筛选器可以识别其 `awsRegion` 位于获批美国区域之外的事件。之后，CloudWatch 警报可以在结果指标超过零时通知公司。

AWS 记录了这一确切的监控流程：将 CloudTrail 事件发送到 CloudWatch Logs，定义指标筛选器，分配 CloudWatch 指标，并创建用于发送通知的警报。请参阅 [Monitoring CloudTrail log files with CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/monitor-cloudtrail-log-files-with-cloudwatch-logs.html) 和 [creating metric filters and alarms for CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudwatch-alarms-for-cloudtrail.html)。

多区域跟踪会记录所有已启用区域中的事件。当启用一个选择加入区域时，CloudTrail 会在该区域中创建每个多区域跟踪的相同副本，从而在区域被启用时支持自动覆盖。请参阅 [CloudTrail multi-Region trails and opt-in Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails.html)。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### C. 在每个区域中定期运行 Lambda 函数

这种方式不必要地复杂，且不能有效满足要求：

- 每小时运行一次并非**尽快**发出警报。
- Lambda 函数和 EventBridge 规则需要在每个区域中进行部署和生命周期管理。
- 该选项未提供向新推出区域自动部署的机制。
- 使用 CloudTrail、CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器和警报，是监控 AWS API 活动的原生事件驱动解决方案。

### D. 查询 Amazon Inspector 以获取服务活动

Amazon Inspector 是一项漏洞管理服务，用于扫描 EC2 实例、ECR 容器映像和 Lambda 函数等受支持资源。它不是按区域记录 AWS API 或服务活动的通用审计日志。CloudTrail 才是记录此类活动的正确服务。

### E. 为美国区域附加 SCP 允许策略

可以实施 SCP 允许列表策略，但该选项仅表示附加另一项 `Allow` 策略。AWS Organizations 默认附加 `FullAWSAccess` SCP，而有效的允许列表设计必须有意地替换现有允许策略，或者在相关层级以其他方式构建这些策略。仅附加一项额外的条件式 `Allow`，并不是这里所述直接且可靠的区域限制方式。

相反，根节点上的显式 `Deny` 会覆盖其下级的允许，并立即在整个组织中强制执行边界。AWS 特别建议使用拒绝语句实施广泛限制，并记录了 `Deny` 加 `aws:RequestedRegion` 的模式。因此，A 是明确无误的治理控制措施，而不是 E。

en.question: A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Users recently began to experience errors when traffic was directed to some of the EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer discovers that the Auto Scaling group reports the problematic instances are healthy despite the application errors. User experience returns to normal after the DevOps engineer resolves the application errors on the problematic instances. The company wants to ensure that traffic is routed only to healthy instances that are not experiencing application errors. The company also wants a support team to receive a notification if the traffic routing configuration changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?
