options.D: 将日志组配置为保留期 30 天。创建一个 CloudWatch subscription filter，使用 Amazon Data Firehose 将日志事件发送到 S3 存储桶。创建一个 S3 Lifecycle 策略，在 90 天后将对象移动到 Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)，并在 180 天后移动到 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive。

zh.explanation:
## 问题要求

该解决方案必须在尽量降低成本的同时提供三个访问层级：

1. 将日志保留在 CloudWatch 中可搜索状态 **至少 30 天**。
2. 在 **至少第 90 天之前**保持**低延迟访问**。
3. **第 180 天之后**，由于检索很少且延迟不重要，应针对最低存储成本进行优化。
4. 保持较高的数据可用性和保护能力。

## 正确答案：D

将 CloudWatch Logs 日志组配置为 **30 天保留期**，并使用 **CloudWatch Logs subscription filter** 将传入的日志事件流式传输至 **Amazon Data Firehose**。随后，Firehose 可以将记录作为 S3 对象直接传输到 Amazon S3。

AWS 文档说明，CloudWatch Logs subscription filters 可以将日志事件发送至 Data Firehose，而 Firehose 会自动缓冲传入记录并将其作为 S3 对象传输。与仅为将数据写入 S3 而运行 Kinesis Data Streams 消费者应用程序相比，这种方式更简单且更具成本效益（[CloudWatch Logs subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html)、[sending CloudWatch Logs to Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/writing-with-cloudwatch-logs.html)、[Firehose data delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/basic-deliver.html)）。

最终的访问模式如下：

- **第 0–30 天：** 日志仍可在 CloudWatch Logs 中搜索，同时也会复制到 S3。
- **第 30–90 天：** S3 副本保留在其初始存储类中，提供低延迟访问。
- **第 90–180 天：** 转换至 **S3 Standard-IA**，该存储类仍提供毫秒级访问，并在多个 Availability Zones 中冗余存储数据。
- **第 180 天之后：** 转换至 **S3 Glacier Deep Archive**，这是成本最低的 Glacier 归档类，适用于访问罕见且检索可耗时数小时的场景。

AWS 建议将 S3 Standard-IA 用于无法重新创建的低频访问数据的主副本；与 One Zone-IA 不同，它能够应对一个 Availability Zone 丢失的情况。AWS 还列出了 S3 Glacier Deep Archive 的平均检索时间为 **9–48 小时**，并建议将其用于大约每年访问一次的数据，这符合第 180 天后的要求（[S3 infrequent-access classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)、[S3 Glacier class comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。这些都是受支持的 S3 Lifecycle 转换（[S3 Lifecycle transitions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)）。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

- **CloudWatch metric stream 会流式传输 CloudWatch metric 数据**，而不是 CloudWatch Logs 日志事件。因此，它不会归档所需的应用程序日志。AWS 将 metric streams 描述为持续流式传输 CloudWatch metrics，通常通过 Data Firehose 或快速 S3 设置实现（[CloudWatch metric streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Metric-Streams.html)）。
- Metric streams 不会按照此选项所述使用 Kinesis Data Streams。
- 在第 180 天后检索罕见且延迟不重要的情况下，S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 的成本也高于 Deep Archive。
- 此外，CloudWatch Logs **Infrequent Access** 类不支持 subscription filters，因此无法支持正确的实时日志传输架构（[CloudWatch Logs class features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CloudWatch_Logs_Log_Classes.html)）。

### B

- 此选项同样使用 **metric stream**，它导出的是指标而不是实际日志事件。
- **S3 One Zone-IA** 仅在一个 Availability Zone 中存储数据。AWS 指出，它的可用性和弹性低于 S3 Standard-IA，并且无法应对该 Availability Zone 的物理丢失。这与日志可用性和数据保护很重要的要求相冲突（[S3 infrequent-access classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。
- 对于很少检索且没有延迟要求的数据，S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 在长期存储成本方面不如 Deep Archive。

### C

- subscription filter 可以将日志事件发送到 **Kinesis Data Streams**，但 Kinesis Data Streams 不会直接将文件写入 S3。下游消费者（例如自定义应用程序或 Data Firehose）必须处理这些记录并存储结果。AWS 将消费者描述为处理记录，然后将结果存储在 S3 等服务中（[Kinesis Data Streams concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/key-concepts.html)）。此选项缺少所需的消费者，因此其方案不完整，并且在运维方面比 D 更复杂。
- **S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval** 提供毫秒级访问，专为大约每季度访问一次的数据而设计。在第 180 天后延迟并不重要，因此这种性能并非必需，成本效益不如 S3 Glacier Deep Archive（[S3 Glacier class comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。

en.question: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has all features enabled and has AWS CloudTrail trusted access configured for the management account. An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic is configured for notifications. The company needs all AWS events in all AWS Regions in the organization to be recorded and retained in an audit account. The company needs near real-time notifications of any failed login attempts. A DevOps engineer has created an organization trail in the management account to log events for all Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account. In the audit account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to failed login events in CloudTrail. Configure the EventBridge rule to notify the SNS topic.
options.B: Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Configure an Amazon Athena table to read from the new S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that queries the Athena table for failed login events and publishes the findings to the SNS topic. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes.
options.C: Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account and a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the management account. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the log group to create a custom metric for failed logins. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that uses the custom metric and notifies the SNS topic.
options.D: Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the audit account. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream in the audit account. Configure a subscription filter on the log group to send the logs to the data stream. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to filter the data stream for failed logins. Publish the results to the SNS topic.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The organization already has a multi-Region organization trail, so the remaining design must:

1. Centrally retain the organization’s CloudTrail records in the **audit account**.
2. Detect failed AWS Management Console sign-in attempts with **near-real-time** notification.
3. Minimize custom components and ongoing operations.

## Correct answer: C

Configure the organization trail to deliver its durable log files to an **S3 bucket in the audit account** and also deliver events to a **CloudWatch Logs log group in the management account**. Then use a CloudWatch Logs metric filter, a CloudWatch alarm, and the configured SNS topic.

This is the AWS-native monitoring pattern for CloudTrail:

- CloudTrail can use an S3 bucket in another account, while its CloudWatch Logs log group must be in the trail’s current account. For an organization trail created in the management account, placing the log group in the management account is therefore correct. AWS explicitly states that a trail can use an S3 bucket belonging to another account, but the CloudWatch Logs log group must exist in the current account. See [Creating a trail for your organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-an-organizational-trail-in-the-console.html).
- The audit account’s S3 bucket provides centralized retention. The bucket policy must allow CloudTrail to write the organization trail’s logs, as documented in [CloudTrail organization trail S3 bucket policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-s3-bucket-policy-for-cloudtrail.html).
- AWS documents the direct workflow of sending CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs, applying metric filters, creating metrics, and configuring alarms and notifications in [Monitoring CloudTrail log files with CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/monitor-cloudtrail-log-files-with-cloudwatch-logs.html).
- AWS provides the specific failed-login filter pattern:

  ```text
  { ($.eventName = ConsoleLogin) && ($.errorMessage = "Failed authentication") }
  ```

  A CloudWatch alarm can use the resulting metric and publish to SNS. To notify on any attempt, the alarm can be configured with a threshold of at least one matching event. See [Example AWS Management Console sign-in failures](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudwatch-alarms-for-cloudtrail.html).

This solution uses only managed integrations and no polling code or stream-processing application, giving it the least operational effort.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

An EventBridge rule in the audit account does not automatically receive organization-wide CloudTrail events merely because the trail writes log files to an S3 bucket in that account.

AWS service events are sent to the **default event bus of the account in which the service event occurs**. Receiving events centrally from other accounts requires explicit cross-account EventBridge permissions and event forwarding, neither of which is included in the option. See [Events from AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-events.html) and [Grant permissions to allow events from other AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-cross-account.html).

CloudTrail does provide console sign-in events to EventBridge, but CloudTrail events are delivered to the default event bus, not derived centrally from the S3 destination. See [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html). Therefore, the single rule in the audit account is insufficient as described.

### B

This option stores the retained logs in the **management account**, not the required audit account. It also introduces an Athena table, Lambda function, custom polling logic, and a scheduled EventBridge rule. Polling every five minutes is less immediate and requires substantially more operational effort than the native CloudWatch Logs metric-filter and alarm integration.

### D

CloudTrail cannot directly deliver the organization trail to a CloudWatch Logs log group in the audit account when the trail is owned and configured in the management account. AWS states that the CloudWatch Logs log group must exist in the trail’s current account. See [Creating a trail for your organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-an-organizational-trail-in-the-console.html).

Additionally, Kinesis Data Streams, a subscription filter, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink introduce unnecessary streaming infrastructure and application management. CloudWatch Logs metric filters and alarms provide the required detection and SNS notification with much lower operational overhead.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Organizations 中拥有一个组织。该组织已启用所有功能，并且已为管理账户配置 AWS CloudTrail 可信访问。已配置一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题用于发送通知。公司需要将组织中所有 AWS 区域内的所有 AWS 事件记录并保留在一个审计账户中。公司需要对任何登录失败尝试进行近实时通知。一名 DevOps 工程师已在管理账户中创建了一个组织跟踪以记录所有区域的事件。哪种解决方案能够以最低的运维工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置该跟踪以将日志发布到审计账户中的一个新 Amazon S3 存储桶。在审计账户中，创建一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以响应 CloudTrail 中的登录失败事件。配置该 EventBridge 规则以通知 SNS 主题。
options.B: 配置该跟踪以将日志发布到管理账户中的一个新 Amazon S3 存储桶。配置一个 Amazon Athena 表以从新的 S3 存储桶中读取数据。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，查询 Athena 表以获取登录失败事件，并将发现结果发布到 SNS 主题。创建一条 Amazon EventBridge 计划规则，每 5 分钟调用一次该 Lambda 函数。
options.C: 配置该跟踪以将日志发布到审计账户中的一个新 Amazon S3 存储桶，以及管理账户中的一个新 Amazon CloudWatch 日志组。在该日志组上创建一个 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器，为登录失败创建自定义指标。配置一个使用该自定义指标并通知 SNS 主题的 CloudWatch 警报。
options.D: 配置该跟踪以将日志发布到审计账户中的一个新 Amazon CloudWatch 日志组。在审计账户中创建一个 Amazon Kinesis 数据流。配置该日志组上的订阅筛选器以将日志发送到数据流。使用 Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink 筛选数据流中的登录失败事件。将结果发布到 SNS 主题。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该组织已具有多区域组织跟踪，因此其余设计必须：

1. 将组织的 CloudTrail 记录集中保留在**审计账户**中。
2. 针对失败的 AWS Management Console 登录尝试进行**近实时**检测和通知。
3. 尽量减少自定义组件和持续运维工作。

## 正确答案：C

配置组织跟踪，将其持久日志文件传送到**审计账户中的 S3 存储桶**，同时也将事件传送到**管理账户中的 CloudWatch Logs 日志组**。然后使用 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器、CloudWatch 警报以及已配置的 SNS 主题。

这是适用于 CloudTrail 的 AWS 原生监控模式：

- CloudTrail 可以使用其他账户中的 S3 存储桶，但其 CloudWatch Logs 日志组必须位于该跟踪的当前账户中。对于在管理账户中创建的组织跟踪而言，因此将日志组置于管理账户中是正确的。AWS 明确说明，跟踪可以使用属于其他账户的 S3 存储桶，但 CloudWatch Logs 日志组必须存在于当前账户中。请参阅[为组织创建跟踪](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-an-organizational-trail-in-the-console.html)。
- 审计账户的 S3 存储桶提供集中保留功能。该存储桶策略必须允许 CloudTrail 写入组织跟踪的日志，具体如 [CloudTrail organization trail S3 bucket policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-s3-bucket-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) 中所述。
- AWS 在[使用 CloudWatch Logs 监控 CloudTrail 日志文件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/monitor-cloudtrail-log-files-with-cloudwatch-logs.html)中记录了直接将 CloudTrail 事件发送至 CloudWatch Logs、应用指标筛选器、创建指标以及配置警报和通知的工作流程。
- AWS 提供了专用于登录失败的筛选器模式：

  ```text
  { ($.eventName = ConsoleLogin) && ($.errorMessage = "Failed authentication") }
  ```

  CloudWatch 警报可以使用生成的指标并发布到 SNS。为了对任何一次尝试发送通知，可以将警报配置为阈值至少为一个匹配事件。请参阅[示例 AWS Management Console 登录失败](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudwatch-alarms-for-cloudtrail.html)。

该解决方案仅使用托管集成，不需要轮询代码或流处理应用程序，因此运维工作量最低。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

审计账户中的 EventBridge 规则不会仅仅因为跟踪将日志文件写入该账户中的 S3 存储桶，便自动接收组织范围内的 CloudTrail 事件。

AWS 服务事件会被发送到**发生该服务事件的账户的默认事件总线**。要从其他账户集中接收事件，需要显式配置跨账户 EventBridge 权限和事件转发，而选项中均未包含这些内容。请参阅[来自 AWS 服务的事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-events.html)和[授予权限以允许来自其他 AWS 账户的事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-cross-account.html)。

CloudTrail 确实会将控制台登录事件提供给 EventBridge，但 CloudTrail 事件会传送到默认事件总线，而不是从 S3 目标位置集中派生。请参阅[通过 AWS CloudTrail 传送的 AWS 服务事件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)。因此，按描述仅在审计账户中创建一条规则是不足够的。

### B

此选项将保留的日志存储在**管理账户**中，而不是所需的审计账户中。此外，它引入了 Athena 表、Lambda 函数、自定义轮询逻辑以及计划 EventBridge 规则。每 5 分钟轮询一次的即时性较低，并且比原生 CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器和警报集成需要多得多的运维工作。

### D

当组织跟踪由管理账户拥有和配置时，CloudTrail 无法将该组织跟踪直接传送至审计账户中的 CloudWatch Logs 日志组。AWS 指出，CloudWatch Logs 日志组必须存在于跟踪的当前账户中。请参阅[为组织创建跟踪](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-an-organizational-trail-in-the-console.html)。

此外，Kinesis Data Streams、订阅筛选器和 Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink 会引入不必要的流式基础设施和应用程序管理。CloudWatch Logs 指标筛选器和警报能够以低得多的运维开销提供所需的检测和 SNS 通知。

en.question: A company runs a microservices application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Users recently reported significant delays while accessing an account summary feature, particularly during peak business hours. A DevOps engineer used Amazon CloudWatch metrics and logs to troubleshoot the issue. The logs indicated normal CPU and memory utilization on the EKS nodes. The DevOps engineer was not able to identify where the delays occurred within the microservices architecture. The DevOps engineer needs to increase the observability of the application to pinpoint where the delays are occurring. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the AWS X-Ray daemon as a DaemonSet in the EKS cluster. Use the X-Ray SDK to instrument the application code. Redeploy the application
options.B: Enable CloudWatch Container Insights for the EKS cluster. Use the Container Insights data to diagnose the delays.
options.C: Create alarms based on the existing CloudWatch metrics. Set up an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send email alerts.
options.D: Increase the timeout settings in the application code for network operations to allow more time for operations to finish.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The EKS nodes show normal CPU and memory utilization, but users experience latency in an account-summary workflow that likely crosses multiple microservices. The engineer therefore needs **distributed request tracing**, not additional infrastructure-utilization metrics or alerting. The solution must reveal how a request flows through the services and where time is spent.

## Correct answer: A

**Deploy the AWS X-Ray daemon as a DaemonSet in the EKS cluster, instrument the application with the X-Ray SDK, and redeploy it.**

AWS X-Ray collects trace data for application requests and records downstream calls to microservices, databases, AWS services, and web APIs. Its trace map can identify bottlenecks and latency spikes across a distributed application. The X-Ray SDK instruments incoming and outgoing requests, while the X-Ray daemon collects the generated trace segments and sends them to the X-Ray service. Running the daemon as a Kubernetes DaemonSet provides an X-Ray collector on the EKS worker nodes for the instrumented workloads.

AWS documents that applications must be instrumented with the X-Ray SDK and configured to use a collector such as the X-Ray daemon. It also describes X-Ray as providing detailed request and downstream-call information specifically for identifying latency and bottlenecks. See [What is AWS X-Ray?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html) and [Use the X-Ray SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray-interface-sdk.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Enable CloudWatch Container Insights

Container Insights is useful for EKS infrastructure and container-performance telemetry, such as CPU utilization, memory utilization, pod restarts, and node or pod health. AWS documentation shows that its dashboards and performance logs focus primarily on these resource-level metrics. It does not, by itself, provide the end-to-end request traces needed to determine which microservice or downstream operation is responsible for latency. Because existing metrics already show normal resource utilization, distributed tracing is the more appropriate diagnostic capability. See [Viewing Container Insights metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Container-Insights-view-metrics.html).

### C. Create CloudWatch alarms and send SNS notifications

Alarms and SNS notifications can alert the team when an existing metric crosses a threshold, but they do not add new request-level observability. They would indicate that a condition occurred without showing where time was spent as the request traversed the microservices.

### D. Increase application network timeouts

Increasing timeouts does not identify the source of the delay. It could make users wait longer and potentially conceal failures or bottlenecks. Timeout changes are a resilience or behavior adjustment, not an observability solution.

Therefore, **A** is the only option that provides end-to-end distributed tracing to pinpoint latency within the microservices architecture.

zh.question: 一家公司在 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上运行微服务应用程序。用户最近报告，在访问账户摘要功能时出现显著延迟，尤其是在业务高峰时段。一名 DevOps 工程师使用 Amazon CloudWatch 指标和日志来排查该问题。日志显示 EKS 节点的 CPU 和内存利用率正常。DevOps 工程师无法确定微服务架构中的延迟发生位置。该 DevOps 工程师需要提高应用程序的可观测性，以精确定位延迟发生的位置。哪种解决方案能满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 AWS X-Ray daemon 作为 DaemonSet 部署在 EKS 集群中。使用 X-Ray SDK 对应用程序代码进行插桩。重新部署应用程序。
options.B: 为 EKS 集群启用 CloudWatch Container Insights。使用 Container Insights 数据诊断延迟。
options.C: 基于现有 CloudWatch 指标创建告警。设置一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题以发送电子邮件提醒。
options.D: 增加应用程序代码中网络操作的超时设置，以便为操作完成留出更多时间。

zh.explanation:
## 场景与要求

EKS 节点显示正常的 CPU 和内存利用率，但用户在一个很可能跨越多个微服务的账户摘要工作流中遇到延迟。因此，工程师需要的是**分布式请求追踪**，而不是额外的基础设施利用率指标或告警。该解决方案必须揭示请求如何流经各项服务以及时间耗费在何处。

## 正确答案：A

**将 AWS X-Ray daemon 作为 DaemonSet 部署在 EKS 集群中，使用 X-Ray SDK 对应用程序进行插桩，然后重新部署应用程序。**

AWS X-Ray 会收集应用程序请求的追踪数据，并记录对微服务、数据库、AWS 服务和 Web API 的下游调用。其追踪地图可以识别分布式应用程序中的瓶颈和延迟峰值。X-Ray SDK 会对传入和传出的请求进行插桩，而 X-Ray daemon 会收集生成的追踪段并将其发送到 X-Ray 服务。将 daemon 作为 Kubernetes DaemonSet 运行，可在 EKS 工作节点上为已插桩的工作负载提供 X-Ray 收集器。

AWS 文档说明，应用程序必须使用 X-Ray SDK 进行插桩，并配置为使用 X-Ray daemon 等收集器。文档还说明，X-Ray 可提供详细的请求和下游调用信息，专门用于识别延迟和瓶颈。请参阅 [What is AWS X-Ray?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html) 和 [Use the X-Ray SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray-interface-sdk.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 启用 CloudWatch Container Insights

Container Insights 对于 EKS 基础设施和容器性能遥测非常有用，例如 CPU 利用率、内存利用率、Pod 重启以及节点或 Pod 运行状况。AWS 文档表明，其控制面板和性能日志主要侧重于这些资源级别的指标。仅靠它本身无法提供确定哪个微服务或下游操作导致延迟所需的端到端请求追踪。由于现有指标已显示资源利用率正常，分布式追踪是更合适的诊断能力。请参阅 [Viewing Container Insights metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Container-Insights-view-metrics.html)。

### C. 创建 CloudWatch 告警并发送 SNS 通知

告警和 SNS 通知可以在现有指标超过阈值时提醒团队，但它们不会增加新的请求级别可观测性。它们只能指出发生了某种状况，却无法显示请求穿越各个微服务时，时间具体耗费在何处。

### D. 增加应用程序网络超时时间

增加超时时间并不能确定延迟的根本原因。这可能会让用户等待更长时间，并且可能掩盖故障或瓶颈。超时设置变更属于韧性或行为调整，而不是可观测性解决方案。

因此，**A** 是唯一能够提供端到端分布式追踪，以精确定位微服务架构内延迟的选项。

en.question: A company uses a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to upload AWS CloudFormation templates to an Amazon S3 bucket. The pipeline uses the templates to deploy CloudFormation stacks that match the names of the templates. The company has experienced issues when it tries to revert templates to a previous version. To prevent these issues, the company must have the ability to review template modifications before the modifications are deployed to production. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure a connection in AWS CodeConnections to a Git repository. Store the templates in the Git repository. Configure a pull request workflow to review template modifications. Configure AWS CloudFormation Git sync for the stacks.
options.B: Add a manual review action in the pipeline to review modifications to the template code before the stack deployments.
options.C: Update the pipeline to invoke an AWS Lambda function to check the template modifications before the stack deployments.
options.D: Configure a connection in AWS CodeConnections to a Git repository. Store the templates in the Git repository. Configure the pipeline to include a source action that uses the connection. Add a manual review action to the pipeline to review template modifications before the stack deployments.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The current process stores CloudFormation templates in Amazon S3 and deploys them through CodePipeline. This does not provide the same native change-review and version-history workflow as a Git repository, which makes reverting and reviewing template modifications more difficult. The company needs human review **before** production deployment and wants the solution with the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct answer: A

**Configure AWS CodeConnections to a Git repository, use pull requests for review, and configure CloudFormation Git sync for the stacks.**

CloudFormation Git sync is purpose-built for this workflow. AWS states that Git sync lets teams manage stacks with source control and use **pull requests and version tracking** to configure, deploy, and update stacks. CloudFormation monitors the repository and automatically updates the associated stack after approved changes are committed or merged. It can also add a pull-request comment describing the stack changes before the update occurs. See [Syncing stacks with source code stored in a Git repository with Git sync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/git-sync.html).

Git sync uses CodeConnections to connect CloudFormation to the Git provider. With a pull request workflow, team members review and approve template changes before merging them; after acceptance, CloudFormation deploys the changes automatically. CloudFormation also maintains a history of commits applied to the stack. See [How Git sync works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/git-sync-concepts-terms.html).

This solution directly addresses both problems:

- Git version history makes rollback to an earlier template revision straightforward.
- Pull requests provide native review, comments, and approval before deployment.
- CloudFormation Git sync removes the need to maintain separate S3-upload and pipeline approval mechanics, resulting in the least operational overhead.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Add only a manual review action to the existing pipeline

A CodePipeline manual approval action pauses the pipeline until an approver approves or rejects it, but it does not by itself move the templates into source control or provide Git-native diffs, pull requests, and version tracking. AWS documents that an approval action presents an optional review URL and comments and then resumes or fails the pipeline based on the response. See [Manual approval actions in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals.html).

Therefore, this option can provide a deployment gate, but it does not adequately resolve the template versioning and reversion problem described in the scenario.

### C. Invoke a Lambda function to check modifications

This requires the company to develop, test, secure, operate, and maintain custom Lambda validation logic. It also describes an automated check rather than a clear human review and approval workflow. A custom function would have substantially more operational overhead than the managed Git sync and pull-request capabilities.

### D. Use a Git source action and add a CodePipeline manual review action

This option would provide source control and could gate deployment, so it is technically capable of meeting much of the requirement. However, it retains and expands the pipeline workflow by requiring a CodeConnections source action plus a separately configured manual approval stage. For CloudFormation deployments, AWS documents the pattern of creating a change set, pausing for manual approval, and then executing the change set. See [Add a manual approval action for a CloudFormation deployment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-cloudformation-action.html).

Compared with option A, this introduces more pipeline configuration and ongoing administration. CloudFormation Git sync already supplies repository monitoring, version tracking, pull-request review, optional change summaries, and automatic stack synchronization as a managed workflow. Thus, D is not the solution with the least operational overhead.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS CodePipeline 中的管道将 AWS CloudFormation 模板上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。该管道使用这些模板来部署名称与模板名称相匹配的 CloudFormation 堆栈。该公司在尝试将模板还原到先前版本时遇到了问题。为防止这些问题，公司必须能够在修改部署到生产环境之前审核模板修改。哪种解决方案能够以**最低的运维开销**满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 AWS CodeConnections 中配置到 Git 存储库的连接。将模板存储在 Git 存储库中。配置拉取请求工作流程以审核模板修改。为堆栈配置 AWS CloudFormation Git sync。
options.B: 在管道中添加手动审核操作，以便在堆栈部署之前审核对模板代码的修改。
options.C: 更新管道以调用 AWS Lambda 函数，在堆栈部署之前检查模板修改。
options.D: 在 AWS CodeConnections 中配置到 Git 存储库的连接。将模板存储在 Git 存储库中。将管道配置为包含使用该连接的源操作。在管道中添加手动审核操作，以便在堆栈部署之前审核模板修改。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

当前流程将 CloudFormation 模板存储在 Amazon S3 中，并通过 CodePipeline 部署这些模板。与 Git 存储库相比，这种方式无法提供同样原生的变更审核和版本历史工作流程，因此使还原和审核模板修改变得更加困难。公司需要在部署到生产环境**之前**进行人工审核，并且希望采用**最低运维开销**的解决方案。

## 正确答案：A

**配置 AWS CodeConnections 到 Git 存储库，使用拉取请求进行审核，并为堆栈配置 CloudFormation Git sync。**

CloudFormation Git sync 专为此工作流程设计。AWS 表示，Git sync 使团队能够通过源代码控制来管理堆栈，并使用**拉取请求和版本跟踪**来配置、部署和更新堆栈。CloudFormation 会监控存储库，并在获批的更改被提交或合并后自动更新关联的堆栈。它还可以在更新发生前添加一条描述堆栈更改的拉取请求评论。请参阅 [Syncing stacks with source code stored in a Git repository with Git sync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/git-sync.html)。

Git sync 使用 CodeConnections 将 CloudFormation 连接到 Git 提供商。通过拉取请求工作流程，团队成员可以在合并模板更改之前对其进行审核和批准；接受后，CloudFormation 会自动部署这些更改。CloudFormation 还会维护已应用于堆栈的提交历史记录。请参阅 [How Git sync works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/git-sync-concepts-terms.html)。

该解决方案直接解决了这两个问题：

- Git 版本历史使回滚到较早的模板修订版本变得简单。
- 拉取请求在部署前提供原生审核、评论和批准功能。
- CloudFormation Git sync 无需维护独立的 S3 上传和管道审批机制，因此运维开销最低。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 仅在现有管道中添加手动审核操作

CodePipeline 手动审批操作会暂停管道，直到审批者批准或拒绝该操作，但它本身不会将模板移入源代码控制，也不会提供 Git 原生差异比较、拉取请求和版本跟踪。AWS 文档指出，审批操作会显示可选的审核 URL 和评论，然后根据响应恢复管道或使管道失败。请参阅 [Manual approval actions in CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals.html)。

因此，此选项可以提供部署关卡，但无法充分解决场景中所述的模板版本控制和还原问题。

### C. 调用 Lambda 函数来检查修改

这要求公司开发、测试、保护、运行和维护自定义 Lambda 验证逻辑。它描述的也是自动检查，而不是明确的人工审核和审批工作流程。与托管式 Git sync 和拉取请求功能相比，自定义函数会带来显著更高的运维开销。

### D. 使用 Git 源操作并添加 CodePipeline 手动审核操作

此选项能够提供源代码控制并可限制部署，因此从技术上讲可以满足大部分要求。但是，它保留并扩展了管道工作流程，需要一个 CodeConnections 源操作以及一个单独配置的手动审批阶段。对于 CloudFormation 部署，AWS 文档介绍了创建变更集、暂停以进行手动审批，然后执行变更集的模式。请参阅 [Add a manual approval action for a CloudFormation deployment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-cloudformation-action.html)。

与选项 A 相比，此选项引入了更多管道配置和持续管理工作。CloudFormation Git sync 已经作为托管工作流程提供存储库监控、版本跟踪、拉取请求审核、可选变更摘要和自动堆栈同步。因此，D 不是运维开销最低的解决方案。

en.question: A company uses a trunk-based development branching strategy. The company has two AWS CodePipeline pipelines that are integrated with a Git provider. The pull_request pipeline has a branch filter that matches the feature branches. The main_branch pipeline has a branch filter that matches the main branch. When pull requests are merged into the main branch, the pull requests are deployed by using the main_branch pipeline. The company's developers need test results for all submitted pull requests as quickly as possible from the pull_request pipeline. The company wants to ensure that the main_branch pipeline’s test results finish and that each deployment is complete before the next pipeline execution. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the pull_request pipeline to use PARALLEL mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use QUEUED mode.
options.B: Configure the pull_request pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use QUEUED mode.
options.C: Configure the pull_request pipeline to use PARALLEL mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode
options.D: Configure the pull_request pipeline to use QUEUED mode. Configure the main_branch pipeline to use SUPERSEDED mode.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs different concurrency behavior for two pipelines:

- **Pull-request pipeline:** Every feature-branch pull request should receive test results as quickly as possible. Independent PR executions therefore should not wait for one another.
- **Main-branch pipeline:** Merged changes must be processed in order, without a newer execution overtaking an older one, so that test and deployment processing is allowed to finish in sequence.

## Correct answer: A

**Configure the `pull_request` pipeline to use PARALLEL mode and the `main_branch` pipeline to use QUEUED mode.**

- In **PARALLEL** mode, executions are independent, begin without waiting for other executions, and have no execution queue. AWS specifically identifies development environments with separate feature branches as a use case. This minimizes the time developers wait for pull-request test results.
- In **QUEUED** mode, waiting executions retain their order and do not overtake executions that have already started. A stage is locked while processing an execution, and subsequent executions wait in order for that stage. This ensures that main-branch test and deployment executions are not skipped or superseded by newer merges.

These behaviors are defined in the AWS documentation for [CodePipeline execution processing modes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html). CodePipeline also documents that the execution mode controls whether consecutive runs are queued, superseded, or run in parallel; QUEUED and PARALLEL require a V2 pipeline, as shown in [Set or change the pipeline execution mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/execution-modes.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **B — PR: SUPERSEDED; main: QUEUED:** The main-branch choice is appropriate, but SUPERSEDED mode is wrong for pull requests. In SUPERSEDED mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution waiting between stages, and the superseded execution does not continue. Consequently, some submitted pull requests might not receive complete test results.

- **C — PR: PARALLEL; main: SUPERSEDED:** PARALLEL is appropriate for fast PR feedback, but SUPERSEDED is inappropriate for the main branch. A newer merge could supersede an older waiting execution, so the older execution's remaining tests or deployment stages might never run.

- **D — PR: QUEUED; main: SUPERSEDED:** Both selections conflict with the requirements. QUEUED mode makes PR executions wait at locked stages, increasing feedback latency, while SUPERSEDED mode can prevent an older main-branch execution from completing all remaining stages.

zh.question: 一家公司采用基于主干的开发分支策略。该公司有两个与 Git 提供商集成的 AWS CodePipeline 管道。`pull_request` 管道具有与功能分支匹配的分支筛选器。`main_branch` 管道具有与 main 分支匹配的分支筛选器。当拉取请求合并到 main 分支时，将使用 `main_branch` 管道部署这些拉取请求。公司的开发人员需要尽快从 `pull_request` 管道获取所有已提交拉取请求的测试结果。公司希望确保 `main_branch` 管道的测试结果完成，并且每次部署完成后才执行下一次管道执行。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 `pull_request` 管道配置为使用 PARALLEL 模式。将 `main_branch` 管道配置为使用 QUEUED 模式。
options.B: 将 `pull_request` 管道配置为使用 SUPERSEDED 模式。将 `main_branch` 管道配置为使用 QUEUED 模式。
options.C: 将 `pull_request` 管道配置为使用 PARALLEL 模式。将 `main_branch` 管道配置为使用 SUPERSEDED 模式
options.D: 将 `pull_request` 管道配置为使用 QUEUED 模式。将 `main_branch` 管道配置为使用 SUPERSEDED 模式。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司需要为两个管道采用不同的并发行为：

- **拉取请求管道：** 每个功能分支拉取请求都应尽快获得测试结果。因此，独立的 PR 执行不应相互等待。
- **Main 分支管道：** 合并的更改必须按顺序处理，较新的执行不能超越较早的执行，以便测试和部署处理能够依次完成。

## 正确答案：A

**将 `pull_request` 管道配置为使用 PARALLEL 模式，并将 `main_branch` 管道配置为使用 QUEUED 模式。**

- 在 **PARALLEL** 模式下，各次执行相互独立，无需等待其他执行即可开始，并且没有执行队列。AWS 明确指出，具有独立功能分支的开发环境是一个适用场景。这可最大限度地缩短开发人员等待拉取请求测试结果的时间。
- 在 **QUEUED** 模式下，等待中的执行会保留其顺序，且不会超越已开始的执行。处理某次执行时，阶段会被锁定，后续执行会按顺序等待该阶段。这确保 main 分支的测试和部署执行不会因较新的合并而被跳过或取代。

这些行为在 AWS 关于 [CodePipeline execution processing modes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html) 的文档中进行了定义。CodePipeline 还说明，执行模式控制连续运行是排队、被取代还是并行运行；如 [Set or change the pipeline execution mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/execution-modes.html) 所示，QUEUED 和 PARALLEL 需要 V2 管道。

## 其他选项错误的原因

- **B — PR：SUPERSEDED；main：QUEUED：** main 分支的选择是合适的，但 SUPERSEDED 模式不适用于拉取请求。在 SUPERSEDED 模式下，较新的执行可以超越在阶段之间等待的较早执行，并且被取代的执行不会继续。因此，某些已提交的拉取请求可能无法获得完整的测试结果。

- **C — PR：PARALLEL；main：SUPERSEDED：** PARALLEL 适合快速提供 PR 反馈，但 SUPERSEDED 不适合 main 分支。较新的合并可能会取代较早的等待中执行，因此较早执行剩余的测试或部署阶段可能永远不会运行。

- **D — PR：QUEUED；main：SUPERSEDED：** 两种选择都与要求冲突。QUEUED 模式会使 PR 执行在线程锁定的阶段等待，从而增加反馈延迟；而 SUPERSEDED 模式可能会阻止较早的 main 分支执行完成所有剩余阶段。

en.question: A DevOps engineer needs to configure an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that publishes container images to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The pipeline must wait for the previous run to finish and must run when new Git tags are pushed to a Git repository that is connected to AWS CodeConnections. An existing deployment pipeline needs to run in response to the publication of new container images. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure a CodePipeline V2 type pipeline that uses QUEUED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all tags. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches container image pushes to start the existing deployment pipeline.
options.B: Configure a CodePipeline V2 type pipeline that uses SUPERSEDED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all branches. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches container image pushes to start the existing deployment pipeline.
options.C: Configure a CodePipeline V1 type pipeline that uses SUPERSEDED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all tags. Add a stage at the end of the pipeline to invoke the existing deployment pipeline.
options.D: Configure a CodePipeline V1 type pipeline that uses QUEUED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all branches. Add a stage at the end of the pipeline to invoke the existing deployment pipeline.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement analysis

The image-publishing pipeline must satisfy three independent requirements:

1. **Do not supersede an earlier run**—new executions must wait and run sequentially.
2. **Start when Git tags are pushed** through an AWS CodeConnections source.
3. **Start an existing deployment pipeline when a new image is published to ECR.**

## Correct answer: A

A **CodePipeline V2** pipeline in **QUEUED** execution mode is the required combination. In QUEUED mode, executions are processed one at a time in queue order, and AWS explicitly states that this mode requires a V2 pipeline. This ensures that a newly triggered execution waits rather than overtaking the previous execution. See [How pipeline executions work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html).

V2 is also required for advanced trigger filtering, including **Git tag** filters. AWS's pipeline-type comparison states that QUEUED mode and triggers that filter Git tags, pull requests, branches, or file paths are supported by V2 but not V1. See [What type of pipeline is right for me?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipeline-types-planning.html). For CodeConnections source actions, a push trigger can specifically use Git-tag include and exclude filters, so configuring an include pattern that matches all tags meets the source-trigger requirement. See [Automate starting pipelines using triggers and filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines-triggers.html).

Finally, successful ECR image pushes produce events that can be matched by EventBridge. The rule can use an `ECR Image Action` pattern with `action-type: PUSH` and `result: SUCCESS`, with the existing CodePipeline pipeline configured as the target. See [Create an EventBridge rule for an Amazon ECR source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/create-cwe-ecr-source-console.html).

Therefore, **A** meets all three requirements.

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **B:** `SUPERSEDED` does not guarantee that every previous run finishes before a newer run progresses; a newer execution can overtake an older one. It also filters **branches**, while the requirement is to start on new **Git tags**. Although V2 and the EventBridge integration are appropriate, these two settings violate the execution and source-trigger requirements.

- **C:** A V1 pipeline does not support trigger filtering on Git tags. It also uses `SUPERSEDED`, which allows newer executions to overtake older waiting executions instead of preserving sequential processing. Adding a final stage to invoke another pipeline does not correct either fundamental mismatch and would couple deployment triggering to this pipeline rather than directly matching successful ECR image-push events.

- **D:** QUEUED execution mode is not supported by V1 pipelines, and branch filtering does not meet the Git-tag requirement. The proposed downstream stage therefore cannot make this configuration valid.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师需要配置一个 AWS CodePipeline 管道，将容器镜像发布到 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 存储库。该管道必须等待上一次运行完成，并且必须在新的 Git 标签被推送到已连接至 AWS CodeConnections 的 Git 存储库时运行。现有部署管道需要在发布新容器镜像时运行。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置使用 QUEUED 模式的 CodePipeline V2 类型管道。向管道定义中添加一个包含所有标签的触发器筛选器。配置一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以匹配容器镜像推送事件并启动现有部署管道。
options.B: 配置使用 SUPERSEDED 模式的 CodePipeline V2 类型管道。向管道定义中添加一个包含所有分支的触发器筛选器。配置一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则，以匹配容器镜像推送事件并启动现有部署管道。
options.C: 配置使用 SUPERSEDED 模式的 CodePipeline V1 类型管道。向管道定义中添加一个包含所有标签的触发器筛选器。在管道末尾添加一个阶段来调用现有部署管道。
options.D: 配置使用 QUEUED 模式的 CodePipeline V1 类型管道。向管道定义中添加一个包含所有分支的触发器筛选器。在管道末尾添加一个阶段来调用现有部署管道。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和需求分析

镜像发布管道必须满足三个独立要求：

1. **不得取代先前的运行**——新的执行必须等待并按顺序运行。
2. 通过 AWS CodeConnections 源在推送 **Git 标签** 时启动。
3. **在新镜像发布到 ECR 时启动现有部署管道。**

## 正确答案：A

使用 **QUEUED** 执行模式的 **CodePipeline V2** 管道是所需的组合。在 QUEUED 模式下，执行会按照队列顺序逐个处理，并且 AWS 明确指出此模式需要 V2 管道。这可确保新触发的执行会等待，而不是超越先前的执行。请参阅 [How pipeline executions work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html)。

V2 也是高级触发器筛选所必需的，其中包括 **Git 标签** 筛选器。AWS 的管道类型比较说明，QUEUED 模式以及可筛选 Git 标签、拉取请求、分支或文件路径的触发器由 V2 支持，而 V1 不支持。请参阅 [What type of pipeline is right for me?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipeline-types-planning.html)。对于 CodeConnections 源操作，推送触发器可以专门使用 Git 标签包含和排除筛选器，因此配置一个匹配所有标签的包含模式即可满足源触发器要求。请参阅 [Automate starting pipelines using triggers and filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines-triggers.html)。

最后，成功的 ECR 镜像推送会生成可由 EventBridge 匹配的事件。该规则可以使用带有 `action-type: PUSH` 和 `result: SUCCESS` 的 `ECR Image Action` 模式，并将现有 CodePipeline 管道配置为目标。请参阅 [Create an EventBridge rule for an Amazon ECR source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/create-cwe-ecr-source-console.html)。

因此，**A** 满足全部三个要求。

## 其他选项为何不正确

- **B：**`SUPERSEDED` 不保证每次先前运行都会在较新的运行继续之前完成；较新的执行可以超越较早的执行。它还筛选 **分支**，而要求是在新的 **Git 标签** 上启动。尽管 V2 和 EventBridge 集成是合适的，但这两个设置违反了执行和源触发器要求。

- **C：**V1 管道不支持 Git 标签的触发器筛选。它还使用 `SUPERSEDED`，这允许较新的执行超越较早的等待执行，而不是保持顺序处理。在末尾添加一个阶段来调用另一个管道，既不能纠正这两个根本性的不匹配，也会将部署触发与此管道耦合，而不是直接匹配成功的 ECR 镜像推送事件。

- **D：**V1 管道不支持 QUEUED 执行模式，并且分支筛选不符合 Git 标签要求。因此，所提议的下游阶段无法使此配置有效。

en.question: A company is running an application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company needs to implement comprehensive logging for the control plane and the nodes. The company must analyze API requests to the Kubernetes control plane and must monitor container performance on the nodes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Enable AWS CloudTrail for control plane logging. Deploy Logstash as a ReplicaSet on the nodes to collect logs from the nodes. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to store and analyze the logs for the control plane and the nodes.
options.B: Enable control plane logging for the EKS cluster. Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Use CloudWatch Container Insights to collect logs for the nodes and the containers. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query and analyze the logs for the control plane and the nodes.
options.C: Enable API server control plane logging for the EKS cluster. Send the logs to Amazon S3 Deploy Kubernetes Event Exporter to the nodes to collect logs from the nodes. Send the logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query logs for the control plane and the nodes. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.
options.D: Use AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry to collect logs for the control plane and the nodes. Stream all the logs to Amazon Data Firehose. Use Amazon Redshift to analyze the aggregated log data for the control plane and the nodes.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs a low-operations observability solution that provides both:

1. **Kubernetes control plane visibility**, especially the ability to analyze requests made to the Kubernetes API server.
2. **Node and container performance monitoring** for the EKS worker nodes and workloads.

## Correct answer: B

**Enable EKS control plane logging to CloudWatch, use CloudWatch Container Insights for nodes and containers, and analyze the logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights.**

Amazon EKS control plane logging can send the `api`, `audit`, `authenticator`, `controllerManager`, and `scheduler` log types directly to CloudWatch Logs. In particular, Kubernetes **audit logs record the users, administrators, and system components that affected the cluster**, making them appropriate for analyzing Kubernetes API activity. AWS manages the control plane log delivery after it is enabled. See [Send control plane logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-logs.html).

CloudWatch Container Insights provides Kubernetes metrics at the **pod, node, and cluster levels** and collects infrastructure metrics and container logs through the CloudWatch agent and Fluent Bit. It can be managed through the Amazon EKS add-on lifecycle, reducing deployment and maintenance overhead. See [Enhanced Container Insights for Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/container-insights-eks-classic.html) and [Send container logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Container-Insights-EKS-logs.html).

CloudWatch Logs Insights can then query the EKS control plane audit logs. The EKS observability dashboard itself provides Logs Insights queries based on control plane audit logs and allows advanced queries to be opened in CloudWatch. See [Monitor your cluster with the observability dashboard](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/observability-dashboard.html).

This provides the required control plane auditing, node/container performance visibility, and centralized analysis through native AWS integrations with the least operational overhead.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. CloudTrail, Logstash, and OpenSearch Service

CloudTrail records calls to the **Amazon EKS service API**, such as EKS console and EKS API operations. It is not a replacement for Kubernetes API server and Kubernetes audit logs from inside the cluster. See [Log Amazon EKS API calls as AWS CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html).

Additionally, operating Logstash as a ReplicaSet and maintaining an OpenSearch ingestion and analysis pipeline introduces substantially more operational overhead than the native EKS-to-CloudWatch and Container Insights integrations. A ReplicaSet is also not the normal node-wide deployment model for ensuring a collector runs on every node; a DaemonSet is generally used for that purpose.

### C. S3, Kubernetes Event Exporter, Athena, and QuickSight

EKS control plane logging is natively delivered to **CloudWatch Logs**, not directly to Amazon S3. An additional export or subscription pipeline would be required. Moreover, Kubernetes Event Exporter exports Kubernetes events; it does not provide comprehensive node and container performance monitoring equivalent to Container Insights. The S3, Athena, and QuickSight pipeline also adds components and configuration without reducing operational overhead.

### D. AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry, Firehose, and Redshift

This is an unnecessarily complex custom telemetry pipeline. It does not replace enabling EKS-managed control plane log types for Kubernetes API and audit data, and it requires deploying and managing collectors, delivery streams, schemas, and Redshift resources. Redshift is also not the most direct managed service for interactive operational log analysis when the logs can be queried natively with CloudWatch Logs Insights.

zh.question: 一家公司正在 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上运行应用程序。该公司需要为控制平面和节点实施全面日志记录。该公司必须分析对 Kubernetes 控制平面的 API 请求，并且必须监控节点上的容器性能。哪种解决方案能够以最低的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 为控制平面日志记录启用 AWS CloudTrail。在节点上将 Logstash 作为 ReplicaSet 部署，以收集节点日志。使用 Amazon OpenSearch Service 存储和分析控制平面及节点的日志。
options.B: 为 EKS 集群启用控制平面日志记录。将日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch。使用 CloudWatch Container Insights 收集节点和容器的日志。使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 查询和分析控制平面及节点的日志。
options.C: 为 EKS 集群启用 API 服务器控制平面日志记录。将日志发送到 Amazon S3。在节点上部署 Kubernetes Event Exporter 以收集节点日志。将日志发送到 Amazon S3。使用 Amazon Athena 查询控制平面和节点的日志。使用 Amazon QuickSight 进行可视化。
options.D: 使用 AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry 收集控制平面和节点的日志。将所有日志流式传输到 Amazon Data Firehose。使用 Amazon Redshift 分析控制平面和节点的聚合日志数据。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查的内容

该公司需要一个低运维的可观测性解决方案，同时提供以下两项能力：

1. **Kubernetes 控制平面可见性**，尤其是分析向 Kubernetes API 服务器发出的请求的能力。
2. 对 EKS 工作节点和工作负载进行**节点及容器性能监控**。

## 正确答案：B

**将 EKS 控制平面日志记录启用并发送到 CloudWatch，使用 CloudWatch Container Insights 监控节点和容器，并使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 分析日志。**

Amazon EKS 控制平面日志记录可以将 `api`、`audit`、`authenticator`、`controllerManager` 和 `scheduler` 日志类型直接发送到 CloudWatch Logs。尤其是，Kubernetes **审计日志会记录对集群产生影响的用户、管理员和系统组件**，因此适合用于分析 Kubernetes API 活动。启用后，AWS 会管理控制平面日志的传输。请参阅 [Send control plane logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-logs.html)。

CloudWatch Container Insights 可在**Pod、节点和集群级别**提供 Kubernetes 指标，并通过 CloudWatch agent 和 Fluent Bit 收集基础设施指标及容器日志。它可以通过 Amazon EKS add-on 生命周期进行管理，从而减少部署和维护开销。请参阅 [Enhanced Container Insights for Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/container-insights-eks-classic.html) 和 [Send container logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Container-Insights-EKS-logs.html)。

随后，CloudWatch Logs Insights 可以查询 EKS 控制平面审计日志。EKS observability dashboard 本身就提供基于控制平面审计日志的 Logs Insights 查询，并允许在 CloudWatch 中打开高级查询。请参阅 [Monitor your cluster with the observability dashboard](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/observability-dashboard.html)。

该方案通过 AWS 原生集成提供所需的控制平面审计、节点/容器性能可见性和集中式分析，并且运维开销最低。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. CloudTrail、Logstash 和 OpenSearch Service

CloudTrail 会记录对 **Amazon EKS 服务 API** 的调用，例如 EKS 控制台和 EKS API 操作。它不能替代集群内部 Kubernetes API 服务器日志和 Kubernetes 审计日志。请参阅 [Log Amazon EKS API calls as AWS CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html)。

此外，将 Logstash 作为 ReplicaSet 运行并维护 OpenSearch 摄取和分析管道，相较于原生的 EKS 到 CloudWatch 以及 Container Insights 集成，会带来显著更高的运维开销。ReplicaSet 也不是确保采集器在每个节点上运行的常规节点范围部署模型；通常会为此使用 DaemonSet。

### C. S3、Kubernetes Event Exporter、Athena 和 QuickSight

EKS 控制平面日志记录原生发送到 **CloudWatch Logs**，而不是直接发送到 Amazon S3。因此需要额外的导出或订阅管道。此外，Kubernetes Event Exporter 导出的是 Kubernetes 事件；它无法提供与 Container Insights 等效的全面节点和容器性能监控。S3、Athena 和 QuickSight 管道也会增加组件和配置，并不能降低运维开销。

### D. AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry、Firehose 和 Redshift

这是一个不必要地复杂的自定义遥测管道。它不能替代为 Kubernetes API 和审计数据启用 EKS 托管的控制平面日志类型，并且需要部署和管理采集器、传输流、架构及 Redshift 资源。当日志可以使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 原生查询时，Redshift 也不是进行交互式运维日志分析的最直接托管服务。

en.question: A company wants to improve its security practices by enforcing least privilege across all projects. Developers must be able to access Amazon EC2 resources but not Amazon RDS resources. Database administrators must have access only to Amazon RDS resources. Every employee has a unique IAM user. There are already pre-existing IAM policies for developer and database administrator job functions. All AWS resources are already tagged with appropriate project tags. All the IAM users are tagged with the appropriate project and job function. The company must ensure that each employee can access only the project that the employee is working on. Which solution will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.A: For each project, create one IAM role for developers and one IAM role for database administrators. Tag the IAM roles with the corresponding projects and job functions.
options.B: Modify the pre-existing IAM policies to include a StringEquals ResourceTag condition for projects that match the PrincipalTag value. Attach the modified policies to the IAM roles for each job function.
options.C: Create an IAM policy that allows users to assume a role when the ResourceTag value matches the PrincipalTag value for project tags and job title tags. Attach the new policy to all IAM users.
options.D: Create an IAM policy that allows users to assume a role when the ResourceTag value matches the PrincipalTag value for project tags and job title tags. Attach the new policy to the IAM roles for each job function.
options.E: Tag the pre-existing IAM policies with the appropriate projects and job functions. Attach the modified policies to IAM roles for each job function.
options.F: For each project, create one IAM group for developers and one IAM group for database administrators. Add the appropriate users to each group so the users can assume their respective IAM roles.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs two independent controls:

1. **Job-function control:** Developers receive EC2 permissions, while database administrators receive RDS permissions.
2. **Project isolation:** A person can use those permissions only for resources belonging to the same project as the person.

The scalable solution is an **attribute-based access control (ABAC)** design using tags on users, roles, and AWS resources. AWS's IAM ABAC tutorial uses this exact pattern: users assume a role only when their tags match the role's tags, and the role's permissions allow access only when the role/principal tags match the target resource tags. See [IAM tutorial: Define permissions to access AWS resources based on tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_attribute-based-access-control.html).

## Correct answers: A, B, and C

### A. Create project- and job-specific tagged IAM roles

Create one developer role and one database-administrator role for each project, and tag each role with its project and job function.

This provides the attributes needed for both controls. For example:

- `Project=ProjectA`, `JobFunction=Developer`
- `Project=ProjectA`, `JobFunction=DBA`
- `Project=ProjectB`, `JobFunction=Developer`
- `Project=ProjectB`, `JobFunction=DBA`

AWS's ABAC tutorial similarly creates separate tagged roles for each project/team combination. Tags attached to an assumed IAM role are available through the `aws:PrincipalTag` request context, enabling downstream resource authorization. See [Pass session tags in AWS STS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_session-tags.html).

### B. Add matching project-tag conditions to the job-function policies and attach them to the roles

The existing policies already separate the service permissions:

- Developer policy: EC2 actions
- DBA policy: RDS actions

Adding a `StringEquals` condition that compares a target resource's project tag with `${aws:PrincipalTag/Project}` limits those actions to the role's project. The modified developer policy is attached to developer roles, and the modified RDS policy is attached to DBA roles.

Both services support tag-based authorization:

- EC2 policies can use resource-tag conditions for supported resource-level actions. AWS also notes that actions such as `Describe*` that do not support resource-level permissions need separate statements. See [Control access using attribute-based access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-policies-for-amazon-ec2.html).
- Amazon RDS supports ABAC policies that compare tags on principals and RDS resources. See [Attribute-based access control in policies with Amazon RDS tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html).

Thus, the role's job-function policy determines **which service** it can access, while the tag condition determines **which project's resources** it can access.

### C. Give every user permission to assume only roles whose tags match the user's tags

An identity-based policy attached to all IAM users can allow `sts:AssumeRole` only when the role's project and job-function tags match the user's `aws:PrincipalTag` values. For IAM roles, the role-resource comparison is typically expressed with condition keys such as:

```json
"StringEquals": {
  "iam:ResourceTag/Project": "${aws:PrincipalTag/Project}",
  "iam:ResourceTag/JobFunction": "${aws:PrincipalTag/JobFunction}"
}
```

This prevents:

- A developer from assuming a DBA role.
- A DBA from assuming a developer role.
- Any employee from assuming a role for another project.

AWS documents identity policies that allow users to assume tagged roles in [IAM: Assume roles that have a specific tag](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_examples_iam-assume-tagged-role.html), and the IAM ABAC tutorial shows the more specific pattern of comparing role resource tags directly with user principal tags.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### D. Attach the role-assumption policy to the job-function roles

The permission to call `sts:AssumeRole` must be granted to the identity making the assume-role request—in this scenario, the IAM user. Attaching that policy to the target roles does not give the users permission to assume those roles. After assumption, the role should provide EC2 or RDS permissions, not permission to bootstrap the original user into the role.

### E. Tag the pre-existing IAM policies

Tagging a managed policy does not make those policy tags the principal attributes used when an employee accesses EC2 or RDS. The relevant `aws:PrincipalTag` values come from the authenticated IAM user, assumed role, or session—not from tags on an attached managed policy. Additionally, merely tagging policies does not add the required resource-tag matching conditions. The permissions policies themselves must contain the ABAC conditions.

### F. Create per-project IAM groups and add users

IAM groups are collections of users to which identity-based policies can be attached. Group membership alone does not grant `sts:AssumeRole`; an appropriate permissions policy still must be attached. AWS also states that groups are permission-management constructs and cannot be authenticated principals in resource-based policies. See [IAM user groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_groups.html).

Groups could optionally be used to distribute the policy from option C, but the steps in F do not create or attach the required conditional assume-role policy and therefore do not meet the requirements by themselves.

zh.question: 一家公司希望通过在所有项目中强制实施最小权限原则来改进其安全实践。开发人员必须能够访问 Amazon EC2 资源，但不能访问 Amazon RDS 资源。数据库管理员必须只能访问 Amazon RDS 资源。每位员工都有唯一的 IAM 用户。开发人员和数据库管理员职能已有预先存在的 IAM 策略。所有 AWS 资源都已使用适当的项目标签进行了标记。所有 IAM 用户都已使用适当的项目和职能标签进行了标记。公司必须确保每位员工只能访问其正在参与的项目。哪种解决方案能满足这些要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 针对每个项目，为开发人员创建一个 IAM 角色，并为数据库管理员创建一个 IAM 角色。使用相应的项目和职能为 IAM 角色添加标签。
options.B: 修改预先存在的 IAM 策略，以包含一个 `StringEquals` ResourceTag 条件，用于匹配 `PrincipalTag` 值对应的项目。将修改后的策略附加到每个职能的 IAM 角色。
options.C: 创建一个 IAM 策略，当项目标签和职位标签的 `ResourceTag` 值与 `PrincipalTag` 值匹配时，允许用户担任角色。将新策略附加到所有 IAM 用户。
options.D: 创建一个 IAM 策略，当项目标签和职位标签的 `ResourceTag` 值与 `PrincipalTag` 值匹配时，允许用户担任角色。将新策略附加到每个职能的 IAM 角色。
options.E: 使用适当的项目和职能为预先存在的 IAM 策略添加标签。将修改后的策略附加到每个职能的 IAM 角色。
options.F: 针对每个项目，为开发人员创建一个 IAM 组，并为数据库管理员创建一个 IAM 组。将相应用户添加到每个组中，以便用户能够担任各自的 IAM 角色。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

公司需要两项相互独立的控制：

1. **职能控制：** 开发人员获得 EC2 权限，而数据库管理员获得 RDS 权限。
2. **项目隔离：** 人员只能对属于同一项目的资源使用这些权限。

可扩展的解决方案是使用用户、角色和 AWS 资源上的标签实现 **基于属性的访问控制（ABAC）** 设计。AWS 的 IAM ABAC 教程使用了完全相同的模式：只有当用户的标签与角色的标签匹配时，用户才能担任该角色；而该角色的权限仅在角色/主体标签与目标资源标签匹配时才允许访问。请参阅 [IAM 教程：根据标签定义访问 AWS 资源的权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_attribute-based-access-control.html)。

## 正确答案：A、B 和 C

### A. 创建按项目和职能划分且已添加标签的 IAM 角色

为每个项目创建一个开发人员角色和一个数据库管理员角色，并使用其项目和职能为每个角色添加标签。

这提供了两项控制所需的属性。例如：

- `Project=ProjectA`, `JobFunction=Developer`
- `Project=ProjectA`, `JobFunction=DBA`
- `Project=ProjectB`, `JobFunction=Developer`
- `Project=ProjectB`, `JobFunction=DBA`

AWS 的 ABAC 教程同样会为每种项目/团队组合创建单独的已标记角色。附加到已担任 IAM 角色的标签可通过 `aws:PrincipalTag` 请求上下文获得，从而实现后续资源授权。请参阅 [在 AWS STS 中传递会话标签](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_session-tags.html)。

### B. 向职能策略添加匹配的项目标签条件，并将其附加到角色

现有策略已经区分了服务权限：

- 开发人员策略：EC2 操作
- DBA 策略：RDS 操作

添加一个 `StringEquals` 条件，将目标资源的项目标签与 `${aws:PrincipalTag/Project}` 进行比较，可将这些操作限制为该角色所属项目的资源。修改后的开发人员策略会附加到开发人员角色，修改后的 RDS 策略会附加到 DBA 角色。

两种服务都支持基于标签的授权：

- 对于支持资源级操作的操作，EC2 策略可以使用资源标签条件。AWS 还指出，不支持资源级权限的 `Describe*` 等操作需要使用单独的语句。请参阅 [使用基于属性的访问控制访问权限](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-policies-for-amazon-ec2.html)。
- Amazon RDS 支持 ABAC 策略，用于比较主体和 RDS 资源上的标签。请参阅 [在 Amazon RDS 标签策略中使用基于属性的访问控制](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)。

因此，角色的职能策略决定其可以访问 **哪种服务**，而标签条件决定其可以访问 **哪个项目的资源**。

### C. 授予每位用户仅可担任标签与该用户标签匹配的角色的权限

附加到所有 IAM 用户的基于身份的策略可以仅在角色的项目和职能标签与用户的 `aws:PrincipalTag` 值匹配时，允许用户执行 `sts:AssumeRole`。对于 IAM 角色，角色资源比较通常使用如下条件键表示：

```json
"StringEquals": {
  "iam:ResourceTag/Project": "${aws:PrincipalTag/Project}",
  "iam:ResourceTag/JobFunction": "${aws:PrincipalTag/JobFunction}"
}
```

这可以防止：

- 开发人员担任 DBA 角色。
- DBA 担任开发人员角色。
- 任何员工担任其他项目的角色。

AWS 在 [IAM：担任具有特定标签的角色](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_examples_iam-assume-tagged-role.html) 中记录了允许用户担任已标记角色的身份策略，IAM ABAC 教程则展示了更具体的模式，即直接将角色资源标签与用户主体标签进行比较。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### D. 将角色担任策略附加到职能角色

调用 `sts:AssumeRole` 的权限必须授予发出角色担任请求的身份——在此场景中即 IAM 用户。将该策略附加到目标角色不会授予用户担任这些角色的权限。担任角色后，该角色应提供 EC2 或 RDS 权限，而不是提供将原始用户引导至该角色的权限。

### E. 为预先存在的 IAM 策略添加标签

为托管策略添加标签，不会使这些策略标签成为员工访问 EC2 或 RDS 时使用的主体属性。相关的 `aws:PrincipalTag` 值来自已验证的 IAM 用户、已担任的角色或会话，而不是来自附加的托管策略上的标签。此外，仅为策略添加标签不会添加所需的资源标签匹配条件。权限策略本身必须包含 ABAC 条件。

### F. 创建按项目划分的 IAM 组并添加用户

IAM 组是用户集合，可以向其附加基于身份的策略。仅靠组成员资格并不会授予 `sts:AssumeRole`；仍必须附加适当的权限策略。AWS 还指出，组是权限管理构造，不能作为资源型策略中经过验证的主体。请参阅 [IAM 用户组](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_groups.html)。

组可选择用于分发选项 C 中的策略，但 F 中的步骤并未创建或附加所需的条件性角色担任策略，因此其本身无法满足要求。

en.question: A company runs a development environment website and database on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. The company wants to make the instance more resilient to underlying hardware issues. The company wants to automatically recover the EC2 instance if AWS determines the instance has lost network connectivity. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group. Set the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to 1.
options.B: Add the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group. Configure a lifecycle hook to detach the EBS volume if the EC2 instance shuts down or terminates
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed_System metric. Add an EC2 action to recover the instance when the alarm state is in ALARM
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the NetworkOut metric. Add an EC2 action to recover the instance when the alarm state is in INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The instance hosts both the development website and its database on EBS storage. The requirement is to recover **that EC2 instance automatically** when AWS detects a system-level impairment, specifically loss of network connectivity caused by the underlying infrastructure.

## Correct answer: C

**C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the `StatusCheckFailed_System` metric. Add an EC2 action to recover the instance when the alarm state is in `ALARM`.**

AWS documents this exact configuration: monitor `StatusCheckFailed_System`, trigger the alarm when the system status check fails, and configure the EC2 **recover** action. System status-check failures include loss of network connectivity, loss of system power, and physical-host hardware or software issues. Recovery migrates/reboots the instance on healthy hardware while retaining its instance ID, private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses, and instance metadata. See [Configure CloudWatch action based recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/cloudwatch-recovery.html) and [Adding recover actions to Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/UsingAlarmActions.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Auto Scaling group with minimum, maximum, and desired capacity of 1

An Auto Scaling group maintains capacity by marking an unhealthy instance for replacement and launching a **new instance** from the group's launch template or launch configuration. It does not perform EC2 recovery of the original instance. For a stateful server containing a database on EBS, replacing it with a newly launched instance also does not inherently ensure that the replacement receives and uses the original instance's data volumes. AWS describes this replacement behavior in [Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-health-checks.html).

### B. Auto Scaling group with a lifecycle hook to detach the EBS volume

A lifecycle hook only pauses an instance during a lifecycle transition so that a **custom action** can be performed. It does not itself detach and reattach the EBS volume, recover the impaired instance, or configure the complete workflow required to make a replacement instance use the volume. Auto Scaling would still replace the unhealthy instance rather than recover the same instance. See [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html).

### D. `NetworkOut` alarm with the recover action in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`

`NetworkOut` measures the amount of outbound network traffic; low or missing outbound traffic does not establish that the underlying EC2 host has failed. Additionally, `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` means that the metric is unavailable or there is not enough information to determine the alarm state—it is not the state indicating a breached failure threshold. See [Metric alarm states](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarm-evaluation.html). Most importantly, AWS states that the EC2 recover action can be used only with `StatusCheckFailed_System`, not an arbitrary metric such as `NetworkOut`.

Therefore, **C** is the solution specifically designed for automatic recovery from an AWS infrastructure-level loss of connectivity.

zh.question: 一家公司在使用 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 存储的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行开发环境网站和数据库。该公司希望使该实例能够更好地抵御底层硬件问题。如果 AWS 确定该实例已失去网络连接，公司希望自动恢复该 EC2 实例。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 EC2 实例添加到 Auto Scaling 组中。将最小容量、最大容量和所需容量都设置为 1。
options.B: 将 EC2 实例添加到 Auto Scaling 组中。配置一个生命周期挂钩，以便在 EC2 实例关闭或终止时分离 EBS 卷。
options.C: 为 `StatusCheckFailed_System` 指标创建 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。当警报状态为 `ALARM` 时，添加一个用于恢复该实例的 EC2 操作。
options.D: 为 `NetworkOut` 指标创建 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。当警报状态为 `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` 时，添加一个用于恢复该实例的 EC2 操作。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该实例在 EBS 存储上同时托管开发网站及其数据库。要求是在 AWS 检测到系统级故障时，特别是由底层基础设施导致的网络连接丢失时，**自动恢复该 EC2 实例本身**。

## 正确答案：C

**C. 为 `StatusCheckFailed_System` 指标创建 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。当警报状态为 `ALARM` 时，添加一个用于恢复该实例的 EC2 操作。**

AWS 记录了这一确切配置：监控 `StatusCheckFailed_System`，当系统状态检查失败时触发警报，并配置 EC2 **recover** 操作。系统状态检查失败包括网络连接丢失、系统断电以及物理主机硬件或软件问题。恢复操作会在运行状况良好的硬件上迁移/重启实例，同时保留其实例 ID、私有 IP 地址、Elastic IP 地址和实例元数据。请参阅 [Configure CloudWatch action based recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/cloudwatch-recovery.html) 和 [Adding recover actions to Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/UsingAlarmActions.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. 最小容量、最大容量和所需容量均为 1 的 Auto Scaling 组

Auto Scaling 组通过将不健康的实例标记为待替换，并根据该组的启动模板或启动配置启动一个**新实例**来维持容量。它不会对原始实例执行 EC2 恢复。对于在 EBS 上包含数据库的有状态服务器，使用新启动的实例进行替换也并不能固有地确保替换实例会获得并使用原始实例的数据卷。AWS 在 [Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-health-checks.html) 中说明了这种替换行为。

### B. 使用生命周期挂钩来分离 EBS 卷的 Auto Scaling 组

生命周期挂钩只会在生命周期转换期间暂停实例，以便执行**自定义操作**。它本身不会分离并重新附加 EBS 卷、恢复受损实例，也不会配置使替换实例使用该卷所需的完整工作流程。Auto Scaling 仍会替换不健康的实例，而不是恢复同一个实例。请参阅 [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html)。

### D. 使用 `NetworkOut` 警报，并在 `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` 状态下执行恢复操作

`NetworkOut` 衡量出站网络流量；较低或缺失的出站流量并不能表明底层 EC2 主机已发生故障。此外，`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` 表示该指标不可用，或者没有足够的信息来确定警报状态——它并不是表示故障阈值被突破的状态。请参阅 [Metric alarm states](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarm-evaluation.html)。最重要的是，AWS 指出 EC2 recover 操作只能与 `StatusCheckFailed_System` 一起使用，不能用于诸如 `NetworkOut` 的任意指标。

因此，**C** 是专门为从 AWS 基础设施级别的连接丢失中自动恢复而设计的解决方案。

en.question: A company operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that host critical applications and handle sensitive data. The EC2 instances must have up-to-date security patches to protect against vulnerabilities and ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations. The company needs an automated solution to monitor and enforce security patch compliance across the EC2 fleet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager and AWS Config with defined patch baselines and compliance rules that run Systems Manager Automation documents.
options.B: Access each EC2 instance by using SSH keys. Check for and apply security updates by using package managers. Verify the installations.
options.C: Configure Auto Scaling groups that have scaling policies based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Configure Auto Scaling launch templates that launch new instances by using the latest AMIs that contain new security patches.
options.D: Use AWS CloudFormation to recreate EC2 instances with the latest AMI every time a new patch becomes available. Use AWS CloudTrail logs to monitor patch compliance and to send alerts for non-compliant instances.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs a fleet-wide solution that both:

1. Automates installation of approved security patches on EC2 instances.
2. Continuously evaluates patch compliance and remediates noncompliant resources.

## Correct answer: A

**Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager and AWS Config with defined patch baselines and compliance rules that run Systems Manager Automation documents.**

Systems Manager Patch Manager is purpose-built to automate operating system and application patching across fleets of managed EC2 instances. It can scan instances for missing patches or scan and automatically install them. A custom patch baseline defines which classifications, severities, and individual patches are approved and therefore what constitutes compliance for the organization. See [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html).

The `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` SSM document can scan managed nodes or install approved patches and reports patch compliance information to Systems Manager. See [SSM documents recommended for patching managed nodes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-ssm-documents.html).

AWS Config complements Patch Manager by evaluating the reported compliance state. The managed rule `EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STATUS_CHECK` checks whether an instance's Systems Manager patch compliance status is `COMPLIANT` or `NON_COMPLIANT`. See [ec2-managedinstance-patch-compliance-status-check](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ec2-managedinstance-patch-compliance-status-check.html). AWS Config can then remediate noncompliant resources by invoking Systems Manager Automation documents, including custom documents if required. See [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html).

This combination provides centralized patch policy definition, automated patch execution, compliance monitoring, and automated remediation.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Manually access each instance over SSH

This is a manual, host-by-host process. It does not provide scalable centralized automation, continuous compliance evaluation, or automatic remediation. It also introduces operational overhead and unnecessary reliance on SSH key access. Patch Manager is specifically designed to perform these operations across managed fleets without administrators logging in to each instance.

### C. Use Auto Scaling and launch templates with patched AMIs

Using patched AMIs is useful for immutable infrastructure and replacement instances, but Auto Scaling policies based on CloudWatch metrics address capacity and performance, not patch compliance. This design does not scan or remediate existing long-running instances, nor does it prove that every instance has all patches required by a defined compliance baseline.

### D. Recreate instances with CloudFormation and use CloudTrail for compliance

Rebuilding instances from patched AMIs can be part of an immutable deployment strategy, but recreating the fleet for every patch is unnecessarily disruptive and does not itself provide operating system patch-compliance evaluation. More importantly, CloudTrail records AWS account actions performed through the console, CLI, SDKs, and APIs; it does not inspect an instance's installed operating system packages or determine patch-baseline compliance. See [What Is AWS CloudTrail?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html). Systems Manager and AWS Config are the appropriate services for that compliance state.

**Answer: A**

zh.question: 某公司运营一组 Amazon EC2 实例，这些实例托管关键应用程序并处理敏感数据。EC2 实例必须安装最新的安全补丁，以防范漏洞并确保符合行业标准和法规。公司需要一种自动化解决方案来监控并强制实施整个 EC2 实例集群的安全补丁合规性。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置 AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager 和 AWS Config，并定义补丁基线和合规性规则，以运行 Systems Manager Automation 文档。
options.B: 使用 SSH 密钥访问每个 EC2 实例。使用包管理器检查并应用安全更新。验证安装情况。
options.C: 配置 Auto Scaling 组，并根据 Amazon CloudWatch 指标设置扩缩策略。配置 Auto Scaling 启动模板，以使用包含最新安全补丁的最新 AMI 启动新实例。
options.D: 每当有新补丁可用时，使用 AWS CloudFormation 通过最新 AMI 重新创建 EC2 实例。使用 AWS CloudTrail 日志监控补丁合规性，并针对不合规实例发送告警。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

公司需要一个覆盖整个实例集群的解决方案，同时能够：

1. 自动在 EC2 实例上安装已批准的安全补丁。
2. 持续评估补丁合规性并修复不合规资源。

## 正确答案：A

**配置 AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager 和 AWS Config，并定义补丁基线和合规性规则，以运行 Systems Manager Automation 文档。**

Systems Manager Patch Manager 专门用于自动化管理的 EC2 实例集群中的操作系统和应用程序补丁。它可以扫描实例以查找缺失的补丁，也可以进行扫描并自动安装补丁。自定义补丁基线用于定义哪些分类、严重性级别和单个补丁获得批准，因此也定义了组织中的合规标准。请参阅 [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html)。

`AWS-RunPatchBaseline` SSM 文档可以扫描托管节点，或安装已批准的补丁，并将补丁合规性信息报告给 Systems Manager。请参阅 [SSM documents recommended for patching managed nodes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-ssm-documents.html)。

AWS Config 通过评估报告的合规状态来补充 Patch Manager。托管规则 `EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STATUS_CHECK` 会检查实例的 Systems Manager 补丁合规状态是否为 `COMPLIANT` 或 `NON_COMPLIANT`。请参阅 [ec2-managedinstance-patch-compliance-status-check](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ec2-managedinstance-patch-compliance-status-check.html)。随后，AWS Config 可以通过调用 Systems Manager Automation 文档来修复不合规资源，必要时也可以使用自定义文档。请参阅 [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html)。

该组合提供集中式补丁策略定义、自动化补丁执行、合规性监控和自动修复。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 通过 SSH 手动访问每个实例

这是一种逐主机执行的手动流程。它无法提供可扩展的集中式自动化、持续合规性评估或自动修复。此外，它还会增加运维开销，并造成对 SSH 密钥访问的不必要依赖。Patch Manager 专为在管理员无需登录每个实例的情况下，对托管实例集群执行这些操作而设计。

### C. 使用带有已打补丁 AMI 的 Auto Scaling 和启动模板

使用已打补丁的 AMI 对不可变基础设施和替换实例很有帮助，但基于 CloudWatch 指标的 Auto Scaling 策略解决的是容量和性能问题，而不是补丁合规性。该设计不会扫描或修复现有的长期运行实例，也无法证明每个实例都安装了定义的合规基线要求的所有补丁。

### D. 使用 CloudFormation 重新创建实例，并使用 CloudTrail 进行合规性检查

从已打补丁的 AMI 重建实例可以是不可变部署策略的一部分，但针对每个补丁都重新创建整个实例集群会造成不必要的中断，而且其本身并不提供操作系统补丁合规性评估。更重要的是，CloudTrail 记录通过控制台、CLI、SDK 和 API 执行的 AWS 账户操作；它不会检查实例中已安装的操作系统软件包，也不会确定补丁基线合规性。请参阅 [What Is AWS CloudTrail?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html)。Systems Manager 和 AWS Config 才是处理此类合规状态的合适服务。

**答案：A**

en.question: A company has implemented a new microservices-based application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. After each deployment, the company wants to validate the critical user journeys and API endpoints before routing traffic to the new application version. The company must implement an automated solution to detect issues in the new deployment and to initiate a rollback if necessary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Set up Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights for the ECS cluster. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to analyze the task states. Program the Lambda function to use the ECS UpdateService API call to initiate a rollback if a specific percentage of tasks fail.
options.B: Set up Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights for the ECS cluster. Configure Application Insights to monitor key performance indicators of the microservices in the critical user journeys and API calls. Create CloudWatch alarms based on the insights. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Step Functions workflow to evaluate the alarms. Configure the workflow to initiate a rollback if necessary by using the alarms' built-in integration with Amazon ECS.
options.C: Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that simulate critical user journeys and API calls. Implement AWS X-Ray tracing for all the microservices Configure X-Ray to send traces to CloudWatch. Create CloudWatch alarms based on error rates and latency metrics. Create an AWS Lambda function to analyze the traces and to initiate a rollback if necessary by using the alarms' built-in integration with Amazon ECS.
options.D: Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that simulate critical user journeys and API calls. Configure the canaries to run against the new deployment. Create CloudWatch alarms that are invoked when canaries fail. Use the alarms’ built-in integration with Amazon ECS to initiate a rollback if the alarms are invoked before traffic is routed to the new deployment.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs a post-deployment validation mechanism that actively exercises the **critical user journeys and API endpoints against the new ECS revision before production traffic is shifted**, and that can automatically roll back a bad deployment. The key optimization is to use managed, native integrations instead of custom Lambda or Step Functions orchestration.

## Correct answer: D

**CloudWatch Synthetics canaries** are designed for active endpoint testing:

- API canaries can make multiple API calls and test REST API functionality.
- GUI workflow canaries can simulate actions such as clicking, entering data, and verifying page elements or text.

This directly addresses the requirement to validate user journeys and APIs. See [Using canary blueprints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_Blueprints.html).

Canaries publish native CloudWatch metrics such as `SuccessPercent`, `Failed`, `Failed requests`, `4xx`, and `5xx`, including per-step metrics when `executeStep()` or `executeHttpStep()` is used. CloudWatch alarms can therefore detect validation failures without custom trace-processing code. See [CloudWatch metrics published by canaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_metrics.html).

Amazon ECS supports associating CloudWatch alarms with deployments. If a configured alarm enters the `ALARM` state, ECS can mark the deployment as failed and, when rollback is enabled, automatically return to the last completed deployment. See [How CloudWatch alarms detect Amazon ECS deployment failures](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/deployment-alarm-failure.html).

For ECS deployment strategies that expose the new revision to test traffic, the green revision can receive test requests while the blue revision continues to receive production traffic. AWS also recommends CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback and lifecycle-stage testing. See [Amazon ECS canary deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/canary-deployment.html) and [Required resources for Amazon ECS blue/green deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/blue-green-deployment-implementation.html).

Thus, D combines managed synthetic validation, native CloudWatch metrics and alarms, and ECS automatic rollback, resulting in the **least operational overhead**. Strictly speaking, ECS polls the configured alarms and performs the rollback; the alarm does not call ECS as a conventional CloudWatch alarm action. The option's “built-in integration” is a reasonable description of this ECS deployment-alarm configuration.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

Monitoring ECS task states and rolling back when a percentage of tasks fail validates only infrastructure-level task health.
