Tasks can remain running while login flows, checkout journeys, or API responses are functionally incorrect. It therefore does not meet the requirement to validate critical user journeys and API endpoints. It also requires custom Lambda code and rollback logic, increasing operational overhead when ECS already supports alarm-based rollback.

### B

Application Insights can help identify application and resource problems, but passive KPI monitoring is not a substitute for actively executing the specified journeys and API calls against the new revision. The EventBridge and Step Functions alarm-evaluation workflow is also unnecessary: ECS can directly monitor configured CloudWatch alarms and roll back a failed deployment. Furthermore, the native ECS alarm integration belongs in the ECS deployment configuration rather than being a built-in Step Functions alarm-to-ECS rollback operation.

### C

The Synthetics portion is appropriate, but requiring X-Ray instrumentation for every microservice and a custom Lambda function to analyze traces adds substantial implementation and maintenance overhead. X-Ray is useful for diagnosing why a request failed, but it is not required to determine whether a canary journey or API check passed. Canary metrics can feed CloudWatch alarms directly, and ECS can use those alarms for automatic deployment failure detection and rollback.

## Final answer

**D**

zh.question: 一家公司已在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 集群上实施了一个新的基于微服务的应用程序。每次部署后，公司都希望在将流量路由到新应用程序版本之前，验证关键用户旅程和 API 端点。公司必须实施自动化解决方案来检测新部署中的问题，并在必要时启动回滚。哪种解决方案能够以**最低的运营开销**满足这些要求？

options.A: 为 ECS 集群设置 Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则来调用 AWS Lambda 函数以分析任务状态。对 Lambda 函数进行编程，使其在特定百分比的任务失败时使用 ECS UpdateService API 调用启动回滚。
options.B: 为 ECS 集群设置 Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights。配置 Application Insights 以监控关键用户旅程和 API 调用中微服务的关键绩效指标。根据洞察创建 CloudWatch 告警。使用 Amazon EventBridge 调用 AWS Step Functions 工作流来评估告警。配置该工作流，以便在必要时通过告警与 Amazon ECS 的内置集成启动回滚。
options.C: 创建 CloudWatch Synthetics canaries 来模拟关键用户旅程和 API 调用。为所有微服务实施 AWS X-Ray 跟踪。配置 X-Ray 将跟踪数据发送到 CloudWatch。根据错误率和延迟指标创建 CloudWatch 告警。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来分析跟踪数据，并在必要时通过告警与 Amazon ECS 的内置集成启动回滚。
options.D: 创建 CloudWatch Synthetics canaries 来模拟关键用户旅程和 API 调用。配置 canaries 针对新部署运行。创建在 canaries 失败时触发的 CloudWatch 告警。如果在将流量路由到新部署之前触发告警，则使用告警与 Amazon ECS 的内置集成启动回滚。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

公司需要一种部署后验证机制，该机制能够在生产流量切换之前，主动针对**新的 ECS 修订版本执行关键用户旅程和 API 端点测试**，并且能够自动回滚存在问题的部署。关键优化点是使用托管的原生集成，而不是自定义 Lambda 或 Step Functions 编排。

## 正确答案：D

**CloudWatch Synthetics canaries** 专为主动端点测试而设计：

- API canaries 可以发出多个 API 调用并测试 REST API 功能。
- GUI workflow canaries 可以模拟点击、输入数据以及验证页面元素或文本等操作。

这直接满足了验证用户旅程和 API 的要求。请参阅 [使用 canary 蓝图](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_Blueprints.html)。

Canaries 会发布原生 CloudWatch 指标，例如 `SuccessPercent`、`Failed`、`Failed requests`、`4xx` 和 `5xx`；在使用 `executeStep()` 或 `executeHttpStep()` 时，还会发布每个步骤的指标。因此，CloudWatch 告警无需自定义跟踪数据处理代码即可检测验证失败。请参阅 [canaries 发布的 CloudWatch 指标](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_metrics.html)。

Amazon ECS 支持将 CloudWatch 告警与部署关联。如果配置的告警进入 `ALARM` 状态，ECS 可以将部署标记为失败；启用回滚后，ECS 可以自动恢复到上一个已完成的部署。请参阅 [CloudWatch 告警如何检测 Amazon ECS 部署失败](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/deployment-alarm-failure.html)。

对于将新修订版本暴露给测试流量的 ECS 部署策略，绿色修订版本可以接收测试请求，而蓝色修订版本继续接收生产流量。AWS 还建议使用 CloudWatch 告警进行自动回滚和生命周期阶段测试。请参阅 [Amazon ECS canary 部署](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/canary-deployment.html) 和 [Amazon ECS 蓝绿部署所需的资源](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/blue-green-deployment-implementation.html)。

因此，D 将托管式合成验证、原生 CloudWatch 指标和告警以及 ECS 自动回滚相结合，实现了**最低的运营开销**。严格来说，ECS 会轮询配置的告警并执行回滚；该告警并不像传统 CloudWatch 告警操作那样调用 ECS。选项中所说的“内置集成”是对此 ECS 部署告警配置的合理描述。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A

监控 ECS 任务状态，并在一定百分比的任务失败时回滚，只能验证基础设施层面的任务运行状况。即使登录流程、结账旅程或 API 响应在功能上不正确，任务仍可能保持运行。因此，这无法满足验证关键用户旅程和 API 端点的要求。此外，当 ECS 已支持基于告警的回滚时，该方案仍需要自定义 Lambda 代码和回滚逻辑，从而增加了运营开销。

### B

Application Insights 可以帮助识别应用程序和资源问题，但被动的 KPI 监控无法替代针对新修订版本主动执行指定的用户旅程和 API 调用。EventBridge 和 Step Functions 的告警评估工作流同样没有必要：ECS 可以直接监控已配置的 CloudWatch 告警并回滚失败的部署。此外，原生 ECS 告警集成属于 ECS 部署配置的一部分，而不是 Step Functions 中内置的、从告警到 ECS 回滚的操作。

### C

Synthetics 部分是合适的，但要求为每个微服务实施 X-Ray 插桩，并创建自定义 Lambda 函数来分析跟踪数据，会增加大量实施和维护开销。X-Ray 对于诊断请求失败的原因很有用，但并非判断 canary 用户旅程或 API 检查是否通过所必需。Canary 指标可以直接馈送给 CloudWatch 告警，而 ECS 可以使用这些告警自动检测部署失败并进行回滚。

## 最终答案

**D**

en.question: A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances and use AWS Lambda functions in multiple AWS accounts. All EC2 instances have the Amazon CloudWatch agent installed. All accounts belong to the same organization in AWS Organizations. The company has created a dedicated central log account. All logs that the applications produce must be sent to a central location. The logs must be encrypted with keys that the company manages. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: In the central log account, enable logs as the data source in CloudWatch. Add the organization ID to the source account list. Create a CloudFormation StackSet by using the template provided by CloudWatch to enable central monitoring in all the organization's accounts.
options.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the central log account. Create an Amazon Data Firehose stream in the central log account. Set the S3 bucket as the destination of the Firehose stream. Create a log subscription in the central log account. Set the Firehose stream as a target of the subscription. Store the subscription log ARN in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for each project to use to send logs to the S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in each account. Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster in the central log account. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue in the central log account. Create an S3 trigger that sends events to the SQS queue each time a new file is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Create a Lambda function that processes each file and sends each file to the OpenSearch Service cluster.
options.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the central log account. Create an Amazon Data Firehose stream in each account. Set the S3 bucket as the destination of the Firehose streams. Create a log subscription in each account with the Firehose streams as a target.

en.explanation:
## Correct answer: A

The company needs organization-wide access to CloudWatch logs from EC2 instances and Lambda functions across multiple AWS accounts, using a dedicated central account and minimizing ongoing administration. Because all accounts are members of the same AWS Organizations organization, the lowest-overhead solution is to use **CloudWatch cross-account observability** with organization-based onboarding.

### Why A is correct

In the central log account, configure CloudWatch as the **monitoring account**, select **Logs** as the telemetry type, and allow the AWS Organizations organization ID as a source. The CloudWatch-provided CloudFormation template can then be deployed through a CloudFormation StackSet to configure all organization accounts as source accounts.

This approach provides centralized visibility into the source accounts' log groups without requiring a separate custom delivery pipeline in every account. AWS recommends organization-based linking because it scales across organizational units and can automatically onboard new accounts that are added to the organization. For the required setup and behavior, see:

- [CloudWatch cross-account observability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account.html)
- [Set up cross-account observability using AWS Organizations and CloudFormation StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account-Setup.html)

The company-managed encryption requirement is met by associating the relevant CloudWatch log groups with **customer-managed AWS KMS keys**. CloudWatch Logs supports associating a KMS key when a log group is created or afterward, subject to an appropriate KMS key policy. See [Encrypt log data in CloudWatch Logs using AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/encrypt-log-data-kms.html).

This native organization-wide configuration has less operational overhead than deploying and maintaining Firehose streams, subscription policies, S3 delivery permissions, queues, Lambda processors, or OpenSearch infrastructure in each account.

### Why B is incorrect

A cross-account CloudWatch Logs subscription cannot be established solely by creating a subscription in the central account and publishing its ARN through Systems Manager Parameter Store. The accounts containing the log groups must have sender-side subscription configuration, while the receiving side needs the appropriate destination and access policy. Storing an ARN in Parameter Store does not cause source-account logs to be forwarded.

AWS documents the required source- and destination-account configuration in [Sending CloudWatch Logs data to Firehose in a different account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CrossAccountSubscriptions-Firehose-Account.html).

### Why C is incorrect

This option creates a complex custom ingestion system consisting of:

- An S3 bucket in every account
- Cross-account S3 event delivery to SQS
- Custom Lambda processing
- A centrally managed OpenSearch Service cluster

The company would have to manage deployment, permissions, encryption, retries, scaling, failure handling, Lambda code, queue backlogs, and OpenSearch capacity. It also does not describe how EC2 and Lambda application logs are delivered into each S3 bucket or how customer-managed encryption is configured across all components. This has substantially more operational overhead than CloudWatch's native organization-level observability capability.

### Why D is incorrect

This architecture could physically deliver log events to a central S3 bucket, and CloudWatch Logs account-level subscription policies can apply a Firehose target to all or selected log groups in an account. Firehose also supports encryption with customer-managed KMS keys. See:

- [Account-level CloudWatch Logs subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters-AccountLevel.html)
- [Data protection and encryption in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/encryption.html)

However, D requires a Firehose stream and subscription configuration in **every account**, together with IAM roles, cross-account S3 permissions, KMS permissions, encryption configuration, monitoring, and lifecycle management. Each new account must also be provisioned with these resources. Therefore, even though this can be developed into a workable delivery pipeline, it has greater operational overhead than the Organizations-based CloudWatch setup in A.

## Conclusion

**Choose A.** CloudWatch cross-account observability, configured through AWS Organizations and a CloudFormation StackSet, provides the most scalable centralized monitoring solution. Associating the source log groups with customer-managed AWS KMS keys satisfies the encryption requirement while avoiding per-account log-delivery infrastructure.

zh.question: 一家公司的应用程序运行在 Amazon EC2 实例上，并且在多个 AWS 账户中使用 AWS Lambda 函数。所有 EC2 实例都已安装 Amazon CloudWatch agent。所有账户都属于 AWS Organizations 中的同一个组织。该公司已创建一个专用的中央日志账户。应用程序生成的所有日志都必须发送到一个中央位置。日志必须使用由公司管理的密钥进行加密。哪种解决方案能够以**最低的运营开销**满足这些要求？

options.A: 在中央日志账户中，将 logs 启用为 CloudWatch 中的数据源。将组织 ID 添加到源账户列表。使用 CloudWatch 提供的模板创建 CloudFormation StackSet，以便在组织的所有账户中启用中央监控。
options.B: 在中央日志账户中创建一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。在中央日志账户中创建一个 Amazon Data Firehose 流。将 S3 存储桶设为 Firehose 流的目标。在中央日志账户中创建日志订阅。将 Firehose 流设为该订阅的目标。将订阅日志 ARN 存储在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中，供每个项目用于将日志发送到 S3 存储桶。
options.C: 在每个账户中创建一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。在中央日志账户中创建一个 Amazon OpenSearch Service 集群。在中央日志账户中创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。创建一个 S3 触发器，使其在每次有新文件上传到 S3 存储桶时向 SQS 队列发送事件。创建一个 Lambda 函数来处理每个文件，并将每个文件发送到 OpenSearch Service 集群。
options.D: 在中央日志账户中创建一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。在每个账户中创建一个 Amazon Data Firehose 流。将 S3 存储桶设为 Firehose 流的目标。在每个账户中创建日志订阅，并将 Firehose 流设为目标。

zh.explanation:
## 正确答案：A

公司需要从专用中央账户访问多个 AWS 账户中 EC2 实例和 Lambda 函数的 CloudWatch 日志，同时尽可能减少持续管理工作。由于所有账户都是同一个 AWS Organizations 组织的成员，运营开销最低的解决方案是使用基于组织的 **CloudWatch 跨账户可观测性**。

### 为什么 A 正确

在中央日志账户中，将 CloudWatch 配置为 **监控账户**，选择 **Logs** 作为遥测数据类型，并允许该 AWS Organizations 组织 ID 作为源。随后，可以通过 CloudFormation StackSet 部署 CloudWatch 提供的 CloudFormation 模板，以将组织中的所有账户配置为源账户。

这种方法可集中查看源账户中的日志组，而不需要在每个账户中单独建立自定义传输管道。AWS 建议使用基于组织的关联，因为它可以跨组织单元扩展，并且能够自动将新加入组织的账户纳入其中。有关所需的设置和行为，请参阅：

- [CloudWatch cross-account observability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account.html)
- [Set up cross-account observability using AWS Organizations and CloudFormation StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account-Setup.html)

公司管理的加密要求可通过将相关 CloudWatch 日志组与 **客户自主管理的 AWS KMS 密钥**关联来满足。CloudWatch Logs 支持在创建日志组时或之后关联 KMS 密钥，但需符合适当的 KMS 密钥策略。请参阅 [Encrypt log data in CloudWatch Logs using AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/encrypt-log-data-kms.html)。

与在每个账户中部署和维护 Firehose 流、订阅策略、S3 传输权限、队列、Lambda 处理器或 OpenSearch 基础设施相比，这种原生的组织范围配置具有更低的运营开销。

### 为什么 B 不正确

无法仅通过在中央账户中创建订阅并通过 Systems Manager Parameter Store 发布其 ARN，来建立跨账户 CloudWatch Logs 订阅。包含日志组的账户必须配置发送方订阅，而接收方则需要适当的目标和访问策略。将 ARN 存储在 Parameter Store 中不会使源账户日志被转发。

AWS 在 [Sending CloudWatch Logs data to Firehose in a different account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CrossAccountSubscriptions-Firehose-Account.html) 中说明了所需的源账户和目标账户配置。

### 为什么 C 不正确

此选项创建了一个复杂的自定义摄取系统，包括：

- 每个账户中的一个 S3 存储桶
- 跨账户从 S3 传输事件到 SQS
- 自定义 Lambda 处理
- 集中管理的 OpenSearch Service 集群

公司必须管理部署、权限、加密、重试、扩展、故障处理、Lambda 代码、队列积压以及 OpenSearch 容量。该选项也没有说明如何将 EC2 和 Lambda 应用程序日志传输到每个 S3 存储桶，或如何在所有组件中配置客户自主管理的加密。这比 CloudWatch 原生的组织级可观测性功能具有明显更高的运营开销。

### 为什么 D 不正确

此架构可以将日志事件实际传输到中央 S3 存储桶，并且 CloudWatch Logs 账户级订阅策略可以将 Firehose 目标应用于账户中的所有日志组或选定日志组。Firehose 也支持使用客户自主管理的 KMS 密钥进行加密。请参阅：

- [Account-level CloudWatch Logs subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters-AccountLevel.html)
- [Data protection and encryption in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/encryption.html)

但是，D 要求在**每个账户**中配置 Firehose 流和订阅，以及 IAM 角色、跨账户 S3 权限、KMS 权限、加密配置、监控和生命周期管理。还必须为每个新账户预置这些资源。因此，尽管该方案可以开发为可行的传输管道，但其运营开销高于 A 中基于 Organizations 的 CloudWatch 设置。

## 结论

**选择 A。** 通过 AWS Organizations 和 CloudFormation StackSet 配置的 CloudWatch 跨账户可观测性，提供了最具扩展性的集中监控解决方案。将源日志组与客户自主管理的 AWS KMS 密钥关联可满足加密要求，同时避免为每个账户构建日志传输基础设施。

en.question: A DevOps engineer needs to implement a CI/CD pipeline in an AWS account. The pipeline must consume sensitive database credentials that are stored in an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter. The Parameter Store parameter is in a separate central account. The DevOps engineer needs to create and integrate the parameter with the CI/CD account. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.A: Use an advanced tier Parameter Store parameter to store the database credentials in the central AWS account.
options.B: Create an IAM role in the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline. Add the full ARN of the parameter to the IAM policy that is associated with the IAM role.
options.C: Use a standard tier Parameter Store parameter to store the database credentials in the central AWS account.
options.D: Use an AWS KMS managed key to encrypt the parameter. Grant decrypt permissions for the KMS key to the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline.
options.E: Use a customer managed AWS KMS key to encrypt the parameter. Grant decrypt permissions for the customer managed key to the AWS account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline.
options.F: Create an AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) resource share in the central AWS account. Share the parameter with the account that hosts the CI/CD pipeline.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The pipeline must retrieve sensitive database credentials from a Parameter Store parameter that is owned by another AWS account. This requires cross-account sharing of an encrypted (`SecureString`) parameter.

## Expected answers: A, E, and F

### A. Use an advanced tier parameter

**Correct.** Parameter Store supports cross-account sharing only for parameters in the **advanced tier**. Standard-tier parameters cannot be shared across accounts. See [Prerequisites for sharing parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html) and [Standard and advanced parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-advanced-parameters.html).

### E. Encrypt with a customer managed KMS key and grant cross-account decrypt access

**Correct.** A shared `SecureString` parameter must be encrypted with a **customer managed KMS key**. AWS explicitly states that the KMS key must be shared separately because AWS managed keys cannot be shared. The central account's key policy must authorize the external account or its role. For cross-account KMS use, the consuming principal also ordinarily needs an IAM permission such as `kms:Decrypt`. See [Prerequisites for sharing parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html) and [Allowing cross-account use of KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-modifying-external-accounts.html).

### F. Create an AWS RAM resource share

**Correct.** The owning central account shares the advanced parameter by adding it to an **AWS Resource Access Manager resource share** and specifying the CI/CD account as a consumer. The RAM permission for Parameter Store provides the resource-side read-only authorization for operations such as `GetParameter`. See [Sharing a parameter](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html).

## Why the other options are not selected

### B. Create a role and add the parameter ARN to its IAM policy

**Not sufficient as written, although it exposes an ambiguity in the question.** Merely adding an ARN to a policy does not grant anything unless the policy also specifies allowed actions such as `ssm:GetParameter`. In addition, retrieving a `SecureString` encrypted under a cross-account customer managed key requires appropriate `kms:Decrypt` authorization.

However, current AWS RAM documentation states that consuming principals can perform only actions allowed by **both** the RAM managed permission and their IAM identity-based policies. Therefore, a correctly written pipeline-role policy allowing `ssm:GetParameter` on the full parameter ARN is also normally required. The full parameter ARN must also be used when retrieving a shared parameter. See [Consuming principals in AWS RAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-terms-and-concepts.html) and [Accessing shared parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html).

Thus, **A/E/F are the intended three answers**, but B would represent an additional required consumer-side step if it were worded as an actual `ssm:GetParameter` permission.

### C. Use a standard tier parameter

**Incorrect.** Standard-tier Parameter Store parameters do not support cross-account sharing. The parameter must be advanced tier. See [Standard and advanced parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-advanced-parameters.html).

### D. Use an AWS managed KMS key

**Incorrect.** AWS managed KMS keys cannot be shared with another account. A shared `SecureString` parameter must use a customer managed key. See [Prerequisites for sharing parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html).

## Conclusion

The exam-intended combination is **A, E, and F**: create an advanced parameter, encrypt it with a shareable customer managed KMS key, and share the parameter through AWS RAM. Operationally, the CI/CD execution role also needs explicit SSM and KMS identity permissions, which makes the three-answer formulation incomplete or ambiguous under current AWS documentation.

zh.question: 一名 DevOps 工程师需要在一个 AWS 账户中实施 CI/CD 管道。该管道必须使用存储在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 参数中的敏感数据库凭证。该 Parameter Store 参数位于一个独立的中央账户中。DevOps 工程师需要创建该参数并将其与 CI/CD 账户集成。哪些步骤组合能够满足这些要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 使用高级层级 Parameter Store 参数，在中央 AWS 账户中存储数据库凭证。
options.B: 在托管 CI/CD 管道的 AWS 账户中创建 IAM 角色。将该参数的完整 ARN 添加到与 IAM 角色关联的 IAM 策略中。
options.C: 使用标准层级 Parameter Store 参数，在中央 AWS 账户中存储数据库凭证。
options.D: 使用 AWS KMS 托管密钥对参数进行加密。向托管 CI/CD 管道的 AWS 账户授予该 KMS 密钥的解密权限。
options.E: 使用客户自主管理的 AWS KMS 密钥对参数进行加密。向托管 CI/CD 管道的 AWS 账户授予该客户自主管理密钥的解密权限。
options.F: 在中央 AWS 账户中创建 AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) 资源共享。将该参数共享给托管 CI/CD 管道的账户。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该管道必须从由另一个 AWS 账户拥有的 Parameter Store 参数中检索敏感数据库凭证。这需要跨账户共享一个加密的（`SecureString`）参数。

## 预期答案：A、E 和 F

### A. 使用高级层级参数

**正确。** Parameter Store 仅支持对 **高级层级** 参数进行跨账户共享。标准层级参数无法在账户之间共享。请参阅[共享参数的先决条件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html)和[标准参数与高级参数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-advanced-parameters.html)。

### E. 使用客户自主管理的 KMS 密钥加密，并授予跨账户解密访问权限

**正确。** 共享的 `SecureString` 参数必须使用 **客户自主管理的 KMS 密钥** 加密。AWS 明确指出，必须单独共享 KMS 密钥，因为 AWS 托管密钥无法共享。中央账户的密钥策略必须授权外部账户或其角色。对于跨账户 KMS 使用，使用方主体通常还需要 IAM 权限，例如 `kms:Decrypt`。请参阅[共享参数的先决条件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html)和[允许跨账户使用 KMS 密钥](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-modifying-external-accounts.html)。

### F. 创建 AWS RAM 资源共享

**正确。** 拥有该参数的中央账户通过将高级参数添加到 **AWS Resource Access Manager 资源共享** 中，并将 CI/CD 账户指定为使用方，来共享该参数。Parameter Store 的 RAM 权限为 `GetParameter` 等操作提供资源端的只读授权。请参阅[共享参数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html)。

## 未选择其他选项的原因

### B. 创建角色并将参数 ARN 添加到其 IAM 策略中

**按原文表述并不充分，尽管它暴露了题目中的一个歧义。** 仅将 ARN 添加到策略中不会授予任何权限，除非该策略还指定了允许的操作，例如 `ssm:GetParameter`。此外，检索由跨账户客户自主管理密钥加密的 `SecureString` 还需要适当的 `kms:Decrypt` 授权。

但是，当前 AWS RAM 文档指出，使用方主体只能执行 **RAM 托管权限** 和其基于 IAM 身份的策略**同时**允许的操作。因此，通常还需要一个正确编写的管道角色策略，以允许对完整参数 ARN 执行 `ssm:GetParameter`。检索共享参数时也必须使用完整参数 ARN。请参阅[AWS RAM 中的使用方主体](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-terms-and-concepts.html)和[访问共享参数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html)。

因此，**A/E/F 是预期的三个答案**，但如果 B 的措辞是实际授予 `ssm:GetParameter` 权限，那么它将代表额外必需的使用方步骤。

### C. 使用标准层级参数

**不正确。** 标准层级 Parameter Store 参数不支持跨账户共享。该参数必须是高级层级。请参阅[标准参数与高级参数](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-advanced-parameters.html)。

### D. 使用 AWS 托管 KMS 密钥

**不正确。** AWS 托管 KMS 密钥无法与其他账户共享。共享的 `SecureString` 参数必须使用客户自主管理的密钥。请参阅[共享参数的先决条件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/parameter-store-shared-parameters.html)。

## 结论

考试预期的组合是 **A、E 和 F**：创建高级参数，使用可共享的客户自主管理 KMS 密钥对其加密，并通过 AWS RAM 共享该参数。在实际操作中，CI/CD 执行角色还需要显式的 SSM 和 KMS 身份权限，这使得根据当前 AWS 文档，该三项答案的表述并不完整或存在歧义。

en.question: A company is using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to develop a microservices-based application. The company needs to create reusable infrastructure components for three environments: development, staging, and production. The components must include networking resources, database resources, and serverless compute resources. The company must implement a solution that provides consistent infrastructure across environments while offering the option for environment-specific customizations. The solution also must minimize code duplication. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development overhead?

options.A: Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.
options.B: Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.
options.C: Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.
options.D: Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The company needs reusable components that combine networking, database, and serverless resources, plus one consistent infrastructure definition that can be customized for development, staging, and production. The least-overhead design is therefore to:

1. Encapsulate repeatable multi-resource patterns as higher-level constructs.
2. Reuse one set of stack classes.
3. Pass environment-specific configuration when those stacks are instantiated.

## Correct answer: C

**Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs from Level 2 (L2) constructs, and use a single parameterized set of deployment stacks.**

AWS defines L3 constructs as patterns that contain collections of resources configured to work together for a task or architecture. AWS also states that L3 constructs can configure multiple resources with the least input and code. Composition allows lower-level constructs such as L2 constructs to be assembled into reusable higher-level components. This is well suited to reusable networking, database, and serverless patterns. See [AWS CDK constructs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/constructs.html).

A single set of stack classes can accept an environment name or configuration properties and apply development-, staging-, or production-specific values. AWS demonstrates extending a stack to accept custom properties and then creating multiple differently configured instances of the same stack class in [Example: Create a CDK app with multiple stacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/stack-how-to-create-multiple-stacks.html). AWS CDK stages similarly support deploying the same grouping of stacks to multiple environments such as development and production, as described in [Introduction to AWS CDK stages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/stages.html).

This approach provides a common infrastructure definition, permits controlled environment-specific customization, and minimizes duplicated construct and stack code.

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A — Incorrect.** L1 constructs are not the appropriate abstraction for reusable multi-resource architectural patterns. An L1 construct maps directly to a single CloudFormation resource and provides no abstraction. A reusable component combining multiple L2 resources is a higher-level composed construct—effectively an L3 pattern—not a custom L1 construct. Although the parameterized single-stack approach is desirable, the proposed construct level is wrong.

- **B — Incorrect.** This has both disadvantages: it incorrectly characterizes reusable composites of L2 constructs as L1 constructs, and it creates separate deployment stack implementations for each environment. Separate environment-specific stacks increase duplicated code and ongoing maintenance compared with instantiating one parameterized stack definition.

- **D — Incorrect.** L3 constructs are appropriate, but maintaining separate deployment stacks for development, staging, and production adds unnecessary duplication. CDK context can supply configuration values, but it does not make three separately maintained stack definitions lower-overhead than one reusable stack class instantiated with environment-specific properties. The AWS examples explicitly support creating multiple configured instances from the same stack or stage definition.

zh.question: 一家企业正在使用 AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) 开发基于微服务的应用程序。该公司需要为三个环境创建可重用的基础设施组件：开发、预发布和生产。这些组件必须包括网络资源、数据库资源和无服务器计算资源。公司必须实施一种解决方案，以在各环境之间提供一致的基础设施，同时提供针对特定环境进行自定义的选项。该解决方案还必须最大限度地减少代码重复。哪种解决方案能够以**最低的开发开销**满足这些要求？

options.A: 在存在可重复模式的位置，基于 Level 2 (L2) constructs 创建自定义 Level 1 (L1) constructs。创建一组部署 stack，并在实例化时将环境名称作为参数传入。为每个环境部署 CDK application。
options.B: 在存在可重复模式的位置，基于 Level 2 (L2) constructs 创建自定义 Level 1 (L1) constructs。为每个环境创建单独的部署 stack。使用 CDK context command 确定向每个环境部署时要运行哪些 stack。
options.C: 在存在可重复模式的位置，基于 Level 2 (L2) constructs 创建自定义 Level 3 (L3) constructs。创建一组部署 stack，并在实例化时将环境名称作为参数传入。为每个环境部署 CDK application。
options.D: 在存在可重复模式的位置，基于 Level 2 (L2) constructs 创建自定义 Level 3 (L3) constructs。为每个环境创建单独的部署 stack。使用 CDK context command 确定向每个环境部署时要运行哪些 stack。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

公司需要可重用的组件，这些组件组合了网络、数据库和无服务器资源，并且需要一个可针对开发、预发布和生产环境进行自定义的一致基础设施定义。因此，开发开销最低的设计应当：

1. 将可重复的多资源模式封装为更高级别的 construct。
2. 重用一组 stack class。
3. 在实例化这些 stack 时传入特定于环境的配置。

## 正确答案：C

**基于 Level 2 (L2) constructs 创建自定义 Level 3 (L3) constructs，并使用一组参数化的部署 stack。**

AWS 将 L3 constructs 定义为模式，其中包含为某项任务或架构配置为协同工作的资源集合。AWS 还指出，L3 constructs 可以使用最少的输入和代码来配置多个资源。组合使 L2 constructs 等较低级别的 construct 能够组装成可重用的高级组件。这非常适合可重用的网络、数据库和无服务器模式。请参阅 [AWS CDK constructs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/constructs.html)。

一组 stack class 可以接受环境名称或配置属性，并应用特定于开发、预发布或生产环境的值。AWS 在 [Example: Create a CDK app with multiple stacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/stack-how-to-create-multiple-stacks.html) 中演示了扩展 stack 以接受自定义属性，以及创建同一 stack class 的多个不同配置实例。正如 [Introduction to AWS CDK stages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/v2/guide/stages.html) 所述，AWS CDK stages 同样支持将相同的 stack 分组部署到开发和生产等多个环境。

这种方法提供了通用的基础设施定义，允许进行受控的环境特定自定义，并最大限度地减少 construct 和 stack 代码的重复。

## 其他选项为何不正确

- **A — 不正确。** L1 constructs 并不适合作为可重用多资源架构模式的抽象。L1 construct 直接映射到单个 CloudFormation resource，且不提供抽象。组合多个 L2 resource 的可重用组件是更高级别的组合 construct——实际上是 L3 pattern——而不是自定义 L1 construct。尽管参数化的单一 stack 方法是理想选择，但所提议的 construct 级别不正确。

- **B — 不正确。** 此选项同时存在两个缺点：它错误地将由 L2 constructs 组成的可重用复合组件描述为 L1 constructs，并且为每个环境创建了单独的部署 stack 实现。与实例化一个参数化 stack 定义相比，单独的环境特定 stack 会增加代码重复和持续维护工作量。

- **D — 不正确。** L3 constructs 是合适的，但为开发、预发布和生产环境维护单独的部署 stack 会增加不必要的重复。CDK context 可以提供配置值，但与使用环境特定属性实例化一个可重用 stack class 相比，它并不会让三个需要单独维护的 stack 定义具有更低的开销。AWS 示例明确支持从同一个 stack 或 stage 定义创建多个已配置的实例。

en.question: A company runs an application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service by using the AWS Fargate launch type. The application consumes messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The application can take several minutes to process each message from the queue. When the application processes a message, the application reads a file from an Amazon S3 bucket and processes the data in the file. The application writes the processed output to a second S3 bucket. The company uses Amazon CloudWatch Logs to monitor processing errors and to ensure that the application processes messages successfully. The SQS queue typically receives a low volume of messages. However, occasionally the queue receives higher volumes of messages. A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution to reduce the processing time of message bursts. Which solution will meet this requirement in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.A: Register the ECS service as a scalable target in AWS Application Auto Scaling. Configure a target tracking scaling policy to scale the service in response to the queue size.
options.B: Increase the maximum number of messages that Amazon SQS requests to batch messages together. Use long polling to minimize the number of API calls to Amazon SQS during periods of low traffic.
options.C: Send messages to an Amazon EventBridge event bus instead of the SQS queue. Replace the ECS service with an EventBridge rule that launches ECS tasks in response to matching events.
options.D: Create an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances. Create a capacity provider in the ECS cluster by using the Auto Scaling group. Change the ECS service to use the EC2 launch type.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The workload is an existing Amazon ECS service on AWS Fargate that pulls long-running jobs from Amazon SQS. The queue usually has little work but occasionally receives bursts. The requirement is therefore to **temporarily add parallel consumers when the backlog increases and remove them afterward**, without paying for idle EC2 capacity.

## Correct answer: A

Register the ECS service as a scalable target in AWS Application Auto Scaling and use a target tracking policy based on the SQS backlog.

Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling can increase or decrease the service's desired task count to keep a target metric near a configured value. AWS specifically documents an SQS queue backlog-per-task metric calculated as:

`ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible / RunningTaskCount`

This metric can be used in a target tracking scaling policy for the ECS service. During a burst, Application Auto Scaling adds Fargate tasks, allowing more messages to be processed concurrently; after the backlog falls, it removes tasks. This directly reduces burst-processing time while retaining Fargate's pay-for-task-resources model and avoiding continuously provisioned infrastructure. See [SQS queue backlog per task](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/application-auto-scaling-target-tracking-metric-math.html) and [ECS target tracking service scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-autoscaling-targettracking.html).

In practice, the scaling metric should preferably be **backlog per running task**, derived from queue size and task count, rather than merely using raw queue depth. This makes the metric respond appropriately as service capacity changes.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### B. Increase SQS batching and use long polling

Long polling reduces empty and false-empty `ReceiveMessage` responses, while batching reduces API calls and associated costs. These are useful SQS efficiency optimizations, but they do not add ECS processing capacity. Because each message can take several minutes to process, retrieving more messages per request does not by itself provide the additional parallel workers needed to clear a burst faster. See [SQS long polling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-short-and-long-polling.html) and [batching message actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-batch-api-actions.html).

### C. Replace SQS with EventBridge and launch an ECS task for each event

EventBridge can use an ECS task as a target and invoke `ecs:RunTask`, but this unnecessarily redesigns the existing durable queue-consumer architecture. More importantly, successful EventBridge target invocation indicates that the task was launched; it does not monitor the several-minute business process through successful completion. EventBridge's delivery retry policy concerns delivery to the target, and events can be dropped after retries unless a DLQ is configured. The existing SQS queue provides natural backlog buffering, while scaling the ECS service supplies controlled parallelism without creating a task-launch workflow per message. See [EventBridge ECS tasks as targets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html) and [EventBridge retry behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-rule-retry-policy.html).

### D. Move the service to EC2 capacity

An EC2 Auto Scaling group capacity provider could scale cluster instances, but it introduces an additional infrastructure-scaling layer and EC2 instance management. It also does not, by itself, specify scaling the ECS service's task count in response to the queue backlog. For a low-volume, variable workload, Fargate is designed for serverless operation, variable demand, and payment only for resources used by running tasks. Moving to EC2 is therefore not the most cost-effective or operationally simple solution. See [Choosing ECS cluster infrastructure and capacity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/clusters.html).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS Fargate 启动类型在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 服务上运行一个应用程序。该应用程序从 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列中使用消息。该应用程序可能需要数分钟来处理队列中的每条消息。在处理消息时，应用程序会从一个 Amazon S3 存储桶读取文件并处理文件中的数据。应用程序将处理后的输出写入第二个 S3 存储桶。公司使用 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 监控处理错误，并确保应用程序成功处理消息。SQS 队列通常接收少量消息。但是，队列偶尔会接收大量消息。DevOps 工程师需要实施一个解决方案来缩短突发消息的处理时间。哪种解决方案能以最具成本效益的方式满足此要求？

options.A: 将 ECS 服务注册为 AWS Application Auto Scaling 中的可扩展目标。配置目标跟踪扩展策略，以响应队列大小来扩展服务。
options.B: 增加 Amazon SQS 请求批量获取消息时的最大消息数。使用长轮询，以在低流量期间尽量减少对 Amazon SQS 的 API 调用次数。
options.C: 将消息发送到 Amazon EventBridge 事件总线，而不是 SQS 队列。使用 EventBridge 规则替换 ECS 服务，以响应匹配事件来启动 ECS 任务。
options.D: 创建一个由 EC2 实例组成的 Auto Scaling 组。使用该 Auto Scaling 组在 ECS 集群中创建容量提供商。将 ECS 服务更改为使用 EC2 启动类型。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该工作负载是一个现有的、运行在 AWS Fargate 上的 Amazon ECS 服务，它会从 Amazon SQS 拉取运行时间较长的作业。该队列通常只有少量工作负载，但偶尔会收到突发消息。因此，要求是在积压增加时**临时添加并行消费者，并在之后将其移除**，同时无需为闲置的 EC2 容量付费。

## 正确答案：A

将 ECS 服务注册为 AWS Application Auto Scaling 中的可扩展目标，并使用基于 SQS 积压的目标跟踪策略。

Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling 可以增加或减少服务所需的任务数量，以使目标指标保持在配置值附近。AWS 专门记录了一个按任务计算的 SQS 队列积压指标，计算方式如下：

`ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible / RunningTaskCount`

此指标可用于 ECS 服务的目标跟踪扩展策略。在突发期间，Application Auto Scaling 会添加 Fargate 任务，使更多消息能够并发处理；积压减少后，它会移除任务。这可直接缩短突发消息的处理时间，同时保留 Fargate 按任务资源付费的模式，并避免持续预置基础设施。请参阅 [每个任务的 SQS 队列积压](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/application-auto-scaling-target-tracking-metric-math.html) 和 [ECS 目标跟踪服务扩展](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-autoscaling-targettracking.html)。

在实践中，扩展指标最好应为**每个运行中任务的积压量**，即根据队列大小和任务数量得出，而不只是使用原始队列深度。这样，指标能够随着服务容量的变化作出适当响应。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### B. 增加 SQS 批处理并使用长轮询

长轮询可减少空的和误判为空的 `ReceiveMessage` 响应，而批处理可减少 API 调用及相关成本。这些是有用的 SQS 效率优化措施，但不会增加 ECS 处理容量。由于每条消息可能需要数分钟才能处理完成，因此每次请求获取更多消息本身并不能提供更快清理突发消息所需的额外并行工作线程。请参阅 [SQS 长轮询](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-short-and-long-polling.html) 和 [批量消息操作](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-batch-api-actions.html)。

### C. 使用 EventBridge 替换 SQS，并为每个事件启动一个 ECS 任务

EventBridge 可以将 ECS 任务用作目标并调用 `ecs:RunTask`，但这会对现有的持久队列消费者架构进行不必要的重新设计。更重要的是，EventBridge 成功调用目标仅表示任务已启动；它不会监控需要数分钟才能完成的业务处理是否成功完成。EventBridge 的传递重试策略涉及向目标传递事件，若未配置 DLQ，事件可能会在重试后被丢弃。现有 SQS 队列提供了自然的积压缓冲，而扩展 ECS 服务可提供受控的并行处理，无需为每条消息创建任务启动工作流。请参阅 [作为目标的 EventBridge ECS 任务](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html) 和 [EventBridge 重试行为](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-rule-retry-policy.html)。

### D. 将服务迁移到 EC2 容量

EC2 Auto Scaling 组容量提供商可以扩展集群实例，但这会引入额外的基础设施扩展层和 EC2 实例管理。它本身也没有指定应根据队列积压来扩展 ECS 服务的任务数量。对于低消息量且需求变化较大的工作负载，Fargate 专为无服务器运行、可变需求以及仅为运行中任务所使用资源付费而设计。因此，迁移到 EC2 并非最具成本效益或运维最简单的解决方案。请参阅 [选择 ECS 集群基础设施和容量提供商](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/clusters.html)。

en.question: A global company uses Amazon S3 to host its product catalog website in the us-east-1 Region. The company must improve website performance for users across different geographical regions and must reduce the load on the origin server. The company must implement a highly available cross-Region solution that uses Amazon CloudFront. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Set up multiple CloudFront distributions. Point each distribution to another S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to direct users to the nearest distribution. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.
options.B: Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure global edge locations. Set up cache behaviors with optimal TTLs for static content and dynamic content. Configure origin failover to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.
options.C: Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure Amazon ElastiCache clusters in multiple Regions to serve as a distributed caching layer between CloudFront and the S3 origin. Set up a replication script to synchronize the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the script to run once a day.
options.D: Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in the eu-west-1 Region. Configure Regional edge caches. Implement AWS Global Accelerator to route requests to the nearest Regional edge location. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and an S3 bucket in a different Region.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company needs one globally performant CloudFront architecture that:

- serves users from geographically close edge locations,
- reduces requests to the primary S3 origin,
- survives an origin/Regional failure by using another S3 bucket in a different Region, and
- requires the least operational effort.

## Correct answer: B

A single CloudFront distribution already routes viewer requests to the CloudFront point of presence that can best serve the request, typically the nearest edge location by latency. CloudFront's edge and Regional edge caches improve performance and reduce requests to the origin. Therefore, separate distributions for each geography are unnecessary. See [How CloudFront works with Regional edge caches](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html).

Origin Shield adds another centralized caching layer in front of the origin. AWS specifically documents that it improves cache-hit ratio, consolidates duplicate requests, and reduces origin load for viewers distributed across different geographical regions. Because the primary S3 bucket is in `us-east-1`, selecting `us-east-1` for Origin Shield is also correct: when an AWS origin is in a Region where Origin Shield is available, AWS recommends enabling Origin Shield in the same Region. See [Use Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/origin-shield.html).

For resilience, CloudFront can place the primary and secondary S3 origins in an origin group and fail over to the secondary origin when the primary returns configured failure status codes. Origin Shield is compatible with these origin groups. See [CloudFront origin failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html).

Finally, S3 Cross-Region Replication maintains object copies in a bucket in another AWS Region without requiring a custom synchronization process. See [Replicating objects within and across Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html).

Thus, **B** combines CloudFront's global delivery, appropriate caching/TTL configuration, Origin Shield, managed S3 replication, and native CloudFront origin failover with the least operational effort.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

This uses multiple CloudFront distributions and Route 53 latency-based routing even though a single CloudFront distribution already directs users to an appropriate nearby edge location. It adds distribution, DNS, certificate, cache-policy, logging, and deployment-management overhead. Moreover, merely routing among distributions whose origins are different buckets does not provide the explicit primary-to-secondary origin failover behavior offered by a CloudFront origin group. It is therefore more operationally complex and less directly aligned with the high-availability requirement than B.

### C

Amazon ElastiCache is not needed as a caching layer between CloudFront and S3; CloudFront already supplies edge caches, Regional edge caches, and Origin Shield. Adding ElastiCache clusters in several Regions introduces substantial cluster-management and networking complexity. A once-per-day custom replication script can also leave the secondary bucket stale and requires the company to operate scheduling, retries, error handling, and monitoring. Managed S3 Cross-Region Replication is the appropriate lower-effort mechanism for copying objects across Regions.

### D

The S3 origin is in `us-east-1`, so choosing `eu-west-1` for Origin Shield is contrary to AWS guidance to use the same Region as an AWS origin when Origin Shield is available there. In addition, Global Accelerator cannot route to CloudFront Regional edge locations as endpoints. Supported standard-accelerator endpoints are Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances, and Elastic IP addresses—not CloudFront edge or Regional edge cache locations. See [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html). CloudFront already performs global edge routing, making Global Accelerator both unsuitable in the stated design and unnecessary.

zh.question: 一家全球性公司使用 Amazon S3 在 us-east-1 区域托管其产品目录网站。该公司必须提升不同地理区域用户的网站性能，并减少源服务器的负载。该公司必须实施使用 Amazon CloudFront 的高可用跨区域解决方案。哪种解决方案能够以**最少的运营工作量**满足这些要求？

options.A: 设置多个 CloudFront 分配。将每个分配指向不同区域中的另一个 S3 存储桶。使用 Amazon Route 53 基于延迟的路由将用户定向到最近的分配。在 us-east-1 中的 S3 存储桶与不同区域中的 S3 存储桶之间启用 S3 复制。
options.B: 在 us-east-1 中启用具有 Origin Shield 的 CloudFront。配置全球边缘站点。为静态内容和动态内容设置具有最佳 TTL 的缓存行为。配置到不同区域中 S3 存储桶的源故障转移。在 us-east-1 中的 S3 存储桶与不同区域中的 S3 存储桶之间启用 S3 复制。
options.C: 在 us-east-1 中启用具有 Origin Shield 的 CloudFront。配置多个区域中的 Amazon ElastiCache 集群，作为 CloudFront 与 S3 源之间的分布式缓存层。设置复制脚本，将 us-east-1 中的 S3 存储桶同步到不同区域中的 S3 存储桶。使用 Amazon EventBridge 将脚本安排为每天运行一次。
options.D: 在 eu-west-1 区域中启用具有 Origin Shield 的 CloudFront。配置区域边缘缓存。实施 AWS Global Accelerator，将请求路由到最近的区域边缘站点。在 us-east-1 中的 S3 存储桶与不同区域中的 S3 存储桶之间启用 S3 复制。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

公司需要一个全球高性能的 CloudFront 架构，该架构应当：

- 从地理位置接近的边缘站点为用户提供服务，
- 减少对主 S3 源的请求，
- 通过使用不同区域中的另一个 S3 存储桶来应对源或区域故障，以及
- 所需运营工作量最少。

## 正确答案：B

单个 CloudFront 分配已能够将查看器请求路由到最适合处理该请求的 CloudFront 接入点，通常是按延迟而言最近的边缘站点。CloudFront 的边缘缓存和区域边缘缓存可提升性能并减少对源的请求。因此，不需要为每个地理区域设置单独的分配。请参阅 [CloudFront 如何使用区域边缘缓存](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html)。

Origin Shield 会在源前方添加另一个集中式缓存层。AWS 明确说明，它可提高缓存命中率、整合重复请求，并减少分布在不同地理区域的查看器对源造成的负载。由于主 S3 存储桶位于 `us-east-1`，因此为 Origin Shield 选择 `us-east-1` 也是正确的：当 AWS 源位于支持 Origin Shield 的区域时，AWS 建议在相同区域中启用 Origin Shield。请参阅 [使用 Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/origin-shield.html)。

为实现弹性，CloudFront 可以将主 S3 源和辅助 S3 源放入一个源组中，并在主源返回已配置的失败状态码时故障转移到辅助源。Origin Shield 与这些源组兼容。请参阅 [CloudFront 源故障转移](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html)。

最后，S3 Cross-Region Replication 可在另一个 AWS 区域的存储桶中维护对象副本，而无需自定义同步流程。请参阅 [在区域内和跨区域复制对象](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)。

因此，**B** 结合了 CloudFront 的全球交付、适当的缓存/TTL 配置、Origin Shield、托管式 S3 复制以及原生 CloudFront 源故障转移，同时所需运营工作量最少。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

尽管单个 CloudFront 分配已可将用户定向到适当的附近边缘站点，此选项仍使用多个 CloudFront 分配和 Route 53 基于延迟的路由。这增加了分配、DNS、证书、缓存策略、日志记录和部署管理方面的开销。此外，仅在源为不同存储桶的多个分配之间进行路由，并不能提供 CloudFront 源组所提供的明确主源到辅助源故障转移行为。因此，与 B 相比，它在运营上更复杂，也不如 B 直接满足高可用性要求。

### C

不需要使用 Amazon ElastiCache 作为 CloudFront 和 S3 之间的缓存层；CloudFront 已提供边缘缓存、区域边缘缓存和 Origin Shield。在多个区域中添加 ElastiCache 集群会引入大量集群管理和网络复杂性。每天运行一次的自定义复制脚本还可能导致辅助存储桶中的内容过时，并且要求公司负责调度、重试、错误处理和监控。托管式 S3 Cross-Region Replication 才是在区域间复制对象时更省力的适当机制。

### D

S3 源位于 `us-east-1`，因此为 Origin Shield 选择 `eu-west-1` 违反了 AWS 的指导：当 AWS 源所在区域支持 Origin Shield 时，应使用与源相同的区域。此外，Global Accelerator 无法将请求路由到 CloudFront 区域边缘站点作为端点。支持的标准加速器端点包括 Network Load Balancers、Application Load Balancers、EC2 实例和 Elastic IP 地址，而不包括 CloudFront 边缘站点或区域边缘缓存站点。请参阅 [AWS Global Accelerator 中标准加速器的端点](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html)。CloudFront 已执行全球边缘路由，因此在所述设计中，Global Accelerator 既不适用也没有必要。

en.question: A company is using AWS CodeDeploy to deploy applications to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. During a recent deployment, several EC2 instances failed to update successfully. A DevOps engineer must investigate the root cause of the failures and must determine which specific deployment lifecycle events encountered errors. What is the MOST operationally efficient way to access and analyze the detailed deployment logs for troubleshooting?

options.A: Use SSH to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
options.B: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store CodeDeploy logs. Update the appspec.yml file to copy logs to the S3 bucket. Query the S3 bucket by using Amazon Athena
options.D: Send CodeDeploy agent logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the CloudWatch agent. Analyze the logs by using CloudWatch Logs Insights.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The engineer needs the **most operationally efficient** way to investigate failures across multiple EC2 instances and identify errors in specific CodeDeploy deployment lifecycle events. The key requirement is centralized collection and searchable analysis of the detailed CodeDeploy agent and deployment logs, rather than connecting to instances individually.

## Correct answer: D

**Send CodeDeploy agent logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the CloudWatch agent, and analyze them with CloudWatch Logs Insights.**

AWS explicitly documents that the CloudWatch agent can collect both:

- The CodeDeploy agent log, such as `/var/log/aws/codedeploy-agent/codedeploy-agent.log`
- The aggregate deployment log, such as `/opt/codedeploy-agent/deployment-root/deployment-logs/codedeploy-agent-deployments.log`

These can be sent to instance-specific log streams in centralized CloudWatch log groups. See [Send CodeDeploy agent logs to CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/codedeploy-agent-operations-cloudwatch-agent.html).

AWS also specifically recommends CloudWatch for centrally monitoring CodeDeploy log files instead of viewing them instance by instance. The deployment and script logs contain deployment events, errors, and script output that can reveal which lifecycle event or hook failed. See [View log data for CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-view-logs.html).

Once centralized, CloudWatch Logs Insights can interactively search, filter, correlate, and aggregate log data across the affected instances. AWS states that Logs Insights helps identify potential causes of operational issues and validate fixes. See [Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. SSH to every failed instance

SSH can provide access to the local CodeDeploy logs, so it is technically possible. However, it requires connecting to and inspecting each failed instance separately, potentially maintaining SSH keys and network access. AWS recommends centralized CloudWatch monitoring rather than viewing CodeDeploy logs instance by instance. Therefore, this is not the most operationally efficient approach.

### B. Use Systems Manager Session Manager for every failed instance

Session Manager is operationally preferable to SSH because it does not require inbound SSH access or SSH key management. However, this option still requires an engineer to open a session to each affected instance and manually inspect its local logs. It does not provide the centralized cross-instance querying and correlation available through CloudWatch Logs Insights, so it is less efficient than D.

### C. Copy logs to S3 through `appspec.yml` and query with Athena

This requires implementing and maintaining custom deployment-hook scripts, an S3 log-delivery convention, and Athena tables or parsing logic. It can also be unreliable for this purpose if the lifecycle event responsible for copying the logs is itself skipped or fails. CodeDeploy already has a documented integration pattern for forwarding its agent and deployment logs through the CloudWatch agent, making the proposed S3/Athena solution unnecessary operational overhead.

Therefore, **D** is the best answer.

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 AWS CodeDeploy 将应用程序部署到一组 Amazon EC2 实例。在最近一次部署期间，多个 EC2 实例未能成功更新。DevOps 工程师必须调查这些失败的根本原因，并确定哪些特定的部署生命周期事件遇到了错误。访问和分析详细部署日志以进行故障排除的**运维效率最高**的方法是什么？

options.A: 使用 SSH 连接到每个未能成功更新的 EC2 实例。读取 CodeDeploy agent 的日志。
options.B: 使用 AWS Systems Manager Session Manager 连接到每个未能成功更新的 EC2 实例。读取 CodeDeploy agent 的日志。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon S3 存储桶来存储 CodeDeploy 日志。更新 appspec.yml 文件以将日志复制到 S3 存储桶。使用 Amazon Athena 查询该 S3 存储桶。
options.D: 使用 CloudWatch agent 将 CodeDeploy agent 日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch Logs。使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 分析日志。

zh.explanation:
## 题目要求

该工程师需要采用**运维效率最高**的方法来调查多个 EC2 实例上的失败，并识别在特定 CodeDeploy 部署生命周期事件中发生的错误。关键要求是集中收集并可搜索地分析详细的 CodeDeploy agent 和部署日志，而不是逐一连接到各个实例。

## 正确答案：D

**使用 CloudWatch agent 将 CodeDeploy agent 日志发送到 Amazon CloudWatch Logs，并使用 CloudWatch Logs Insights 进行分析。**

AWS 明确说明，CloudWatch agent 可以同时收集：

- CodeDeploy agent 日志，例如 `/var/log/aws/codedeploy-agent/codedeploy-agent.log`
- 聚合部署日志，例如 `/opt/codedeploy-agent/deployment-root/deployment-logs/codedeploy-agent-deployments.log`

这些日志可以发送到集中式 CloudWatch 日志组中按实例划分的日志流。请参阅 [Send CodeDeploy agent logs to CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/codedeploy-agent-operations-cloudwatch-agent.html)。

AWS 还特别建议使用 CloudWatch 集中监控 CodeDeploy 日志文件，而不是逐个实例查看。部署和脚本日志包含部署事件、错误和脚本输出，可用于确定哪个生命周期事件或 hook 失败。请参阅 [View log data for CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-view-logs.html)。

日志集中后，CloudWatch Logs Insights 可以跨受影响的实例交互式搜索、筛选、关联和聚合日志数据。AWS 指出，Logs Insights 有助于识别运维问题的潜在原因并验证修复措施。请参阅 [Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. 通过 SSH 连接到每个失败的实例

SSH 可以访问本地 CodeDeploy 日志，因此从技术上讲可行。但是，这需要分别连接并检查每个失败的实例，并且可能需要维护 SSH 密钥和网络访问。AWS 建议使用集中式 CloudWatch 监控，而不是逐个实例查看 CodeDeploy 日志。因此，这不是运维效率最高的方法。

### B. 对每个失败的实例使用 Systems Manager Session Manager

Session Manager 在运维方面优于 SSH，因为它不需要入站 SSH 访问或 SSH 密钥管理。但是，此选项仍要求工程师打开与每个受影响实例的会话，并手动检查其本地日志。它无法提供 CloudWatch Logs Insights 所具备的跨实例集中查询和关联功能，因此其效率低于 D。

### C. 通过 `appspec.yml` 将日志复制到 S3 并使用 Athena 查询

这需要实施和维护自定义部署 hook 脚本、S3 日志传输规范以及 Athena 表或解析逻辑。如果负责复制日志的生命周期事件本身被跳过或失败，此方案还可能不可靠。CodeDeploy 已提供通过 CloudWatch agent 转发其 agent 和部署日志的文档化集成模式，因此所提出的 S3/Athena 方案会带来不必要的运维开销。

因此，**D** 是最佳答案。

en.question: A company built its serverless infrastructure on AWS. The infrastructure consists of an Amazon API Gateway REST API, multiple AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon EventBridge. The company wants to be aware of any new supply chain attacks that the company's CI/CD pipelines do not catch. The company needs a solution to detect malicious activity in the deployed application. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS WAF for the API Gateway REST API. Configure an AWS WAF ACL. Add the known bad inputs managed rule group.
options.B: Enable Amazon GuardDuty. Enable Lambda Protection. Use EventBridge for event notifications.
options.C: Deploy AWS CloudFormation Guard in the CI/CD pipelines. Write rules to catch the supply chain attacks.
options.D: Create a firewall in AWS Network Firewall. Configure a policy. Add the managed rule for the Emerging Threats rule group.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The company is concerned about a supply-chain compromise that passes through CI/CD controls and becomes active **after deployment**. Therefore, the solution must monitor the running serverless workload for malicious behavior and generate notifications when suspicious activity is detected.

## Correct answer: B

**Enable Amazon GuardDuty, enable Lambda Protection, and use EventBridge for event notifications.**

GuardDuty Lambda Protection monitors the network activity generated when Lambda functions are invoked and analyzes it for potential threats. This is appropriate for detecting runtime behavior from a compromised function or malicious dependency that was not identified during the build and deployment process. GuardDuty can generate Lambda-specific findings for behaviors such as communication with command-and-control infrastructure, cryptocurrency-related endpoints, malware drop points, and Tor nodes. See [Lambda Network Activity Monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/lambda-protection.html) and [Lambda Protection finding types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/lambda-protection-finding-types.html).

GuardDuty findings are delivered to EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can filter GuardDuty findings and route them to a target such as Amazon SNS or a Lambda function for notification or automated response. See [Using Amazon EventBridge for GuardDuty findings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_eventbridge.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. AWS WAF with the Known Bad Inputs managed rule group

AWS WAF protects the API endpoint by inspecting incoming web requests. The Known Bad Inputs rule group blocks request patterns associated with vulnerability discovery and exploitation, such as certain RCE attempts. It does not monitor the behavior of deployed Lambda code or detect a malicious package that begins making suspicious outbound connections after deployment. See [Known bad inputs managed rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-baseline.html).

### C. CloudFormation Guard in the CI/CD pipelines

CloudFormation Guard performs policy-as-code validation of structured data such as CloudFormation templates and change sets. It is useful for preventive governance, compliance, and deployment-safety checks, but it does not analyze the runtime behavior of deployed Lambda functions. The scenario specifically requires detection of attacks that the CI/CD pipelines failed to catch. See [Guard features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cfn-guard/latest/ug/what-is-guard.html).

### D. AWS Network Firewall with an Emerging Threats rule group

AWS Network Firewall filters traffic at the perimeter of a VPC by using stateless and stateful rule groups. It is a VPC network filtering and intrusion prevention control, not a service specifically designed to monitor Lambda runtime network activity and produce Lambda-focused compromise findings. It would also require the relevant traffic to be routed through firewall endpoints and would not inherently cover non-VPC Lambda networking. See [Filter network traffic using AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/network-firewall.html).

Therefore, **B** provides the required post-deployment threat detection and notification capability for the serverless application.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS 上构建了其无服务器基础设施。该基础设施包括一个 Amazon API Gateway REST API、多个 AWS Lambda 函数和 Amazon EventBridge。该公司希望能够发现其 CI/CD 管道未捕获的任何新的软件供应链攻击。该公司需要一种解决方案来检测已部署应用程序中的恶意活动。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 为 API Gateway REST API 启用 AWS WAF。配置一个 AWS WAF ACL。添加 Known Bad Inputs 托管规则组。
options.B: 启用 Amazon GuardDuty。启用 Lambda Protection。使用 EventBridge 进行事件通知。
options.C: 在 CI/CD 管道中部署 AWS CloudFormation Guard。编写规则来捕获软件供应链攻击。
options.D: 在 AWS Network Firewall 中创建防火墙。配置策略。添加 Emerging Threats 规则组的托管规则。

zh.explanation:
## 问题所问内容

该公司担心软件供应链遭到入侵，而该入侵能够绕过 CI/CD 控制措施并在**部署后**变得活跃。因此，该解决方案必须监控正在运行的无服务器工作负载是否存在恶意行为，并在检测到可疑活动时生成通知。

## 正确答案：B

**启用 Amazon GuardDuty，启用 Lambda Protection，并使用 EventBridge 进行事件通知。**

GuardDuty Lambda Protection 会监控调用 Lambda 函数时产生的网络活动，并对其进行分析以发现潜在威胁。这适合检测在构建和部署过程中未被识别的、来自已遭入侵函数或恶意依赖项的运行时行为。GuardDuty 可以针对诸如与命令与控制基础设施通信、加密货币相关端点、恶意软件投放点和 Tor 节点等行为生成 Lambda 专属发现结果。请参阅 [Lambda Network Activity Monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/lambda-protection.html) 和 [Lambda Protection finding types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/lambda-protection-finding-types.html)。

GuardDuty 发现结果会传送到 EventBridge。EventBridge 规则可以筛选 GuardDuty 发现结果，并将其路由到 Amazon SNS 或 Lambda 函数等目标，以进行通知或自动响应。请参阅 [Using Amazon EventBridge for GuardDuty findings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_eventbridge.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A. 使用 Known Bad Inputs 托管规则组的 AWS WAF

AWS WAF 通过检查传入的 Web 请求来保护 API 端点。Known Bad Inputs 规则组会阻止与漏洞发现和利用相关的请求模式，例如某些 RCE 尝试。它不会监控已部署 Lambda 代码的行为，也不会检测在部署后开始建立可疑出站连接的恶意软件包。请参阅 [Known bad inputs managed rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-baseline.html)。

### C. CI/CD 管道中的 CloudFormation Guard

CloudFormation Guard 会对 CloudFormation 模板和变更集等结构化数据执行策略即代码验证。它适用于预防性治理、合规性和部署安全检查，但不会分析已部署 Lambda 函数的运行时行为。该场景明确要求检测 CI/CD 管道未能捕获的攻击。请参阅 [Guard features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cfn-guard/latest/ug/what-is-guard.html)。

### D. 使用 Emerging Threats 规则组的 AWS Network Firewall

AWS Network Firewall 使用无状态和有状态规则组在 VPC 边界过滤流量。它是一种 VPC 网络过滤和入侵防御控制措施，并非专门设计用于监控 Lambda 运行时网络活动和生成以 Lambda 为中心的入侵发现结果的服务。此外，它要求相关流量通过防火墙端点进行路由，也无法天然覆盖非 VPC Lambda 网络。请参阅 [Filter network traffic using AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/network-firewall.html)。

因此，**B** 为该无服务器应用程序提供了所需的部署后威胁检测和通知功能。

en.question: A company has a stateless web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in a target group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Amazon Route 53 manages the application domain. The company updates the application UI and develops a beta version of the application. The company wants to test the beta version on 10% of its traffic. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST number of configuration changes?

options.A: Deploy the beta version to new EC2 instances in a new target group. Associate the new target group with a new ALB. Update the existing Route 53 record to use a weighted routing policy. Add a new Route 53 record that points to the new ALB with the same routing policy. Assign a weight of 90 to the existing record. Assign a weight of 10 to the new record.
options.B: Deploy the beta version to new EC2 instances in a new target group. Associate the new target group with the same ALB listener rule. Assign a weight of 90 to the existing target group. Assign a weight of 10 to the new target group.
options.C: Refactor the application to implement a feature flag for the beta version by using AWS AppConfig. Use the feature flag to enable the beta version for 10% of the EC2 instances.
options.D: Containerize and deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the beta version by using the CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes deployment configuration.

en.explanation:
## What the question is asking

The application already uses an Application Load Balancer, and the company wants approximately 10% of incoming requests to reach a beta version while minimizing configuration changes. The best solution should reuse the existing ALB and Route 53 configuration rather than introduce a new load balancer, redesign the application, or migrate to another compute platform.

## Correct answer: B

Deploy the beta version to a separate target group and modify the existing ALB listener rule's `forward` action to include both target groups with weights of 90 and 10.

Application Load Balancers support forwarding a matching request to multiple target groups. AWS documents that each target group can be assigned a weight from 0 through 999 and that requests are distributed according to the relative weights. Therefore, weights of 90 for the existing target group and 10 for the beta target group produce the required 90/10 traffic split. This requires only the beta EC2 instances, a new target group, and one modification to the existing listener rule; the existing ALB and Route 53 record remain unchanged. See [Application Load Balancer forward actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-action-types.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

Route 53 weighted routing can distribute traffic between resources according to relative record weights, so a 90/10 DNS split is technically possible. AWS specifically notes that weighted routing can be used to test new software versions. However, this option requires creating and configuring a second ALB and changing the Route 53 records in addition to creating the beta target group. It therefore involves more configuration changes than using the existing ALB's weighted target groups. See [Route 53 weighted routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-weighted.html).

### C

This option requires application refactoring and AWS AppConfig integration, which is substantially more change than modifying an ALB listener action. Additionally, enabling a feature on 10% of EC2 instances is not necessarily the same as routing exactly 10% of requests to the beta version because request distribution among instances can vary. AppConfig does support gradual configuration deployments and feature-flag percentage splits based on context values, but those capabilities require application/configuration integration and are unnecessary when the ALB already provides weighted request routing. See [deploying feature flags with AWS AppConfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/deploying-feature-flags.html) and [AppConfig split operator behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-multi-variant-feature-flags-rules.html).

### D

This requires containerizing the application, migrating it from a direct EC2 deployment to Amazon ECS, and configuring CodeDeploy blue/green deployment resources, which is far more change than necessary. Moreover, `CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` initially shifts 10% of traffic but automatically shifts the remaining 90% after 15 minutes. It is a staged deployment strategy, not an ongoing 10% beta traffic test. See [CodeDeploy deployment configurations for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html).

Thus, **B** meets the traffic-testing requirement with the least number of configuration changes.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个部署在 Amazon EC2 实例上的无状态 Web 应用程序。这些 EC2 实例位于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的一个目标组中。Amazon Route 53 管理该应用程序域名。该公司更新了应用程序 UI 并开发了应用程序的 beta 版本。该公司希望使用其 10% 的流量来测试 beta 版本。哪种解决方案能够以最少的配置更改满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 beta 版本部署到新目标组中的新 EC2 实例。将新目标组关联到一个新的 ALB。更新现有的 Route 53 记录以使用加权路由策略。添加一条新的 Route 53 记录，使其使用相同的路由策略指向新的 ALB。为现有记录分配 90 的权重。为新记录分配 10 的权重。
options.B: 将 beta 版本部署到新目标组中的新 EC2 实例。将新目标组关联到同一个 ALB 侦听器规则。为现有目标组分配 90 的权重。为新目标组分配 10 的权重。
options.C: 重构应用程序，以便使用 AWS AppConfig 为 beta 版本实施功能标志。使用该功能标志为 10% 的 EC2 实例启用 beta 版本。
options.D: 将应用程序容器化并部署到 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)。使用 AWS CodeDeploy 和 `CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` 部署配置部署 beta 版本。

zh.explanation:
## 题目考查内容

该应用程序已使用 Application Load Balancer，公司希望在尽量减少配置更改的同时，让大约 10% 的传入请求到达 beta 版本。最佳解决方案应复用现有的 ALB 和 Route 53 配置，而不是引入新的负载均衡器、重新设计应用程序或迁移到其他计算平台。

## 正确答案：B

将 beta 版本部署到单独的目标组，并修改现有 ALB 侦听器规则的 `forward` 操作，以包含两个目标组，权重分别为 90 和 10。

Application Load Balancers 支持将匹配的请求转发到多个目标组。AWS 文档说明，每个目标组可以分配从 0 到 999 的权重，并且请求会根据相对权重进行分配。因此，现有目标组的权重为 90、beta 目标组的权重为 10，即可实现所需的 90/10 流量拆分。此方案仅需要 beta EC2 实例、一个新目标组，以及对现有侦听器规则进行一次修改；现有 ALB 和 Route 53 记录保持不变。请参阅 [Application Load Balancer forward actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-action-types.html)。

## 其他选项错误的原因

### A

Route 53 加权路由可以根据相对记录权重在资源之间分配流量，因此从技术上讲可以实现 90/10 的 DNS 流量拆分。AWS 明确指出，加权路由可用于测试新的软件版本。但是，该选项除了创建 beta 目标组外，还需要创建并配置第二个 ALB，以及更改 Route 53 记录。因此，与使用现有 ALB 的加权目标组相比，它涉及更多配置更改。请参阅 [Route 53 weighted routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-weighted.html)。

### C

该选项需要重构应用程序并集成 AWS AppConfig，其变更量远大于修改 ALB 侦听器操作。此外，为 10% 的 EC2 实例启用某项功能不一定等同于将恰好 10% 的请求路由到 beta 版本，因为请求在实例之间的分配可能有所不同。AppConfig 确实支持渐进式配置部署，以及基于上下文值的功能标志百分比拆分，但这些功能需要应用程序/配置集成；在 ALB 已经提供加权请求路由时，这并无必要。请参阅 [deploying feature flags with AWS AppConfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/deploying-feature-flags.html) 和 [AppConfig split operator behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-multi-variant-feature-flags-rules.html)。

### D

该选项需要将应用程序容器化、将其从直接部署在 EC2 上迁移到 Amazon ECS，并配置 CodeDeploy 蓝绿部署资源，所需变更远超必要程度。此外，`CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` 会先转移 10% 的流量，但在 15 分钟后会自动转移其余 90%。这是一种分阶段部署策略，而不是持续的 10% beta 流量测试。请参阅 [CodeDeploy deployment configurations for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html)。

因此，**B** 能以最少的配置更改满足流量测试要求。

en.question: A company frequently creates Docker images of an application. The company stores the images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company creates both tagged images and untagged images. The company wants to implement a solution to automatically delete images that have not been updated for a long time and are not frequently used. The solution must retain at least a specified number of images. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies on the ECR repository to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.
options.B: Use Amazon ECR lifecycle policies to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be to retained in the repository.
options.C: Configure an AWS Lambda function to run a schedule to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be retained in the repository.
options.D: Use AWS Systems Manager to run a script by using the aws:executeScript action to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The company needs a native, repository-level mechanism that automatically cleans up both tagged and untagged ECR images while preserving a configured minimum number of images. The key requirement is **least operational overhead**.

## Correct answer: B

**Use Amazon ECR lifecycle policies to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be retained in the repository.**

Amazon ECR lifecycle policies are purpose-built to automate image cleanup. A policy can contain separate rules for tagged and untagged images and can expire images using criteria such as:

- `sinceImagePushed`: expires images older than a specified number of days.
- `imageCountMoreThan`: sorts matching images by push time and expires the older images beyond the configured count, thereby retaining the specified number of recent images.

AWS provides examples of policies that expire images by age and that keep only a specified number of untagged images. After a lifecycle policy is applied, ECR evaluates and expires qualifying images automatically, generally within 24 hours, without requiring a scheduler or custom code. See [Examples of lifecycle policies in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/lifecycle_policy_examples.html) and [Amazon ECR lifecycle policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/LifecyclePolicies.html).

For pull-frequency-based management, current ECR lifecycle policies can also select images using `sinceImagePulled`; however, that criterion is used to transition images to archive storage, after which archived images can be expired using `sinceImageTransitioned`. The age- and count-based expiration described in option B directly satisfies the core cleanup and retention requirements.

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **A. Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies:** ECR repositories are not customer-managed S3 buckets. S3 Lifecycle rules apply to objects in S3 buckets and cannot be attached to an ECR repository or used to manage ECR images. ECR has its own native lifecycle-policy feature.

- **C. Scheduled AWS Lambda function:** A Lambda function could call ECR APIs to list and delete images, but the company would need to develop, schedule, secure, monitor, and maintain the custom function. This creates more operational overhead than a native ECR lifecycle policy.

- **D. Systems Manager `aws:executeScript`:** A Systems Manager Automation runbook could also invoke APIs or scripts to delete images, but it would require custom automation, IAM permissions, scheduling, testing, and maintenance. It is unnecessary when ECR provides lifecycle policies specifically for this task.

Therefore, **B** is the native and lowest-overhead solution.

zh.question: 一家公司经常为某个应用程序创建 Docker 镜像。该公司将镜像存储在 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 中。该公司同时创建带标签镜像和无标签镜像。该公司希望实施一种解决方案，以自动删除长时间未更新且不常使用的镜像。该解决方案必须至少保留指定数量的镜像。哪种解决方案能够以最低的运维开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 ECR 存储库上使用 Amazon S3 Lifecycle 策略，根据镜像年龄或镜像缺少标签自动删除镜像。
options.B: 使用 Amazon ECR 生命周期策略，根据镜像年龄或存储库中需要保留的镜像数量删除镜像。
options.C: 配置 AWS Lambda 函数按计划运行，根据镜像年龄或需要保留的镜像数量删除镜像。
options.D: 使用 AWS Systems Manager 通过 `aws:executeScript` 操作运行脚本，根据镜像年龄或镜像缺少标签自动删除镜像。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该公司需要一种原生的、存储库级别的机制，能够在保留已配置的最少镜像数量的同时，自动清理带标签和无标签的 ECR 镜像。关键要求是 **最低运维开销**。

## 正确答案：B

**使用 Amazon ECR 生命周期策略，根据镜像年龄或存储库中需要保留的镜像数量删除镜像。**

Amazon ECR 生命周期策略专门用于自动化镜像清理。一个策略可以包含针对带标签镜像和无标签镜像的独立规则，并且可以使用以下条件使镜像过期：

- `sinceImagePushed`：使早于指定天数的镜像过期。
- `imageCountMoreThan`：按推送时间对匹配的镜像进行排序，并使超出配置数量的旧镜像过期，从而保留指定数量的最新镜像。

AWS 提供了根据镜像年龄使镜像过期，以及仅保留指定数量无标签镜像的策略示例。应用生命周期策略后，ECR 会自动评估并使符合条件的镜像过期，通常会在 24 小时内完成，无需调度程序或自定义代码。请参阅 [Amazon ECR 中的生命周期策略示例](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/lifecycle_policy_examples.html) 和 [Amazon ECR 生命周期策略](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/LifecyclePolicies.html)。

对于基于拉取频率的管理，当前的 ECR 生命周期策略还可以使用 `sinceImagePulled` 选择镜像；但是，该条件用于将镜像转换到归档存储，之后可以使用 `sinceImageTransitioned` 使已归档镜像过期。选项 B 中描述的基于年龄和数量的过期方式，直接满足核心的清理和保留要求。

## 其他选项为何不正确

- **A. Amazon S3 Lifecycle 策略：** ECR 存储库不是由客户管理的 S3 存储桶。S3 Lifecycle 规则适用于 S3 存储桶中的对象，不能附加到 ECR 存储库，也不能用于管理 ECR 镜像。ECR 具有自身原生的生命周期策略功能。

- **C. 计划运行的 AWS Lambda 函数：** Lambda 函数可以调用 ECR API 来列出并删除镜像，但公司需要开发、调度、保护、监控和维护该自定义函数。与原生 ECR 生命周期策略相比，这会产生更多运维开销。

- **D. Systems Manager `aws:executeScript`：** Systems Manager Automation 运行手册也可以调用 API 或脚本来删除镜像，但它需要自定义自动化、IAM 权限、调度、测试和维护。当 ECR 专门为此任务提供生命周期策略时，这种做法并无必要。

因此，**B** 是原生且运维开销最低的解决方案。

en.question: A company is developing a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The application requires monitoring of custom performance metrics. The company must collect metrics for API response times and database query latency across multiple instances. Which solution will generate the custom metrics with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the instances. Configure the agent to collect the custom metrics. Instrument the application to send the metrics to the agent.
options.B: Use Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus to scrape the custom metrics from the application. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to forward the metrics to CloudWatch.
options.C: Create a custom AWS Lambda function that polls the application endpoints and database at regular intervals. Program the Lambda function to calculate the custom metrics and to send the metrics to Amazon CloudWatch by using PutMetricData API calls.
options.D: Implement custom logging in the application code to record the custom metrics. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to extract and analyze the metrics.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The application runs across multiple EC2 Linux instances and needs to publish application-level latency measurements—API response times and database query latency—as custom metrics. The key requirement is the **least operational overhead**, so the preferred design should use an existing AWS-supported telemetry agent rather than introduce another monitoring service, polling system, or log-query workflow.

## Correct answer: A

**A. Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent, and instrument the application to send metrics to the agent.**

The CloudWatch agent can retrieve custom application metrics through the **StatsD** or **collectd** protocols; collectd is supported on Linux, and StatsD is supported on Linux and Windows. It can then send those metrics directly to CloudWatch. AWS specifically describes StatsD as useful for instrumenting an application's own metrics, including timer and histogram metric types that are appropriate for API and database latency measurements. The application can emit measurements to the local agent, while the agent handles collection, aggregation, and publication across all instances.

This avoids maintaining custom metric-publication code or a separate collector/service architecture. The agent can also aggregate StatsD observations before sending them, which can reduce the number of published data points. See [Collect metrics, logs, and traces using the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html) and [Retrieve custom metrics with StatsD](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-custom-metrics-statsd.html).

## Why the other options are incorrect

- **B — Incorrect.** Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is unnecessary when the required destination and monitoring service is CloudWatch. It introduces a Prometheus workspace and an ingestion architecture. For workloads outside the supported EKS managed-scraper scenario, AMP generally requires a customer-managed collector, Prometheus remote write, or application-side integration. Using AMP and then involving the CloudWatch agent adds components rather than reducing operational overhead. AWS documents the managed collector specifically for scraping Prometheus-compatible endpoints in EKS; otherwise, a customer-managed collector or direct remote write is required. See [Ingest metrics to your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP-ingest-methods.html).

- **C — Incorrect.** A custom Lambda polling solution requires developing and operating polling, scheduling, timeout handling, IAM permissions, metric calculations, and `PutMetricData` calls. Polling endpoints also measures synthetic or externally observed behavior and might not accurately capture every application's internal database-query latency. Although `PutMetricData` can publish custom metrics, implementing this bespoke pipeline has more operational overhead than using the CloudWatch agent's supported application-metric ingestion. See [Use `PutMetricData` with an AWS SDK or CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/example_cloudwatch_PutMetricData_section.html).
